productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Best Ever - what a buy !Best Ever - what a buy !
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought this mini PC because my Dell desktop died. I was thinking about buying a new PC or Laptop anyway and had been researching a new one for a couple weeks , I was leaning towards a Dell laptop because I already owned a Dell desktop and 2 dell laptops.  My work laptop is also a Dell. I had never heard of these mini-computers and saw one when I was browsing on Amazon. Believe me I was very skeptical, I could not believe I had never seen these before, anyway after doing a bunch of research on line and word of mouth from friends and relatives, I decided to give ones of these mini-computers a try.  I really liked the idea of the size.., no more big box under the desk, or on the desk. I also have a couple of giant monitors I wanted to hook up to it so I made sure I got one that would do dual monitors (1 monitor is actually a Amazon Fire TV). I also wanted a large hard drive and a decent amount of ram. I opted for the model with the Windows 11 Pro Intel Core i7-11390H (Turbo 5.0 GHz) 1TB SSD 16GB DDR4 and I can say this thing is lightening speed. At least I think it is. I am using it for just basic things like browsing, watching live sporting events like tennis, F1, etc, streaming movies, videos, doing home taxes, etc. I am not using it for any kind of gaming, so I cant tell you how it would be for that. But I would highly recommend this mini computer. It is fantastic in my opinion.  It was very easy to setup.  I have had it for about 2 months now and I am thinking of buying another one for my Mom who is always complaining that her pc is too slow.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Small computer, big surprise — it handles everything I throw at it dailySmall computer, big surprise — it handles everything I throw at it daily
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I'll admit I had doubts. Something this small — you can see it in the picture with my mouse on it— didn't seem like it could replace a real desktop. But within the first hour of using it, those doubts were gone. It starts up fast, everything responds immediately, and it just feels like a real computer. Because it is one.My day-to-day is pretty simple: browsing the internet, working with AI tools like Claude, video calls, writing documents, and streaming video. I usually have 15–20 browser tabs open at the same time, and this machine doesn't flinch. Not once have I sat there waiting for something to load or catch up.For AI users in particular: if you work with Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity or any browser-based AI tool, the extra memory on this configuration is worth every penny. I can keep multiple AI conversations open, switch between them, and the machine keeps up without breaking a sweat.Setting it up was genuinely easy. This was one of the things that pleasantly surprised me. Windows 11 Pro came pre-installed and already activated. I powered it on, went through the normal Windows setup questions, and within about five minutes I was at the desktop. No product key hunting, no activation screens, no frustration. For those of us who just want to get to work, that matters.Several other things I appreciate.It boots up fast. It runs quietly. Small size frees up so much desk space. productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Fastest Computer I Own -- BUT NOW BECOMES UNUSABLE AFTER WINDOWS UPDATE
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Late 2023 probably: Super fast, compared to my other PCs.  I had a problem connecting an external BD reader (via a SATA-to-USB3 connector), so I cannot use that with this PC.  Otherwise everything is working as advertised, including USB3 for external HDDs.  HDMI and DP also worked fine, as did wireless (USB2 dongle) keyboard and mouse.  My gigabit LAN works just fine.  Windows 11 Pro is successfully activated.  I have not tested USB-C.  I was able to expand the RAM to the maximum 64 GB, but due to unclear documentation, I was not able to add an SSD expansion (which I had bought and then returned).  In fact, I found the documentation so lacking that I tried "Contact Us" with the manufacturer, and did not get a reply.  I finally gave up, and did not add more internal SSD.  Because this PC uses SSD storage, I do NOT use it for a lot of writes and rewrites: that is all done with real, networked HDDs.  (In my experience, SSDs have a limited shelf life if you constantly write and rewrite them.)  This was well worth the money.UPDATE March 2025: I am changing my review from 5 stars to 1 star.  This Mini-PC was working great until a Microsoft (MS) update killed it.  After I log in, the screen goes black.  I can then Ctrl+Alt+Del and THAT window shows up (rest of screen) still black.  I finally muddled through restoring an earlier version of the PC (before the Windows Update).  By the next day the PC had died again because Microsoft insisted on reinstalling the "bad" update.  It took me forever to figure out how to stop MS from reinstalling the update.  (You stop downloads via the Registry.  It still thinks I should install the update, but it seems thwarted -- for now.)  Trying to contact MS proved impossible.  Their automation is such that it doesn't consider that an update is bad.  There is no way to tell them that, that I could find.  I tried looking on the Intel site for a video-driver update, but that accomplished nothing.  Some INTEL GRAPHICS UTILITY (or some such) comes up from time to time and says something is wrong, but it doesn't tell me what.  I go to the MS shop and it says that app is installed and up-to-date.  TWICE I HAVE TRIED TO CONTACT GMKtec support and TWICE it has ignored my entreaties.  I hold open the possibility that my firewall or Ad Blocker or Privacy Badger is blocking something (since I run an email server), but there is no indication ANYWHERE of what I have to let through.  If GMKtec is trying to get through, they are blocked, and the AMAZON page gives no hint on what IPs, etc. need to get through.  In my experience, it is not my PC blocking the connection: it is there is no active GMKtec support, despite what the AMAZON web page says.  So I am STUCK with no longer being able to install MS updates.  And to underline how arrogant MS is, it doesn't give you the ability to block just one update.  In older versions of Windows, you could block a specific update, but not in the newer versions.  If I went back to allowing downloads, it would install the bad update.  The PC is running Windows 11 Pro.  I can still use the Mini-PC; I can just no longer update it with MS updates.  And if you're wondering, I did connect a second monitor and try to get things to work that way, but MS Windows completely freaked out and forgot how to do the desktop.  (I've done it before with other WIndows, and I can navigate mulitple displays just fine with them.  It's something about the video on this PC and Windows 11, is my guess.)  So for now, I can use the Mini-PC but cannot get MS updates for, for example, so-called critical vulnerabilities.  MS is absolutely no help -- their interface has no "update is bad" report function.  And GMKtec, as far as I can tell, does not actively support their product, despite what the implication is on the AMAZON web site.  The Mini-PC worked for for more than a year...until the "bad" MS update.  Oh, yeah, I searched for and downloaded drivers from the GKMtec web site and presumably installed them (that process was clear as mud), so who knows -- maybe I didn't install them.  I wasn't born knowing how hardware works...or software for that matter...

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I've now purchased several of these for myself and my clients with truly excellent results. Fan noise is slight but noticeable yet of no concern to anything I am doing.Additionally, I strongly recommend keeping factory Bios settings as these are ideal including leaving UEFI setting and Secure Boot disabled for you Ubuntu, Kubuntu & Windows builds for best results.I highly recommend this little, elegant system for travel and much more, bringing necessary cables to be able to connect to Big Screen or other display such as Upperizon's excellent Portable displays!This system is also a wonderful Value at the current price point of $229, beyond that price, I would Not consider it...

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This review is for non-techies who want to use this small computer for low key Win 11 operation like docs and web surfing.  The good news is that it can replace a desktop and runs a Win 11 setup out of the box without any modification.A problem for non-techies is that the little manual that comes with the computer is mostly in Chinese and has no quick start instructions that are obvious.  Here is a quick start for getting going with Win 11:You'll need to have a mouse and keyboard that connect to the USB ports on the computer. Bluetooth won't work yet. These can be hard wired or with the wireless chip ("dongle") that plugs into the USB port.  Either way, plug those in.  There are 4 USB ports on the computer.Connect your monitor to the computer with the supplied HDMI cable or with a Displayport cable (if you have that and can't use HDMI)Connect the power plug to the computer, and plug the other end into an AC outlet.Push the computer power button to on.  The power button is right below the Dreamquest logo.Assuming your monitor is on, the Windows registration screen should come up and your mouse and keyboard should work.Go through the Win 11 registration.Some hints about the registration:You get asked if you want to install Windows security including Windows defender.  I would.You get asked if you want to migrate your microsoft apps and settings from another computer .  If you have a microsoft account this is a good idea, but be aware that the only apps brought over are the ones you got through the microsoft store.  Other app names will come in the app list with a message to install them.You get asked if you want to install Microsoft One (Cloud) drive.  That's up to you if you want to use that.When the Windows registration is complete, the first thing to do is run all the security. Some of these take a long time and you don't want your computer to go to sleep in the middle.  So go to settings from the start button, then System, then Power.  Set the sleep time out to never  (change this back if you'd like when everything is done).Go to the all apps list from the Start button and choose Windows Security.  First open  Virus and Threat Protection updates and dun the update check.  On my computer the last update was 5 years ago.  Make sure you have an update no more than a week old.After the update, go to scan options near the top and run full scan.  This may take an hour.Look  at all the Windows Security features and follow up on anything that doesn't have a check mark.Now you can take a look at your apps that are actually installed and decide if you want to buy new copies of ones your want, or do online subscriptions.  If you use Edge and chose to port MS apps, it likely also imported your passwords.You have a lot of personal work to set up the screen the way you like it, but that's independent of the computer.The computer is fast and has an excellent video display.  It takes 25 seconds to boot from the hibernate mode.I'm sure there are some things  I missed here, but hopefully this info will help.The reason for 4 stars rather than 5 are two fold:  First, the lack of a good quick start document in the package and second, the Windows install must be a very old one because the computer needs to do an enormous number, around 10, updates.  These downloads slow down the computer for the first few days of operation.  These are way more updates than should be expected.Still the computer works extremely well and, even with its small size can completely replace a desktop.  It is totally quiet, no fan, gets a bit warm to the touch, but not hot.  I've been pleasantly surprised with it.

The Intel UHD Graphics (i3-10110U/N95) struggles with single-channel memory and low execution units, crippling its gaming performance and barely handling basic 4K video without stuttering. While the older Radeon Vega 5 (4300U) was decent, our 7330U's Radeon Graphics (6 CUs) pushes the boundaries, delivering higher graphics clock speeds (up to 1.8GHz) and significantly better rendering capabilities. It can drive triple 4K@60Hz displays with zero lag, edit photos/videos.

【Generous Storage & Easy Expansion】The KAMRUI Pinova P2 mini desktop computers comes with 16GB LPDDR4X RAM (higher frequency, lower power) for buttery‑smooth multitasking, and a 256GB M.2 SSD for blazing fast boot‑up, quick file transfers, and no more long loading screens. It also features two storage expansion slots (1x M.2 2280 SATA/NVMe PCIe 3.0 slot + 1x M.2 2280 SATA slot), supporting up to 4TB total (not included). You’ll have all the space you need for projects, media, and important data.

【Triple 4K Display Output】The KAMRUI Pinova P2 mini desktop pc is equipped with HDMI 2.0 ×1 + DP 1.4 ×1 + USB 3.2 Gen2 Type‑C ×1 (with DP Alt Mode), enabling simultaneous triple 4K@60Hz output. Whether for home entertainment, remote work, or conference room presentations, it delivers an immersive visual experience. Two USB 3.2 Gen2 Type‑A ports (up to 10Gbps – 21x faster than USB 2.0) make data transfers and device expansion a breeze.

【USB 3.2 Gen2 Type‑C: 10Gbps & Versatile Connectivity】The USB 3.2 Gen2 Type‑C port on the KAMRUI P2 small pc supports 10Gbps data transfer speeds and can also output DisplayPort 1.4 video. Together with Gigabit LAN, Wi‑Fi, and Bluetooth, you get a fast, flexible, and productive connected environment – wired or wireless.

【Space‑Saving Design & Efficient, Quiet Cooling】This Portable KAMRUI Pinova P2 Mini PC features a sleek silver case and measures just 5.05 x 5.05 x 1.73 inches – easy to slip into a bag for business trips. Save desk space further with the included VESA mount (attach it behind a monitor or on a wall). The newly improved cooling system keeps the micro PC running stably even under load; the fan is virtually silent during light use and remains remarkably quiet under load – minimal or inaudible noise, so you can focus completely on what matters most.

【Why KAMRUI? Reliable Technical Support & Warranty】We offer lifetime technical support and a 12‑month satisfaction service for all KAMRUI products. If you run into any issues, simply contact our professional support team – we’ll do everything to provide a solution you’re happy with.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Excellent, lightweight, super portable portable mini computer!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: UPDATE #2: It has now been almost 1.5 years since I purchased this back in November 2024.  I was working away from home last month and had a terrifying moment when I set everything up and turned it on and got the blue screen of death.  I did a hard shut down, turned it back on and got the screen for my monitor and name with a blue circle turning and nothing happening on startup with the Kamrui.  I waited 20 minutes and did a hard shut down several times.  Eventually it said something about "repairing" something and did I want to continue. I said yes.  It did the circle thing for another 20 minutes and then finally booted up.  After that I had no issues for several weeks.  Then last week, same thing happened upon startup.  I started searching for information on this particular device and startup issues and read to do a hard shutdown, unplug anything connected via USB, and then restart.  It started right up - no issues.  I then only did "restarts" instead of actual shut downs for the remainder of the week, but was traveling again so I had to power it down yesterday for my commute.  It worked fine yesterday, but today when I turned it back on I got the circle again. After panicking a couple of times and trying hard restarts, I remembered the USB issue and unplugged those, turned it back on and it booted right up. SOOOO - if you ever have the scary circle or repair screen pop up on startup, do a hard shut down, unplug all your peripherals except your monitor and power cord and then restart.  After it boots up correctly, then reconnect your peripherals.  I have no idea WHY it is doing that, but at least I know how to fix the issue now.  Other than that minor annoyance, the computer still works great. Super quick, great sound, great visuals, doesn't heat up much at all and I'm only utilizing half the memory.UPDATE:  It is now a little over 2 months from when I purchased and started using this.  I had some sort of update overnight and when I turned on my computer, after entering my passcode, it gave me an error that my "user profile failed to load" and my main screen looked liked a fresh install with hardly any apps on there.  I couldn't open Notepad, Word, and none of my auto logins were working.  My files were still there that I had added recently. I rebooted twice.  I was still having issues even after logging back into my Windows and Google accounts, and it appeared to still be updating Windows, so I let it run the update in the background for another 10 minutes, then shut computer off and rebooted one more time.  At that fourth boot, everything came back up looking normal.  My classic windows shell was back, my background and regular screen saver were back, my icons on my desktop were in their correct spots.  It was very weird.  My advice to you is disable automatic windows updates when you first get this, and just try and remember to do those regularly at a time that suits YOU, so you don't get your work schedule impacted by a random update.  Don't immediately panic if you wake up one day to what looks like a fresh install/brand new computer appearance.  Let the computer percolate for 10-15 minutes, then turn off and reboot in safe mode or reboot several times until you get back to the regular working device you are used to.  I will update how things are going with the system again at the end of 6 months.  NOTE: I do carry this in a heavily padded bag with other devices when I travel for work frequently.  So it does get plugged/unplugged, and wagged around a lot.  Not sure if that affects it or not, but since it has 2 SSDs and a sturdy plastic shell, it should be impervious to bumps and knocks, especially since it is very well protected inside the bag.I'm a remote medical transcriptionist who also pet sits away from home. Why get paid for one job when you can get paid to 2 or 3 simultaneously?! I normally use a 17-inch laptop and a portable monitor when I travel, but recently I started getting the blue screen of death showing up on my laptop periodically.  While it was still functional and I could transfer my programs from it, I decided to find a new device. The current crop of laptops were fairly pricey for the size RAM I wanted and most only have one or two USB connections now and I need at least 3, preferably 4. Also, some laptops have data only transfer on their USB-C connections so rather than deal with that I decided to check into mini PCs.  This one had great ratings and I really liked the fact that I could increase it by adding an additional 2.5" SSD drive.  It's super easy to do that. Just release a latch, slightly angle and insert your drive until it connects and seats into the slot.  I know have a computer with two hard drives with an additional Terabyte of storage.  It boots up lightning fast and I was able to download Windows, Word, and all my other applications with no issue whatsoever.  I had cloned my laptop to the SSD, so upon booting it up for the first time my screen saver, settings, icons, etc. were already in place.  I LOVE that it has two HDMI connections.  I didn't think I needed that, until I started working at a facility where I needed to utilize TWO 24" monitors when I'm away from home and not able to use my 39" monitor.  This KAMRUI mini PC weights next to nothing and it's just barely larger in diameter than a slice of sandwich bread.  In addition to the two HDMI ports, it comes with 4 USB ports, a headset jack, and the power cord.  It's so small and light, I'm now able to use it as a portable computer in place of my laptop and I just leave my laptop set up to work on when I'm at home.  When I purchased it they were on sale for $130 and I see they are around the same price currently, so I'll probably invest in another one to clone my laptop to and keep on hand for when my laptop finally bites the dust, so that I can have fully functional workstations wherever I am and won't have to keep unhooking/rehooking things up every week or two.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: A Vast Improvement Over My Older Windows Computers
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I have had my new KAMRUI GK3 PLUS for several days now, and I must say it has been a delightful surprise coming from an older version of Windows and an older desktop computer. What a breath of fresh air!  It is about the size of a double decker grilled cheese sandwich with double decker performance.  I was pleasantly surprised at the speed....not an untamed blur, but very very manageable.  I don't do all the performance testing of professionals, just my own tests in comparison of all the computers I have owned over the years.  This KAMRUI is the fastest Windows machine I have owned personally.  Of course I have not owned the most expensive gaming machines or some of the more expensive video editing computers, but I have always bought and ran low to mid-level consumer computers for home use, and I can say this one outperforms all the others (I personally) have owned.  Of course technology moves fast, and the mini is a good example of that. It was very easy to set up, although the updates did take 45 minutes or so, and I did them without any peripherals attached except a keyboard.Since the original updates, it has asked me to update a couple times since, and I did quickly and without a hitch.  So far, not a single freeze up, just a clean running computer.  I run a lot of YouTube videos, and they are crystal clear, do not freeze, buffer, or distort.  I also do desktop publishing and most other office type requirements without any problem at all so far.  If the saying "You get what you pay for" is really true, then it is doubly true with this KAMRUI mini computer.  For $149-$169 dollars, I just don't see where one could go wrong for the AVERAGE use of a home computer.  All peripherals work as they should including stand alone DVD/RW read/write and burn.  Works great.  Keyboard, mouse, monitor, external hard-drive, and printer are all working flawlessly.  I'm impressed by the performance of KAMRUI's package in such a small form.  Will it perform as well as an Intel i9.....no, it wasn't meant to.  Price one of those.Five stars from this user,  because for me, it lives up to the description listed on Amazon.  I hope anyone that reads this and buys one, finds the same satisfaction I have.  I took a chance on the mini as opposed to going back to a cumbersome tower and all that, and I am a happy camper so far.  Longevity?  Only time will tell, as with all and anything electronic.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Nice for the price. Wifi is not consistant.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This is a great mini PC. For the price, it's unbeatable. Super easy to hook up, it comes with a power cable and a HDMI cable. I used my own HDMI but it's nice that it came with one in case I didn't have one. It fits under my monitor riser perfectly and I like the small footprint.I got this because I was using my laptop as a desktop and then having to unhook everything to take it with me when I need to leave my desk, which was annoying. I didn't want to spend a lot and honestly, I really use this for word processing, emails, and light photo work. So I'm not gaming and I'm not stressing the RAM at all really. It's 'snappy' as a lot of other reviews have commented, but it is not as fast as my LG Gram. Granted, my LG Gram was like 800 bucks and it's got twice the RAM and hard drive. So, again, not a fair comparison.The only downside, *actual* downside, that I found is the wifi. I don't know if it's a software or hardware issue...I know others have commented on it as well, it's true, the wifi does *weird* things. I am literally five feet from my router. None of my other devices will have an issue, just the mini pc. It will go from three bars of wifi down to two then to one then just the little dot, if I turn the wifi off, then back on, presto-fixo- it works again. If that doesn't do it, I have to restart the computer which takes like a single minute to do. The point is though, I notice it when I'm trying to send an email or watch a video clip for work, and it's super annoying to have to shut off the wifi and turn it back on again to get it to work. It wasn't as common right when I set everything up. It took it a week to really start up as a repeat issue, but now I'm worried I'm going to be battling the wifi for as long as I keep this. Just today I've had to toggle it off and on four times. Since other reviewers have the same issue, I'm not sure getting a replacement will help. This will do for now, I'll suck it up and deal with it, but I don't know that I would buy this again because of the wifi problem.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great Mini PC for multi monitor setups
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This Mini PC is nice for my everyday tech needs. I needed a compact desktop for basic web browsing, online shopping, streaming videos, and light office work. This machine easily handles all of that without any issues. Even under load, the fan makes minimal noise, so it never distracts me while I am working or watching movies late at night. The silver design looks stylish on my desk, but it is small enough to pack in a bag if I ever need to take it on a trip. Having 16GB of RAM keeps multitasking smooth when opening several applications at once. Connecting three 4K monitors was simple using the HDMI, DisplayPort, and Type-C ports. The video output is crisp and responsive across all three displays, which makes working from home so much easier. Data transfers are super quick thanks to the fast USB 3.2 ports, and the Wi-Fi connection stays strong and consistent without dropping out. It uses very little power compared to traditional big tower PCs, which helps keep energy costs low. The setup took less than ten minutes from unboxing to sitting at the desktop screen.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: COMPLETELY FAULTY!!! Once plugged in, I started having SERIOUS internet connectivity issues almost immediately. To the point where I genuinely thought that my internet was the problem. So, I scheduled a house call to my internet provider for bright and early the very next morning, as my remote job REQUIRES me to have a certain level of upload and download speeds. I needed it fixed IMMEDIATELY or my position within my company would be subject to termination.My internet company came out, spent almost two whole hours at my house running a multitude of various tests to figure out what the issue was, only for them to meet me in my office at the very end and tell me, "I am no computer expert, but I can tell you right now that your new PC is the SOLE problem for your connectivity issues. It is completely blocking your internet. Your download speed went from over 400MBPS to 0.4 MBPS! Your upload speed went from almost 600 MBPS to a whopping 1.14 MBPS! You're getting worse than dial-up speed because of that PC." And they were absolutely correct because, when I unplugged it, there were ZERO ISSUES with my internet, as per usual.To top that news off, my internet guys also informed me that my supposed LAN port in the back of that PC wasn't even registering as anything of such. It was merely just a hole in the back of the PC labeled as an ethernet port for show. There was no power source to that port whatsoever. Despite the PC powering on, there were no capabilities for anything on that PC. Even the set up for the PC itself took almost two whole hours to TRY to generate.The only thing this PC was capable of was the brightening my screen. I tried many different ways of plugging it in, tried moving my system to various rooms in my house, did A COUPLE of hard resets on both that PC AND my internet, and nothing worked. Come to find out, this PC was 100% faulty and barely a PC at all. And I spent $300 on it, asked for a refund within 48 hours of receiving it on February 10th, returned it February 12th and my refund has now been delayed until March 21st. Well over the 30-day marker for return of funds. Convenient.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Perfect for running video streams and discord!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I was looking for a second PC to run two twitch streams (DashDucks and OurChickenLife) to take the load off of my actual gaming laptop and possibly some light gaming. My initial reaction was this is surprisingly fast for a sub $125 mini PC. It is snappy and loads chrome and the two twitch streams just fine with each stream in a separate window (one on each monitor). I was super happy with finally having the ability to have a PC with dual monitors and at this price point is in incredible.Set up was easy and I was up and running in under 5 minutes. Boot time is under 20 seconds and once I configured it for not needing to login even faster than that. I initially installed Steam, Discord, Chrome, SpeedTest (from the Microsoft store), and an auto clicker mouse program. I ended up deleting Steam and Discord as the game I primarily play struggled even on very low graphics settings. The game in question is Farm Together 2 and would highly recommend if you like farming games. Anyways, it wasn't unbearable but there was noticeable lag when moving around in the game. Discord ran ultra smooth though and there wasn't any lag so would be great for using that on this PC.As for internet speeds and quality goes, I would very HIGHLY recommend using an ethernet cable if you can. My current internet speed is 1.0 GB up and down. Under WiFi, I got a 1/5th of that speed with speeds around 200 down and 150 up despite this PC being literally inches from the router. This is most likely a limit of the WiFi 5 used in this PC and not necessarily a defect.  Once I installed a Cat 6 ethernet cable, I got around my full speed of 930 both up and down. While it was on WiFi, I didn't notice any lag when watching the twitch streams When installing windows updates though, definitely use an ethernet cable.As for noise level this thing is ultra quiet even under 100% CPU usage. Always was cool to the touch when I checked and no burning or any kind of smells like that since I have been using it. I keep it running 24/7 and as of the writing of this review it has been flawless.As for storage and RAM this seems to be good to go right out of the gate. You do have the option to upgrade if you wish, but for my needs the 8GB of RAM is just fine. It hits around 60% usage for RAM with running 2 chrome windows. And for storage with only chrome, speedtest, my mouse program, and edge which was preinstalled storage is very sufficient for me. And you can also upgrade the hard drive (SSD) to 2TB so if in the future I need more space or change how I use this PC I can. And honestly, that is a comforting thought knowing the option is available to me. If you are considering one of the larger storage models I would say go for it versus this 256GB version as it won't be an issue later on, but for me I got this version initially because of budget reasons and it would work for me and my needs. My game would probably run alot better if it had the 16GB of RAM but I am okay with just using it as a media consumption PC.Not having to worry about batteries and all that jazz was a huge selling point for me versus getting, say a Chromebook.  I have this plugged into my battery backup in the event of a power failure which alleviates my worries a bit.My only real complaint with this PC is the placement of the power button. I did accidentally press it causing the PC to go to sleep when connecting my mouse and keyboard, but this can be changed in settings as to what the power button does in settings. I do wish it was in the front, but it isn't anything deal breaking.Overall, this is a great little PC for what I needed it for, which was to run 2 twitch streams via chrome. Your mileage may vary, but I feel confident recommending this PC for light to medium use. I don't do video editing or any intense operations like that so I can't comment on that. USB connections have been stable (no random disconnects) and the HDMI ports have both been running great. It runs Windows 11 just fine and aside from some user stumbles on figuring out where things are now and then (coming from Windows 10) it is just fine.I hope this review has helped you and have a blessed day <3

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: 4 Stars - Hardware Failed, But Outstanding Customer Support & Full Refund
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: My initial review of the KAMRUI E3B Mini PC was a 1-star rating due to a complete hardware failure after five months of use. The system suffered from frequent Blue Screens of Death (BSOD) and would black out and reboot entirely whenever I attempted to play videos or handle multimedia tasks.Following my review, the seller proactively reached out to resolve the issue. They provided excellent customer service and issued a full refund for the product without any hassle. While the specific unit I received had technical flaws, the seller has proven to be highly responsible and trustworthy.As previously stated, the KAMRUI E3B Mini PC failed after five months of use, experiencing constant BSOD crashes and reboots during basic YouTube video playback. The hardware itself was a disappointment for my productivity needs.Recommended if you would like to buy this one then you can at least rest assured that the company stands firmly behind their products and takes care of their customers.My rating to 4 stars purely to reflect their customer support . Not the PRODUCT.--------------------------------------- Previous Rating and Details -----------------------------⭐ One Star - Complete Failure After 5 Months of Use - Do Not Buy!Initial Review: 5 Stars (Mistake!)When I first purchased the KAMRUI E3B Mini PC with AMD Ryzen 7 5825U, I was incredibly impressed. It was fast, quiet, and seemed like a powerhouse in a tiny form factor. For the first few months, it performed flawlessly, and I happily gave it a 5-star rating, feeling confident in my purchase.Unfortunately, that initial excitement has completely evaporated. After only about five months of use, this Mini PC has become utterly unreliable and is actively hampering my work.The system now faces constant, severe stability issues that make it unusable:Frequent Blue Screens of Death (BSOD): The blue screen appears with alarming regularity, often without warning, forcing my work to halt and risking data loss.Video Playback Failure (Black Screen & Reboot): This is the most frustrating issue. I cannot watch videos for any extended period—not even simple YouTube videos. The screen will suddenly go black, and the entire system will immediately reboot. This happens consistently when under any kind of video or multimedia load.Unreliable for Work: The constant crashes and reboots have made this machine completely untrustworthy for daily tasks. I bought this to be a productive workstation, and instead, it has become a source of immense disappointment and stress.Conclusion: A Product That Will Not LastMy initial positive experience has been overshadowed by these critical, deep-seated stability problems. The KAMRUI E3B Mini PC with the Ryzen 7 5825U has demonstrated a severe lack of long-term reliability.The consistent blue screens and the inability to handle basic video playback without crashing strongly suggest a fundamental flaw, possibly with the cooling, power delivery, or specific component quality.Save your money and your frustration. This product will not last, and its early failure is a major letdown. I have downgraded my rating from a temporary 5 stars to a definitive 1 Star.---------------- Previous Rating 5 ---------------------I wasn’t expecting such a powerhouse in such a tiny form factor. This one has blown me away with its performance, versatility, and value. It's my go-to machine now for both work and play.Pros :8 cores make multitasking effortlessTriple 4K display support is perfect for my home setupWiFi 6 & Bluetooth 5.2 is the lightning-fast connectivity.Super compact and easy to mount behind a monitor. Super easy installationCons :Don’t expect high-end gaming, but light titles like CS:GO and Stardew Valley run smooth at 1080p. Great for emulators and indie games. 4K streaming is flawless on Netflix and YouTube.Overall :  This mini PC punches way above its price. Quiet, fast, and shockingly capable—it’s the perfect pick for anyone needing a small but mighty desktop.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Perfect PC: Small, low cost, expandable, fast internet, dual 4K HDMI and plenty of USB ports.Perfect PC: Small, low cost, expandable, fast internet, dual 4K HDMI and plenty of USB ports.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This is the best low cost, super compact PC's I have found on Amazon. It is very inexpensive but still gives you all of the features you need for a compact PC. And it's upgradeable with an expansion bay to hold another SSD drive. This is rare in low cost compact PC's but is a must have. If you don't have this, then you're going to be really limited to what you can do with your PC. This expansion bay allows you to add a huge SSD fast hard drive later to expand the storage space BUT keep the super compact size and not have to add another power supply and another device hanging off the PC. So, if you're looking at another compact PC that is a little smaller than this one, but doesn't have the expansion bay, I highly suggest you get this one instead. You are going to need that one day. Plan ahead and get a system, like this one, that can be expanded. If not, you will likely have to buy another PC in the future that does allow this.I was really shocked how much you get for this super low cost. I would say my favorite things about this PC are: small size, low cost, expandable, fast internet connections, dual 4K HDMI and plenty of USB ports. I also like the cool LED lighting on it.But here is a full list of things I like about this PC:- Great looking (cool LED light strip around entire unit)- Compact size- Very light- Easy to attach to something like your wall, behind a monitor, in a drawer, under a desk- Fast SSD storage instantly shows photos and starts streaming video quickly- Switches between applications faster than I thought it would- Two HDMI ports included. 4K!!!- Great for home theater PC- Very fast WIFI (great for streaming, storing photos and videos, surfing the web, downloading files, etc)- GB Ethernet!- BT 4.2- Expandable storage which is really rare in a unit this small and this inexpensive. This is an absolute must have! Don't get a PC without this!- Such a low price that you can easily get one for each of your children if you want to set up a study room in your house where each child has their own computer. Just add a keyboard, mouse and monitor and you are done!- Windows and other software already pre-installed.- Plenty of USB ports (including faster USB 3!)- Very smooth graphics- Quick multi-tasking- Very responsive- Tons of USB ports- Dual monitor support. Or connect a TV and a monitor or projector and monitor, etc.- 4K video playback- Has a built in fan that comes on when needed to keep the whole system very cool. This will keep your speed high (won't slow down when it gets hot) and will extend the life of the PC. Also you can put it behind your TV and it will still pull in enough air to stay cool. Many of the "fanless" PC's sound good, but sometimes get too hot and slow down or end up not lasting as long.UPDATE: I didn't realize this, but the additional storage area if you want to add another SSD is removable. So, if you don't add the extra SSD, this is even thinner, lighter and smaller than I thought. And if you do add the SSD, you'll have the option to add a HUGE drive if you want! Very cool design... See photos attached.I highly suggest this PC for anyone looking for a compact PC with good expandability, fast connectivity, and all the features most people will need.Highly suggested. Buy with confidence!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Nice little computer with crappy sound
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Amazing what can be had for under $170. Went with the N97 processor, as it had a bit more punch. This unit was a bit lacking in storage but will add an SSD drive to the bay. I would much rather upgrade storage than processor any day of the week - especially on this one which is so easy to do. Just plug and play.Out of the box, pretty impressed. Once the Windows installation was completed, did a reboot. It booted up in under 15 seconds. More than fast enough.This is for my wife, and she doesn't play games. She'll use it for Zoom meetings, some word processing, web browsing and a few other tasks. More than enough for that.I ran a speed test with it and the upload/download were both around 40 Mbps. Not going to break any speed records for Wi-Fi. Likely not an issue if plugged in with a cable. But given that Zoom uses around 10 Mbps, it's more than enough for the tasks she will be using. But if you are looking to do any gaming that require download speed, not going to work well for you over Wi-Fi. You'll need to plug in a cable. Basic web browsing was fast and responsive, thanks to the decent processor. YouTube videos streamed flawlessly with no buffering at all.After a couple hours, the unit was barely warm to the touch.The only big negative so far, the sound. Plugging headphones straight into the unit resulted in a very annoying electrical cycle sound from a ground loop interaction somewhere within. Fortunately, I had a little inline 3.5mm ground loop isolator/filter I wasn't using. Plugged that in and then the headphones into that - perfect. It's an easy solution, and ground loop isolators can be had on here for under $10. You will definitely need one though if you plan on listening to anything with the headphone jack.All in all, super happy with it so far. Since the wife has a small desk, this will be the perfect solution for her. Only took off one star because of the sound issue.Edit: After a few days and a couple of software updates, the internet speed has become excellent. My current speed test was 300 Mbps down and 80 Mbps up - which is being limited by my ISP at those speeds, so the actual ability of the PC may be faster than that. But that's plenty fast for anything net related you could ever want to do.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Suspicious behavior on updates, but ran like a desktop.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I really liked this when I first set it up.  Came with Win. 11 Pro.  Loaded all my standard programs and all ran as expected.  I am not a gamer just a utility based user, word processing and spreadsheets and it actually ran AutoCAD smoothly on basic 2D type drawings.  The initial problem occurred when it would not install one of the cumulative updates.  I had not installed any antivirus just standard windows defender as active protection.  So I did the Windows reinstall process and let it wipe the programs and start fresh.  After initial setup I then did updates first.  It installed the problematic update.  Again loaded all my standard programs, mostly from Ninite’s site.  Then on the next update it got stuck again.  I have 4 other computers in my household and all loaded with the same basic programs and none of those had problems with the updates.  So, I did a reinstall again except this time I set it up to boot from USB and I downloaded the windows ISO from Microsoft. Here is where things got strange.  It acted like it was installing from the USB, but instead, it installed the same as before.  How do I know? Because the USB was setup as a RUFUS install and it did not do any of the settings I had set up in RUFUS.  My suspicion is my version had a hardware malware or program I could not get past and I do not have the knowledge to dig deeper.  Anyway I sent it back. (EDIT 12/01/2025 - Their is the possibility I did not have the boot order set up properly so that the previous statement and the following with a grain of salt)  I have read older versions of AceMagic had hardware malware installed but other reviews later said that had been eliminated.  I am not so sure.EDIT 12/01/2025 - I was contacted by Acemagic customer support and they offered to replace the unit.  They reached out on their own so it looks like their customer support dept. reads these reviews and takes them seriously.  I setup the new unit the same as the old one and no glitches until I tried to install the Windows 11 25H2 update.  Failed.  HOWEVER, this is not the units fault.  Seems this is happening to a lot of people and other systems. The work around is to download the full Windows 11 pro 25H2 ISO and do an upgrade.  Worked like a charm.  The new system seems stable and no hint of malware.  I scanned it pretty good, even looking at bios as well as software.  Based on their customer support, I experienced, I will raise the review by a star.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Small Box, Serious Punch — Surprisingly Capable for the Price
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This ACEMAGIC Mini PC is one of those “don’t judge a book by its size” situations. It’s compact, quiet, and honestly way more capable than you’d expect at this price point.The AMD Ryzen 4300U handles everyday workloads without breaking a sweat—multiple browser tabs, Office apps, light development work, even some basic design tasks all run smoothly. It’s not a gaming rig, but for productivity, media streaming, and general business use, it’s rock solid.Boot times are quick, and Windows 11 Pro comes clean and ready to go, which is a huge win—no weird bloatware circus. The 16GB RAM makes a noticeable difference compared to cheaper mini PCs, especially when multitasking. It feels responsive, not sluggish like a lot of budget boxes.Thermals and noise are also handled well. It stays quiet under normal use, and even when pushed a bit, it doesn’t sound like it’s about to take off. That alone makes it perfect for a home office or tucked behind a monitor setup.Ports are solid—plenty of connectivity for dual monitors, peripherals, and network options. It’s basically a clean, minimal workstation in a tiny footprint.If there’s a downside, it’s upgrade limitations and obviously no high-end graphics power. productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The 4-core performance on this mini PC is surprisingly solid. I’m running it at 1440p primarily as a remote-access media server, and it’s handled everything I’ve thrown at it so far.Some background: certain mini-pc's of this manufacturer were reportedly shipped with spyware, which the manufacturer blamed on a third-party supplier. I wasn’t taking any chances—I did a clean install of Windows 11 right away.Just know that after a clean install, you’ll probably need to manually install Wifi and Bluetooth drivers, and you might not have internet access on the device until you do. Having a second PC handy helps a lot. Ethernet worked for me immediately.Snappy Driver Installer was essential. Bluetooth drivers appeared installed but didn’t show devices until I used it to update the driver—after that, no issues. It also installed the Serial IO driver, which both Windows Update and Intel’s driver assistant missed. Expect a bit of hopping between Snappy, AceMagic’s website, Windows Update, and Intel’s tools to get things fully up and running.Although it's marketed with Wi-Fi 6, I haven’t seen anything close to Wi-Fi 6 speeds. I’m sticking with Ethernet for now, or might try a USB Wi-Fi 6 adapter later.One last thing: this unit gets hot—not just warm—especially under sustained load. I picked up a 140mm fan to place underneath it, which should help. They're not expensive.As a bonus, I tested ChromeOS Flex on this device, and it ran flawlessly. Wi-Fi, Ethernet, Bluetooth, and audio all worked out of the box, and the system felt snappy and responsive. If you're considering a lightweight, fast ChromeOS setup, this box is a great fit.All in all, it’s a great little machine for the price—just be prepared for a bit of setup work if you go the Windows route, and consider extra cooling if you’re running it hard.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Well its been almost a year, 10 months
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Well, I have had this device for 10 months now.  Its been running well, although trying to play even simple games on it has been frustrating.  However I did fins a fix which i have been using for a little over a month, and it is running smother and better than it ever did.  I installed a Linux distro on it, specifically i installed the latest stable LTS Pop!_OS on it, while i have been partial to Manjaro in the past i decided to see if Pop!_OS would work well, and wow it is very clean and the system runs smoother than it ever did with Windows installed on it, even right out of the box.  What attracted me to this device originally was its size, minimal desk space, or in my case counter space.  Its small and compact making it easy to move around or hide behind other things, like the TV for instance.  The size makes it convenient to move and use, making it quite versatile for a few fast setup applications.  The multiple display connection ports, LAN, and USB ports make this thing very handy for its size too.  But I will say that Windows does not let this little beast do its thing, Windows runs too many background processes and seriously bogs the poor thing down.  Even trying to do simple things with windows running, like watching videos, or playing simple games, like Houseflipper, or Inscription on Steam, made the system almost unusable, and made any kind of game play just unbearable.  But about a moth or so ago, i got fed up with windows because it insisted on doing updates while i was trying to do an online Teams meeting for work and well it was just bad all the ways it could be.  Made it seem like is was using a POS machine, which i knew it shouldn't be running that bad.  So i backed up files that weren't backed up already, and did a full clean install of Pop!_OS, and the improvement was noticeable from the moment the machine booted back up after install.  First, boot-up was fast, and there were no issues logging into the device, connecting to the home network was smooth, fast, simple, there were no pop up ads, or notifications trying to get me to install this or that, or a million stupid updates or other background processes slowing me down.  So just to see how well it was going work after, I installed steam, and installed houseflipper and inscryption, both games ran smooth, and clean, absolutely zero lag.  So i decided to really see what i could do, i installed a bit more graphics heavy games, No Mans Sky, Borderlands 3, and Palworld, and i was shocked, all three ran wonderfully, i wasn't able to play these games with Windows installed as the OS, there was no way, those games were absolutely unplayable under Windows.  But with Pop! Linux and steam installed, this little machine turned into a beast!!! I don't know why I waited so long to remove windows from this little machine, but that's probably my only gripe about this machine, is it comes with probably the worst possible operating system installed. There are plenty of other Linux distros out there that would probably work well without issue on this device, Like I said I'v used manjaro before, and still do on an old Acer desktop i got back in 2019, but just wanted to test out Pop!_OS this time and was very surprised! So overall this is a great machine, but I would suggest removing Windows OS if you actually plan to use this machine for anything.

What are the main applications for the Dual Gigabit LAN ports? 
The dual RJ45 Gigabit LAN ports offer extreme network versatility. Beyond standard internet connections, it is ideal for building a soft router, hardware firewall, home server, or setting up isolated network environments for home/office security. 
Does it support multi-monitor setups and 4K display output? 
Yes! The C4 SE features triple display outputs: HDMI 2.0 (4K@60Hz), DisplayPort (4K@60Hz), and a Type-C port (1080p@60Hz). You can connect up to three independent screens simultaneously to enhance your work productivity and multitasking efficiency. 
Can I upgrade the memory and storage on the C4 SE Mini PC? 
Absolutely. It comes with dual SODIMM DDR4 slots, supporting memory expansion up to 32GB (DDR4 2400MT/s). For storage, it features a primary M.2 2280 NVMe PCIe 3.0 x4 slot and an extra M.2 2280 NVMe PCIe 3.0 x1 slot for easy storage expansion. 
Does this Mini PC support 24/7 continuous operation for home servers or soft routers? 
Yes. Equipped with an efficient cooling fan and low-power AMD processor, the C4 SE is engineered for low power consumption and high stability, making it reliable for 24/7 continuous operation.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: A great budget mini pcA great budget mini pc
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The Bottom Line:If you are looking for a budget Mini PC in 2026, you’ve probably seen a dozen "N100" or "N95" Intel boxes. Do yourself a favor and get this Ryzen 5 3550H unit instead. For about as much as an N100 device, you’re getting a real 4-core/8-thread processor that actually handles multitasking without breaking a sweat.Performance & Daily Use:Most budget minis stutter when you have 10+ Chrome tabs and a 4K YouTube video running. Not the C4. The Ryzen 5 3550H might be a few years old, but its multi-core performance still packs a punch.Windows 11 Pro: Comes pre-installed and activated. It’s snappy out of the box.RAM/Storage: 16GB of DDR4 is almost required nowadays. This device is dual-channel capable, but only comes with a single stick of RAM. If you can spare to, get another stick of RAM so you can take advantage of the dual-channel capability.Triple Display Support: Comes with HDMI, DisplayPort, and USB-C, providing flexible options for connecting to your monitors, as well as triple display support.Dual Gigabit LAN: Rare at this price point. Great if you want to use this as a dedicated home server or a hardware firewall.USB-C: It's a full-featured port on the front, which makes cable management for modern peripherals much easier.Linux Potential (The Secret Weapon):If you’re a Linux user, this is a dream. I wiped the Windows drive and installed Ubuntu 25.10. Every driver, such as Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, was recognized instantly. Under Linux, idle RAM usage dropped from 3.2GB to 1.4GB.What could be better?Build Quality: It’s all plastic. It’s a nice matte finish, but it’s very light. Use the included VESA mount to bolt it to the back of your monitor so it doesn't slide around your desk.WiFi 5: In 2026, WiFi 6 is the standard. It’s plenty fast for 4K streaming, but if you have a high-end router, you’ll be capped by the older internal card.The Thermals: While idling in Windows, it didn't take long for the CPU temperatures to reach 140 degrees Fahrenheit. When pushing the unit with 10+ browser tabs as well as a 4k Youtube video playing, temperatures reached 160. Under a heavier load or more strenuous tasks, this device could likely throttle, if not shutdown. Adding some heat sinks or internal fans would make a major difference.Pros:+ Genuine Ryzen 5 power for the price of a Celeron.+ 16GB RAM is a massive plus for 2026 multitasking.+ Triple display and Dual LAN support.+ Extremely easy to open and upgrade.Cons:- Older WiFi 5 standard.- Plastic chassis feels a bit "budget."- Poor temperature controlFinal Verdict: For a home office, a student, or a dedicated Linux lab, the Origimagic C4 is a great value-for-money I’ve found this year. It turns "budget computing" into a "pro experience."Edit: After a bit of fiddling around with it, I ended up taking the board out of the casing and removed the cpu fan. What I found was a little bit of old thermal paste. I wiped the old stuff off and applied a bit of new thermal paste, put it all back together, and now I'm noticing much better temperatures. Fixing this small issue raises my rating of the device to 5 star.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: My wife made me get rid of my two huge 400 DVD Carousels & I still wanted to watch the DVDs, so I used MakeMKV to rip them to my Synology NAS & I got this to make a Video Server using ZenPoint DigitalCenter to play them on our 4k TV.  I did a couple of upgrades, two Crucial 16GB SODIMM modules and a Samsung 2TB M.2 PCIe NVME GEN 3 SSD.  OrigiMagic was nice & put a 16GB SODIMM module in, so I could have saved a few bucks just adding a second module, but I couldn't find the same brand they used & I like to have matching pairs, so I bought a matching pair.  I had a 2TB GEN 4 stick and GEN 4 is supposed to work in GEN 3 slots, but it seemed to work & then crashed uglily.  So I got the GEN 3 stick & it's working flawlessly.  It was getting really hot tho & that has two problems 1) thermal throttling & 2) really short SSD life, so I got a heatsink.  Still hot & throttling.  So I tried a mess of heatsinks.  ASIN B07KDDKDNN, wrong fin orientation, hot; B0D2677M5K, angled fins, better but still hot; B0DKBMVMS1 Graphite/copper top & B0DKBNFVX9 Graphite/copper bottom, better but still hot; & finally B0DKBLNM5K copper top & ‎B0BV2GCP3W copper bottom, best but still hot. There is no airflow thru the bottom of this thing & no heatsink is going to solve that. I found a really tiny really quiet fan, ASIN B0B1V3NZJD, that plugs into a USB port for power. Throttling happens about 75C & with the fan, the SSD runs in the low 40C range; problem solved! I was looking for low power, so I removed the WiFi module, and that got the power down to 22 Watts. The performance is definitely not in the supercomputer range, but it plays movies with no hiccups & that's all I want!Amazon sells a huge variety of these mini pc's & I'd have returned this one in a heartbeat & got one with a fan that cools the SSD, but I wasn't able to find one with a bottom fan.  Lotta hours wasted searching...If you are willing to attach a bottom fan, highly recommended.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: It came in a simple white box with a thin pamphlet. The case is plastic but feels sturdy. It's a bit larger than portrayed in the photos. Win11 was pre-installed but I installed Ubuntu 25.10 linux.  The OS install from a thumbdrive went without a hitch, including shrinking the Windows partition to allow room for Ubuntu. It took about 15 minutes overall.  Once linux was installed, I paired it with our bluetooth mouse and keyboard. It found our 2.4 wireless network with no problem.  It has a fan but is almost totally silent. At first I let it hang off the back of the tv on a USB cord, then realized it was hovering over the tv's cooling vent and drawing in warm air. But it didn't get hot, and the fans were quiet.  It now resides on the back of our new lg SmartTv using a large piece of Velcro stickum. Honestly, it's the perfect little min-pc for internet surfing and media streaming.  Bootup is very fast. It appears to stream movies no problem. I haven't tried games or any benchmarks, but it should run older, non-graphically intensive games. The Ryzen 5 3550H is generally rated at about 50% faster than the Intel N150.

Loads of USB ports and supports up to 4 displays. Great mini pc! 2 yr warranty a plus. Great price during the holiday sales.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: My desk doesn't look like a hot messMy desk doesn't look like a hot mess
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I used to keep a standard desktop tower under my desk. It wasn’t huge, but the tangle of power cables, ethernet cord, and monitor wires driving me nuts every time I looked down. I wanted a cleaner setup, so I decided to swap it out for a mini PC just to streamline things. Setup was a breeze—plugged in the monitor, keyboard, and mouse, and it was ready to go. What I love is how compact it is. You can tuck it in a corner or mount it straight to the back of your monitor. I went with the back-mount option, which cleared the tower off my desk. Now I mostly use it for day-to-day stuff around the house: sorting family files, online banking, printing documents, and streaming educational videos for my kid. For internet, switching between Wi-Fi and ethernet is straightforward. The storage out of the box handles basic documents fine, and I like that I can easily upgrade it down the road if I start running low on space. Just keep your expectations in check: it’s a mini PC, not a high-performance workstation, so don't expect it to crunch heavy-duty tasks. But if you just want to declutter your workspace and need a reliable machine for daily chores, it fits the bill.

description: The Gate of Smooth Gaming: In competitive gaming, every frame matters. Introducing Acer's VG270K gaming monitor - the UHD resolution monitor that can keep up with your game play. Through AMD FreeSync technology, the game’s frame rate is determined by your graphics card, not the fixed refresh rate of the monitor, giving you a serious competitive edge. Plus, users can enjoy a comfortable viewing experience while gaming via flicker-less, low dimming and ComfyView display. The design saves space on your desk and lets you place multiple monitors side by side to build a seamless big-screen display. (UM.HV0AA.106)
features: Quality Visuals: The VG270K 27" IPS monitor with 3840 x 2160 UHD resolution in a 16:9 aspect ratio presents stunning, high-quality images with excellent detail. The zero-frame design does away with the thick frames found on conventional monitors freeing up precious screen space.

AMD FreeSync Technology: Say “goodbye” to stuttering and tearing. With AMD FreeSync, the monitor’s frames are synced with the graphics card’s frames, which eliminates screen tearing and provides the smoothest gaming experience.

Quick Refresh Rate: Different content has different refresh rate and resolution requirements. If you are playing an FPS or racing game, you will need a monitor with a high refresh rate. However, if you are doing office work or streaming videos, a higher resolution will be more beneficial. With DFR technology, users can choose a higher resolution, or a higher refresh rate based on what is suitable for them.

Responsive: Up to 0.5ms GTG (Gray to Gray) response time enhanced gamers’ in-game experience. No matter if the fast-moving action or any dramatic transitions will be rendered smoothly without the annoying effects of smearing or ghosting

ZeroFrame Design: With a Nitro VG270K monitor, you’ll want to see as much of the display as possible. Get more real estate with the near bezel-less design, allowing you to see more and do more. The ZeroFrame design lets you place multiple monitors next to each other for a seamless, almost uninterrupted view.

HDR Enabled: Change how you see your games with Acer HDR 10 support for up to a wide DCI-P3 95% color gamut. HDR will improve overall quality and contrast to taking your gameplay to the next level with improved color accuracy.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: After about a week of using this monitor, I think it's fair to say that this monitor is very "meh." Nothing about it is particularly bad, but nothing about it is really that good, either.As this monitor claims, it does indeed have DCI-P3 color space support. However, when it's on, you can't change any brightness, contrast, or any color settings; if you try, the monitor automatically defaults back to "Standard" color mode (sRGB). By default, this monitor is quite dim, so this limitation is definitely an issue. You'll either have to put up with the monitor being dim, or settle with Standard color mode where the colors are noticeably quite flat and desaturated. Even after messing with the color settings, it seems like this monitor just isn't great at representing colors that well.This monitor also supports HDR, and in my testing with it, it's not bad, but it's not great either. Again, the issue of this monitor's brightness strikes. Colors definitely do seem a bit better--they're not as desaturated, and they feel like they pop a little bit more--but even after calibration, the brightness just wasn't really there. It's certainly not terrible, and I found it looked decent, but it's nothing to write home about.The fact that this monitor supports 4K and has DFR are two pretty neat points about it, I'll give it that. Especially considering that the monitor is 27", a 4K resolution means that this monitor features a very high pixel density. I've personally always prioritized that over screen size, and this monitor is certainly excellent in that regard. DFR is also a welcome feature; it does lower your resolution to 1080p--and at 27", individual pixels become much more noticeable at that resolution--but the monitor becomes capable of 144hz instead of a maximum 72hz at 4K. I'd say it's a decent trade-off, even if you are sacrificing a not-insignificant amount of quality in exchange for a higher refresh rate.Moving on to the stand that the monitor comes with, it's arguably the worst part. It is not height adjustable, which is certainly a huge flaw, especially when considering that the stand is quite short; the monitor sits only 6 inches or so above your desk, so if you have more than one monitor, it's likely this one will be the shortest one out of all of them with this stand. Also, it just doesn't hold your monitor very still. One bump into your desk, or really any vibrations or tremors, will cause it to wobble around.Overall, while this monitor is indeed very competitively priced, if you're in the market for a 4K monitor, I'd highly recommend passing on this one. As they say, you get what you pay for, and as another reviewer here stated, there's indeed a reason why this monitor is priced the way it is. It tries to include all the features of a more expensive monitor, but considering how lackluster they all are, I don't think it's worth it. Save up your money for something better; you'll be glad you did, because you'll certainly be getting something better than this.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Perfect little Plex server — fast transcoding, barely sips power
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Picked this up as a dedicated Plex server and it's been fantastic. Intel Quick Sync handles 4K HDR transcoding effortlessly, including tone-mapping down to 1080p, and it does it drawing a tiny fraction of the power a dedicated graphics card needs for the same work. Setup was painless, it runs cool and quiet, and the 5GbE port and dual M.2 slots give it room to grow. It's been rock solid running 24/7. If you want a small, efficient, always-on media server, this is an easy recommendation.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: The Little Lunchbox That CouldThe Little Lunchbox That Could
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: My gaming laptop ran into some fan troubles that made it unusable during my return to my parents house. At first I thought about buying a casting device for my phone, but then this neat little PC came up for recommendations. After a day or so of research on these types of pcs (and the decent price), I decided to give it a shot.Now let me be clear: I knew from the get-co that this was in no way a “native” gaming, PC nor do I recommend it being used as one (locally anyway). But I did test The Sims 2 Legacy and other retro games, something like that is okay. That all being said, using this lunchbox as a “Cloud-gaming” gaming PC is absolutely perfect in my experience! For AAA games (most games in general really) this is the way to go for this device.Wi-Fi connection is pretty darn good for me so I can’t complain. I’ve tested Xbox CloudGaming, GeForce Now and PlaystationPlus so far. Xbox and GeForce run really solid, while PlayStation is a hit or miss. There’s also another cloud provider called ShadowPC but I didn’t get to try it (may update this when I do).Speed wise, shockingly good for its size. I have it connected with my 34” 175hz monitor and am able to run 99hz. Not bad from what I expected.Style wise, I can’t lie…it’s so gosh darn adorable and matches my old pink desk setup. I remember my mom seeing it for the first time and saying “That little thing is a Computer?!” Haha. Its size and low power/fan makes it feel as if there’s no electronic device near the desk. Usually loud fans from consoles or gaming pcs are something my parents are used to, so this little lunchbox really threw a curveball at their expectations when I said I was ordering a new PC. I’m probably going to leave it with my parents as it’s a great media PC and a handy one for Cloud gaming in case I want to leave my gaming laptop at home.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on August 9, 2025Reviewed in the United States on August 9, 2025

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This is a pretty amazing little computer! Although it's tiny and therefore very portable, you obviously need a monitor and keyboard/mouse to go with it. We thought we'd try this as a replacement for the little Lenovo laptop that we've had anchored to a desk for most of it's life anyway, as that laptop isn't upgradable to Win11. This one comes with Win11 Pro, so it should be good for the foreseeable future. It is surprisingly much faster than our little laptop, and has been flawless so far.Getting it up and running was easy, and for routine web browsing and light duty work it barely gets even warm. It easily handles Office Pro applications, and I've even successfully run an architectural CAD program on it. It takes a few seconds or so to render and while I prefer running this software on a computer with a little more horsepower, it's certainly doable. It has also easily handled some photographic image editing. I have not tried video editing or gaming, and my guess is it'll struggle more with these, but assuming you have reasonable expectations it's definitely worth the price paid.Hopefully it holds up as long as the several older laptops I have that are about to be retired with Win10. Two of those started life with Win7 and have been going for years. Time will tell.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: A solid small footprint device for running Windows 11 Pro
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I've had good luck with this brand and purchased a similar model earlier (N150). I've also recommended GMKtec to a couple of co-workers. I work in the IT Management Consulting field. My main machine is a Mac, but I often have a need to use some business software that does not run on the Mac (Visio). When Windows 10 fell out of support, I didn't need a high-end Windows machine for my everyday work, so I opted to replace my unsupported Windows 10 machine (which is now running Linux) with the other GMKtec model. I run that GMKtec device headless, and RDP into it from my Mac. This means I do not turn it off. My plans for this device are to install Linux on it.If you are looking for a solid, economical Windows 11 PC (the small footprint is a bonus as well) without spending a fortune, this is the device.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: First, I am not a gamer so... I was pleasantly surprised at how this little PC worked. It was very easy to get started with. Comes with Windows 11. It's great for basic tasks like surfing the net, email, watching videos, etc. The actual speed it shows is right around 1800 MHz base.  The graphics seem to be fine for both windows and Linux using an inexpensive HDMI TV as monitor. WiFi connection was simple. Boot was quick for both windows and Linux. There's not any fans so there's no noise. At 512 GB there's plenty of storage for OS and an external USB drive would be an easy addition if more storage was needed.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: The Little Engine That Could (and Then Some)
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: When you buy a mini PC equipped with an AMD Ryzen 9 7940HS, you expect a solid office machine. What you actually get is a surprisingly potent "everything" box that punches way above its weight class. After putting this unit through its paces—including a fresh OS install and some gaming stress tests—here is the breakdown of why this "lil guy" has become a daily driver.The Performance: Raw Power in a Small PackageThe heart of this machine is the 7940HS APU, and it is an absolute beast for this form factor.* Daily Tasks: Effortless. Whether it’s heavy multitasking, dozens of browser tabs, or 4K streaming, it doesn't flinch.* Gaming (The Real Surprise): While it won't replace a dedicated high-end rig for AAA titles at Ultra settings, the integrated Radeon graphics are remarkably capable.* MMOs: Ran Star Trek Online and Star Wars: The Old Republic without a hitch.* Optimization: You’ll need to tweak your settings, but the "raw power" of the APU allows games to still look great while maintaining smooth frame rates.* Connectivity: The Wi-Fi is rock solid, which is crucial for a device often used as a secondary streaming or media node.The Setup & Troubleshooting (A Nerd’s Note)If you’re planning on doing a fresh install of Windows 11, be prepared for a little bit of legwork. I encountered some initial slowdowns and driver headaches.> Pro Tip: If you run into AMD driver installation errors (like I did), ensure you have the Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable packages installed. This was the "magic fix" that cleared up my driver conflicts.>Another major culprit for initial sluggishness was Core Isolation (Memory Integrity) in Windows 11. Disabling this feature significantly improved the responsiveness of the system.The Noise & Thermals: A Tale of Two OSsThe hardware behaves very differently depending on what software is steering the ship:* Windows 11: The fan tends to run loud and stays at a high RPM almost constantly. It’s noticeable, especially in a quiet room.* Linux: Interestingly, the machine runs much quieter on Linux. If you're looking for a silent home server or a dedicated terminal, Linux seems to handle the thermal curves much more gracefully.The VerdictThis mini PC was originally meant to be a "secondary" device for streaming, but it’s so fast and capable that I find myself using it every single day.The Good:* Incredible CPU performance for the size.* Legitimate gaming capability for MMOs and lighter titles.* Compact and aesthetically pleasing.The Bad:* Fan noise can be aggressive on Windows.* Requires some technical "tinkering" (Drivers/Core Isolation) to reach peak performance.Final Thought: If you aren't afraid to dive into the settings and handle a few driver hiccups, this 7940HS unit is a powerhouse. It’s a perfect bridge between a basic NUC and a full-sized gaming desktop. I'm looking forward to seeing just how many tasks I can throw at it before it breaks a sweat.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: Kleine Krawallschachtel ! Sehr gute Ausstattung zum günstigen Preis, ABER sehr LAUT!Kleine Krawallschachtel ! Sehr gute Ausstattung zum günstigen Preis, ABER sehr LAUT!
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: Verpackung gut, PC schnell und gut, PC  laut Norton Antivirus virenfrei, ABER das Teil macht im Ruhezustand 35 dB mit einem fiependen Geräusch, der Lüfter ist im Dauerbetrieb, er schaltet sich NIE aus. Unter Last erreicht man am Gerät locker 43 dB - 48 dB. Ich muss jetzt erst einmal schauen, ob er mir nicht doch zu laut ist, ggf. geht er leider zurück. Sehr schade, schöner Mini PC (Festplatte gem. DiskMark Lesen 3700MB/s Schreiben 3200 MB/s)  als kleiner Krawallmacher. Leider ist der Lüfter noch lauter geworden, der Verkäufer wollte mir auch nicht entgegenkommen, daher geht der Mini PC leider zurück ( schade man hat viel Arbeit bis alles installiert ist und die Lizenzen muss man auch wieder frei machen, wäre schön gewesen wenn der Verkäufer sich hier flexibel verhalten hätte) , ich werde mich jetzt für einen Blackview entscheiden, diese sollen laut verschiedenen Tests die Leisesten am Markt sein und sehr hochwertige Bauteile verbauen, ich lasse mich überraschen und werde berichten.UPDATE: Habe den Blackview MP 100 mit einem Ryzen 5 7430U erhalten und ich will ehrlich sein, der BOSEGAME hat eine bessere/schnellere Festplatte, ein besseres Wärmemanagementsystem ( max. Temperatur 70 Grad unter Last, der Blackview 85 Grad), Der MP 100 ist leider genauso laut , er hat aber nicht diesen Pfeifton welcher beim Bosegame gestört hat.Mein Fazit: der BOSEGAME ist ein hochwertiger MiniPC mit einer schnellen Festplatte einen gutem Benchmark Ergebnis und im Verhältnis zu anderen MiniPC mit gleicher Lautstärke. Wenn es Bosegame jetzt noch schafft, die Lüftersteuerung zu optimieren, wäre der MiniPC ein absoluter Hit.  Für den Preis von ca. 300 Euro kann man den PC bedenkenlos kaufen!!!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Pleased so far and Dual Boots nicely with Linux
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: UPDATE 2: Have since purchased a total of 4 of these units for family members and friends that I have set up.  And although the processor has changed from the original 5700u model, the 5800h processors have been just fine as well.  For most people, this is a very good unit.  Upon opening one of the units, the NVME 2280 SSD was made by Crucial which was assuring. I can't speak to the others as I suspect the components are commodity based.  Three of the units have been set up as dual boots with Windows 11 and Linux Mint.  The last model stuck with Windows 11 solely because the user had a number of Adobe programs he needed (Adobe will one day regret not being cross-platform compatible).  I can't say enough about how good these units has performed.  Coupled with a Roku 43" 4k TV as the monitor, the result is outstanding.UPDATE: Bought a 2nd unit for a another family member. Equally pleased as with the first unit.  Both units are dual booted with Linux Mint 21.3 along side the OEM's Win 11 Pro.  Anyone doing that, I suggest making the USB boot drive from the ISO using Rufus instead of the Linux USB Image Writer (Rufus somehow seems to play better with the crappy Windows UEFI).  Also in the BIOS > Boot screen,  turn Off secured boot and switch the order of the bootloader under Advanced to Linux (gives you a choice at boot between Linux as the default or Windows). If you want to hide Linux, switch the bootloader order back to Windows first and it boots only in Windows.Been running for weeks and no issues thus far.  Also recently purchased a Beelink 7840HS for myself that has been great. The performance on the 7840HS is noticeably faster, but this 5700u model holds its own and is fine for most people that aren't gaming.
