productPageReviews.reviewTitle: This monitor didn’t just change my setup I now see in 4K, and possibly in the fourth dimension
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Let me preface this by saying I’ve never written a review longer than a haiku, but the ASUS 27” 4K Eye Care Monitor (VY27UQ) deserves a literal standing ovation—and since I sit for 14 hours a day, that’s saying something.I bought this because my previous monitor was about as vibrant as a DMV waiting room. When I upgraded to this majestic beast of pixels, it was like removing a film from my eyeballs that had been there since 2002. I loaded up a 4K wallpaper of a mountain range and I’m pretty sure a hawk flew out of the screen and nested on my ceiling. That’s how real it looks.Let’s break this beauty down:UHD 3840 x 2160: This isn’t just Ultra High Definition. This is Ultra Holy-Cow-I-Can-Count-The-Pores-On-This-YouTuber’s-Nose Definition.IPS Panel: The colors are so consistent from every angle that I now invite guests over just to sit beside me and whisper, “Look at the reds, Brad. Just LOOK at them.”HDR10: I watched a documentary about mushrooms and the spores basically levitated out of the screen. It’s like being part of a planetarium exhibit that cost $249 and came with free shipping.Adaptive Sync: My games no longer tear like emotionally unstable relationships. I play, it adapts. I cry a little. Not out of lag, but out of joy.Eye Care Plus / Blue Light Filter / Flicker Free: My eyes used to dry out faster than hotel shampoo. Now? They’re practically spa-treated. I stare at this monitor for hours and my retinas send me thank-you notes.Built-in speakers: Are they audiophile grade? No. But will they save your butt during a Zoom call when your headphones are tangled in a knot made by a spiteful ghost? Absolutely.DisplayWidget: I didn’t even know I needed this until I started using it. Now I adjust brightness and color like I’m piloting the bridge of the Starship Enterprise.3-Year Warranty: I’ve had shorter romantic relationships than this warranty. ASUS believes in this monitor more than I believe in finishing my laundry.Let’s be real: For $249, this is probably the best thing I’ve ever bought that didn’t require monthly payments, a therapist’s approval, or a permission slip from my significant other.I now gaze lovingly at this screen even when it's off. My productivity is up, my gaming has improved, and I’m pretty sure I look slightly cooler just sitting next to it. My cat has started sleeping in front of it like it’s a tiny sun.Final thoughts:If you need a monitor, this is it. If you don’t need a monitor, you’re wrong. Buy it. Mount it. Bask in it. And when someone comes over and says, “Wow, that’s a nice monitor,” you can lean back, nod slowly, and whisper:“It’s more than a monitor. It’s a lifestyle.”

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Arrived Broken and Completely Ruined the Experience
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I was really excited to try this ASUS 27” 4K Eye Care Monitor because the specifications looked excellent on paper. No matter how good the features are, none of that matters when the product cannot be used properly right out of the box. Receiving a damaged monitor is extremely frustrating, especially for an item like this where the screen condition is the most important part of the purchase.The packaging should protect the monitor better during shipping because displays are fragile and expensive. When someone orders a monitor, they expect to be able to set it up and start using it, not deal with damage, returns, replacement delays, and wasted time.I cannot fairly judge the display quality, speakers, eye care features, or performance because the product was already broken when I received it. Based on the specs, it may be a good monitor if it arrives in perfect condition, but my actual experience was very poor.Overall, this was a very disappointing purchase. I expected a premium 4K monitor, but instead received a broken product that I could not properly use. One star.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Can't imagine much better at this price point
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Been using the standard (no USB-C ports) monitor for a couple days now, and I'm super impressed.Let's get the negatives out the way up front: The standard, cheaper version has no USB connectivity. I wish the silver stand and white cables were black instead. I wish it had even a basic set of built-in stereo speakers. Response times and refresh rates are decidedly unimpressive, but if you're not a gamer, you really won't notice or care.For me, these aren't deal breakers for a display that otherwise gives you so much at such a good price point.OK, let's move on to the long list of positives: Super easy to assemble, comes with HDMI and display port cables, very easy to connect on the back vs. bottom. The raise/lower and tilt stand is fantastic for dialing in a great viewing angle. The matte screen handles overhead light and ambient light superbly - annoying glare and reflections are exceptionally well managed. Straight out the box, brightness and contrast are fairly high and good if you like things punchy; color temp is a tad warm to be easier on the eyes. It's super easily adjusted if you prefer a bit cooler and even more accurate and there are many other profiles you can try to match what works best for you - the nice joystick based control on the bottom front lip of the monitor is great and IMO preferable to the buttons you have to reach around back or bottom edges for on other displays. I've done a fair bit of photo editing (not as a pro colorist, just an experienced hobbyist) and the reach the monitor has into shadows and highlights is very good. Gamut coverage is superb at this price point. No dead pixels. What more could you ask for, really?Conclusion: If you're not a gamer, don't require built-in speakers or USB-C, and want to get a great display at a great price, put it in your cart and buy it now. You won't regret it.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Honestly, wasn’t expecting it to be this good. I figured when I started it up that it would be broken considering the horrible packing job that was done. Monitor was just floating in a box four times the size with no packing or anything. The tape was there for decoration essentially.  Anyways, it’s so thin and light I was really surprised it’s a really good monitor and for the price it’s great.  Better than some monitors I’ve gotten for three times the price.It has basic monitor setting capabilities via the side buttons. Can we talk about the fact it has dedicated buttons and not just that weird stick a lot of companies are switching to? Loved this. It has basic customizable settings for gaming, movies, etc so nothing crazy. Played various games with it and no tracking or anything and THAT was the biggest shocker. It’s a real ips and not a va. I know that shouldn’t be a surprise but you’d be shocked how often some sellers on Amazon do the switch up.One complaint is the fact the company shipped it with a display cable and not an hdmi. Everything is hdmi now. I dont have a port for anything other than an hdmi and if you use an adapter, there’ goes the whole quality standard and reason for using the display cable in the first place. So I had to go out to find an hdmi to even just test the screen which was more of a hassle than I wanted. The cable it came with is going in a drawer to be forgotten forever. Oh and it has built in speakers. They aren’t the best but considering, I was impressed with how big of a performer it is.My last note is the c type port in the monitor is so close to the edge that it’s very hard to find a cable that is thin enough to connect. Picture is included for reference. A lot of the cables I get are chinky c types for durability reasons and none of then were thin enough to connect. I use a docking system for my computing needs which happens to directly use the usb c specifically. So overall, it’s a great monitor. Like really good overall capabilities.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on May 29, 2026Reviewed in the United States on May 29, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Nice monitor, but don’t use HDR if your using a modern AMD graphics card rx 9060 xt or better. Turning on HDR turns everything into a washout nightmare. Windows and HDR Games included. You can use the monitors OSD to turn HDR on but of corse you still have to turn on HDR in windows and thats when everything goes south. I have since read that this brand of monitor is notorious for this problem. I wish I would have searched the reviews els-ware. I don’t believe I would have bought it had I known. So I can only recommend this if you don’t really care about using the HDR feature. Wow what a disappointment. Now I’m adding more to this review after finding out Sceptre saying hdr compatible is not true hdr. A monitor must be capable of achieving at least 400nit and this monitor will only reach 330nit. so not even compatible with HDR. No wonder I’m having so trouble getting HDR to work with windows. I’ll never buy another Sceptre product. it’s just a selling gimmick to get you to buy then and rip you off.

description: Samsung's Odyssey G55C QHD Gaming Monitor provides 1.7x the pixel density of Full HD with incredibly detailed images, making gaming more lifelike than ever before. Featuring 165Hz refresh rate and 1ms response time (MPRT) for ultra-smooth action and frames with minimal blur. The 1000R display fills your peripheral vision and draws you into the game. AMD FreeSync™ keeps the monitor and the graphics card refresh rate in sync, and reduces image tearing for seamless, smooth scenes. Experience awe-inspiring graphics with HDR10, providing near limitless shades, for deep dark blacks and luminous whites. Eye Saver Mode minimizes blue light and reduces eye strain, enabling extended periods of game play.¹"1ms" means one millisecond which is the range of avg. response time between 1.00ms to 1.99ms truncated to whole number. Based on MPRT measured under internal test conditions. Results may vary by content and monitor settings (requires ‘Extreme mode' setting). MPRT(Moving Picture Response Time) measures the time taken for a pixel to transition from one image frame to another (motion blur measurement).
features: BOOST YOUR REALITY: Your gaming world, more lifelike than ever. With 1.7x the pixel density of Full HD, QHD resolution offers razor-sharp, highly detailed visuals. Experience a wider view with more space to immerse yourself in every moment of action

EXHILARATE YOUR SENSES: Experience the next level of heart-pounding gaming; Vivid scenes wrap even more tightly around you with the 1000R curved display, filling your peripheral vision and drawing you right into the character's shoes

STAY IN SYNC WITH ALL THE ACTION: AMD Radeon FreeSync keeps your monitor and graphics card refresh rate in sync to reduce image tearing, providing a superfluid entertainment experience. Watch movies and play games without interruptions

FIND HIDDEN DETAILS OTHERS MISS: Awe-inspiring graphics with HDR10; A kaleidoscope of shades brings game scenes to life with incredible vibrancy; Uncover secrets hiding in the shadows with deep dark blacks, luminous whites & detailed resolution

FRESH EYES WIN MORE: Eye Saver Mode minimizes blue light to help keep your eyes relaxed and comfortable when gaming for extended periods; The Odyssey G5 also reduces irritating and tiring screen flicker, so you can focus longer

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Earns its reputation for working great with Linux. Solid laptop.Earns its reputation for working great with Linux. Solid laptop.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Mint Linux 23.3 with kernel 7.0.0-28-generic installed effortlessly with all keyboard features including function keys working as they should. Even the calculator pop-up key works out of the box, as does a screenshot app using Fn+PrtSc. No problems with detection of any of the hardware components. I get download speeds very close to the 500 Mbps speed delivered by my ISP.This is my first ThinkPad. I've been an HP laptop user for decades but for whatever reason decided to try a Lenovo this time around, largely because of Lenovo's commitment to supporting my favorite operating system. There are some minor differences in keyboard layout, and I'm having to adjust to those. No fault of the laptop itself. The keys feel great, particularly their crisp, fast responsiveness. What I did find is that the touchpad, compared to those of my HP EliteBooks, is EXTREMELY prone to unintended palm contact and "cursor jump." There are clunky ways of addressing this using various command-line and graphical tools, but in the end, I created a keyboard shortcut (superkey+t) to toggle the touchpad on and off. This works very nicely in my case because I work 95% of the time using a wireless mouse. If my typing posture were better, maybe that wouldn't be an issue.The pointer, by the way, works as it should. I don't and never have used the pointer on any laptop, but for those who do, it works fine. I disabled mine in BIOS.I purchased the AMD version of this model and I'm surprised at how little heat is generated. Probably because I'm not a gamer or video editor, I never hear a fan switch on. Battery life seems very good. The display is nothing to rave about, but it's perfectly fine and streaming video is more than adequate. Again, all the display controls in Mint Linux work as they should.Included with my laptop was a nice little USB-C "dock" dongle that supplies a gigabit ethernet port, HDMI port, USB 3.0 ports, SD/TF slots, and a mini headphone jack. It works great.The E16 is attractive, sturdy-feeling, and seems made for Linux.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Samsung Galaxy Chromebook Go — Affordable, Lightweight, and Built for Basic Computing
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The Galaxy Chromebook Go is exactly what it appears to be: an affordable Chromebook designed for web-based work, education, and everyday tasks. It is not a performance machine, but for the right user it delivers a reliable and straightforward experience.The biggest strengths are portability and simplicity. The laptop is lightweight, easy to carry, and boots quickly. ChromeOS remains one of the easiest operating systems to maintain, making this a good choice for students, casual users, or anyone who primarily works in a browser.Battery life is another positive. In normal use, it easily gets through a day of web browsing, email, document editing, and video streaming without constantly searching for a charger.The 14-inch display provides a comfortable amount of screen space for schoolwork and everyday tasks. While the resolution and color quality won't compete with premium laptops, it is perfectly adequate for browsing, Google Docs, YouTube, and video calls.The integration with Android phones is convenient, particularly for users already invested in the Google ecosystem. File transfers, notifications, and cloud synchronization work smoothly.Performance is where expectations need to be realistic. The Intel Celeron processor and 4GB of RAM handle basic tasks well enough, but heavy multitasking can slow things down. Running numerous browser tabs, streaming video, and using multiple applications simultaneously will push the system to its limits.Storage is limited at 64GB, although ChromeOS relies heavily on cloud services, which helps offset the smaller local storage capacity. For users who primarily work online, this is less of a concern than it would be on a traditional Windows laptop.The build quality is respectable for the price point. It feels durable enough for student use, travel, and everyday carrying. The lightweight design makes it easy to toss into a backpack without much thought.Overall, the Galaxy Chromebook Go is a practical budget laptop that performs well within its intended role. If you need a device for web browsing, email, schoolwork, streaming, and cloud-based productivity, it offers good value. Just don't expect the speed, multitasking ability, or storage capacity of a higher-end laptop.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Incredible product. Much more solidly built than I had expected.I purchased this because my 2017 MacBook Pro I-7 would warm up considerably during heavy work (I am a data scientist and push the machine to crunch very large sets before I move a project over to AWS for its computing power). This product was more than I expected. It is light weight, strong, and folds conveniently into a size that fits in an outer pocket of my backpack, thus I carry it with me wherever I go. Even when I am not crunching numbers, I place my Mac on it. The typing angle is perfect for long coding sessions and makes my hands feel much better.The item does adjust for the size of the laptop. My MacBook Pro is a 15 inch, but my ASUS laptop is a 17 inch. With a quick turn of the pressure dial on two of the legs, the X-stand adjusts between my Mac and ASUS so that each has a SOLID platform to rest on. And the room below the machines is ample to provide good airflow to keep the machines cooler.I wholeheartedly and enthusiastically recommend the X-Stand, especially if your "office" is more often on your back and your workstation is any desk surface you can find like mine tends to be. It conveniently folds into a small size and provides an adjustable, solid platform to air your laptop. I may purchase additional ones so for when (as too often happens) this great product is discontinued - should it every be - or for holiday gifts for my other geek friends.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Durable aluminum construction. Adjustable for multiple laptop sizes. No big bulky cheap plastic cooling pad to lug around, which effectively defeats the purpose of the portability of the device I need it for. This stand folds up into a very compact form factor that fits perfectly into one of the pockets in my laptop bag, no fuss, no problem. No useless fans that generally never improve temperatures in any meaningful way that the fans in the laptop don't already accomplish themselves if they have ample room to breathe, not to mention promoting more dust and dirt getting pushed into the laptop vents, all at the expense of more fan noise and using up one of the already scarce USB ports on the laptop to power them, therefore no mechanical moving parts that will inevitably break or die.This is getting use with a 17.3" MSI Stealth GS76 laptop sporting a Core i7 11800H and a 16 GB RTX 3080 - This laptop gets mighty hot during gaming sessions, and sometimes even during general tasks when sitting flat on a surface. I already have to max the fans to 100% during gaming sessions so as it is. I'm always trying to prop something under the rear outer edge of the laptop to elevate it a little for better airflow, what a pain. This little stand has solved all my problems and really helps a lot to allow the fans in the laptop to work more effectively, pulling much more airflow through the vents underneath, as well as more room for hot air to exhaust away from it, and has such a small footprint where it makes contact with the underside so as not to block airflow into the vents. I get incredibly better cooling results with this stand.My only complaint related to this stand is directed at myself because I didn't get one sooner. It's exactly what I've had in mind and have been looking for.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: PERFECT Stand/Easel for iPad Pro Artists and Creatives!PERFECT Stand/Easel for iPad Pro Artists and Creatives!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: So since the iPad Pro release I've been on a mission to find a good stand to simple prop the iPad up a bit for sketching.  I'm a product designer by trade so I'm not doing insanely intricate work (mostly concept sketching) and after years of sketching a Cintiq, I'm used to sketching at somewhat of an angle.  I originally purchased a stand that was marketed as an iPad Pro/Macbook Air Stand from a much more expensive (almost triple the cost) and well-known brand, but it fell short in more ways than one.  THIS, however, is perfect for iPad Pro sketching.  It works so well that in fact, I'm going to also write the seller to make sure they add it to the description.The problem with the "other" stand(s) is they simply aren't portable.  Why would you want to buy a huge clunky stand (yes it might be pretty and textured aluminum and Apple make it more appealing by offering it in their online store) and not be able to just throw it in your bag?  The Steklo X-Stand features very well thought out design and construction along with the portability you want for the products it supports.  I do have one small gripe however, and that is the "feet" at the bottom that stabilize the laptop (by your wrists if you were typing) are a bit long.  They stick out above the edge of the iPad Pro but for MacBook Pro customers this probably wouldn't be a huge deal depending on what model/how you type.  For me personally I will probably Dremel them down a hair shorter so they're flush with the screen (I'm on the fence though as they do offer a good place to rest the Pencil) and still do their job of holding the unit in place.  In all reality the feet haven't really bothered me yet on a physical level (I've only been using it for a few days) so I guess it's more of an OCD thing.  The feet and back supports are soft polymer that provide plenty of grip/stability and I don't see them scratching any type of metal, but I use a case regardless.If you're looking for a great way to prop up your iPad Pro for sketching/drawing/painting whatever, you've found it!  Don't go blowing all kinds of money on a more expensive stand when it's simply not necessary and lacks portability.  I've added some customer images for anyone who'd like to see it modeled with an iPad Pro.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: A lightning fast laptop! Very good deal!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Being a PC guy that knows his stuff, I am very pleased with this refurbished laptop. It works like new. They wiped the HD and fresh installed Windows 11. No bloatware! However, you will need to install an anti-virus program. I recommend Avast free. I have been using it for a good 15 years with zero malware or virus infections, and it is 100% free. SPEEDY! I am also an emulator master. This little laptop runs the most power hungry games in MAMEUI64 at FULL SPEED WITHOUT ANY FRAME SKIPPING! I was amazed. It really is an awesome laptop. I will likely buy another one of these  to keep in case. Works great with USB hubs and the HDMI is 1080p and looks great. A+A+A+
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on July 12, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I am very pleased with the condition and function of this lap top. The battery is nearly full strength and there is no visible damage or indication of wear. They put a skin on the outside, I assume to cover any marks or scratches, but this computer is in such good shape, I doubt there could have been much. My only complaint is some bloat wear added for "PC app store" that commandeers the computer at first, literally blocking you from doing almost anything else until you open an account, CC and all. I managed to finally get past it to settings where I could go in and delete that app. It is not the same as the Microsoft app store. Other than that, it is almost undistinguishable from a new laptop.UPDATE: I really liked this laptop, the size was perfect and it seemed to be working like new. A couple of months later, it just stopped working. I don't know what happened, one minute it was working fine, the next it was dead. Black screen. Nothing. I had assure, so I sent it in and they couldn't fix it. If I didn't have assure, I would have been out for the whole thing. I m so glad I back up everything on an external drive. I recommend you do that also, no matter what computer you have!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Dell Latitude - I was expecting better
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I actually purchased 2 of these laptops, both advertised to be in excellent condition, which they were. I love the touch screen, size and weight of this laptop, but not so enchanted with the battery life, which on full charge only lasts a max of 2 hours or so. Both laptops have the 43Wh battery which I upgraded to 63Wh thinking my battery life would significantly improve, but that did not happen. That's okay though because I am only on about an hour a day anyway. However, why the 1 start rating is that both these laptops continually freeze up, which is terribly frustrating. And when they freeze, the only resolution is to power the off the laptop and re-boot. I don't like unreliable laptops and unfortunately I have found both of mine are exactly that. Sadly, for medical reasons, I did not start to use these laptops until after the return date expired, otherwise, they would have been returned. I have purchased other refurbished laptops from Amazon and they have all been excellent purchases. I guess I was due to run into a couple of lemons.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Couldn’t go wrong with this selection. Great quality metal construction great keyboard great touchpad fingerprint sensor works well. Impressed so far by the battery life as it can last for hours of casual use and also standby mode allows for the battery to last a long time as well. Performance is fantastic for the price range. I was looking at a previous generation i7 and thought it was a good performer but when comparing it to this generation’s i5 the i5 blows it out of the water. DDR5 RAM WiFi 6 it has it all. Love how it has thunderbolt 4 connectivity and HDMI 2.1 for future proof compatibility. Micro SD slot just in case you run out of space so there’s very little worry about storage for my needs. The slight downside is the weight as it is slightly hefty. I compared it to the 14” yoga with the same specs but chose this version because of the larger monitor size for just $3 more so it was a no brainer. The hefty quality of the laptop grows on you though since it just adds to the sturdy feel to the device. It’s not that it’s too thick it’s actually a very thin laptop but it just weighs around 6 pounds if I’m not mistaken. Overall I would highly recommend this laptop for the price it blows every other laptop in the price range out of the water.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Actually NO stars. I ordered this unit to take on some trips - I wanted a durable small lightweight laptop that I didn't need to worry about. Within a few minutes the screen came on - but it was flashing on and off and only half showing. That was the first problem. Then I tried to type - several of the keys were stuck and inoperable. Within 1 hour of receiving the unit, I started my return with Amazon. I boxed it up and took it to UPS with a few days. I asked for replacement unit because I thought that the next one would likely be better... NOT - see that other review too. It came damaged and unusable. I give up. Not sure what I will do now, but obviously these refurbished units (even with a good rating) are not worth buying at all.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The computer itself is great. Not a mark on it! The battery seems to last a long time and charges back up quickly. (2-4 hours) Wi-fi was a breeze and I love the slightly smaller size compared to larger and heavier laptops. You can’t go wrong buying this at this price! Now, all that being said - setup was NOT the piece of cake I was hoping for and it took me down rabbit holes I wish I had never gone down! The first question it asks you is do you want to start from scratch on this computer? Or do you want your laptop to be familiar like your others? We’ll just sync it up to the cloud and boom you’re done. I vacillated. I chose to go cloud. Yeah no. Spent the next 2 days trying to undo and opt out of iCloud. Should have been simple enough. It was not. The ultimate outcome was my HP got ruined in the process with a Critical Error - start menu won’t work. No files on my computer and Microsoft will not support windows 10 anymore so I can’t get a fix. Tried internet fixes to no avail, so now that sits broken in my closet. Bottom line. This is a great computer. Buy it if you get the chance, but put some serious thought as to whether you want to sync it to the cloud or start fresh! I wish I had started fresh!

Bought a screen protector for it that makes the screen more anti-glare/helps prevent fingerprints, as I think this little machine is going to get a lot of use! Love how the keys and touch pad feel, hopefully I can take good care of it and make it last forever.With it being a 2-in-1, wasn’t sure if the hinges would be solid enough. However, as you can see in the video, it’s challenging to open it one-handed, so I think they’ll hold up well. Another thing I like about it is how quiet it is compared with my old gaming laptop.Not sure what the other reviewer meant about their pen that came with the computer not being branded ... mine says Lenovo right on the top (see picture).Don’t forget to update the drivers before you start using it – easy to do through Lenovo’s website. Also, one helpful thing to note is that due to the smaller 14” size, it doesn’t come with a 10-key pad. Not an issue for me, but maybe for some? To give an idea on size, the screen is slightly bigger than an 8.5x11 piece of paper.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This product is tops for running a very resource demanding real time stock trading program that was choking my 5 year old, top of the line laptop. I bought the 24 GB Ram version, 16K is just not enough. The FHD display in this unit is actually better than a 4k display for this type of use because text does not become too small, and I run the system with a big 36" monitor. Easy to set up. productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on December 13, 2025

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The laptop works as computer fairly well and is fast enough. Completely usable for most basic functions, web browsing, office apps, listening to music. Reasonably light weight, construction is OK where most of the case is plastics. Next up and deducted a star here. The screen is pretty low end just muddy or greyish looking from most any angle even after using the included AMD video software I was not able to get a very suitable picture, but I will use it anyway. Only one USB-C port and the laptop which arrived with a USB-C type charger which does work, but no small round tip charger where an input for this charger type is present on the laptop. Good thing this laptop also works with my DELL docking station and no drivers were required. Was able to access Lenovo support website and update two hardware drivers w/o any problem ( was hoping there might be a video update ). BIOS and another non-essential hardware item were the only items auto detected for updates.UPDATE: 2 months and Laptop has failed. No proper tech support from Lenovo. Opened a support case and per direct instructions from Lenovo I go to Lenovo website to download a recovery image file and it says no OS installed on that serial number, Lenovo cannot or will not enable access to acquire a recovery file even if the laptop is under warranty.Amazon tech support simply gave me Lenovo tech support number. I looks like the 'ol circle pull is on now. I would bypass Lenovo from now on. I left inquiry as to help with the reseller, will have to see if they want a tug too I guess.Kudos to Amazon as they did step in and allow me to return this unit for a 90% refund.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on September 7, 2025

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Selling functioning but defective laptops. Do not buy from this seller.Selling functioning but defective laptops. Do not buy from this seller.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I purchased this used laptop for light documentation work and basic web browsing. Based on the advertised CPU and 16 GB of RAM, I expected it to handle simple tasks without any issue.Unfortunately, after using it more recently, I found that the laptop is extremely slow and lags when opening apps or websites. This was surprising given the listed specifications. I initially trusted the seller and did not run performance tests right away because I did not need to use the laptop much immediately after purchase. By the time I noticed the issue, the return window had already passed.After running benchmark tests with the laptop set to high performance mode and all unnecessary programs closed, the results were very concerning:CPU performance: 0th percentile, with maximum clock speed around 2.6 GHzEffective RAM speed: 0th percentile, around 10 GB/sBattery life: less than 4 to 5 hours with light documentation workIn my opinion, this level of performance is not acceptable for a regular used laptop. While I am not saying the specifications were falsely advertised, the actual performance of this unit is far below what I would consider reasonable. It feels more like a defective or severely underperforming device than a normal used laptop.Had I discovered this earlier, I would have returned it immediately. Unfortunately, I only found out after the return period had expired.I would not recommend buying a used laptop from this seller unless you are able to thoroughly test the device immediately upon arrival.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This is a Chromebook and NOT a laptop. There is a big difference. I have a Lenovo Yoga laptop that I use for my business with Microsoft desktop apps, Adobe Photoshop and other editing software. I also have a 2TB drive to store work, media and games. It also has a Radeon graphics card for my games. It is touchscreen and folds in half to use like a tablet. I say all this to show what I am comparing this Lenovo Chromebook 2-in-1 to.The Lenovo Chromebook 2-in-1 has a smaller CPU, 4GB memory and 128GB storage on more of a memory chip, rather than an SSD drive. It also does not come with a 10-key pad to the right of the keyboard. The price is $1,000 less than what I paid for my Lenovo Yoga. So, you may be asking, why did I get this Chromebook, when I already have a much more powerful laptop. That is an excellent question.I am going on a cruise soon and I want a laptop that I can use, but won't be heartbroken if it gets lost, stolen, or broken. But, I also don't want a bad laptop that is going to frustrate me by poor performance. The Chromebook is actually better for this trip than a regular laptop, in my opinion.Comparing the Chromebook to my Yoga laptop. This Chromebook starts up and is ready in half the time of my laptop. That is important, when I just want to hop on the internet and get quick info on the next port or excursion. The touchscreen is just as responsive as my laptop. the keyboard keys are the same as my laptop in touch and feel. And surprisingly, Youtube videos and online app videos play very smooth and are the same quality as my laptop. All this without a separate video card.Just think of this as your cell phone with a much larger screen and an attached keyboard. It does not do any desktop apps or PC games, but like your cellphone, you can go to the Google Play store and download any app or game that you can normally play on your cell phone. Sort of like a big iPad. For me, this is the perfect travel device. My Yoga laptop, with all my work and passwords, stays securely at home and this Lenovo Chromebook goes with me as the perfect research and entertainment tool for my cruise, without any fear of losing it.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I genuinely love this machine. The Lenovo Yoga 9i 2-in-1 Aura Edition hits a sweet spot that very few Windows laptops manage: it’s versatile, well-built, lightweight, and actually enjoyable to use day to day.The display is excellent. Brightness is genuinely impressive and easily on par with my MacBook Pro M5 Liquid Retina. Colors are vibrant, contrast is strong, and it holds up well even in bright rooms. For drawing, note-taking, and PDF work, it’s a great panel.Build quality is solid without feeling heavy. It feels like a premium device but doesn’t punish you for carrying it around all day. The 2-in-1 hinge is sturdy and confidence-inspiring, and tablet mode is actually usable instead of being a gimmick.Performance is… fine. The processor is a bit underpowered if you’re expecting workstation-level speed, but that’s not really what this machine is for. For meetings, note-taking, PDF annotation, browsing, and general productivity, it’s perfectly adequate. If you’re trying to render video or compile large projects, look elsewhere.Out of the box Windows experience is the usual mess. Too much bloatware, McAfee junk that should not exist in 2026, and some general Windows jank. Stylus and touch interactions can occasionally feel slightly off, but again, this is Windows being Windows. Nothing is broken, just occasionally inelegant.Where this thing absolutely crushes everything else is Lenovo’s handwriting-to-text software. It’s absurdly good. I can handwrite notes during a meeting, casually and quickly, and walk out with a clean, typed document ready to share. It’s fast, accurate, and shockingly reliable. This alone makes the laptop worth owning if you live in meetings or do a lot of handwritten thinking.PDF annotation is also excellent. Doodling, marking up documents, signing, highlighting, exporting with annotations intact, all quick and painless. This is clearly what Lenovo optimized the Yoga line for, and it shows.The included stylus is solid and practical. About 18 hours of battery life, charges easily, feels good in hand, and doesn’t feel like an afterthought accessory.Bottom line:This is not a raw power machine. It is an outstanding productivity, note-taking, and creative thinking device. The combination of a great screen, good pen, genuinely useful handwriting recognition, and flexible 2-in-1 form factor makes it incredibly useful in real life. Despite the Windows annoyances, I really enjoy using it, and that’s saying something.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Practically impossible to add a 2.5" drive
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Overall great product and great value. However I wish they explicitly stated that you need additional parts to add a 2.5" drive. The laptop does have internal room for a 2.5" hard drive, however it's practically impossible to add it. Adding the drive requires a special cable, bracket and screws that are not included with the laptop. Finding them is nearly impossible as Lenovo seems to have discontinued them. The actual parts from Lenovo cost a ridiculous $200 dollars and can only be found on strange, third party sites. Amazon does carry a few 3rd party parts that should work, however some reviews say they don't and I still haven't been able to find the screws for the bracket.If you plan on upgrading the hard drive you're much better off buying a larger M.2 drive and replacing it (just make sure it's not SATA 3). Cloning and swapping the M.2 drive was easy, I'm just disappointed I wasn't able to add the 2.5" drive I already owned.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Computer great, refurbish quality missed a major issue.Computer great, refurbish quality missed a major issue.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This review is mostly about the refurbish service, the computer itself is absolutely fantastic.  My expectations for a refurbished computer was that I would get something that would show very modest wear, but work perfectly. I was delighted when I first opened my new Lenovo computer. The screen, keyboard, and touchpad appeared like it was brand new had never been touched. I was initially delighted with my purchase and started loading software and restoring my data. On the second day however, I noticed some unusual indentations around the power button. As I explored it further, I found that the computer had probably been dropped on its side. It actually bent the case enough to make the SD card slot unusable. It also makes the USB connectors quite tight (which may not actually be a bad thing in and of itself - but it's not right). The bottom of the case shows a physical crack and I am moderately concerned about whether there's some hairline fractures or other damage that isn't immediately obvious. The bottom line is, I've decided to keep the computer since it seems to be working fine and I really appreciate the pristine screen and keyboard that I received. I don't use the SD card slot so it's not a big deal to me for that. But I guess I'm just a little disappointed to have received a laptop that was clearly dropped hard enough to bend the case.  I know this happed before shipping as the box it was delivered in showed no signs of any drop.  It is a bit of a testament to the high-quality build that Lenovo puts into their computers but not a great example of careful oversight on the Amazon reconditioning service.  I think they should have been more descriptive about this kind of damage on this particular item (maybe offered it with a bit more discount?)

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: If you want to play a game, this will do it. No questions asked.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This laptop plays everything from Shooters to grand strategy without any issue at all. I play Helldivers and Europa Universalis when I come home from work and this functions better than my Xbox.Obviously the battery life is about non-existent when you're playing anything besides minesweeper, but that's normal. The fans are loud, but again that's normal.I haven't had issues with overheating and I play for hours at a time with multiple tabs open and active. When it does get hot it doesn't stay hot, and if I ever get concerned I can just shut the lid for a minute and come back.The display is large and clear, and the RGB keyboard isn't distracting like I expected. If anything, the lights help me press hotkeys in the dark.For a first gaming laptop I very much recommend. Maybe wait till it's on sale again. I got it at $300 off during prime day.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Best Mid Price Gaming PC Option in Summer 2025
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Pros:* Fast, cool, and quiet. After hours of gaming with Stalker 2, Cyberpunk 2077, and BG3, max temp hit by the CPU was only 79 degrees C, and that only for a very brief time. My old ASUS Tuf would be at least ten degrees hotter after such a test. Also of note, at the end of that test, the fans do not sound like Blackhawk helicopters under military power, an annoying characteristic that both my older Asus and older HP Omen had. Test was done "vanilla" with no external cooler fans, repasting, etc.* Nicely configured hardware. The 5060, Ryzen 7, and WD SSD drive all work well together.* WD SSE drive, very high quality, reads at 6300 mbps.* Second SSE slot is open.* Caser very easy to open, well organized.* Good build quality. The Acer feels very solid and can be opened with one hand. The unit has no "flex".*  Good gaming performance. Cyberpunk 2077 at 2K / high detail can hit 65 fps with ray tracing on and can reach well over 100 FPS with ray tracing off.* Reasonable price and good component value. Costs $100 more than similarly configured laptops selling with 4050 GPUs, 16 GB RAM, and 512 GB HDs, machines much worse in all ways.Neutral:* FHD screen, fast but dim. Typical of midrange laptops. I suggest using an external monitor anyway, but if you plan on playing all the time off the laptop, you may want a better screen option, which will likely cost a lot more.* Port selection is adequate. 3 3.2 USB As, 1 USB 4.0 C, 1 HDMI, SD card reader, headphone jack. Decent, but a Thunderbolt port and / or additional C port would be welcome.Cons:* Front of lid seems to be easily smudged and seems a fingerprint magnet.* Usual annoying bloatware that needs deletion, including world's worst AV software (McFluffy).* Need to set up / sign into MS to launch the operating system. Owners should have the option to bypass this annoying step.* Documentation is close to non-existent, both in terms of what's in the box and what's online.* 32GB RAM comes as two 16 GB chips, so upgrading to 64 GB means having to buy two new chips instead of one. Every PC maker seems to do this, which does not make it any less annoying. Give me one 32 GB chip, charge me $20 more.Note: Make sure to purchase directly from Amazon. Third party sellers often void mfgr warranties by adding components themselves and some will ship returned machines as new. Amazon is the only PC seller I'd buy from on their site.Bottom Line: Well balanced, well made, and reasonably priced for high value components.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: 3 months review, AI Architect and Engineer
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: After running this machine for three months as my daily driver — and I mean daily, 10–12 hours of cross‑platform AI workloads, model prototyping, GPU‑accelerated pipelines, and multi‑container dev environments — I can say the Nitro V 16S punches just above its price bracket. Acer doesn't have the best rap, but this device is surprisingly good.Concise takeaway:It’s a legitimately capable AI engineering laptop with 572 AI TOPS, a surprisingly efficient Ryzen 7 260, and an RTX 5060 that handles modern AI frameworks with ease. Once you remove the unnecessary OEM software, it becomes a fast, stable, high‑throughput workstation.*If you want more speed get rid of the Microsoft pre installed junk like teams, Xbox etc if you're not a gamer, and remove Killer E2600 it's garbage and notorious for bugs and network issues.For AI engineers, or devs the important part isn’t gaming FPS — it’s CUDA throughput, tensor performance, and VRAM efficiency.Handles PyTorch, TensorFlow, ONNX, NVIDIA NeMo, and RAPIDS without issueGreat for fine‑tuning 7B–13B models, LoRA training, and quantized inferenceThe 572 AI TOPS number isn’t marketing fluff — it translates into noticeably faster transformer inference compared to last‑gen midrange GPUs and there has been some bad ones out there. Just my opinionFor cross‑platform AI (Windows + WSL2 + Docker), the GPU stays consistent and doesn’t throttle under sustained load.CPU (Ryzen 7 260)This is where your observation matches mine:The CPU occasionally kicks in harder than expected, even during GPU‑bound tasks.My findings:The Ryzen 7 260 has aggressive boost behaviorWindows 11’s scheduler sometimes misassigns GPU tasks to CPU threadsAcer’s default power profiles are overly “performance‑happy”After tuning (and removing bloat), the behavior improves.Here is exactly what I removed **Microsoft bloatware preinstalled Microsoft junk (Teams preview, Xbox overlays, OEM telemetry, etc.) frees up RAM and stops background CPU spikes.2. Removing Killer E2600 softwareThis is a must.The Killer suite is notorious for:High DPC latencyRandom CPU usageNetwork prioritization bugsOnce removed, networking becomes stable and CPU behavior normalizes.3. Custom power tuningSetting a manual power plan (Ryzen Balanced + GPU Max Performance) gives the best AI workload consistency.One more thing I will mention is the display though it's not great it's easy on the eyes. Once you tune the CPU and get rid of the junk there is no more fan spikes due to the CPU spiking this removing the noise levels. This is a solid device and I do value my devices.One thing to keep in mind, this is a gaming device I am using for AI development and long coding sessions etc, it works great so no knocks on the gamers our there.real customer who paid for this device. productPageReviews.reviewTitle: You are paying extra for the NVIDIA card, but don't you dare use it
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Alright.  Okay.  Geeze.  This thing costs more than $1000, so I'd like it to meet some minimum quality bars, such as continuing to work six months later.  Or at all.Let's back this up a little: when I got it, it appeared to be great and fine.  Cool.  I spent several months using it happily without noticing any problems, but pretty soon I ran into an issue: whenever a "big" program would open (game, OBS, Adobe Premiere), the program itself would work but afterward the whole laptop would slow to a crawl and become very difficult to use.  Mainly it would stutter when switching between programs (such as between Edge and VS Code... or notepad...).But a restart would fix it!  I was restarting multiple times a day sometimes, pretty much any time I wanted to stop and then start a game again (on the gaming laptop...).  And I'm not talking crazy complicated games either, even indie stuff like Peak or Abyssus would do it.  If I exited out and then opened them up again, they would slow to a crawl.At some point I opened up the Nitrosense slopware and thought "what if I push up the quality bar?", which I did and then the whole thing became completely unusable all the time instead of just occasionally.  Nice.Probably you have figured out what's wrong now (maybe also if you read the title of my review), but if not, my final step on the journey was going into the graphics setting and essentially turning off the NVIDIA GPU.  Success!  After that one single a restart, I can now go multiple days with fine and normal functioning of the system....Except I can't use the video card I paid for.  There is now a class of programs that I can use once but then have to restart the computer afterward because they absolutely need a good video card, and if I dare to use this expensive card I paid for for the thing it's supposed to do, I will pay for it again with time and frustration.So, yeah... is that Acer's fault?  NVIDIA's?  AMD's?  I guess it's probably my fault for wanting to game on my gaming laptop.  Whichever it is, the unholy combination that ended up on my desk in the form of this laptop is actively emotionally painful to me since I spent so much on it and can't use it for the thing I wanted to use it for.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Excellent build quality and great for basic computer task.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Long battery life. Good form factor. I know I am in a shrinking minority, but modern the modern windows OS is spyware that harvests the entirety of your digital life and butchers it up for sale (default use of OneDrive - required activation).To avoid that, I installed Linux. The "AI" chips can take a nap until native support comes in later iterations, but the CPU is up to the task. It took a little BIOS tinkering, and after I arm wrestled the partitions away from Window's bit locker, I am left with a secure, fast, and wonderful laptop.Windows deserves -27 stars. But Acer, for the quality of the machine, deserves the full five. It is solid with a tight quiet chassis. The screen is pleasant enough and bright when needs be. The keys are crisp with a pleasant backlight. But the feature I adore most is the battery life. I have had many laptops, and they have all disappointed me in terms of battery life. Yet this has broken the streak of disappointments. Even with aggressive installations and tinkering, it has remained at a healthy percentage for longer than I would have guessed. A pleasant surprise, to be sure.Please know this is not a gaming laptop. I bought this for basic computering tasks and not for ray tracing and online dopamine hits in whatever game is in vogue with spotted teenagers. So if you want a computer for basic computer tasks (word processing, web surfing, multimedia whatnots), this is a solid choice. If you want a laptop for gaming, reconsider. But know this carries my discerning approval.Cheers!

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Had this for 6 months after using a macbook air for 4 years. Here are the biggest differences, understanding that a Macbook air is a much higher quality laptop and so some of this is expected. Perhaps if I had used a dell or hp for 4 years, the differences would not have been as noticeable.- Trackpad response time is slower compared to the macbook air, granted macbook's have one of the best. When I click on a browser tab, I have to wait a second before I move the mouse pointer away otherwise it drags the tab out of the browser window.  Very frustrating to train my fingers so slow down and having to drag the tab back into the browser window.- Camera is blurry for video meetings though the performance is perfectly fine.- Screen display is not very bright even when maxed out- Sound/speakers do not put out enough sound for a group around you to hear clearly- Issues with the lid sensor due to hall effect, preventing the laptop from turning on as it thinks the lid is still closed. Holding the power button for 30 seconds does a full power down that allows the lid sensor/magnet to release and then you can power on.- Start up time feels slow but again, I'm comparing to a macbookI would say this laptop is fine for general home use but if you are working continuously on it for extended periods of time, you'll experience small things that slow you down.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Gigabyte nowadays uses an AI-fueled control center with a closed ecosystem and unique connections. This AI will constantly 'optimize' your system resources, sabotaging any hope at reasonable gaming performance. This feature cannot be removed, and also cannot be fixed using any third-party software because of the unique connections being entirely unreachable to anything but the built-in control center, which they really want to force you to use at any cost. With the MUX switch off, performance tanks beyond low, causing constant graphics glitches, flickering, screen tearing, and an incredibly unpleasant experience in any game. With the MUX switch on, these glitches stop, but the performance is still somehow worse than a laptop I got in 2022 that uses a 4060, while also heating up so uncontrollably that my hands begin sweating no matter where I rest them on the keyboard. This isn't a gaming laptop. It is an unoptimized travesty that I was constantly fighting a losing battle with.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: This is a really nice upgrade for me!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This computer is a really nice upgrade from my old HP laptop. It runs so smooth! I'm not too tech savvy so I just use it for basic things like music and watching videos, which works well while running multiple apps and download large files. The screen is pretty nice looking. I saw some folks complaining about a yellow tint to the screen well you can turn the eye shield settings off and the color is back to normal. Took 10 seconds to figure out in the settings. It runs pretty quiet when the fan is on. It's a little big so I keep it sitting on a desk most of the time. It also says not to sit directly in your lap. I really have no complaints about it. Was very easy to set up and I even got my stuff backed up from my old laptop so my screensaver was even the same!  Opens and closes smoothly. The keyboard lights up which my old laptop didn't do, so I was happy to see that feature. I did add a little camera cover to it for like $6 here on Amazon. Other than that, it's really been great. I don't run any games on it so I can't speak for that performance but it's been perfect for my needs. Really glad I purchased this laptop.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: If you're hesitating about buying this Asus ROG Strix, don't doubt it—buy it. I’ve been using it for a month now, and it has been excellent since day one. Here is a review coming from my experience:Pros:Performance: The CPU and GPU are incredibly powerful; they handle everything with almost 0 problems.Audio Quality: The Dolby Atmos implementation is excellent, even without external speakers or headphones. It sounds crisp and immersive.Build & Cooling: As expected from the premium ROG line, the chassis quality is top-class, and the cooling system keeps thermals well-managed.Screen: For the $1,299 price point, it’s a great panel. It’s vibrant and clear, though I wish it were slightly brighter.Cons:Windows Hello: It’s a nice feature, but it’s inconsistent. It frequently fails to recognize me, forcing me to use my PIN. It should be more reliable, especially in low light.Network Port (LAN): I’ve noticed the physical port feels a bit loose. Sometimes the cable loses connection, which forces a switch to Wi-Fi, incredibly annoying during gaming. I have to position the cable just right to keep it stable. (I recommend checking if your unit has this issue early on).RAM: 16GB is starting to feel limiting in 2026. For a smooth, future-proof experience, I highly recommend upgrading to 32GB or more.Recommendation:-Use it with the AC on if you want to cool your laptop enough so this one doesn't suffer of thermal throttling and if you can afford a great laptop cooler buy it (I recommend Llano coolers.)-Boot from 0 (if you know how to do it): This is for you to start in 0 and avoid Asus services and extra-softwares that it comes by default. Use G-Helper instead of Armoury Crate btw.Verdict: I have zero regrets. Despite the minor issues with the LAN port and the webcam sensor, this laptop is a beast and offers fantastic value for the money.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Run, run as FAST as you can from ASUS
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: If I could give this laptop zero stars I would and hopefully this review saves someone from ever buying an ASUS laptop or any of their products. I bought this laptop in late September of 2025 as a birthday present for myself and by early-mid December I was already having issues. The cpu and gpu were both running at 100% usage, the cpu was getting up to 89 degrees Celsius, and my fps was dropping to single digits (anywhere from 1-8 fps constantly) any time I would try to play ANY game, to try to help that, I bought an $80 laptop cooling stand to try to cool the laptop down and it was STILL reaching high 80’s. I sent the computer in for repair under warranty back in December of 2025. I got the laptop back and everything was somehow worse and the repair summary they sent said that all they did was change a pad and add tape. I got tired of messing with it so I didn’t do anything with it for 3 months. It is now march of 2026 as I’m writing this review and I just sent the laptop back for repair a second time last weekend. I got an email yesterday saying that their “repair technicians” (if you can even call them that) found no issues with the unit and they will be sending it back unrepaired unless I provide more information even though I’ve been on the phone with ASUS around 7 times in the past week confirming what I sent the laptop in for. Do NOT buy anything from asus, it’ll save you money and time. Go buy yourself a better computer from a company that actually cares about and helps their customers.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Let me just say this upfront: this laptop feels like it’s going to outlive me… or at the very least survive my daily “throw it in the bag and run” lifestyle.After spending years with a Chromebook (and yes… “hated” might be strong, but also… not inaccurate), I knew I was not about to make another regret purchase. I missed that classic, reliable, Windows-era laptop vibe—like 2015 called and said, “we did it right back then.” So I did what any determined, slightly burned consumer would do: I researched. And researched. And then researched some more.Because here’s the thing—I’m not a tech wizard. I’m a 44-year-old businesswoman who just needs her laptop to work without acting like it needs emotional support every time I open a spreadsheet.And this one? Oh, it DELIVERS.✔️ The keyboard has that satisfying little click that makes you feel productive even when you’re just typing emails✔️ It’s sturdy—like, “toss it in your bag and don’t say a prayer over it” sturdy✔️ Battery life? Impressive. We love a device that doesn’t quit before we do✔️ Wi-Fi and Bluetooth connect seamlessly (because I do not have time for technological attitude)I made sure to get enough storage so I wouldn’t be dealing with lag or buffering, and guess what—no drama. None. It just… works. Imagine that.For someone who’s constantly on the go—office, travel, coffee shop pretending to be productive—this laptop checks every box without trying to be something it’s not (looking at you, Chromebook era 🙃).Bottom line: it’s reliable, it’s efficient, and for the price, it’s a solid investment. No regrets, no complaints, just a laptop that finally understands the assignment.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: RTX 5070 Ti Gaming Laptop That Truly Replaces a DesktopRTX 5070 Ti Gaming Laptop That Truly Replaces a Desktop
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This is a very powerful laptop with an impressive display, and it’s not even as thick as I expected. In fact, it’s slightly thinner than the Legion 5 I upgraded from, which I bought about six years ago. The keyboard, touchpad, and battery life were not major factors in my purchasing decision, as I use this laptop primarily as a desktop replacement connected to an external monitor.In the Time Spy benchmark, it scores around 17,600 on average, which is better than many laptops with similar specifications. I was expecting a little more, but at the end of the day, it’s just a benchmark.In real-world gaming, however, the performance exceeded my expectations. In modern games such as BF6 and MW3, the visuals are excellent, and very few compromises are needed. Even when adjustments are necessary, I prefer using High settings instead of Ultra and slightly lowering demanding options such as shadows. There’s no need to push everything to the extreme. Modern DLSS technology is excellent, and I can easily achieve well over 100 FPS. BF6 is more CPU-demanding than MW3, yet both games run exceptionally well.I purchased this laptop primarily for FPS gaming, and I’m happy to say it performs even better than I had hoped.I use it as my main gaming station, connected to a 34-inch ultrawide monitor running at 3440×1440 resolution. This setup requires even more GPU power than the laptop’s native display, yet it still delivers excellent gaming performance. The laptop sits on a slim cooling pad, which I believe is important for maintaining healthy operating temperatures.I’m also happy with my decision to choose a GPU with 12GB of VRAM for future-proofing. From what I’ve seen so far, 16GB of system RAM is still sufficient for today’s games, making the overall specifications feel very well balanced.Overall, this was an expensive purchase, especially when buying online, but it was absolutely worth it. This is my first experience with an Acer product, and I’m very impressed. Great job, Acer.

Wake up your system securely and access your confidential files in less than a second—keeping your personal data safe from prying eyes at the office or in public spaces.

【USB 4.0 Future-Proof Connectivity】Future-proof your workstation with next-level expansion capabilities. productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Really worth it for the price, even the current price despite it jumping up
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: So far so good. This thing handles photoshop better than I had hoped. I use it mostly for work and art. I would say that battery is okay. A little bit overblown by what the reviews had me expecting, but I'm sure if I put it into economy mode, it'd be much better. But if you are using programs that utilize resources, it really doesn't stand up to the battery life promised. If you just use it for word processing and the internet, you'll love it. Incompatibility is definitely less of an issue than I thought it would be, as every program I've tried has worked fine. My dumb self didn't realize it was touch screen, so that was a nice extra bonus. If you don't like AI components, or how annoying microsoft is, you might get annoyed by this laptop, just a lot of extra time scrubbing stuff from it. Overall, though, for the price was definitely worth it. I caught it at $550, and that feels like a steal for what it can do and the features it has. Really pleased so far. I'll edit the review if anything changes.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on March 30, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Great for home use. I have an Acer Aspire that is still going strong since 2012, and that was a big consideration to go with Acer again.  The old one had a 17" screen, this is 16", which I find to be quite suitable. It is definitly, much lighter than the old one, but in that regard, I am probably being Mr. Obvious.  I have always liked a keyboard that had a number pad. With this being a smaller footprint than my old model, which had a full size number pad, I have had a period of adjustment getting used ton this one.  I love the backlit keyboard. It turns off with no activity, but just touch any key and it's on.  This machine is pretty quick, well suited for home use, browsing the internet, steaming etc. with no issues.  And lastly, for the pricepoint, I think it would be hard to beat.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on March 11, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Update: After loving this for several months I encountered an issue when I needed to connect to the GlobalProtect VPN for work. The Snapdragon processor doesn't play well with the download files and I couldn't find the correct exe. file that would allow me to connect. If you plan to use this for work make sure your IT team has a compatible link for you.I felt like I was looking for the unicorn of laptops until I found this. I wanted a numeric keyboard, backlit keyboard and the ability to connect to two external monitors - this has all of those plus a touchscreen! I use Google and Dropbox for file storage so the 512GB of storage works for me and saved me a little money on a laptop with more storage.This was easy to set up and start using, removing some of the ads and junk loaded in was easy. I connected two external laptops, one via HDMI and one via USB-C (this laptop thankfully supports video) and they worked right away without having to refine any settings or search for monitors which made me SO happy. I'm able to charge via the second USB-C port so I'll never have to choose between connecting to a monitor or charging. Connecting Bluetooth devices like keyboard, mouse, headset or Airpods was really easy and I find that they work seamlessly with the laptop, no lag at all.I find this to be fast and makes reading emails and searching online a breeze because I'm not waiting for things to load like I was on my previous Chromebook - it feels like a big upgrade.I've never had a Snapdragon processor but so far I'm happy with it. I find that it's fast and the battery life is fantastic, one charge lasts all day depending on what I'm using it for.I would absolutely recommend this to someone looking for an affordable laptop for day-to-day tasks and connecting to external equipment when needs turn to more work-related jobs.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great gaming laptop for the price!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Ive had this laptop for about 2 weeks now. I was nervous buying this because theres so many mixed reviews, but here is my pros and cons and honest opinion (coming from someone who only plays sims and gta5).Ive watched so many Youtube reviews and read so many comments and amazon reviews so it was a very thought out purchase lol.It really has good graphics and runs everything smoothly. Loading times are under 10 seconds no matter what game I am playing.Ive never had a gaming laptop before so i really did my research before buying, and i love this laptop. Light up keyboard, Non flimsy screen (because some people were stating that it wobbles but i dont have a problem with that). battery life does really well and also charges conveniently.All of the features like windows 11 and just the keyboard set up on the laptop is a1 in my opinion. Comes with Omen and Nvidia which just helps you game better. lots of perks with EA and omen discounts steam discounts etc etc.Laptop set up was super simple, downloading apps and things are super easy and fast. I can run my sims game in the background while i google something or watch youtube videos so the ram is nice and i got the 8gb which i was doubting it would be enough ram but its plenty. same for gta5.if youre a casual gamer and still want to have a laptop for day to day basis/ school, i would recommend.i have plenty of storage so far as well. i think it came with 600 gb?? i have about 1000 mods/cc for sims alone with gta and still have a good 500gb left if not more.has bluetooth which i really love to connect my airpods and xbox controller to it. they said it came with an alexa but i havent yet found it or even bothered to look as theres so much to discover when using this and setting up.theres only one or two things ive noticed that i dont like about this laptop but its nothing to not make me buy the laptop again if needed. i noticed your fingerprints are very likely to show all over this laptop lol. outside, mouse pad, screen. lol. nothing to crazy youll just need to wipe often. another thing is the fan is very loud when you have games running. it was noticeable at first because my old laptop wasnt like that but its only because your laptop is processing graphics etc at such a fast pace which is a good thing. i got used to the sound quickly. and the last thing is the mouse pad gets stuck. when i click too much or too hard when gaming it gets pushed down and will get stuck. longest its lasted was like probably less than 5 minutes. just little bit annoying but you can still tap and use mouse any other ways.overall, im really happy with this purchase. its my first gaming laptop let alone brand new out the box and im satisfied with it.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: I thought the reviews were BS, but nah this good
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I genuinely do not understand where the negative reviews are coming from because this is a steal of a laptop. The battery lasts up to like 4-5 hours when not on charge, the screen does go up to 144Hz, the RTX runs really well, and it does have an extra RAM slot so you can change them out. Oh also, the laptop is made of that "not very cheap" plastic which makes it by far the most durable PC I've ever had. Though I am going to still be careful with it of course.I would say that my only criticism would be that the bottom was INCREDIBLY hard to take off which would make it very difficult for repairs, cleaning, and changing hardware. I had to be very gentle at removing it for almost an hour for it to come undone. OH ALSO thank you to whoever decided to put normal Philips head screws on the bottom cause the last 2 laptops I had, had these star shaped ones which were very very annoying.Edit: It has been a bit longer since and I am still rather happy with this laptop. Though I do have a gripe about the keyboard. Ever since I got it, sometimes the laptop will slow down to a very very slow speed (Which is not the end of the world for me, but it is annoying for about 2 minutes) and I cannot seem to find why it is doing it. Other than that, everything is running pretty good and I am still satisfied. Thank you :3

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: Completa a buen precioCompleta a buen precio
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: Es una computadora muy completa, la memoria RAM (2 ranuras con 4gb cada una) es suficiente para realizar tareas de navegación y multimedia, he tenido abiertas al mismo tiempo las diferentes tiendas de juegos, páginas web, música en Amazon music y no he tenido ningún problema, sin embargo, decidí comprarle memoria RAM en mi caso 32gb + 4gb de las que ya trae, espero corra aún mejor y sé que estará sobrada.Al principio me preocupo la pantalla, se veían como flashazos muy leves (casi imperceptibles), después de actualizar todos los drivers, Windows, BIOS, etc., ya no volvió a suceder.La pantalla es de 60Hz con 250 nits.El sonido, si bien esta firmado por Bang&Olufsen, no es nada del otro mundo, tenemos que ser conscientes de que es una laptop y el sonido se escucha simplemente decente.Por cierto, en otra opinión se comenta sobre lo de la BIOS, lean esa opinión antes de encender su lap por primera vez.Algunos se quejan de que es muy ruidosa y solo sucede a veces cuando activas el modo rendimiento (aun así, creo que no conocieron las laptops de los años 2000), sin embargo, tu puedes controlar el ventilador (ECO, Silencioso, equilibrado, alto rendimiento)Trae la aplicación OMEN que es excelente para hacer limpieza, personalizar su funcionamiento y optimizar la laptop, se agradece.No trae la letra ñ, pero puedes modificar la disposición del teclado, así como también puedes cambiar el idioma de Windows ya que trae la edición HOME, se tiene que descargar el idioma y después aplicarlo.Efectivamente trae la tarjeta RTX 3050, no la he usado mucho, pero corre muy bien StreetFighter5, CounterStrike, Age of Empires 3 y 4, con gráficos moderados o altos.El procesador es Core i5 12500HCarga muy rápido, en una hora de 80%, si la usas en modo equilibrado te dura 3 horas o más la batería, en alto rendimiento 1 hora.Incluye 1 mes de Microsoft365. 1 mes de McAfee y 1 mes de GamePass.La caja traía un pequeño detalle que no afecto en nada al equipo.No hay muchas reseñas de esta computadora en internet, sin embargo, después de revisar las ACER, ASUS y LENOVO, por sus precios no ofrecen las capacidades de esta (por ejemplo, ampliar la memoria RAM hasta 64GB y el almacenamiento) la recomiendo 100%, yo la compre por 15mil pesos (860USD).

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: Soy de México y para un envío internacional llegó bastante rápido (3 días), el paquete llegó en buen estado en excepción por la caja de Amazon que llegó un poco matrada.Ahora unas recomendaciones para algunas personas en su primer uso y por el que muchas personas tienen problemas con el bitlocker.PRIMER ENCENDIDO DEL DISPOSITIVOEn su primer encendido configurar la configuración básico como se debe, siempre vincular en ese momento una cuenta de Microsoft (Hotmail, outlook) esta parte en la actualidad ya es obligatoria lo digo por que he visto muchas personas que aún no tienen una cuenta de Microsoft en su dispositivo, una ves que logren entrar hasta su escritorio, lo primero que no deben de hacer es irse a su navegador a descargar sus programas de trabajo o sus videojuegos, eso es para después.ACTUALIZACION DEL SISTEMAActualizar el sistema operativo para todos los dispositivos electrónicos debe ser el primer paso que se debe de hacer para un buen funcionamiento, ya que estás actualización quitarán muchos de los problemas en rendimiento, seguridad, etc.Para esto se tienen que ir a la configuración>Windows update, en esta podrán ver las actualizaciones disponibles tendrán que empezar a descargar e instalar, esto se debe de hacer las veces necesarias hasta que ya no aparezcan más actualización.Va a llegar un punto donde el dispositivo actualizará la BIOS y el FIRMWARE, está se instalara de forma diferente desde el recovery del dispositivo (no se espanten si los ventiladores del dispositivo estan al máximo, es normal eso), una ves que de instalen en su reinicio está la posibilidad que de salta la famosa pantalla Bitlocker, si realmente configuraron bien en su primer encendido con una cuenta de Microsoft ya validada, solo tienen que ir a la página que les dice en esa ventana desde otro dispositivo inteligente (otras computadora o celular) solo tienen que iniciar sesión con si cuenta que ingresaron en la computadora al inicio, si todo fue correcto en la página les aparecerá la si clave de recuperación, solo tienen que meterla en la pantalla de Bitlocker (la clave solo de compone de números).Una ves que ya pasaron la ventana del Bitlocker puede que si ingresaron una contraseña para su inicio por seguridad puede que les salte un mensaje que la contraseña no cumple con el formato y no podrán acceder. Esto solo se soluciona ahí mismo, les saltará una ventana de cambio de contraseña, primero les pedirá iniciar sesión con su cuenta de Microsoft por seguridad al cambiar la contraseña, está la pueden cambiar por otra diferente o la misma que tenías. En mi caso cuando se cambió mi contraseña la pantalla se puso en negro posiblemente por los drives de los gráficos, en mi caso solo puse la contraseña en el teclado y me dejó entrar a mi escritorio, como tal es como si se apagará la pantalla pero sigue en la pantalla de bloqueo.Una ves terminado eso, una vez más verifiquen si hay más actualizaciones del sistema y hacer de nuevo las instalaciones necesarias, si ya no aparecen más pues ya puedes irte a tu navegador a descargar tus programas favoritos y tus videojuegos.RENDIMIENTOen cuanto al rendimiento es bastante bueno, una recomendación es que expandan la memoria RAM a 16GB ya que con 8GB se queda corta actualmente.Y esto sería todo por esta reseña espero que les alla sido de ayuda.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Like any pre-built computer/laptop. For sure know what you're getting into
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Out of the box, this computer works great. I can play games like Fortnite and The Finals at 4k at 200+ FPS. The cooling system works well by itself too, the card is usually around 65-70 Celsius at the end of an hour or so gaming session. The laptop cannot show CPU Temps, there is a preinstalled app that lets you "see" it. But that is a pure guess. The only component that gives thermal readings is the GPU.The screen is bright and beautiful, the screen is also a WLED screen which isn't mention. So it's not OLED but it's still really good. It's a big size, although if you want a gaming laptop that is expected.The main issue I have with this computer is the bloatware that is preinstalled.It comes with McAfee anti-virus, which is quite possibly, if not THE, worst anti-virus software on the market. It also comes pre-installed with its own ASUS monitor program, which only has features that can be easily accessed in the settings menu. Said ASUS Program also takes up a ton of memory space by letting itself run by default on the computer.Overall, if you can get it on sale for less than two thousand. It's a good purchase. Otherwise I would hold off.
