productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Here's an honest review highlighting what I think most of y'all will want to know!24 hour ownership and here's what I've found.This laptop is surprisingly powerful! i7 13620h paired with 32gb Ram and a 5070 GPU. This is running BF6 at 90FPS consistently with the graphics maxed out and runs Star Citizen at 70FPS with the settings at max. I have very minimal stuttering moments with this laptop under heavy load and have no major complaints for the playability and function.Audio quality is laptop grade. This is not going to "WOW" you in anyway. If you're an audiophile looking for soundwave bliss, laptops aren't for you. The speakers are downward facing toward the front corners of the laptop and are plenty loud enough with smooth quality.The display is a respectable 16" (that's measured diagonally) and is very responsive. I haven't dabbled aggressively into advertisement creation or video editing yet but it seems to be quite clear with no visible deficits.Battery life is accurate to the advertisement and seems to have some protective features you can use in the GiMate software.Boot times are generally quick and I don't have too much more to say about that.The keys feel great to type on, they're not loud at all and the trackpad is accurate and responsive. I wish the track didn't travel downward so much when firm clicking but it does work very well.The hinges feel sturdy and smooth, and the screen does open to 180 degrees with minimal effort.Now, for the yellow and red flags.First, the Gigabyte Pre-installed GiMate software is a little unnecessarily flashy and doesn't offer much customization control, which on a gaming laptop is disappointing to say the least. I mean you cannot use the software to control fan speed curve, OC frequency, etc. etc. It has some pre-programed settings for performance or balance or eco modes but does not give the user the ability to fine tune these settings.The software also has AI built into it which chews up Ram. I've discovered it running idle, not open or being utilized and it's taken up as much as 2.5gb of my available ram. There is also no setting I can find to disable just the AI and if you delete the AI file the entire program will no longer run. Huge thumbs down if you want to use it but want to save RAM.The RGB portion of the program is not bad, but needs work. It does not cooperate with windows very well at times and while changing colors or patterns I've noticed some strobing effect while it is sorting itself out.The keyboard portion of the laptop just feels a bit lacking. The speakers don't face up, there's a large amount of flat, black, unused space around the keyboard edge and it just feels like they could have done a little more to spice it up or give the user some quality of life features here.When under heavy load the fans will kick on to keep temps under control, and they ramp up to full speed which produces a fair bit of noise. It works though! This unit has not broken 71 degrees (Celsius) even under heavy usage.Lastly, the charging cable is a straight plug, meaning there is no bend to it like many other laptop charging cables out there. This means that when plugged in you have a cord sticking straight out the left side of the laptop and taking up space on the desk around the computer. One thing I've always appreciated about 90 degree plugs is the ability to run that straight back the desk and neatly out of the way.All in all, this laptop is flat out incredible for its price point and features. The power packed in this unit competes with my $2000 desktop build. It starts up quickly and quietly, it's efficient and runs my games very well. I couldn't complain about it because, well, I bought a laptop to play games and build digital content. It does both very well!If you're looking for a laptop that can give you a quality gaming experience and doesn't break the bank, look no further. This one is a keeper!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: My Gigabyte Aorus 16X Gaming Laptop is finally hereMy Gigabyte Aorus 16X Gaming Laptop is finally here
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: For a Guy  who's on the hunt for a laptop that can handle both my day job in graphic design and my weekend gaming sessions, I finally pulled the trigger on the Gigabyte Aorus 16X this year. Priced around $1,600 for the mid-tier config (Intel Core i7-14650HX, RTX 4070 GPU, 32GB DDR5 RAM, 1TB SSD, and that stunning 16-inch 2560x1600 165Hz display), it seemed like a steal compared to bulkier beasts from ASUS or MSI. think rendering 4K timelines in Premiere Pro, cranking through Cyberpunk 2077 on ultra settings, and even some light 3D modeling in Blender—I'm ready to share my unfiltered take. Spoiler: It's a powerhouse with some quirks, but it earns its spot in my daily driver lineup. I'll break this down into pros and cons first, then dive into a deeper section-by-section review. This isn't just spec-sheet fluff; it's based on real-world grinding, from airport lounges to late-night raid bosses.ProsExceptional Performance: The i7-14650HX and RTX 4070 combo crushes gaming (100+ FPS in most AAA titles at 1440p) and creative workloads without breaking a sweat. No throttling during long sessions.Excellent Connectivity: Thunderbolt 4, HDMI 2.1, Ethernet, Wi-Fi 7—hook up external monitors or docks effortlessly.Limited RGB: 3-zone keyboard lighting is cool but no per-key customization; projector light is gimmicky and drains battery if left on.Impressive Battery Life for a Gamer: Up to 6-7 hours of light productivity (web, docs, streaming) thanks to NVIDIA Optimus switching.Upgrade-Friendly: Easy access to two SODIMM slots and dual M.2 bays for future-proofing RAM and storage.Robust Build and Cooling: Sturdy aluminum lid, solid chassis with minimal flex, and effective vapor chamber cooling keeps temps under 85°C even under load.ConsLoud Fans: They ramp up to jet-engine levels during intense gaming or rendering, making it tough for shared spaces.Gorgeous Display: 16-inch QHD IPS panel with 165Hz refresh, Dolby Vision HDR, and 500+ nits brightness—vibrant colors and smooth motion for both work and play.Bulky Power Brick: The 240W adapter is chunky and has a straight cable that sticks out awkwardly; no L-shaped plug for tidy setups.Software Glitches: Gigabyte Control Center crashes occasionally, especially when tweaking profiles on the fly. RGB control can be finicky.Port Placement: All on the sides—no rear ports for cleaner desk setups. MicroSD reader feels cheap compared to full-size SD.Average Webcam in Low Light: 1080p IR cam is fine for Windows Hello, but grainy for Zoom calls without good lighting.Clean Out-of-Box Experience: Minimal bloatware; AI features in the Control Center (like auto-gear shifting) actually help optimize power without hassle.Weight and Portability: At 5.1 lbs, it's not backpack-friendly for long hauls—feels more desk-bound than ultra-portaUnboxing and Initial SetupThe box arrives with the usual suspects: the laptop, a hefty power brick, and a quick-start guide. No fancy sleeve or extras like some Razer models, but that's fine—Gigabyte keeps it practical. Setup was a breeze: Boot into Windows 11, run the Gigabyte Control Center for drivers, and you're golden in under 30 minutes. The IR webcam nailed facial login right away, and the pre-installed RGB Fusion synced effortlessly (mostly). One hiccup: The Control Center app glitched once during initial profile setup, forcing a restart. Not a dealbreaker, but it hints at the software quirks I'll gripe about later.Design and Build QualityGigabyte nailed the "stealth gamer" aesthetic here. The matte black aluminum lid with subtle Aorus branding looks professional enough for client meetings, but flip it open, and the aggressive vents and RGB keyboard scream "beast mode." At 14 x 10 x 1.1 inches and 5.1 pounds, it's slimmer than the MSI Raider GE78 but still chunkier than a MacBook Pro 16. The chassis feels premium—no creaks or flex, even when palm-resting during intense typing. The rear light bar projects the Aorus logo onto your desk, which is a fun touch (though I disabled it to save battery). Ports are plentiful: 2x USB-A 3.2, 1x Thunderbolt 4, 1x USB-C 3.2 (with DP), HDMI 2.1, Ethernet, and a headphone jack. Wish they'd added a rear USB-C for docking, but the included layout works for most setups.Display and AudioThis is where the Aorus 16X shines brightest—literally. The 16-inch IPS panel hits 2560x1600 at 165Hz with G-Sync support, delivering buttery-smooth gameplay in titles like Forza Horizon 5 (144 FPS locked) and crisp visuals for photo editing in Lightroom. Colors pop with 100% DCI-P3 coverage, and HDR content (Netflix, YouTube) looks cinematic thanks to Dolby Vision and 500 nits peak brightness. Viewing angles are wide, and anti-glare coating kills reflections in bright rooms. For audio, the quad speakers pump out surprisingly rich sound with decent bass—better than the tinny output on my old Dell XPS. Not audiophile-grade, but immersive for movies or Spotify during renders.Performance: Gaming, Productivity, and MultitaskingNo sugarcoating: This thing flies. In benchmarks, it edged out the Lenovo Legion Pro 5 in Cinebench R23 multi-core (18,500+ points) and Handbrake encoding, thanks to the 16-core i7 and 140W RTX 4070. Gaming? Cyberpunk 2077 with RT Ultra at 1440p averaged 85 FPS with DLSS; Shadow of the Tomb Raider hit 140+ FPS on high. Creative apps love it—Blender viewport rendering was 20% faster than my previous RTX 3060 rig, and Premiere Pro exports flew by. The 32GB RAM handles 50+ Chrome tabs plus Photoshop without swapping. AI features? The Control Center's "AI Nexus" auto-switches GPU modes seamlessly, boosting efficiency for mixed use. Upgrades are straightforward: Pop off the bottom panel (six screws), and you've got room for 64GB RAM and a second SSD.Keyboard, Trackpad, and InputThe per-key-ish RGB keyboard (it's zoned, but customizable) has 1.7mm travel with snappy feedback—great for typing reports or mashing WASD. NumPad integration via touch is handy for spreadsheets, though accidental activations happen. The glass trackpad is huge and precise, with haptic feedback that rivals Apple's. Windows Hello via IR cam is lightning-fast, and the 1080p webcam holds up for Teams calls (just light it well).Battery Life, Thermals, and PortabilityBattery surprised me: 6.5 hours of web browsing/Office work at 50% brightness, dropping to 4 hours with light photo editing. Gaming unplugged? Expect 1-1.5 hours max—plug in for the full show. Thermals are a mixed bag: Vapor chamber cooling keeps the CPU/GPU under 85°C in balanced mode, but fans hit 50dB+ during stress tests, sounding like a vacuum cleaner. It's warm on the keyboard (up to 95°F), but not uncomfortable. At 5.1 lbs, it's portable for a 16-incher, but the brick adds bulk to your bag.Software and SupportGigabyte Control Center is the weak link—it's bloated with RGB tweaks and monitoring, but crashes when switching power modes (fixed by reinstalling from their site). No McAfee nonsense, though, and Windows updates integrate smoothly. Warranty is standard 1-year, with decent RMA experiences from forums (quick swaps for DOA units). Gigabyte's site has solid driver support, but don't expect hand-holding like Dell. I'll try using a program like SignalRGB and see how it fairs instead.Who Should Buy This?If you're a hybrid user—gaming after hours, creating by day—the Aorus 16X is a value champ at $1,600. It punches above its weight against pricier Lenovo or ASUS options. Skip if you need whisper-quiet operation (go XPS) or ultra-portability (MacBook). Overall, I'd repurchase in a heartbeat—it's boosted my workflow and frag count without regrets. Solid 8.5/10. If you're eyeing it, grab the i7/4070 config; the i9 upgrade isn't worth the extra $300 for most.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great Performance - When it works - Wish more timely support was available
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Owned for about a week of occasional gaming for testing as i planned to be traveling and wanted an option to do so while away. Great price performance all around. I have an external GSYNC HDR monitor i push it to at home and everything is almost on par with my desktop.I Did all the updates for drivers, bios and utilities and all was well. Satisfied I let it be for about a week until I began traveling yesterday and went to boot up a game i had tested before and its slow to launch, all inputs lag and i get about 5fps on all titles, that were previously tested and running well. productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I’ve been using this MSI Cyborg 17 for both work and gaming, and it has exceeded my expectations.The 17.3-inch 144Hz display is smooth and immersive, making games look great while also providing plenty of screen space for productivity. The Intel Core 7 processor paired with the RTX 5060 handles everything I throw at it, from multitasking and content creation to modern AAA games with excellent performance.The 16GB DDR5 RAM and 1TB SSD make the system feel fast and responsive. Boot-up times are quick, applications load almost instantly, and there’s plenty of storage for games and files.I also appreciate the lightweight design for a 17-inch gaming laptop. The translucent black chassis gives it a unique futuristic look without being too flashy. Connectivity is solid with USB-C, Wi-Fi 6E, and enough ports for my accessories.The cooling system does a good job during long gaming sessions. The fans become noticeable under heavy load, but temperatures stay well under control, which is expected for a gaming laptop.Overall, this is an excellent value if you’re looking for a powerful gaming laptop that also works well for everyday use. I would definitely recommend it to anyone looking for strong performance, a large high-refresh-rate display, and modern hardware at a competitive price.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great laptop, could have been designed better
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Overall I'm happy with the laptop.  Let's start with the Cons.1) There is only 1 usb-c and 2 usb-a ports which is insufficient.2) The usb ports and the 3.5mm headset port are all positioned right on the right side where a right handed person would use a mouse so it's a poor design.  They should be on the back, which is completely unutilized.3) The rtx5060 isn't terribly impressive but not terrible.  It feels comparable to the 4060 in my 2023 model gaming laptop.  If you're gaming you'll want to use the msi center app and turn on performance mode.  By default it is in a hybrid mode managed by AI that worries too much about energy conservation...4) There is only one SSD slot so it doesn't support more than one drive which is bizarre heading into 2026.The laptop is listed a as not supporting gen5 nvme m.2 SSDs but that's not true.  I upgraded to a 2TB gen5 with no issues, however windows 11 24h2 wouldn't recognize any ssd with either the stock 4th gen 1tb or the 5th gen 2TB I installed so I had to get the IRST driver from the MSI website in order to install windows.  You'll also want to grab the other msi drivers if you're doing a fresh install because by default the USB drivers Windows 11 applies transfers data at roughly 5% of capacity.I like that the bright colorful rgbs are only on the keyboard so when the lid is closed you're not lighting up the whole house at night.I also upgraded the ram from 16gb ddr5 to 32gb and upgraded the wifi from the 6e card to the BE200 wifi 7 card.

Pure performance. No distractions. 

Must-have gaming performance in a stunning, streamlined design featuring Intel Core processors, a WQXGA 120Hz 300 nits display and a stylish anodized aluminum lid. 
16.0-inch 16:10 WQXGA (2560x1600) 120Hz Anti-Glare Non-Touch 300nits WVA/IPS with ComfortView Plus Display

Playtime. Anytime. 

Play the latest games with graphics that rival reality. Play with players on console. Play with the peripherals that you love. When it comes to playing your way, Windows 11 makes it happen. 
Game changing graphics 
Step into the future of gaming and creation with NVIDIA GeForce RTX 50 Series Laptop GPUs, powered by NVIDIA Blackwell and AI. 
AI-boosted gameplay: Unleash next-level performance and image quality with DLSS 4. Achieve ultra-smooth frame rates with Multi Frame Generation and enhanced Ray Reconstruction. 
Competitive advantage: Compete faster with NVIDIA Reflex 2 technology featuring Frame Warp, which further reduces latency based on the game’s latest mouse input. 
Comfort focused design 

Intentionally designed for comfortable, everyday use. Alienware 16 Aurora’s streamlined design offers advanced thermal support without the need for a rear thermal shelf. The laptop’s smaller profile makes it an easy fit into bags and backpacks for on-the-go performance. 
Easy to carry. Hard to put down. 

Premium build: Alienware 16 Aurora is designed with premium materials, such as an anodized aluminum lid featuring an iridescent Alienware logo and magnesium alloy interior frame. 
Fluid contours 

Soft, smooth contours make the laptop more comfortable to hold, complimented by a stunning new colorway Interstellar Indigo with a satin finish. 
Comfort ensured 

Opening and closing your laptop lid just got easier thanks to an angled front edge. Plus, a gently pillowed palm rest ensures comfort during any gaming session. 
Ready for tomorrow 

With ample storage and memory, Aurora is built to game and multitask today and beyond. This laptop features two upgradeable PCIe Gen 4 SSD slots and two user-upgradeable DDR5 SO-DIMM memory slots. 
Purchase model configurations will vary. Subject to third party purchase of additional storage. SSDs are user-replaceable for up to 2TB of total SSD storage. It's recommended to add a bracket and thermal pad when you add 2230 SSD to upgrade your storage capacity. 
Essential power in a focused design 

Alienware 16 Aurora delivers an immersive gaming-first experience in a sleek, focused design. Get the performance you need, anywhere – powered by Intel Core processors and laptop GPUs ranging from NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060. 
Precision cooling for maximum efficiency 

The new Cryo-Chamber design optimizes airflow, cooling and performance. 
Intentional airflow: Air is strategically pulled in above the keyboard and in the Cryo-Chamber, and out four exhaust vents on the sides. 
Quiet and cool: Expertly designed fans keep the system running smoothly and quietly. 
Built to last: Efficient thermal design protects internal components and extends the life of the system.

Our advanced cooling technology, Alienware Cryo-tech, is designed to maintain system stability even during the most demanding sessions. 
Dual fans 

Two fans with ultra-thin blades pull cool air in from the top and bottom; exhaust hot air out 4 vents to help enable higher performance. 
Copper heat pipes: Three copper heat pipes dissipate heat from the CPU and GPU ensuring seamless gaming. 
Blend into any environment 

Activate Stealth Mode with F7 to switch performance to Quiet Mode for a more subtle, covert experience. 
Quiet mode lowers noise produced by your system's cooling fans when possible. While your computer's performance might be slightly impacted, this option may also reduce both CPU and GPU power consumptions.

Balanced power 

The perfect balance of performance and portability in a stunning chassis. Ready to run your favorite games seamlessly with up to 110W Total Performance Power. 
Up to 110W: Total Performance Power is the combined maximum of TGP and TDP, enhancing overall performance across all you do.

items.text: Our advanced cooling technology, Alienware Cryo-tech, is designed to maintain system stability even during the most demanding sessions.

items.title: Dual fans
items.text:
Two fans with ultra-thin blades pull cool air in from the top and bottom; exhaust hot air out 4 vents to help enable higher performance. 
Copper heat pipes: Three copper heat pipes dissipate heat from the CPU and GPU ensuring seamless gaming.

items.title: Blend into any environment
items.text:
Activate Stealth Mode with F7 to switch performance to Quiet Mode for a more subtle, covert experience. 
Quiet mode lowers noise produced by your system's cooling fans when possible. While your computer's performance might be slightly impacted, this option may also reduce both CPU and GPU power consumptions.

items.title: Total command
items.text:
Convenient presets: Maximize your gameplay with performance presets for the power you need, no matter what you're doing. 
Performance overlay: Manage and see CPU, GPU, memory and thermals stats without exiting the game. 
AlienFX: Customize your setup with lighting settings that extend to all your Alienware accessories, as well as key binds and calibration. 
AlienVision: Toggle external Alienware monitor hardware-based overlays on/off to help you focus on the targets at hand.

items.title: Balanced power
items.text:
The perfect balance of performance and portability in a stunning chassis. Ready to run your favorite games seamlessly with up to 110W Total Performance Power. 
Up to 110W: Total Performance Power is the combined maximum of TGP and TDP, enhancing overall performance across all you do. 
Up to 65W: Total Graphics Power means higher GPU performance with more realistic gameplay. 
Up to 45W: CPU Thermal Design Power means full power devoted towards processing tasks in real-time. 
Available on configurations with NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 with Dynamic Boost.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Honest review. Included the "faults", but definitely 5*, even with them.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I love this laptop. In fact, I love it so much, I ordered all Alienware gear after how impressed I was with this product. It is a little heavy, but it is not overwhelming. Given all that is packed into this thing, you wouldn't expect it to be light. I imagine some of that weight is in the body. It had better be tough to protect all the high end components inside. It does die pretty quickly if you use it on battery mode only. I have only done this a few times, since I am mostly using it near an outlet anyway. It is a bit louder than I would like when using heavy processes like games. Again, these things are to be expected on a laptop running a 50 series graphics card and graphics heavy games. It is plenty powerful enough to run games on high graphics settings. It does get pretty warm too, but again, not crazy hot. I wouldn't want to game with it in my lap though. The picture quality is fantastic. The Alienware dashboard is great. There are lots of options to customize things your way. I was a little worried about the color at first, but now I love it. I built my whole gaming area around this color now. I have used it for gaming, digital art, and plenty of videos. It handles everything like a champ.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Matryoshka Doll Packaging, But A Trojan Horse InsideMatryoshka Doll Packaging, But A Trojan Horse Inside
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: ​The packaging was top-tier. It arrived incredibly fast, safely and securely packed inside an Amazon box, which contained an MSI box, which contained another box. It was like unboxing a high-tech Matryoshka doll. I also appreciated that the driver required a secure delivery code, ensuring the package actually made it into the right hands.​Unfortunately, that’s where the good news ends.​Once I opened the final doll, the unit I received was deeply problematic from day one. The display suffered from severe, constant graphics glitching right out of the box. Even more alarming, upon closer inspection, I noticed highly suspicious battery swelling that was actively pushing against the chassis.​Because of these blatant hardware and safety defects, this unit had to go straight back. Leaving a buyer stuck dealing with a hazardous, defective device like this with absolutely no resolution makes for an incredibly exhausting experience. I’ve attached photographic evidence clearly showing the screen failures and the battery hazard so others know what to look out for.​Given the hardware lottery and the safety risk of a swollen battery, I can't recommend risking your money on this specific unit. Look elsewhere to avoid weeks-long headaches.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Can't even play World of Warcraft.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I really was looking forward to this laptop, but very disappointed in how it handles games.  The first game I downloaded was WoW, and I can't even play it, the graphics rip, tear, and hitch constantly, and even worse if I use the HDMI to plug in a big monitor, plus the memory usage when just running WoW alone would go up to 80%, there is no reason it should be doing that, unless it's all the bloat ware running in the background, which I tried to get rid of most of it.  As far as the Noise Level that was not an issue, and I do like the build, the design allows breathing room so it doesn't overheat, which is very important in a gaming laptop.I haven't really got a chance to see how well the battery life is, because I've spent the majority of my time just trying to get WoW to run without graphic issues, and  because of the graphic issues I am returning it.  Here is the deal, I am technical, and I work on computers for a living, but when I buy a computer, that claims to run games with ease, that is what I expect!  I shouldn't have to do a ton of stuff to just play a simple game like World of Warcraft, this should work out of the box without tweaking anything.  I am giving this a 3 star because I do love the case design, that is an A+, if it weren't for that it would get a 1 star.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Older generation CPU modest stats but upgradable with a bit of effortOlder generation CPU modest stats but upgradable with a bit of effort
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Decent laptop for the price with Windows 11 Pro and barely sufficient RAM and storage but upgradable. The CPU is an older generation but still performs reasonably well for everyday work. Battery life is mediocre, the chassis is all plastic and feels a bit cheap, and the touchpad click is the weakest part of the machine. The 8GB it ships with is on the low side for Windows 11, and upgrading the memory makes this a much more useful laptop. RAM and SSD are both upgradable, but there are no instructions in the box and none I could find online, so I worked out the disassembly myself and wrote it up below with pictures.Detailed Review:Performance is reasonable for the price. The Core i7-9750h is a previous generation cpu from 2019. That said, it's a respectable 6 core CPU and it handles normal daily work well provided enough RAM and SSD. For browsing and general use it performs reasonably well out of the box.  If, however, you want to do a bit more with this I'd highly recommend upgrading the RAM and SSD storage.Windows 11 Pro is worth noting. Many systems/laptops at this price ship with Home, and Pro gets you additional features like BitLocker, Remote Desktop hosting, and group policy. If any of that matters to you, it's real money you're not spending separately.Battery life is mediocre. I didn't expect anything stellar at this price and it matches my expectations. Worth noting that the battery is listed as 5000mAh which isn't very big for a 6 core cpu at full speed.  Cooling fans needed for this cpu reduce runtime even more.The chassis is all plastic and feels somewhat cheap. It isn't terrible but it's plastic so it's no macbook but then you're not gonna get a macbook at under $400 either.The touchpad is where things get a little more obviously deficient.  The click action is very firm and doesn't feel responsive so double clicking is kind of a coin flip.Upgrading the RAM and SSD is easier said than done. The 8GB of stock memory is a bit low for Windows 11. It works, but 8GB is about as low as you'd want for an Windows 11 system and adding memory is what turns this from adequate into a much more useful machine. Both the memory and the SSD are upgradable, and the listing advertises support for far up to 32GB of RAM but there are no upgrade instructions in the box, and surprisingly, I could not find any online either. No service manual, no teardown guide, nothing. For a machine where upgrade unlocks it's full potential, the lack of printed or online upgrade instructions is a real gap.After some trial and error I was able to open the chassis and do the upgrade so I thought I'd share my process for others in case it helps:1. Turn the laptop upside down and locate the screws on the bottom.2. There are several different sizes, so make sure to keep note of which screws go where. I laid them out in the same pattern as the case and took a picture so I could identify which screw went where during reassembly.3. Take a thin metal spudger, or a butter knife in a pinch, and gently pry the bottom panel away from the main body. I started at the front right corner near the model label and worked slowly across the edge, along the side away from the hinge.4. Watch for the magnets that hold the lid shut. They will grab a metal spudger.5. There are about 6 tabs along the long side. You need to pry the side away from the panel slightly to release them.6. Once you get around the corners, the remaining tabs unclip with a slight bit of pressure.7. Memory and SSD are easily accessible once the bottom panel is off.It isn't hard but since the chassis is plastic scratching or breaking parts is possible so work slowly and carefully without too much force.Suggestions for the manufacturer: First, replace the touchpad with one that has separate left right buttons instead of the clickable pad.  Second, publish an upgrade guide or post a video to help people upgrade.Overall this is a decent machine for the money. Older CPU that still gets the work done, Windows 11 Pro included, unremarkable battery, plastic build, a touchpad click I'd change, and genuinely upgradable internals once you know how to get inside. Budget for a memory upgrade and it becomes a considerably more useful laptop than it is out of the box.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Really nice laptop for everything except hardcore gamingReally nice laptop for everything except hardcore gaming
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I will try to be as thorough as I can on this review. But if you don't want to read this entire review, the summary is that I highly recommend this laptop for most of the day to day uses you may need to do with a laptop.Picked up this laptop and got it set up. Set up was super easy which was basically setting up Windows access. It comes with a one month Office 365 subscription but then it bumps to $99 a year after that (nothing to do with the laptop, but wanted to mention it).Is this a hard core gaming rig? No. It has 8GB RAM (and the OS will take half of that) and 256GB disk. The CPU is decent for day to day use. The display is 1920x1080 so it is great for basic things like watching a movie, checking email or social media and playing some games. Will it run Call of Duty at a high FPS? No. But for basic gaming it worked well. I tried some basic Steam games and it worked fine.It has a nice assortment of USB ports as  well as an HDMI connector and a wired LAN connector which is very nice when using this on a desktop. The WiFi and bluetooth are solid. No issues at all connecting to my ear buds and home WiFi.A few comments.The camera is not IR so it will not do Windows Hello face recognition. You have to set up fingerprints and/or PIN. Not a huge deal IMO. A face recognition is nice, but not required. The camera is not a super high resolution but good enough for a Zoom call for sure.It does not have a touch screen. But it has a nice trackpad and enough USB ports you can run a mouse dongle.The cooling fans are under the laptop (which is standard on laptops these days) so if you are using it on your lap for anything graphically intensive like gaming you may need a cooling pad otherwise it will cook your legs. Again, not a big deal since pretty much all laptops are set up this way these days.It does not come with any media for the OS. I want to try a Linux build but if I do that, I will need to find a Windows 11 boot. Not sure about the licensing for Windows if I do that.I am not sure the price of this rig. When I grabbed it the Amazon price was $350'ish which would be a nice price for a laptop like this. It would be something very nice for a younger user or an older user that wants to use social media and such. Or even a work laptop for email/Slack/zoom whatever.So, I highly recommend this rig for anything but really hardcore gaming performance.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Decent budget worker, but keep your charger handy!Decent budget worker, but keep your charger handy!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I picked up this BTDD 15.6-inch laptop primarily for daily office work, web browsing, and some light multitasking. For the price point, it’s a capable machine, but there are a few important tradeoffs you should know before buying.🚀 Performance & StorageThe Core i7-9750H processor is a few generations old now, but because it has 6 cores, it still handles everyday tasks like a champ. It boots up incredibly fast thanks to the 256GB SSD, and opening 15+ Chrome tabs while editing a Word document didn't cause any stuttering.Note on Storage: If you plan on downloading a lot of large software or storing tons of video files, that 256GB SSD will fill up quickly. You may want to look into an external drive or cloud storage.🖥️ Display & BuildThe 1080p FHD screen is sharp, and the 180° hinge is actually super convenient when you want to lay the laptop completely flat on a desk to share your screen with a classmate or coworker. The backlit keyboard feels comfortable to type on, which is a massive plus if you're writing long essays or reports late at night.🔋 The Catch: Battery LifeThe main drawback here is the 5000mAh battery. Combined with an older, power-hungry i7 processor, the battery life is pretty underwhelming. I averaged about 3 to 4 hours of continuous use (medium brightness, streaming music, and typing) before needing a plug. If you're a student running from class to class all day, you will definitely need to pack the charger.📋 Quick Pros & ConsPros:Very snappy performance for standard business/school apps.Keyboard backlight makes night typing a breeze.Good port selection, including Type-C.Crisp display with excellent viewing angles.Cons:Short battery life (plan on staying near an outlet).256GB storage is a bit tight by modern standards.💡 Final VerdictIf you need an affordable laptop for a desk-bound setup, a home office, or dormitory use where an outlet is always nearby, this is a fantastic value. If you need true all-day portability without a charger, you might want to look elsewhere.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: I am very satisfied.I am very satisfied.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I really like this computer because the screen and keyboard work together seamlessly; you can tilt the screen back to whatever angle suits you best. If you only need the screen—say, to watch TV—the keyboard sits behind it, keeping things visually clean and uncluttered. Another feature I love is the LED lighting under the keyboard; the lights all snap on at once, creating a striking visual effect that signals the keyboard is active, and they automatically turn off after three seconds of inactivity. Startup takes a little time initially—since you have to set up an account and run Windows updates—but once everything is configured, the performance is great. My needs are simple—I mostly use it for watching TV—and overall, I am very satisfied.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I got this laptop for my daughter, she's 7 and had recently started using laptops in school. I figured given what she's been tasked with so far, the price point and this being convertible, I felt this was best suited for her instead of her older brother.  Those feelings were justified after a few days of use.  What do we like, not like?What we like:My daughter loves the convertible feature of this laptop.  As shes more accustomed to a tablet, having the ability to essentially make this one, was a huge win for her.  She can fold it in half, load up her favorite streaming app and she's off and running.Battery life, seems pretty good.  Honestly hard to judge because my daughter refuses to run on a battery unless she has to.Has a camera, which is nice for Skype etc but expectations should be low.Charges via USB C, cable could be a tad longer but is still a good length.What we dont like, but make sense given the price point:Not that fastest laptop.  She was able to play Minecraft on this, no dedicated GPU obviously, and it ran just fine.  However, we have seen slowdown.  Typically when launching a browser, the url/search box doesn't recognize typing right away.  However, I'm inclined to believe this is a Windows, Edge concern not the system.  If you open up Google docs, typing is fast and responsive.  I went as far as deleting as much bloatware as I could, wasnt much honestly, in order to help performance but didnt make a big difference.Speakers are awful.  Expected though given the price point.  Kids typically use headphones in school, so low quality speakers make sense.What's annoying:Why is the power button on the middle of the right side of the keyboard, next to USB ports?  I've accidentally hit the button 3 times in my limited use.  I thought it was just me and my clumsy hands but turns out, my daughter has done it too.  You shouldn't be able to easily, accidentally power off a device.This laptop gets hot when in use and plugged in.  My daughter found out the hard way not to let this sit on her lap for an extended time while plugged in.  She was like a frog in a pot of water being boiled.  She didnt notice that her legs had turned red until after she was done with a particular session.  She wasnt hurt and maybe she shouldve known better but the air vents are all on the bottom and they dont move a ton of air.  Considering the thickness, fan quality and the fact she was charging, it makes sense.  I would definitely suggest a laptop fan or pad.Why I gave it 4 stars despite the concerns:For the price point and the target market, this makes sense.  Thin, versatile, has a touch screen and offers everything a student may need.  Long term I might be concerned about the vendor, not sure what bios or firmware upgrades will look like in the future.  Im a computer Systems Administrator so security and keeping computers up to date is important to me.  However, if you just need to get through school, this will get the job done.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I picked up this flip laptop, mainly for basic tasks and some light browsing, and honestly, it’s been a pretty decent deal considering the price. The build quality definitely feels a bit on the cheaper side: the plastic casing is kind of flimsy, and the USB ports are snug to the point where plugging in thicker cables can be a bit of a hassle. But, for what I’m using it for, I can’t really complain too much. Once I swapped out Windows for Linux, the performance picked up noticeably, making it feel a lot more responsive than it initially did. The laptop’s versatility with its 360° hinge is also a plus; I find myself switching between laptop and tablet mode depending on whether I’m taking notes or just watching videos.The display is one of the standout features for me. At 16 inches with a full HD resolution, the screen is bright and clear, which is great for streaming shows or working on documents. At this price, it does have some backlight bleed. The backlit keyboard is another feature I appreciate, especially since I often work in dim lighting. Typing is comfortable enough, though the keys do feel a little shallow compared to more premium laptops.  I haven’t pushed it too hard with demanding software, but for web browsing, word processing, and the occasional video call, it does the job smoothly. The battery life is reasonable as well, lasting me a decent amount of time without needing to recharge.Connectivity options are pretty solid, with a good mix of ports including USB 3.0, Type-C, HDMI, and even a TF card slot, which is handy for transferring photos from my camera. The inclusion of WiFi 6 and Bluetooth 5.2 is a nice touch, ensuring fast and stable wireless connections. Overall, while this laptop isn’t going to win any awards for build quality or premium features, it offers great value for money if you’re looking for something affordable and versatile for everyday use.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on June 1, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great everyday laptop — does exactly what we need it to doGreat everyday laptop — does exactly what we need it to do
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: We picked this up for basic home use — streaming, browsing, light office work — and it handles all of it without a hiccup. Setup was straightforward and painless, which is always a good sign out of the box.The 16-inch screen is a nice size for this price range, and the display is sharp enough for video and everyday tasks. The keyboard is a standout — good size, comfortable to type on, and the backlight is a practical touch for low-light use.Battery life has been solid. We're not pushing it hard, but it gets through a full day of typical use without needing to be plugged in constantly.The 2-in-1 design gives you a lot of flexibility. We mostly use it in standard laptop mode, but the tent and tablet modes are genuinely useful depending on what you're doing. The 360° hinge feels sturdy.One thing to be aware of going in: 128GB of storage is on the lighter side, but the SSD is upgradeable up to 2TB, so that's a manageable limitation. productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great value convertible laptop with a few limitationsGreat value convertible laptop with a few limitations
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This is obviously not a gaming laptop, but that does not make it a bad laptop. In fact, for its intended purpose, I think it performs surprisingly well.The first thing I noticed was how slim, lightweight, and portable it is. The build quality feels solid, and it has a good selection of ports on both sides. It is clearly designed for mobility, school, office work, and everyday use rather than demanding workloads.Performance has been very good for normal tasks. Web browsing, YouTube, Netflix, Zoom meetings, email, office applications, online classes, and general productivity all run smoothly. The Intel i3 processor is one of the strongest points of this machine. Many budget laptops use much slower processors, but this one feels responsive and stays reasonably cool during regular use.I also tested it for coding and development work. Since much of my work involves cloud based tools and services such as ChatGPT, it handled lightweight Python projects, dashboards, spreadsheets, database tasks, and local web applications without any issues.One feature I ended up appreciating more than expected is the convertible touchscreen design. The screen can fold completely into tent or tablet modes, and the display automatically rotates depending on how it is positioned. This is surprisingly useful when sharing content with someone else or using the laptop in tighter spaces. The touchscreen also works well and adds flexibility that is uncommon at this price point.As expected, there are limitations. The included 8GB of RAM is enough for normal multitasking, but it is not a machine for running many heavy applications at once or keeping hundreds of browser tabs open. Storage is also somewhat limited out of the box, so users with large software libraries or media collections may want additional storage.For gaming, expectations should remain realistic. There is no dedicated GPU, so modern AAA games are not the target audience. However, lighter games, indie titles, Minecraft, Roblox, older games, and classic emulators should run just fine.One pleasant surprise is that the laptop can be upgraded. It includes two RAM slots, with one slot available for expansion, and the M.2 SSD can also be replaced with a larger drive. However, my own upgrade experience was more complicated than expected.After replacing the SSD with a larger drive, cloning the original installation did not work properly and I had to perform a clean Windows installation. During setup, Windows did not initially recognize the built in WiFi adapter, requiring me to use an external USB WiFi adapter to complete the installation. Fortunately, Windows Update later installed most of the important drivers, including WiFi, Bluetooth, audio, and graphics updates through Intel's software. Even so, some unknown devices remained in Device Manager, and I was unable to find an official driver package for this specific model.Because of that, I would consider the upgradeability both a benefit and a caution. It is absolutely possible to upgrade the RAM and storage, but I would only recommend doing so if you are comfortable troubleshooting Windows installations and driver related issues. I tried to find out if there was a way to contact the vendor/manufacturer but I had no luck finding someone to ask for drivers.My biggest complaint is the speaker quality. The built in speakers sound somewhat muffled and lack clarity. They are perfectly usable for meetings, videos, and casual use, but they are definitely one of the weaker aspects of the laptop.Overall, I think this is a very good laptop for students, office work, travel, coding, web browsing, streaming, and everyday productivity. It offers a responsive processor, a useful convertible touchscreen design, and upgrade potential at a reasonable price. As long as you understand its limitations and do not expect workstation or gaming laptop performance, it delivers a very good experience for the money.

Rendering in my 3D CAD software is fast and smooth. Some people report that this machine can run hot but I haven't done any gaming yet. For daily work it runs cool and completely silent. It feels solid and well made compared to other laptops in the same price range. My only complaint is that it only came with 16GB of RAM. 32GB should be standard for any mid-range laptop, especially one billed as a gaming machine. Both slots are filled so my only option is to replace both 8's with 16's. The 8's will go to waste. I'm surprised the camera is only 720p. All modern machines in this price range should be full HD. As for battery life, I have not yet been able to test it. I use this exclusively as a stationary workstation.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: It's a capable entry gaming laptop, but-
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: It's a good entry level gaming laptop that will run games okay out of the box, but you need to install a second stick of ram to get all the performance this machine has to offer, especially if you want very high fps for esports since that is more taxing on the cpu.This laptop has only one stick of ram (single channel), that makes the processor use only a 64 bits bus instead of a 128 bit bus, which noticeably bottlenecks it, even for basic, non gaming tasks. Adding a second ram with the same capacity, speed and CAS latency is best to enable dual Channel, this will do two things, it will double the capacity to 32gb which is the sweet spot atm (16 gb is becoming the new 8 gb ram AKA not enough), and doubles the cpu bus width to 128 bits.With 1x16gb ram my cpu used to max out and gpu sat around 50% usage (in some games), but after installing a second stick of ram it now has overall  higher fps, uses the gpu more, has better 1% and 0.1% lows and normal, everyday usage is noticeably snappier. It has a capable cpu, it's just limited by the single channel ram.Lucky for you this laptop uses ddr4 ram which is still much, MUCH cheaper than ddr5 ram. Ram prices are not expected to come down at all until 2028 at the very least, so yeah...For those who don't know, if you decide to buy this laptop and add a second stick of ram, make sure to buy SODIMM ram, not the bigger, normal PC ram which don't fit in laptops

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The Ryzen AI Max APU is the best way to balance high performance and efficiency. Dedicated GPUs are buggy with Windows. This avoids that issue entirely. It scales with power limits very cleanly. You can go between 100+ watts of maximum performance or 15 watts of silence. Do yourself a favor though if you're looking to extend battery life. Go into the BIOS and disable all of the cores on CCD1. This cuts your CPU cores in half. If you bought this gaming laptop for the purpose of gaming, you won't need those extra CPU cores anyways, and the power savings by disabling that whole cluster is significant, it also helps allocate more power to the integrated GPU when running limited power. You'll still have 6 cores/12 threads which is plenty for gaming. With those cores disabled, games have playable framerates with just 20-25W allocated to the APU. That comes out to 30-35W total power draw. That means on a full charge you can game on the go for over 2 hours without recharging. And of course at full power any game will run smoothly.The lid and bottom panel are aluminum, the inside of the clamshell is plastic. It's a well built laptop. The speakers are kinda bad, but can be made decent with EQ software. There's a white keyboard backlight that you can turn up stupidly bright. I do wish it could do colors, though. Keyboard feels nice enough, as does the trackpad. Thermals are excellent, you can easily run this with no fans at lower power profiles. The fans generally don't run loud under heavy workloads.  I love how thin and light this laptop is. Doesn't feel or even really look like a gaming laptop at all. The screen is really high quality for an IPS display. Great brightness as well.At the $2k price its hard to recommend unless you're looking for the most flexible laptop in terms of both low power and high power usage. This beats the usual problems with switching between dedicated and integrated graphics any day. You can absolutely get more powerful laptops at this price, but they can't match the seamless experience or the efficiency. Or the thinness and light weight. But if you're looking for the most ultrabook-gaming laptop there is, this is it.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on July 3, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: ASUS TUF Gaming A14 Copilot+ PC Gaming Laptop, 14” WQXGA 16:10
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This review is for the AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 392, 8060S GPU, 32GB RAM, 1TB SSD, model FA401.The AI Max+ platform is very strong for AI workloads at a reasonable cost.  I'm using it for image processing, where the 8060s is far better than even the best 2026 intel iGPUs.  As a gaming laptop you can run the CPU/iGPU up to about 100W which in turbo mode does engage both fans with some noise, but it is not too bad.  You can manually create custom fan and power profiles and the BIOS has a good amount of controls also.The included 200W power supply is rather bulky compared to the typical GaN low power USB ones seen all over, but it will power and charge the A14 all day long without getting too warm.  Alternatively a USB-C GaN power brick that plugs directly in the wall can be used but it occupies the only TB/USB 4 port.  The other USB-C port does not provide charging.  A true 100W PD (20V at 5A) charger and 5A cable are needed for decent performance, so it is suggested to get a charger rated at 140-160W.  Below 100W, a USB charger will still work but the laptop performs more like it is on battery.  Overall this is a good value laptop especially when on sale.One of the main reasons for getting this A14 is that it has two M.2 2280 slots.  Despite the specs or what is written online I was able to install two 8TB double sided PCIe 4 SSDs for testing and that work just fine.  In heavy use a few mm of silicone heatsink pads will be helpful in transmitting heat to the shell.  The supplied 1TB SSD (appears to be a Samsung 990 EVO Plus) has a metal thing around it.The one negative is that although the matte display has enough resolution at 2560x1600, it is barely sRGB and notably lacking in red gamut.  I do not recommend doing any color critical work with it.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Clean setup for a reception desk or small office
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: We installed this computer at the front desk of a small business where it is used for scheduling, customer records, email, invoices, printing, and browser-based applications. The all-in-one design was the main reason we selected it because there is no separate computer tower taking up space around the reception counter.The Ryzen 5 3500U and 16GB RAM have been sufficient for our daily workflow. We frequently keep several browser tabs, a spreadsheet, email, and our scheduling software open at the same time. The 512GB SSD provides more than enough storage for this type of business use.The computer includes both Wi-Fi and an Ethernet port. We chose wired Ethernet because the reception desk already had a network connection, but having wireless connectivity available gives us more flexibility. It also has enough standard USB ports for our printer, barcode scanner, keyboard receiver, and other accessories.This model does not have an integrated camera or microphone, which is not an issue for reception use. It is not meant for demanding graphics work, but as an everyday office desktop, it has been dependable and space-efficient.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Good school computer that does not take over my desk
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I needed a desktop computer for school but did not have much room in my apartment. This all-in-one PC has worked well because the computer is built into the display, so there is no tower sitting under the desk. The included wireless keyboard and mouse also keep the setup fairly clean.I normally have a browser with multiple tabs open, a PDF textbook, Spotify, and Word or Excel running at the same time. The Ryzen 5 processor and 16GB RAM have handled that kind of multitasking without becoming frustrating. The 512GB SSD provides enough room for my assignments, downloads, and personal files, although Windows shows less than the full advertised capacity, which is normal.The Full HD screen is comfortable for writing papers and watching lectures. It is a 60Hz display, so I would not buy it specifically for competitive gaming, but it is completely fine for schoolwork, streaming, and casual use.My only real complaint is the lack of a built-in camera and microphone. I added an inexpensive USB webcam for online classes, and after that the setup worked well.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on August 16, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Solid home-office performance with useful display output
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I use this AOC desktop for email, spreadsheets, browser-based business tools, video playback, and general administrative work. The 16GB RAM makes a noticeable difference when I have several applications open, and the 512GB SSD keeps Windows and everyday programs feeling responsive.The 23.8-inch display is a comfortable size for a home office. I also connected a second monitor through HDMI, and Windows recognized it without any trouble. It is important to understand that the HDMI port is output only. You can connect this computer to another monitor, TV, or projector, but you cannot use the AOC screen as an external monitor for a laptop or game console.There is no built-in webcam or microphone, so I use a USB webcam with its own microphone for Teams and Zoom meetings. The built-in speakers are fine for hearing calls and watching training videos, although a headset provides better privacy.This is not a high-end workstation, but for normal office productivity it performs well and keeps the desk much cleaner than my previous tower computer.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on August 13, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Very good for everyday entertainment, but know its limits
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I wanted a computer that could handle normal work during the day and streaming or casual games in the evening. For that purpose, this AOC all-in-one has performed well. The Ryzen 5 processor and integrated Radeon Vega 8 graphics are capable of video streaming, browser games, older titles, and less-demanding games at reasonable settings.The 23.8-inch Full HD screen produces a clear picture for movies and YouTube. The built-in speakers are convenient for everyday viewing, although they do not replace a dedicated speaker system. Bluetooth support also makes it easy to connect my wireless headphones.This should not be confused with a gaming desktop. The display is 60Hz, and the integrated graphics are not designed for new AAA games, high settings, or heavy 3D workloads. Buyers expecting that level of performance should look for a system with dedicated graphics.For browsing, streaming, office tasks, and casual entertainment, however, the performance is balanced. The 16GB RAM is especially useful when switching between work applications and media without restarting the computer.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I’ve been using the KAIGERR gaming laptop for nearly a week now, and overall I’m quite satisfied with it. For AAA titles, it’s still playable if you’re willing to lower some graphics settings and effects. productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I actually purchased this all in one for my mother. She previously had an HP touchsmart all in one that the mother board just went out on. The Pictures show it correctly! The description does not!I have since gotten it all set up for my 87 year old mother. It was very easy to set up. Just a few more visits and I will have everything back on it and settled in for her like on her old computer. SHE LOVES IT! Loves the larger edge to edge screen and the feel of the new wireless keyboard (her previous wireless older HP keyboard was pretty clunky compared to new standards). Old dogs can learn new tricks!!!!  And lets hear if for my computer/technology savoy 87 year old mother!!! She is pretty handy with her iphone and texting too, by the way!Purchase it fast. It looks like the price is rising on it. It has gone up $16 since my purchase a week ago. No hesitation recommending this product.

Nach dem ich in mehreren Systemen die deutsche Sprache als Leitsprache eingegeben hatte, erhielt ich u.a. auch die Nachricht , dass ich das Gerät in italienischer Sprache bestellt habe. Das ist wohl ein Witz! Ansonsten bin ich mit Gerät zufrieden.

Acquistato da poco e sono  soddisfatto. Versione 21.5" con 8 GB di RAM processore ATHLON 3050u con scheda video integrata e HARD DISK SSD da "soli" 256 GB. In teoria non è una configurazione fra le più potenti. Anzi è un entry level!Si installa velocemente mediante CORTANA per Windows, e presenta poche utili applicazioni di default.Antivirus preinstallato ecc. quindi niente perdite di tempo inutili nelle configurazioni iniziali.Molto silenzioso anche quando messo sotto stress. Sufficienti porte USB, lettore DVD, prese per cuffie, schede di memoria, presa HDMI. Ha tutto il necessario in pochissimo spazio.Lo schermo risulta elegante e con buoni colori. Direi piuttosto grande se utilizzato davvero come PC quindi a distanza da tastiera. Un po' meno grande come TV da camera con le varie app.Utilizzo video impeccabile per una risoluzione FULL HD. Neflix e Disney plus girano benissimo.Discreta la videocamera integrata ma non eccezionale. Ottimo poterla oscurare con un comodo sportellino.Peccato per mouse e Tastiera USB e non wireless. Svolgono il loro lavoro senza infamia e senza lode ma aumentano il numero di cavi visibili ed è un peccato. Bastano 20/30 euro per rimediare e prendersi a parte tastiera e mouse senza fili.Giochi come Cycling Manager, Football Manager e i vari Total War girano senza particolari problemi, anzi veloci e quasi a dettagli massimi. Non ho provato con titoli più pesanti come FIFA 21 ma trattandosi di una scheda video integrata in quel caso potrebbe non cavarsela.L'SSD è velocissimo ma davvero poco capiente (SOLO 256 GB) quindi per archiviare molti documenti potrebbe essere utile acquistare un HD esterno con più spazio. Tuttavia nella pratica ho avuto diversi PC con HD da 500 GB, altri da 1000 GB e non li ho mai usati tutti.Entro certi limiti girano bene anche i programmi di fotoritocco e i Cad di disegno tecnico.Quanto al rendering dipende dal livello richiesto ma per lavori veloci rimane comunque su buoni livelli.In altre parole a meno che non si voglia GIOCARE con gli ultimissimi e migliori giochi in circolazione è un PC che consiglio a tutti.Il punto è che reputo il rapporto qualità/prezzo davvero eccellente visto che per avere prestazioni leggermente migliori bisogna spendere quasi il doppio.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The beast!!!  Expensive for sure, but worth every penny. Get it while you can.  Originally ordered on the 2nd of May from another seller on Amazon, but that order was cancelled because the item was OOS/unavailable.  I had to wait about a week to find another one on line on Amazon and ordered it, Overnight Shipping through FEDEX because that option was available.  Long story short, the item did not come the next day as expected - BUT - the seller got the item to FEDEX late the next day.  Because it was a weekend and FEDEX was involved, I did not get the item until Monday.  I was in touch with the seller, and they refunded the full Overnight Shipping fee to me no questions asked.  Great Stuff - thanks and a shout out to BEST WAY TECH.  Anyways, the outer shipping box was bruised/slightly crushed, so I took pictures before signing for the item.  When I opened the outer shipping box there was no apparent damage to the CPU box, but I noticed that it looked like the outer seal had been broken (or carefully peeled back and resealed), took pictures of that also.  Upon opening the box to unpack the computer the first thing that was apparent was that the CPU was in the plastic bag, BUT - the cloth LENOVO bag was not on it, nor was it anywhere in the box.  Bummer, coz I would have used it to wrap up the CPU when I took it out and about.  Anyway, plugged it in for a bit and then fired it up.  Gorgeous screen, vibrant colors, awesome.  Ran dxdiag and device manager to see what internals it was going to show me.  Speccy and HWINFO too.  But because it did not come in the cloth bag I wanted to make sure, so I opened it up (I already had Samung 9100 2TB and Samsung 900 pro 4TB on hand).  Two 1TB NVMEs inside (both PCIe 4.0) and 64 GB DDR5-6400MHz (CSODIMM) - (2 x 32 GB).  Everything seemed to be and is currently working just great.  Fast......really fast.  My only downer is the missing cloth bag......maybe I can reach out to the seller to see if they will provide one.  But either way this is a great unit.  Prices are fluctuating so you might get a better deal so good luck to you if you are looking for one of these.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on May 21, 2025

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This laptop is the best gaming laptop of 2025 in my opinion. Mine is the RTX 5080 variant with 64GB RAM and 2TB SSD. This laptop has the best rtx 5080 mobile compared to other brands of the same  GPU, outperforming even some of the 5090 variants like razer. Maybe it has to do with the cooling design or even its high wattage I’m not sure, but it delivers for hours without throttling and good temperature. Every game I played gets 65-100fps without DLSS in ultra settings, some even higher (i do turn down raytrace to medium) Its OLED screen definitely makes a difference to the gaming experience as it literally brings the colors to life. My only complaint and I hope Lenovo sees this, is the trackpad. Because the build quality is premium with complete metal and the screen and keyboard are so perfect but the trackpad lacks in quality and feels out of place in this premium laptop. It also lacks windows hello and I understand Lenovo probably thought to exclude it to give a competitive pricing but the trackpad needs an upgrade. Otherwise everything else is great and I even love the look this year with their RGB but I hope they upgrade the trackpad and maybe include windows hello next year while leaving everything else as it is. Also another thing to keep in mind is that this product in this listing is being sold by a third party seller. Mine was opened by the seller’s Lenovo authorized technicians to upgrade my RAM and SSD. Initially I was pissed because I only found out after looking at the “carefully put back seal”,  but after a thorough inspection I confirmed there were no scratches or defects or out of the ordinary and it is still “new” as I also confirmed the date of the laptop’s purchase by the third party and its serial number on Lenovo’s website and everything seemed ok. In the end I decided to keep it because it was upgraded to double the RAM and SSD at the same base price as u would find it on the Lenovo website and that saved me probably another $500-$700 if I were to buy it from Lenovo. But seller should definitely mention they manually upgraded the devices in the description. However, they were honest and replied to all my messages in a timely manner. In the end it’s going to be about how comfortable you are with that and how much you are getting for the money you spent. It’s going to be a month soon and I am loving it so far.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: We regularly acquire mini PCs in our office to test out enterprise network software in a controlled environment.  This BMAX MaxMini B2 mini PC seems just right for my next project, and after using it a couple of days, I'm impressed.(See my video for setup and initial use)The packaging looks nice with a gaming theme although I wouldn’t recommend this PC for gaming.  Inside the box is the mini PC, HDMI cable, VESA mount adapter, and power supply.  The device is very light yet looks very premium.  I love how glossy the top cover is of this mini PC, it looks very nice, but is horribly a fingerprint magnet.  The device has enough air vents to cool down this little beast.  I like that the amount of IO ports on this computer is just enough as a casual productivity device as well as an entertainment device.  Initial setup was very quick and easy, I was able to get it running in just a few minutes.  Once logged in, Windows will perform major updates, and that will take a little while to finish.  I suggest to just let it run for a couple of hours so as not to interrupt whatever you need to do.  Once the updates were finished, I was able to load productivity and office apps very easily.  This device was also able to play 4K videos without any issues.  Great for media consumption.  The quad core CPU is very capable of handling multi-tasking office apps and I was able to load at least 4 apps without any performance issues.  The 8GB memory is the sweet spot for office computers these days, anything lower than that can be an issue with multi-tasking.  I also opened up the device and for this model there are 2x M.2 slots, one of the slots (in use) is M.2 SSD, and the extra one is M.2 NVME.  The NVME slot is great if you need a faster SSD later on.  I also noticed that this model has 2.5 SATA bracket on the cover to install a 2.5 drive, but I could not find any SATA port nor did this include any SATA cable for expansion, but that’s fine for me as I don’t plan on using a 2.5 inch drive.I intend to use this device with Linux in our labs, and installing Linux on this computer is a breeze.  All the hardware were detected (using Linux Mint) and functioning properly (including Bluetooth and WiFi).  In a Linux environment, everything in this computer feels faster and snappy compared to Windows.  Linux also has a better memory management and I was able to load more apps at the same time without encountering any issues.  In all my testing the temperatures in this computer is just averaging at around 60 degrees Celsius, that is pretty cool in current standards considering how small this device is.So far, I am very impressed with the performance of this little beast.  I intend to use this as a headless console for software development, and the performance far exceed for what I need.  If you are looking for an office computer with a very small footprint, this mini PC is an excellent option.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Fast international shipping and works just as expected!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Was able to screw it onto the back of a 32" TV which i use as primary screen, and have added a second screen to the side for the Zoom (I teach from home).  I have tried the option to add a third screen and that worked great.  It does get warmer that i thought, though it hasnt gotten terribly hot yet.  The 12Gb RAM makes handling documents a breeze ( I use 100+ page Powerpoint files which stress most systems, not this one), and with the addition of a windows camera this is perfect for teachign from home.I am not an avid gamer so the few strategies games I play work just perfectly.  probably wouldnt run latest/greatest games as the Arc Iris graphics processing unit is not on par with the typical gamer video card, but it is good enough to play Skyrim.It arrived (really fast shipping to Costa Rica!) with windows 11 pre-installed, and ready to go.  I turned it on, added details to creat emy account, and installed my own version of MS Office 365, Zoom and Chrome etc, and was ready to go in about 30-40 minutes.The best thing about this is its size, and the punch it packs for the size.  I have 2 portable LCDs screen (15" and 11"), and when travelling I take the 2 screens, this computer and a wireless keyboard mouse combo, which work as well as and takes a little less space that my 15" laptop!  I woudfl highly recommend such a small computer to anyone sitting on the fence, and this particular one (the BMAX B6) seems to be the best buy, and a greta sweet-spot above the cheesy-low powered ones and below the pricey ones. productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This is the fourth Mini PC in a row I have purchased. I returned the first the first three (2 Beelinks and a Guzila).The problem with the ones I returned was that all of them claimed to handle 4K video and NONE of them did.  A couple would reach 720p once in a while and the other usually only ran well at 480P.This one is better.  It "almost" handles 4k but freezes every 3-10 seconds for a moment...however, it seems OK at 1080 HD...so I give up.  I am going to keep it. The problem is not my Internet connection or wi-fi... I am using hard-wired RJ45 Ethernet with and extremely fast Internet connection.  My laptop flawlessly handles 4K on two 32" monitors simultaneously like a champ on the same connection.I don't know what it is...do I keep getting lemons?  The customer reviews on all four of these largely make no mention of 4K problems.With all that said (and putting the 4K issues aside) I really love this BMAX.  It is otherwise quick and powerful and juggles dozens of web pages at the same time with ease so I am keeping it.  It has great I/O ports intelligently located...AND....  I just don't have the energy (or money) to return and upgrade one more time. (I have already spent twice what my first Beelink cost.)It's a good purchase, but if you are adamant about streaming 4K...I hope you have better luck than I did.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I already have a fairly beefy desktop along with a laptop that have Linux Mint installed. They are what I use on a daily basis. FWIW, I've been running Linux for years and it does everything I need.But, I found that I needed a MS Windows computer for some specific business purposes.Since this wasn't going to be my primary machine, I thought I'd try one of the Minis. The major criteria I had were size, capability and cost.I think that I chose well. It has enough power to do what I need it to do. I have it paired with two 15.6" portable monitors which it has no problem feeding. This setup is small enough that I can put it away easily when not needed. This is NOT a gaming rig.Two things that really impressed me about BMAX relate to how they configured the machine for first run and setup:1. They default to setting up Windows 11 with a Local Account rather than MS' wishes to have you create an online account. This is BMAX's choice as an OEM. I personally do NOT want a MS account. I just want to use MY computer.2. There was NO crapware installed. Configuring MS Windows is already a complete PITA. The fact that BMAX saved me the trouble of removing unwanted things makes me very happy.I can easily see myself recommending in the future some of BMAX's other offerings to friends in the future who need a decent computer at a good price. This one hits all the marks for me.It's just a shame that I have to keep Windows installed on it.  ;)It has earned Five Stars.

Die Anschaffung erfolgt primär für den Einsatz im Homeoffice und zur Wiedergabe von Multimedia/Streaming z. B. über Beamer oder TV im Urlaub.Seit einigen Jahren habe ich einen Mini-PC im Einsatz, damals geringfügig günstiger als dieses Exemplar. Die Leistung war noch grenzwertig bei Multitasking waren schnell die Leistungsgrenzen erreicht, auch die Wiedergabe von 4K als Homeoffice-Client war grenzwertig.Die "neuere" Generation versprach höhere Leistung insbesondere bei Multimediawiedergabe und 4K-Auflösung.Es wäre sicher noch günstiger gegangen, dieses Gerät versprach allerdings 8 / 128 GB Speicher und einen etwas kräftigeren Prozessor. Nach etlichen Vergleichstests im Netz habe ich mich dann für dieses Gerät entschieden.Das Unboxing war schnell erledigt. Dem Gerät selbst waren das Netzteil sowie ein HDMI-Kabel beigefügt. Weiteres Zubehör gab es nicht, war auch nicht nötig.Nach Anschluss des Mini-PC per HDMI an den Fernseher/Monitor begann die Einrichtung des Vorinstallierten Windows 10. Diese war, wie gehabt, selbsterklärend. Zeitlich hielt sich alles im Rahmen, da das System bereits vorinstalliert ist. Dennoch braucht die Einrichtung noch seine Zeit, wie bei Microsoft üblich. Für einen Mini-PC dieser Preisklasse aber absolut in Ordnung. Mehr Zeit brauchten dabei die nach der Installation nötige Updates.Performancetechnisch gibt es nichts zu beklagen. Ich bin kein guter "Benchmarker", ich schwöre eher auf die praktische Anwendung. Natürlich ist das System noch "blank" und bis auf wenige Apps wie z. B. VLC zur Medienwiedergabe, Citrix für die Verbindung zum Firmenserver und einen Virenscanner habe ich noch nicht viel installiert. Dennoch kommt der "Kleine" gut mit der Medienwiedergabe in 4K aus dem Heimnetz (NAS) klar. Daneben ist auch noch Multitasking möglich, dank Grafikprozessor und Speicherreserve.Alles in Allem bekommt man eine gute Leistung für einen guten Preis. Wirkliches Gaming oder prozessorlastige Anwendungen sollte man nicht erwarten, Cloud-Gaming habe ich noch nicht getestet. Dafür ist dieses Gerät aber auch nicht gebaut. Hierfür müsste man deutlich tiefer in die Tasche greifen.Für Homeoffice, Medienwiedergabe auch in hoher Auflösung und anständiges Arbeiten aber ist das Gerät absolut Mittel der Wahl.Und wer noch nicht genug hat darf sich freuen: die Hardware scheint Windows 11-geeignet.Nach den Updates wurde die Möglichkeit des Upgrades zwar nicht angeboten, allerdings zeigte die Integritätsprüfung "grünes Licht" und über Microsoft lief die von dort aus angestoßene Installation (webbasiert) auch problemlos an.  Es dauerte zwar gefühlt eine halbe Ewigkeit bis zum "Ende" und auch da waren noch Updates empfohlen, nach einiger Zeit aber lief alles problemlos in "neuem Look". Bisher jedenfalls :-)Weitergehende "Tests" habe ich nicht vorgenommen (mehrere Monitore,...) da ich sie für meine Zwecke nicht benötige. Hier scheint es aber auch noch Reserven zu geben.Ach ja: die "Lüftung". Mein bisheriger Mini-PC hat die Hitze zwar gut weggesteckt, wurde aber zeitweilig doch recht warm und die Leistung ging in den "Keller". Für einen Bürorechner, der selten auf Volllast läuft ok, aber eben ohne "Reserven". Hier ist ein aktiver Lüfter verbaut, der bei Bedarf anspringt. Einerseits ist das aber bei üblichem Gebrauch selten der Fall (dann ist das Gerät nahezu geräuschlos unterwegs) und der Lüfter selbst verursacht auch keine übermäßige Geräuschemission. Das ist absolut zu verkraften. Wer es aber gern absolut still mag sollte damit rechnen ;-)Fazit: ein preis-leistungsmäßig kaum zu übertreffender Mini-PC der für die üblichen Büroanwendungen ebenso ausreichen sollte wie für eine "einfache" Medienwiedergabe in hoher Auflösung, durch Win11-Kompatiblität auch noch mit "Zukunft". Kompakt und gut für den Schreibtisch.Ich habe bisher nichts zu meckern!
Très bien en cour de tests

Hallo, ich habe das Gerät nun schon seit zwei Jahren im Dauerbetrieb als Homeserver. Obwohl es dafür ja nicht ausgelegt ist läuft es ohne jegliche Probleme. 8GB Ram und die verbaute CPU sind für das von mir Installierte Linux System absolut ausreichend. Wie es sich unter Windows verhält kann ich leider keine Angaben machen, benutze kein Windows. Der Stromverbrauch bei normal Last beträgt im Schnitt zwischen 8 und 10 Watt. (Unter Volllast ca 15 Watt) Ein recht guter Wert der die Stromrechnung nicht nach oben treibt. Der Geräuschpegel ist minimal und nur unter größere Last leicht wahrzunehmen. Andere Mini Pc's haben in der Regel meist ein Wärmeproblem was dann zu einen unerwünschten Runtertackten führt. Bei diesen Gerät habe ich bisher kein solches Problem festgestellt. Selbst bei Volllast bleib die Temperatur im Rahmen (max 80-85C). Wenn man in Betracht zieht das die Kühllösungen bei den Mini PC's immer eher ein Kompromiss sind, ist dieser Wert schon sehr gut. Im Normalbetrieb liegt der Wert bei ca. 45-50 Grad.Mein Fazit: Viel Gerät für wenig Preiß :). In dieser Preißklasse ein gutes Gerät bei den man nicht viel falschen machen kann.
