productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Excellent Mini PC for Living Room Bigscreen TV with the right keyboard/mousepad/browser and settings
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: We are thrilled with this little device!!! Especially for the price (169.00 w/ free shipping). Simple to set up and config. Everything was plug n play and mostly automatic.  It's awesome with plenty of power and umpf to do the simple things that we want/need.  It's placed at the 85 inch bigscreen in our main/living room at home.  We haven't had cable/satellight for many years.  We watch what we want on websites. With AV, browser settings and extensions we watch anything we want, w/o ANY commercials, popups or adds EVER (including p!r@ted movie sites).  We have it config'd to power on the TV and PC and log in automatically at a specific time daily, with same for shutdown each night.  It boots up fast and is ready to go in a minute or so.  No issues with the installed Win11 Pro.  It has no trouble with 6 or so different browser tabs open and running, notepad++, a screen capture tool, and remote VPN tool which is really all we do on it.  I have been super impressed with the audio but mostly the picture quality and the device responsiveness. The HD is soo crisp, clear and bright.  Everything looks amazing in movies.  Audio is just the 3.5 audio port to a decent desktop speaker/subwoofer system, and it sounds great. This is way better than the same setup we have had with a couple year old Dell SFF (this is faster and has noticably better video). With a mini BT keyboard/touchpad/remote, this is the perfect seemless set up for us.  Not gamers (lots of movies), but this makes for simple entertainment, or news, or movies, or shopping, or research, or paying bills, or social media, or remoting/VPN to work (IT System/Network Engineer), or whatever we want to do from the easy chair in the living room. Even at a much higher price point this mini PC would be a great value and is an excellent system for us. The local storage specs are fine, but irrelevent to me as it's all cloud now.  The other specs are fine too, but more importantly, we haven't encountered a single negative and everything just works and works very well.  Hopefully, we will see some longevity, but we'll see on that. We love it so far and highly recommend it.

description: Experience unparalleled gaming with the ROG Strix SCAR 18. Powered by the latest Intel Core Ultra 9 HX275HX processors and NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 Laptop GPU, it delivers stunning performance. The advanced ROG Intelligent Cooling system, with a vapor chamber, sandwiched heatsink, Tri-fan design, and Conductonaut Extreme liquid metal, ensures peak performance under intense workloads. Enjoy breathtaking visuals on the 2.5K ROG Nebula HDR Display with a 240Hz refresh rate and 100% DCI-P3 color accuracy, enhanced by a dual ACR anti-reflective coating. With tool-less access for easy upgrades and 3 months of PC Game Pass, this laptop is designed to elevate your game.
features: BEST-IN-CLASS PERFORMANCE – Achieve unrivaled performance with Windows 11 Pro an Intel Core Ultra 9 275HX processor, and an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 Laptop GPU at 175W TGP.
HIGH-PERFORMANCE MEMORY AND STORAGE – Multitask seamlessly with 32GB of DDR5-5600MHz memory and store all your game library on 2TB of PCIe Gen 4 SSD, with raw throughput up to 7,000MB/s.

TOP-TIER ROG NEBULA HDR DISPLAY – Experience breathtaking visuals for gaming, creating, and entertainment, with Mini LED technology, 2,000+ dimming zones, dual ACR layers, a 240Hz refresh rate, and 100% DCI-P3 color for vibrant, lifelike imagery.

STATE-OF-THE-ART ROG INTELLIGENT COOLING – ROG’s advanced thermals keep your system cool, quiet and comfortable. State of the art cooling equals best in class performance. Featuring an end-to-end vapor chamber, tri-fan technology and Conductonaut extreme liquid metal applied to the chipset delivers fast gameplay.

SHOW OFF YOUR STYLE – Express yourself with the customizable AniMe Vision, showcasing text, animations, or your own creations on the lid of your laptop. The full-surround RGB light bar creates a striking 360° glow, while Stealth Mode turns off all lighting for a sleek, professional look around the base.

UPGRADE WITH TOOL-FREE ACCESS - Forget about a screwdriver, and customize RAM, SSD, and fans by sliding a latch on the bottom half of the device. A removable frame protects other hardware and offers deeper access for advanced users.

MUX SWITCH WITH ADVANCED OPTIMUS – A MUX Switch boosts gaming performance by 5-10% by routing frames directly from the dGPU. Advanced Optimus improves battery life by automatically switching between the iGPU and dGPU depending on the task, without restarting.
3-MONTH PC GAME PASS INCLUDED – Enjoy a free 3-month pass and access over 100 high-quality games. With new games added regularly, there’s always something fresh to play.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: ASUS ROG Strix Scar 18 — Started Amazing, Fell Apart in Hours
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought the Scar 18 expecting a monster. And at first, that’s exactly what it looked like. The first couple hours were perfect — smooth performance, great FPS, VR running better than I’d ever seen, and flat‑screen games looking incredible. I genuinely thought I finally found the laptop that could handle everything I threw at it.Then, in a matter of hours, it all fell apart.It started with small glitches…A few screen tears here and there.A weird flicker.A gray flash that didn’t make sense.I brushed it off at first — new drivers, new hardware, maybe just early quirks.But it didn’t stop.It got worse.Then came the crashesGames started freezing.VR apps would lock up.Windows itself would hang or stutter.Everything that was smooth earlier suddenly felt unstable.I wasn’t tuning anymore — I was babysitting the system.The anti‑aliasing ghosting wasn’t normal ghosting — it was THREE DESKTOPSThis was the moment I realized something was seriously wrong.Moving the mouse or a window left a triple ghost image behind it — three faint copies of the desktop trailing across the screen. Not in a game. Not in VR.In Windows itself.It looked like the entire display pipeline was desyncing.And once that started, it never stopped.VR went from “almost perfect” to “unusable”Every fix made it worse.Every tweak broke something else.Performance dropped, stability tanked, and the whole VR experience collapsed.I wasn’t improving anything — I was fighting the laptop nonstop.Then the problems spread to flat‑screen gamesTomb Raider — a game that should run flawlessly on hardware this strong — suddenly had:ghostingtearingunstable frametimesrandom crashesweird motion artifactsIt felt like the system was falling apart piece by piece.The worst part? It happened FASTThis wasn’t a slow decline over weeks.It wasn’t a bad update months later.It happened within hours of owning it.One moment it was perfect.The next, it was a mess of tears, gray screens, crashes, ghosting, and instability that spread from VR into Windows and then into every game I tried.Final VerdictThe Scar 18 has insane specs, but the experience I had was exhausting. I expected a powerhouse. What I got was a system I had to babysit, troubleshoot, and fight constantly — only to end up getting nowhere.For the price, I expected stability.Instead, I got a laptop that fell apart faster than I could fix it.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on June 29, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This is a powerful laptop, no doubt.  I loved the way it made my games look for the first week or so.  But now I am in a rabbit hole, that I can't find my way out of, and the laptop that I spend SO MUCH money on, is useless to perform the only task I purchased it for.I am unable to game with this laptop, because it randomly crashes and black screens in the middle of online gaming.  Gaming is built around progression and statistics.  Losing all my long earned inventory, or causing my team to lose because I cannot see, or I crashed,  or ruining my stats multiple times a night is the anthesis of a gaming laptop.  Its an anti-gaming laptop.Before you purchase this laptop, or any Asus laptop, please do a simple google search "Asus laptop black screen"I have done so much, I have done driver installs, driver cleaning utilities, bios updates, armory crate (asus software) uninstall tool, clean reinstall, and on and on.  I have followed step by step guides, Asus forum solutions, AI solutions.  Sometimes I can game for an hour and a half straight, sometimes I boot up my computer, and start a game I crash in three minutes.  -this is not a thermal issue, I may play for 22 minutes and black screen reboot, and then I may play for 5 minutes black screen, reboot, then I may play for an hour and a half, black screen, reboot.  Same game, same resolutions, same settings, same night.  When I was considering a gaming laptop for my son, we went with an HP omen, he has had no problems.  He games more often than I do, and his PC seems more reliable.Don't know what to say, not trying to be hyper critical, but I am regretting my purchase.I am changing my reveiw.  It turns out windows 11 is the culprit.  A recent update fixed a couple week clash with nVidia software, and the laptop is functioning well.running some very hi resolutions for long periods of time.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Biggest RTX 5090 scam I've seen in years - pure lottery whether it even works
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I've been an ASUS fanboy for 7–8 years straight - ROG laptops, motherboards, GPUs, everything. Never once let me down in gaming or heavy programming workloads. That's why when the 2025 ROG Strix SCAR 18 with RTX 5090 dropped I didn't even hesitate - bought it the second it was available.Four days later I was already losing my mind.Black / gray screen crash in literally every demanding game after 5–40 seconds. I tried everything known to man:• Clean Windows 10 + Windows 11 (every build including latest insider)• Every NVIDIA driver branch from 551.xx to 572.xx (full DDU wipe in safe mode every single time)• BIOS rollback + latest BIOS flash• Every Armoury Crate power profile (Silent → Performance → Turbo → Manual)• iGPU disabled, hybrid mode off, pure dGPU only• Undervolts, overclocks, stock - nothing matteredThe ONLY thing that stopped the crashes was installing G-Helper and forcibly capping Core Clock at 1600–1650 MHz in Ultimate mode.After that - no more black screens… but the 5090 was running at roughly 40–55% of its real potential.For 3500–4500+ dollars I basically got a prettied-up 4080/4090-class laptop from two years ago.Turns out this is a massive widespread issue specifically with ASUS RTX 5090 implementations (especially the 175W–200W variants in SCAR 18 and SCAR 16).Huge threads on Reddit, ASUS ROG forums, Discord - tons of people in late 2025–early 2026 reporting exactly the same nightmare.In the end I gave up and returned it.My hardware-nerd friends (guys who daily bench and reverse-engineer this stuff) unanimously told me:"Right now just grab ASUS with 5080 or 5070 Ti - same real-world gaming performance, zero of these insane driver/BIOS lottery problems so far."The laptop itself is gorgeous - screen is insane, keyboard feels premium, speakers are surprisingly good, cooling looks monstrous on paper.But when you're paying flagship money for a silicon & firmware lottery where your 5090 might decide to work at half power or not work at all - that's straight-up unacceptable.Buy this thing only if you're ready to:Spend 2–4 weeks dancing with BIOS, drivers and third-party toolsBe mentally prepared for RMA/returnPray that by the time you read this ASUS finally released a proper fix (as of January 6, 2026 - they still haven't)Very sad to write this about ASUS.Hope this review saves at least a couple of people from throwing 4k+ into the trash and months of frustration.

Who is the BOSGAME E2 AIR designed for? 
BOSGAME E2 AIR is designed for home users, students, remote workers and small offices looking for a compact and affordable desktop computer for everyday tasks, online learning, web browsing, office work and media streaming. 
Can the E2 AIR handle Microsoft Office and daily work tasks? 
Yes. The AMD Ryzen 5 3501U processor and 8GB DDR4 memory provide smooth performance for Word, Excel, PowerPoint, email management, video meetings and multitasking during daily office work. 
Is the E2 AIR suitable for online classes and remote learning? 
Absolutely. The E2 AIR supports video conferencing platforms, online learning applications, web research and document editing, making it a practical desktop solution for students and remote learners. 
Can I browse the web while using multiple applications? 
Yes. The Ryzen 5 processor and SSD storage allow you to run multiple browser tabs, office applications and media content simultaneously with responsive performance. 
Is the E2 AIR good for family use? 
Yes. The E2 AIR is ideal for everyday household computing, including online shopping, bill payments, video streaming, homework, social media and casual productivity tasks. 
Does the E2 AIR support multiple monitors? 
Yes. The E2 AIR supports up to three displays through dual HDMI ports and USB-C video output, helping users expand their workspace for multitasking and productivity. 
Can the memory and storage be upgraded? 
Yes. The E2 AIR features dual DDR4 memory slots supporting up to 32GB RAM and allows SSD upgrades, providing flexibility as your storage and performance needs grow. 
Does the E2 AIR support 4K display output? 
Yes. The dual HDMI ports support 4K@60Hz output, delivering sharp image quality for office work, video playback and everyday entertainment. 
What wireless connectivity does the E2 AIR offer? 
The E2 AIR includes dual-band Wi-Fi 5 and Bluetooth 5.0 for reliable wireless networking and convenient connections to keyboards, mice, printers, speakers and other devices. 
Why choose the BOSGAME E2 AIR instead of an entry-level Intel mini PC? 
The AMD Ryzen 5 processor offers strong multitasking performance, integrated Radeon graphics and smooth everyday computing capabilities, making the E2 AIR an excellent choice for office work, home use, online learning and media entertainment.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought this to replace an aging (and venerable) NUC 7 to run my observatory which requires telescope control, dome rotation, basic/initial data stacking and plate solving. IYKYK. I required this to run on 12V. At least when I bought this, this was not specified to run on 12V on Amazon, though Bosgame's website indicates it runs on 12-20V. For my fellow astronomers out there, this is true.Background: I replaced the 512GB SSD with a 2TB SSD (Silicon Power 2TB NVMe M.2), upgraded to 32GB RAM (Timetec 32GB KIT(2x16GB) DDR4 2400MHz), and replaced the WiFi card with an Intel AX210. None of this was necessary, and this unit was still cheaper than any alternative I found with a processor at this performance level. The Wifi module upgrade was $26 and installed in 4 minutes. The RAM and SSD upgrades were easy for someone who can barely use a screwdriver and knows little about computers. Note: there is only one slot for the SSD. Opening this up showed decent quality control and an easy layout to work with.Power consumption: A stress test with N.I.N.A image capture, PHD2 guiding, Cartes du Ciel, Gemini mount control, ASCOM Hub (for dome control), and, just to make it interesting, SIRIL (astronomy image processing program) stacking 450 subexposures peaked at 37 watts before settling down to 25-26 watts with BIOS settings unchanged from factory settings ("Balanced performance"). Under "normal" conditions, meaning capturing images; controling the dome and mount and cameras; and PHD2 guiding running, this hummed along between 15-21 watts, so less than 2 amps. This is slightly less than my NUC7 with an i5-7260U processor, but this AMD 3550H processor has twice as many cores and threads. The speed improvement over my old processor was significant and immediately noticeable. This will also run laps around Intel N100-N300 processors while allowing for dual-channel RAM.WiFi - Astronomers will know why I automatically upgraded the WiFi module before even turning the computer on. For most users, the standard WiFi module will be more than good enough, but I'm running this 65 feet from my house. The computer is inside a fiberglass observatory. With the upgraded module, download speeds were around 240-260 Mbps in perfect conditions in the observatory with the computer away from the metal telescope pier and without an USB Wifi antenna. With the computer attached to a steel pier, the signal dropped (very expectedly) down to a respectable 35-70 Mbps download (enough for Windows Remote Desktop). As planned, I use this with a relatively cheap TP-Link USB wifi antenna away from the telescope pier. Wifi speeds in this configuration range between 150 to 220 Mbps download. The connection is quite stable and still plenty fast over Windows Remote Desktop. For comparison, inside my house, download speeds were over 600 Mbps, so the physics of walls and distance still apply. In my use so far, I have not had any latency issues controlling this from inside my home (with the computer outside in the observatory) using Windows Remote Desktop in a suburban neighborhood with quite a number of Wifi networks visibile (houses are close together). The connection does not drop.I ran a CrystalDiskMark Read/Write Test with the somewhat generic SSD I bought to replace this was a respectable ~2800MB/s write and a RNK4K speed of ~280MB/s. It is no speed demon, but this was both better than I expected and more than good enough for astronomy.In indoor and outdoor testing, I've only ever heard the fan turn on at initial startup. Even while "stress testing," I never heard the fan turn on during normal use. This thing was cool to the touch indoors and outdoors. I did check temps via HWmonitor a couple of times and never saw temperatures approach 50C. Heavy gamers might have a different experience here. It should be noted that astronomy programs intended to run telescopes and observatories do not tax processors and memory like modern games do, so gamers' mileage may vary. However, image stacking and processing programs can tax processors and memory a little and the fan never turned on and power consumption remained below 40 watts in my limited use.Cons:1. The plastic quality is somewhat to be desired. I'm nitpicking hard here as that same plastic allows for more effective WiFi range than my NUC had, which was a metal Faraday cage of otherwise beautiful build quality. I'd rate the build quality as good enough, particularly at this price.2. No SATA expansion slot: Hence the reason why I got a 2TB SSD. I knew this going in, and now you do. I will not take a star off of my rating for this because they do not advertise this as having the capability to add a second SSD/SATA drive.3. This is advertised as only being able to use 2400Mhz DDR4 memory, but the module inside the unit was 2666Mhz DDR4. I don't know whether this was faster memory operating at 2400Mhz or whether the motherboard/processor can handle faster memory, but I had bought new memory sticks for this computer before I knew I could potentially squeeze out a little more speed with 2666Mhz DDR4. It is difficult to call this a con because I don't know the actual limitations of the computer. For most users, this underpromise and overdelivery might be a good thing. If expecting to upgrade from 16GB RAM immediately, check with BOSGAME first to ensure it can only operate with 2400Mhz.Overall, in the two weeks I've had this, I've been happy with its performance for astronomy. It has significantly better performance than an ASIAir and uses marginally more power than otherwise lower-performing N97, N100-N305 Intel processors. 1-1.5A under normal loads is extremely reasonable either in the field or in an observatory. This thing is a steal thus far.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great Mini PC and would recommend to anyone that wants a small capable machine
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: System is pretty decent for the purpose purchased - looking for a small mini-PC that takes up very little space, inexpensive, and allows retro gaming w/ RetroArch/Duckstation via running a Linux.  I installed Bazzite OS on it in a decent amount of time (20 minutes), and all the hardware works as is - network, graphics, usb, etc.  No issues.  The Vega 8 graphics card is decent for what is needed here - not going to run AAA games on it via Steam, but can run a lot on lower settings.  It came w/ Windows 11 24H2, but I don't need that and opted to put the Bazzite on it.Pros:Runs Linux w/o issue (Bazzite anyway)Has 16 Gigs of RAM - plenty for retro gaming and for most things512 Gig SSD allows storing lots of retro games, and a few Steam gamesEasy to open the computer (4 screws) and can upgrade memory and/or SSDCame with cable to add a 2.5" SATA drive if desiredCame with VESA mount if you want to mount to back of monitor/TVDrives a 1920x1080 display easily via HDMI (has 2 ports, but not sure if I'd drive 2 with it)Cons:Plastic case and is very light - doesn't feel as quality as my others from Geekom or GMKTecRAM was a single stick in single channel (16 Gig) but other slot is empty so could upgrade - this just means that the system won't be the fastest; I would have preferred 2 8GB sticks for dual channelRecommendations:If you get this, I'd recommend changing RAM out for 2 8GB sticks or adding an additional 16GB stick if you need it - and maybe changing the NVME SSD out for a 1 or 2 TB version if you are going to install a lot.  Alternatively, spend $200-$300 more and get one that comes with 32 GB RAM and a 1+TB SSDUltimately it depends on your needs... if you want a machine to do basic apps like Office, browse the internet, etc, or play Retro games, this will work as it is.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: great budget computer, good retro gaming experience
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Great piece of hardware. I haven't run any games yet, but for general web surfing and checking e-mails, this thing is pretty fast for what I expected to do. Boot up time is pretty fast, and I got it on discount for $300, which is a great deal for my low expectations. Exceeds expectations. Lots of hard drive space for the price. I couldn't find any other models with a similar harddrive space at this price point, so that is a plus. I tried installing steam on it to turn it into a budget steam machine, and it worked. I tried a few demos from recent releases however, and came out with mixed results. Ascend to zero demo didn't really work out right with a lot of frame lag. Imperial ambitions on the other hand worked quite well since it didn't have many moving animations. I booted up doom 64 from my library, and that worked fine. I also tried low magic age from my library, and that worked pretty well. So gaming wize, the machine can handle up to an n64, but will probably struggle with more recent games with 3d. For a device that was not designed for gaming though, I think it's still great as a budget retro machine. Boot up is very fast, and it barely takes up space in my apartment. Great piece of hardware if you're on a budget.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: A bizarrely powerful, capable, workstation PC/NUC
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Dev:Excellent for GameDev. Runs Unity 3D scenes well enough to make games, but I wouldn't build the final executable with this. I would offload that to Unity services etc.It runs Godot / Redot nicely in a scene with lots of objects. Handles Rider nicely. Vivaldi and Discord on a second screen while sharing desktop, all worked nicely.3D ModelingI was able to cook up to 1 million poly (tris) in Blender and yes, it WILL run Cycles, but denoising will be slow, and cycles iterations will be slow. So, great for modeling, sculpting etc, not great for rendering. Maybe see if it supports an eGPU? Theoretically it does with the USB 4.0 / USB-C support.GamingIt runs 2 screens 4K@60hz nicely, but you'll get a lot more bang for your buck gaming if you're at 1080p. I was able to run Fortnite with 1080p @ 60hz solid with 60% 3D resolution and everything on low. Satisfactory with low-med settings ran nicely. Don't expect to be frying people on Fortnite and your Satisfactory builds shouldn't be super congested in one area. Break it up on the map for better perf. Other games like Frostpunk or IDUN will run, but you might encounter jumps/stuttering in some scenes / UI.Pros:-> It's amazingly quiet for how powerful it is.-> The ports, size, and overall capabilities are better than expected.-> It's a solid media center, workstation, technical bench, surveillance station etc.-> Throws some heat, but nothing crazy.-> Preloaded with Windows-> Boots fast, like bizarre fast.-> Impressive wifi speeds, seriously. This thing bucks. I have an ASUS ROG Ally X (2TB) and this NUC's wifi outpaces it.-> Comes with a convenient bracket for wall/desk/monitor mounting. You can stash this thing out of sight or just put it somewhere out of the way at your workstation.-> It's a solid piece. Does not feel cheap to handle, and care was taken with presentation and assembly.-> Comes with a 4K capable HDMI cable.Cons:<- It's not as capable for gaming as I'd like, but that may be a non-concern with an eGPU setup.<- I wish the specs were more clear, does it support more than 1 M.2/NVME? Does it have additional space for RAM modules? I'll have to open it up and see I suppose.<- It comes with the bloatware version of0 windows (may disregard your selections for prompts like skydrive etc).<- Bulky power supply and prongs can't be pivoted so you'll either need a short extension cable to make it fit on a congested surge protector.Honestly though, the cons seem trivial. This is a solid unit for anyone who needs a relatively inexpensive but oddly capable workstation, which is exactly what we needed.Cons aside, this unit deserves 5 stars.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: First off this is not a sponsored review, I bought this unit with my own money. For $500, it works surprisingly well. I bought mine configured as “161” and now it’s changed again. But my specs are confirmed from opening the unit, 7840HS, x1 stick of 16GB DDR5 5600MTs, 1TB Gen4 M.2 SSD. Right away, I made a bootable usb of SteamOS 3.8 on my Mac and plugged into this. I booted into bios and then booted up the usb and install was a breeze! SteamOS works amazing on this device! 16GB is enough for older games and lighter titles but I would try to get two sticks as this will unlock the full potential of the 780m by doubling the memory bandwidth with dual channel instead of single channel (using both ram slots). With 16GB RAM in single channel config, Fallout 4 low settings preset at 1080p will run around 30-40 fps, latest ratchet and clank game will run around 30-40 fps low settings at 1080p with FSR set to “balanced.” Would be nice to pay around $400 for something like this, but considering the current market, $500 isn’t that bad right now. If one were to part this out with an 8700g build in itx, I feel the price holds up well even for 2025 prices. I did buy a 32GB ram kit and will post results soon in this review.*update*Performance pretty much doubled going to dual channel. If you’re playing newer stuff like spider-man, Jedi survivor, Indiana Jones, you’ll want a 32GB ram kit (x16 sticks @5600mts). Otherwise, for older stuff, you could just stick to a 16GB kit (x8GB @5600mts) and sell the one stick that comes with it or buy another 16GB stick and have 32GB but I like to buy a kit all at once so timings match up. That’s a lot, but if you know, then you know :) all together I’m in for about $650 and I’m super pleased.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: Bought instead of a laptop with larger portable screen and I love it.
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: Needed to replace my notebook as I got yet another flakey Intel Core processor. I didn't really need portable so decided to go with this. Haven't had an AMD processor before and so far I'm loving it, no random weird issues and it has been rock solid stable and so much faster than I was expecting.My monitor can power this and connect video with a single usb-c all with a single cable. I decided to go this route as I needed a bigger screen rather than portability. Notebooks tend to only stick larger screens on their highest end system which I couldn't justify the price. I didn't plan on this being portable but this thing is so small and only uses 35w when I push it hard. I decided to get a portable 4K 18.5" 16:10 screen 500nits, which will fit in my 15.6" laptop bag along with this PC and a small battery pack so I'm portable enough to fit my needs.  Keep in mind I'm not gaming, but mostly writing or occasional 3d graphic rendering. Nice thing is if any one component dies, the entire thing is not a write-off. The portable screen and this unit were bought on a flash sale for less than 800CAD. I've had two lesser powered Lenovo notebook write-offs in 3 years each costing around $1600.

Worked fine for a couple weeks but it randomly started losing hdmi signal and never able to recover. only way to fix it is to restart the computer which is a pain to deal with when actively using the conouter. Do not buy, don't be fooled by the low price and decent specs. Avoid that brand.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: Great little PC and good value for money
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: Great little PC and good value for money. It has been nicely reconditioned with not even a scratch on it. We are an all Mac household, but every once in a while you run into a We are an all Mac household but every once in a while, you run into an application that only runs on a Windows PC and so this is a great low-cost solution. While it’s advertised as having Wi-Fi and Bluetooth connectivity, this is not equipped internally. Rather, two very cheaply made dongles are supplied that will use up two of the USB ports. The Wi-Fi dongle was so cheap that it ended up being unuseable and kept dropping my Wi-Fi. I had to buy a separate TP link Wi-Fi dongle on Amazon for around $25 instead. If you’re handy, you can buy the Intel WLAN card for around 30 bucks. Also on Amazon, assuming yours has the antenna already installed like mine. They don’t all come this way.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great transition laptop for a longtime Lenovo user
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought this for my wife. I personally use a MacBook M4 and love it, but she was so used to her work Lenovo that she wanted an easy transition rather than switching to a Mac. This IdeaPad delivered exactly that.It worked right out of the box, and the setup process genuinely impressed me. It's about 1000 times better than laptop setups used to be. Total time to get her style preferences configured and her settings restored from backup was around 20 minutes. It's not quite Apple simple, but honestly I can't complain given how smooth it was.The laptop itself is light and easy to carry around. The best part for me, though, is the keyboard. It feels perfect to type on, solid key travel and a comfortable layout.Between the fast setup, the portability, and that keyboard feel, this has been a great pick for her. Five stars, no hesitation.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I'd give this 4 1/2 stars if I could because for the most part, it does everything pretty well. The only cons are the lack of a USB-C port, the DDR4 RAM and spotty Bluetooth range. But these are minor details, given the price. The only other problem was an issue with the sound card (or software) that produced intermittent distortion when feeding speakers through the audio output jack. A restart would usually fix it and I reloaded the driver but it was still cropping up. However, this has not occurred for over a month now, so perhaps it has self-corrected through updates and such because it is no longer a factor.As for the PROS:  1. The tiny footprint makes it virtually invisible on the desktop. You can also mount it in back of the monitor. 2. It is absolutely silent. I have never heard the fan run. 3. It performs very well for all the tasks I do, which is to say, simultaneous streaming, internet browsing and other routine functions. I think it is capable of more demanding workloads, if necessary, with plenty of  RAM and storage. 4. It has ample ports for multiple screens and devices. 5. Windows 11 is preloaded and contrary to some reports I've read, installed cleanly with no bloatware.I replaced an aging, albeit powerful, laptop for this to get a bigger monitor and clear up desk space. After using it daily for a few months, aside from the early glitches, it's been great. Unless you require gaming or video editing power, this inexpensive mini makes a lot sense.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Very powerful little computer that is great as server, and is upgradable.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Very nice little package which installs Win11 Pro on first boot (need wired ethernet). I now have 2 of them providing Plex server for TVs and backup for other computers. Quiet and cool.It has 2 slots each for memory and m.2 SSD disk. I got the 16 gb + 1 TB configuration, then added a 2 TB SSD in the second slot. Now I have 3 TB total with 1 TB system disk and 2 TB data disk.One system had a single 16 gb memory card while the other had two 8 gb. I replaced an 8 gb card with 16 gb and now have 24 gb in each.It is a little tricky doing the upgrade. Remove feet, then with small phillips remove screws. You may have to slap a corner in your hand to get them out of the hole. Pull the back slightly from cover and use a card to run around the edge. Work to pull the insides from case. Do not jerk as there are a couple wire to the case. Add SSD and memory at top. The tricky part is the power button. Put cover on side with power down and place in case. Then slide computer in. Make sure it fits to edges and you can see all connectors, then re-screw.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Solid machine if you can get past battery life and sound quality.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I got this about a month ago for combination work and gaming. I run a dual-partition Windows/Linux and do most of my work on the Linux side (scientific code development and testing) and gaming/writing/editing on the Windows side.The laptop runs well, but not any faster than the last-gen hardware I'm used to; for high-performance, CPU-parallelized code, it's about the same as my old Gigabyte Aero from 2018. The graphics card, however, is solid, and the 4070 should hold up well even against the new 50XX series GPUs that have recently released, and the speedup over the 30XX series is cards is noticeable.The multiple, expandable SDU memory slots are convenient for partitioning, and it's hard to see needing more than 1-2 TB of storage on a personal machine, so this checks all the boxes for my needs.Battery life is mediocre. It drains pretty quicker than I'd like (4-6 hrs) when I'm developing/testing code on the Linux side if I'm not plugged in. The windows side is worse, but I'm mostly gaming there and there's more bloat, so that's expected. I've not tried the USB-C lightning charging, but I wouldn't expect that to change the battery's capacity in any meaningful way.My main complaint is in the sound quality, which is sub-par. If you're using headphones all of the time then it's no issue, but the sound quality from the speakers is really rough. The sound is tinny, quiet, and sometimes muffled.Last thing I'll say is that I like the size. 16" is a great middle-ground between the 15" models that I find too small to game on (and often miss some features, e.g., a Num pad), and the 17" models which can be a little large to tote around between work and home, or on travel. This thing has some heft, at ~10 lbs, but it fits well in a bag/briefcase/carry-on, and feels sturdy.Overall, I'd recommend it if you're thinking about getting it. It's not your best gaming machine, nor is it your best work setup, but I think it splits the difference pretty well as an all-rounder.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on February 17, 2025

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Very impressed with this Mini PC!Very impressed with this Mini PC!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: First off, it's small but it's very capable. I'm not a gamer, just use it for web browsing, emails, etc. run LibreOffice for my documents/spreadsheets/etc. and it handles everything I've thrown at it so far. I've had this PC for just over a week now and not had any issues with it. I set it up initially with the preinstalled Windows 11 Pro 24H2 then updated it, using Windows Update, to 25H2 and no other updates were available. Not one problem. Next, I downloaded the latest Windows 11 ISO from Microsoft, wiped the drive, and installed a fresh install of Windows 11 25H2, downloaded the latest AMD/motherboard drivers from Geekom, installed them. Ran the updates, and again not one issue.Next I installed Kubuntu (Linux) alongside Windows and dual boot. Again, no problems. My Wi-Fi, NVMe, secondary SSD, and AMD chipset/motherboard were all recognized "out of the box" when Kubuntu installed. It just worked!Impressions so far:1. For it's size it's amazing actually! it's fast, it looks really nice on my desk. It's so small I have it sitting on top of my external BD-R and the BD-R is huge compared to it.2. Noise level is minimal. Even when updating, installing apps, etc. the fan will speed up as the CPU temp increases but not so much that it is really even noticeable.3. It will be easy to upgrade if I ever decide to do that. It's upgradable to 64 GB of RAM but the 16 GB that came with it are more than enough for my use, but the memory sticks are easy to get to and easily replaced. I purchased the model with the 1 TB NVMe so there's plenty of "native" storage. I also had a Crucial 1TB SSD, so I took the bottom of the PC off and there is a neat little slot built onto the bottom plate just for that. I put that SSD in the PC, powered up and I use that drive to store my documents/data/etc. and not touch the main NVMe.4. Connectivity!!The front of the PC has the following ports:Two type A USB 3.2 Gen 2 port, one of which supplies power for charging if you need it.A mini jack for headphones/microphoneThe back of the PC has the following ports:Three USB 3.2 Gen 2 ports, one type A port and 2 type C ports. The two type C ports are also display ports.There is also one USB 2 type A port on the back for USB keyboards or other similar peripherals.There are two HDMI ports on the back to connect to a monitor or TV.There is one 2.5 G Ethernet portThe left side of the PC has an SD card reader.It also has Wi-Fi 6 and Bluetooth built in and from my testing they both work with no issues.Would I recommend this PC. ABSOLUTELY!

It was refreshing to power it on and get straight to work instead of spending the first hour uninstalling unnecessary software.The mini form factor is fantastic. Whether you're using it for everyday tasks or more demanding workloads, it handles everything with ease.The build quality is exactly what I've come to expect from Lenovo: solid, reliable, and well thought out. Every computer I own is a Lenovo, and after using this one, I have no intention of switching brands. They consistently deliver dependable, high-quality systems that simply work.If you're looking for a compact desktop that doesn't sacrifice performance, this is an easy recommendation. features: POWERFUL OFFICE & LIGHT GAMING MINI PC --- The GMKtec NucBox G10 features the AMD Ryzen 5 3500U (4C/8T, up to 3.7GHz) with Radeon Vega 8 Graphics up to 1200MHz. Built on Zen+ 12nm architecture, it delivers 35% faster performance than Intel N150/N100 series chips, making it ideal for light gaming, video playback, home office, and multitasking workstations.

HIGH-SPEED 16GB DUAL DDR4 + 512GB PCIe SSD --- Comes preinstalled with 16GB dual-channel DDR4 (2×8GB) and a 512GB M.2 PCIe 3.0 SSD for blazing-fast boot, load, and transfer speeds. Easily upgradeable up to 32GB RAM and 2×8TB SSDs with dual M.2 2280 PCIe 3.0 slots for unmatched storage flexibility.

SMOOTH TRIPLE 4K@60Hz DISPLAY OUTPUT --- Supports triple-display setup via HDMI 2.1 TMDS, DisplayPort 1.4, and USB-C. The Radeon Vega 8 GPU handles 4K@60Hz video editing, office visuals, and casual design tasks smoothly. Ideal for financial trading, productivity dashboards, and multi-window workflows.

2.5GbE ULTRA-FAST NETWORKING + SERVER READY --- Equipped with a 2.5GbE RJ45 LAN port, the G10 offers up to 2500Mbps stable wired internet speed. Perfect for office work, media server setups, Pfsense, Untangle routers, or secure network appliances. No more bottlenecks in data-intensive environments.

COMPACT SIZE, FULL I/O, NEXT-GEN WIRELESS --- Palm-sized mini desktop comes packed with dual USB 3.2 Gen1, USB 2.0, USB-C (Full-Function: PD/DP/Data), DisplayPort, HDMI, and 3.5mm audio jack. Stay connected with WiFi 5 + Bluetooth 5.2. Great for office desks, minimalist setups, or VESA mounting.

RELIABLE SUPPORT & 1-YEAR WARRANTY INCLUDED --- GMKtec provides a full 1-year warranty from purchase date, covering all hardware faults due to workmanship. Our professional after-sales team is always ready to assist you, ensuring peace of mind and long-term support with every Mini PC.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: A lot of hype from the mini communityA lot of hype from the mini community
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: ***************UPDATE*************** 06/22/2025Upgraded memory to 96GB DDR5 Corsair Vengeance 5600Upgraded GPU to RTX 4070 OC (ASUS)Add-On Crucial Gen5 1TB m.2Including a new videoGreat Gaming PC! I have put this through a lot and I am impressed. Longevity is proving it's going to be around for a while.***************UPDATE*************** 12/2/2024Installed a MINISFORUM DEG1 External GPU Dock. This along with a RX 7700 XT from ASUS woke this machine up! I am talking Twin Turbo with a Hybrid Super Charger! My Games came to life @2K Resolutions on COD BO6. I get 112-120fps using this computer and the eGPU with GPU. I am now moving this from a 3 Star to a 5 Star review. Once I hooked up this eGPU and GPU my memory timings are faster. The whole machine is very impressive. Yes, it is a lot of money to spend, but, you get all the fun without the clutter.If you buy this PC, you need to buy the MINISFORUM DEG1 External GPU Dock with it and you can get it here on Amazon!Pros:1. It is small and will not take up a lot of room2. ECO friendly if you care about that3. Low power consumption which was nice on my off grid battery powered system. Max usage was around 45 watts when not in performance mode.4. 32GB DDR5 with 16 threads is nice to have in a little build like this.5. Expandable m.2 storage slot (I added an additional Gen4 7,100 m.2)6. Looks nice7. Expandable GPU Oculink slot8. Plenty of I/O for a mini unit9. Quick customer support response10. Plays Halo Infinite Great! 100+ FPS at medium settings 1080p11. Supports 3 monitors at 4K12. Included bracked went on the back of my monitor easily.Cons:1. Price point. You can build a system with the same specs for the same price using the AMD 8700G Processor.2. Does not support XMP Profiles, 99% of all memory modules have this support.Nov 21, 2024 12:27 AMHi Christopher,--Thanks for reaching out to us,All GMKtec Mini PCs doesn't support XMP;--Please let me know if you need further assistance, thank you.--Kind regards,TerrySales & Customer Support Manager3. This is advertised as a Gaming PC. I have ran several titles on this machine. Call of Duty Warzone BO6 & Fortnite (Low-Medium Settings averaged 30-45fps @720p & 1080p)4. After 15min of long use, I witnessed screen tearing in 4K watching YouTube videos5. Within 5min of launching into Fortnite or COD, I noticed tearing in game and terrible video lag. Mostly in COD. The COD issue could be with COD and not this PC as the COD Code has many complaints for Console and PC's on Reddit.6. UEFI not supported. Uses old BIOS GUI7. Cooling fan is sub par (Needs a way to update it with a Noctua Fan & or LED Lights)8. Included bracket could be built a little more friendly as to not remove the rubber footing from the case when installing on the back of a monitor or a 3rd party mount.There are more pros than cons. If you are in the market or have some cash to burn, this could be a fun little toy for most. I did purchase the eGPU Oculink Dock for this model. I will update with those specs and data when it gets here the first of December. Overall I think in 2024 we could have done a little better. I understand it is hard to balance TDP while expecting fast CPU & APU power. This can cause a system to get very hot.I'll update more in the next 2 weeks.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: The BMKtec NucBox K8 plus is tiny but solid, it is quite, cool running, and is a true speed demon!The BMKtec NucBox K8 plus is tiny but solid, it is quite, cool running, and is a true speed demon!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought a GMtec NucBox k-8 in July 2024 to replace my DELL Inspiron 17-7000 2n1 Intel i7-8565U / 16GBRAM Win 11, and I chose the k8 32gb+2TB configuration because my Dell was getting sluggish and unreliable. I found an ad for the NucBox Mini PC and decided to take a chance with GMKtec; this was the best tech decision I ever made.I am so pleased with GMKtec that I bought 'another' NEW k8 plus in Nov. 2024 (for my wife).When ordering, I discovered that GMKtech has improved the k8 plus, so I was excited.  I'm very glad I bought another Nucbox k8 plus (32gb with 2tb ssd) because this improved k8 model is even better!  It runs cooler, and is quieter than the prior generation and now includes Oculink! And they added another power option (the redesign has 4 power options and even the top watts is quite with the improved fans & cooling.This new K8 plus is so smooth, quite & cool that I can ramp up the processor (via BIOS) for extreme speed; giving me even more speed control.  I am 100% satisfied with GMKtec; they make great products.I was, and I remain happy with my older k8 build, but I'm 'especially happy' with the new improved Nucbox k8.My primary usage is business research and communications, so I keep excessive #'s of open tabs in BRAVE, usually 30 to 40 tabs, along with multiple programs running. With the improved k8 I can use High Performance in BIOS.The lower performance k8 settings also run VERY FAST, with no lag, with all my apps & tabs, running videos, and live stream TV without any problem, and I can set it on high, extreme performance with no issues.I love the generous connectivity options of the k8.Bottom line is: this is an excellent computer, very competitively priced, and the bonus of a micro-box, so my desktop is a cleaner, and I can even use the included VERSA mount for placing the k8 onto the back of my monitor!If someone wants to run multiple monitors, the new K8 box is your ticket. Personally, I don't need multiple monitors, I use a 34 inch HD curved Dell desktop monitor & I'm very happy.FYI, I use Logitech Wireless Ergo m575 Rollerball with Logitech MX wireless keyboard, both running from a single USB, fortunately the K8 box provides generous connectivity.I am no longer dependent on Dell where customer service & support has diminished dramatically. The Dell new product line is unimpressive, especially after using the GMKtec K8. GMKtec has replaced Dell as my new, reliable PC vendor!I wish GMKtec would offer a K-8 option preloaded with 96GB Ram (the Max), this is the only improvement can suggest because everything else is perfect! And, yes, I know, no one 'really' needs 96GM RAM, but I 'want' 96, and would gladly pay more to get it shipped with 96 already installed. But know this 32gm is more than most people will ever need, I'm just a Tech nut and tend to go overboard.  Best of all, the pricing by GMKtec is VERY competitive (you get much more for your money here).

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Solid little mini PC with great upgrade options, but the factory SSD is disappointing
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought the GMKtec M8 (Ryzen 5 PRO 6650H version) for everyday use, light productivity, and as a compact home server setup. Overall I’m happy with it — it runs quietly for normal tasks, stays cool enough, and the dual 2.5GbE LAN ports plus OCuLink make it more versatile than most other mini PCs in this price range.The best part is how easy it is to work on. No tools needed to open the case, and everything is straightforward to access. Upgrading the NVMe SSD or swapping the WiFi card takes just a minute. Even better, it has two full M.2 2280 slots plus OCuLink. On most mini PCs, adding OCuLink means you lose the second NVMe slot, but the GMKtec M8 lets you have it all — no sacrifices. That’s a big win for future-proofing.My only real complaint is the storage that comes installed. The factory NVMe drive is only hitting just over 2,000 MB/s on both reads and writes. When I checked, it turned out to be a Gen3 drive even though the slots support Gen4 speeds up to 7,400 MB/s. It works fine for daily tasks, but it’s slower than expected for a “fast” mini PC in 2026. I’ll be swapping it out for a proper Gen4 SSD soon.Everything else performs as advertised for the price. Good value if you plan to upgrade the storage yourself. Would recommend with the note that you’ll probably want to replace the included SSD for best results. Also, it came with Windows 11 Pro 24H2, no malware, no bloatware and upgraded to 25H2 automatically through Windows Update online.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on April 18, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Perfect little powerhouse for video editing and work on the goPerfect little powerhouse for video editing and work on the go
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I’ve been using this little PC for a while now, and honestly, it blew me away. It’s super fast, totally silent, and feels rock solid even when I’m editing videos or running several apps at the same time. Everything just works smoothly — no delays, no heating, no noise.I use it with a 14-inch portable monitor, a wireless keyboard and mouse, and the whole setup fits perfectly in my backpack. It’s amazing to carry my full workspace anywhere — plug it in, and I’m ready to work in seconds.The USB-C port was a big reason I upgraded from my previous GMKtec model, and I love how versatile it is for connecting displays and accessories. The triple 4K output is great too — perfect for editing or reviewing projects across multiple screens.It boots up almost instantly, transfers files incredibly fast, and stays cool no matter how long I work. For such a tiny machine, it packs serious power.If you’re looking for a compact, quiet, and powerful mini PC for creative work or just everyday use, this one is perfect. It really feels like having a desktop powerhouse that fits in your hand.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Expectations in Performance! My first reaction upon receiving the GMKtec NucBox G10 was—how could it be so small! It fits in the palm of your hand, takes up absolutely no desk space, and is incredibly easy to move and carry. Despite its compact design, the performance truly amazed me.The high-performance processor runs incredibly smoothly, effortlessly handling daily office work, multitasking, and even 4K video playback, without any lag. Even more impressive is its cooling system, which maintains stable temperatures even during long hours of operation, and the noise level is virtually imperceptible—the fan is barely audible.It's also fully equipped with a comprehensive selection of ports, including USB, HDMI, and Type-C, allowing for easy connection to an external monitor, keyboard, and hard drive. Its low power consumption and quiet operation make it ideal for a bedroom or a quiet office environment. Its system compatibility is excellent, with Windows 11 running right out of the box, and Linux support is also seamless.Overall, this mini PC combines a compact design with powerful performance and high expandability, making it ideal for space-conscious users who don't want to compromise on performance. I would not hesitate to recommend it to a friend!

AMD Ryzen 5 3500U VS Intel Twin Lake N150 Processor Testing

Can the BOSGAME E2 Neo handle gaming? 
Equipped with the Ryzen 5 3500U CPU & Radeon RX Vega8 Graphics, capable of handling light gaming and casual titles. While it may not be suitable for demanding AAA games at high settings, it performs well for older or less graphically intensive games. 
What should I do if the machine cannot start after the system update? 
If the computer cannot start after the system update, please visit the technical support page of the BOSGAME brand official website, download the driver file of the mini computer E2 Neo model, and reinstall the drivers. 
Is the RAM and storage upgradable? 
Yes, the BOSGAME E2 Neo is designed with expandability in mind. The 16GB of DDR4 RAM can be upgraded to a maximum of 32GB, and the 512GB NVMe SSD can be replaced with an SSD of up to 2TB for additional storage. 
Does the USB-C port support video output? 
Yes, the BOSGAME E2 Neo’s USB-C port supports video output at 1080P@60Hz. In addition, you can use the two HDMI ports on the device to connect monitors at 4k@60Hz. 
Can I mount the BOSGAME E2 Neo to the back of a monitor? 
Sue，the BOSGAME E2 Neo includes VESA mount support, so it can be directly mounted to the back of a monitor. However, except for its compact size makes it easy to place on a desk or in other small spaces.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Absolute Mini PC Perfection!!!Absolute Mini PC Perfection!!!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I really love this mini pc and it was a breeze to set up. It’s small and takes up very little space and seems very well built. I was able to get it going and everything I do runs flawlessly and fast including many of my higher end games. It comes with Windows 11 pre-installed, no issues there. It also makes next to no noise, the fan is super quiet. Also, after a few hours gaming I checked it and it was still cool to the touch. So if you’re looking for a powerhouse for a mini of, the Bosgame P3 Plus Mini is 1000% the way to go. Super affordable also!! The $1000+ PC’s at Best Buy doesn’t even come close. You would need almost $1200-$1800 for a comparable set up from the store. So please do yourself a favor and grab one of these while you can! You’re welcome!!!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: If you already have a good HD TV or a HD monitor , Mini-PC is a great choice!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This system as little and light as is, it really packs a lot of Windows 11 PC capable of doing pretty much what ever you want it to do.  It comes with the semi-current AMD Ryzen 7 CPU (current one cost a little more) , 32GB of DDR4 RAM (Expandable to 64GB), 1TB of m.2 NVMe SSD with a 2nd open slot for a secondary drive, and a 3GB of (Shared) AMD Radeon Graphics Memory, what more can you ask for at this price?  I bought this mini-pc to replace my travel/work 15in. laptop being used as a TV, connected to a big TV in my bedroom.  It has the same spec as my 15in. laptop, and it cost me $200 less.  I only had to connect a USB keyboard and a wireless mouse, connect it to my TV with the supplied HDMI cable, and it's all good to go!I already have a Microsoft account with back-ups from my other laptops, so the setup was very easy.  I only had to copy the settings and the apps installed from the laptop that was connected to my TV.  This TV laptop I was using, was upgraded to 64GB RAM, and with two 2TB SSD.  This was originally going to become my travel laptop for photography stuff, so this BOSGAME P4 Plus served its purpose to replace it.To use this Mini-PC with 32GB RAM, 1TB SSD for a TV-Media Center, it's got more than enough to do whatever.  Works like 20 times faster than my old Windows 10 (Win11 unupgradable AMD A10, 24GB Max RAM, sloooooow PC) that I gave a serious Karate chop to.  Damn!  That felt so good!!  I should have taken a photo of the aftermath, and sent the photo to Microsoft to let them know how I feel about them.  May be I should do that with the Windowsphone 10 I still have in my "Junk Box".☝🏻😂My main PC has a AMD Ryzen 9 from 3 years ago, and it's an ASUS gaming laptop.  Has 64GB RAM, and has great graphics with the Nvidia card with its dedicated memory.  However, doing a task like editing photos, I really can't notice the difference in processing speed with the current and semi-current Ryzen 7 with the same amount of RAM.  The only difference I notice is when I'm editing a large file size video, where the AMD Ryzen 9 and Radeon working with the Nvidia GeForce graphics card really out preforms my other machines with the Ryzen 7 with the shared memory Radeon card.So, if photo or video editing isn't the game, this Mini-PC will probably serve it's purpose, with lots of useable ports where you can connect a lot of things an make a wired mess.From about 15 years ago, I've been saying "a huge desktop and tower computers are a thing of the past".  They run hot, consume a lot of wattage, take up space, and heavy.  Right about the time Intel Core i5 came out, hi-spec laptops began to come down in price.  Then, ASUS, Dell (Alienware), and Samsung just went nuts coming out with a high priced big "Gaming Laptops" (still weighed about 10Lbs) just overwhelming the desktops.  Yeah, I had one from ASUS, but is was a replacement for an outdated tower PC I just got tired of upgrading.This is my very first purchase of a "Mini-PC", and I am just overwhelmingly impressed with this "BOSGAME".  I have it on for 10 hours now, running updates, installing additional apps; etc., and it runs quiet, and much cooler (like room temperature) opposed to my "TV purpose laptop" does.Size is 5" x 5" Square, and only 1 - 3/4" in height.  When I travel I need my laptop. I also, take my own movies and dramas to watch and stream with it.  Now, I can just take this little bugger, along with a mouse and a mini keyboard, and just plug it in to the hotel's TV.  I can now use my laptop as my laptop. 😂👍🏻

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Snappy, small, silent, so far very impressed
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I’m really impressed with this thing. I recently got a Mac Mini M4 and was smitten by the form factor, and my mother-in-law needed a new Windows PC. Enter this thing, which I decided to try based on the reviews despite never having heard of BOSGAME. It isn’t a gaming powerhouse or anything (and probably compares poorly to the Mac Mini for performance, which is hard to beat for its typical used sale price of ~$450), but is quite quick for typical Windows usage with size where it matters with 32GB of RAM and decent-sized SSD.  It’s tiny, seemingly silent, has a decent array of ports (more USB-C would be ideal, but not a huge deal), and I got everything set up and installed with zero issues - no crashes or anything like that.It should last her many years and would be a great buy for the money assuming it does. I checked out budget mini-mid tower PCs like the Dell Optiplex I was replacing and they all were more expensive/bigger/uglier.  Will update if things go south, but for now I’d highly recommend for this use case.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Unbelievable Power in a Tiny Package!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I needed a new "mini" computer for living room and I decided to take a chance on this E2 Mini PC, and I am absolutely blown away. This little machine is a powerhouse.Performance & Speed:Right out of the box, this PC is snappy and responsive. The combination of the Ryzen 5 3550H processor and 16GB of RAM handles everything I throw at it without a single stutter. I can have multiple browser tabs open, be on a video call, and run office software all at the same time, and it doesn't miss a beat. The 512GB NVMe SSD is incredibly fast—boot-up takes just a few seconds, and programs launch almost instantly. It's a huge upgrade from my old desktop.Setup & Features:The setup was as simple as plugging it in. What really sold me was the triple display support. I have a portable monitor connected through the USB-C port, and it works flawlessly. It has completely transformed my productivity. The Gigabit Ethernet port provides a stable, fast internet connection, which is essential for my work.Design:The compact size is the best part. It's so small that I have it mounted to the back of my portable monitor, leaving my end table completely clear. It's silent, sleek, and stays surprisingly cool even under load.Overall:This mini PC has exceeded every expectation. It's the perfect solution for anyone needing a powerful and reliable computer for office, business, or school work without sacrificing desk space. If you're looking for a compact desktop that delivers serious performance, look no further. Highly recommended
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on July 24, 2025

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Until recently I didn't realize mini-pcs were a thing. However, they make perfect sense!  In replacing my old Windows 10 desktop, I knew that I didn't want a laptop because I have two large monitors and don't travel with my personal computer. Desktops are still big and clunky with unexpectedly high costs.  The mini PC fits perfectly into the middle. It has the power and hardware specs of a desktop without the higher price tag.This particular one which I purchased has been flawless so far. Out of the box it goes through the Windows 11 setup process and matches the specs that I ordered. It is fast, quiet and everything I needed with an upgraded computer.  Importantly, it is also everything I did NOT need.  This does not ship with a keyboard or mouse, which is perfect because I did not want either.  My biggest concern purchasing was the video connections. All the mini pcs advertise the same 3 monitor connectivity, but in order to support that you need 3 different cables. My two monitors were both using display port (DP), and now I'm using one DP and one HDMI.  About half the time the HDMI connected monitor will work in the monitor's auto detect setting and switch seamlessly between this mini pc and my work laptop which is still using two DP.  The other half of the time I have to go into the monitor settings and switch the input to HDMI.  Thankfully, I only switch between computers about once per day, but if it becomes too annoying I will get an HDMI to DP adapter.One knock against the system is that I originally tried to put a SDD hard drive from my previous computer into this mini pc, but I could not remove the plastic fan component to get at the slot. The booklet indicates removal is possible and the slot exists, but I didn't want to break it so I stopped trying.  Instead I used Windows Disk Management to create a partition and manually copied the files I needed.If you're looking to upgrade and have the same type of setup as me, you won't be disappointed with this powerful little machine.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: Good VM Host or Office Mini PC
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: The primary factor in selecting this Mini PC was price having set a limited budget. I wanted Windows 11 Pro (not Home), a multi core CPU with minimum 32 GB ram and 1TB SSD storage. I did consider the cost of upgrading the ram / storage but in the end selected a model that I was unlikely to need to upgrade. I also limited my selection to manufacturers with drivers available online.The first thing that struck me about the H77 mini PC is how compact it is.The case is well ventilated with fans top and bottom. Access to the user upgradeable memory and single M.2 sata is straightforward but not tool free. The case can also house a single 2.5 inch SSD (not supplied) and an internal sata cable for this is provided.The fan noise varies depending how hard the CPU is working. It isn’t silent but I’ve not found it too distracting nor annoying so far. The case hasn’t ever felt over hot. The separate mains power adapter supplies 20V at up to 6A, and when the CPU is pushed you can certainly feel that in the warm air from the fan exhaust.There were quite a few updates required to the supplied Windows 11 Pro (23H2) when first powered on. I was able to create a local Administrator account (and not link to a Microsoft Account).I wanted a Mini PC for use primarily as a homelab to experiment with virtual machines. VirtualBox 7.1.4 installed without issue and I was able to import and run various Windows and Linux VMs created on earlier versions.The CPU choice wasn’t a major factor for me but I was mildly disappointed to discover that the AMD Ryzen Master application wouldn’t install as the H77 uses a mobile CPU version. I wasn’t previously aware of this restriction, but I don’t think it would have affected my choice.I’ve been impressed by the speed of the H77 generally and particularly with the VMs compared to how they run on my other host PCs. Cad applications that usually hog the CPU haven’t done so on the H77, although I’ve not yet had a chance to really stress test this.The graphic performance was not a factor for me but the benchmarks in this respect were slightly underwhelming.My only previous experience with Windows 11 was using a couple of laptops and that more or less convinced me to stick with Windows 10 for a while longer. However, I have to say I rather like Windows 11 on this Mini PC. I found I could customise things far more to my liking, although there remain a few irritations. The absence of third party bloatware is a plus.So far I’ve only had one issue: The H77 wouldn’t always boot. The solution turned out to be the selection of HDMI cable. I transport the H77 between sites and thus use different screens, cables and keyboards etc. I suspect that newer specification HDMI cables are required even though I’m mostly only using FHD 1080p displays.Overall, I’ve been very pleased with the H77 so far. It has more than met my expectations in terms of performance for my limited budget. Recommended as VM host and for office type applications, but not as a games PC.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Helpful tips when replacing an older computer
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I replaced my old, HP tower with the 32 GB/1 TB  ACEMAGIC. Here are some tips from my installation.1. The old computer attached to my monitor via an HDMI to VGA cable (the VGA has screws). To connect to the new device, you will need an HDMI to HDMI cable. A short cable is supplied with the ACEMAGIC.2. If your Windows updates are taking hours to load or appear to freeze, this is not an issue with the hardware, but with Windows 11. Make adjustments to the Windows "Delivery Optimization" settings.3. If your ACEMAGIC is getting hot (warm is normal), stand the unit on its side (on the side without outlets or vents).4. This unit has 4 standard USB ports and 2 USB3 ports (color-coded blue). USB3 is many times faster. For best results with a hub, make sure the hub's slots are USB3 and plug the hub itself into one of the unit's SBC3 outlets.5. Before changing out your old computer, be sure to back up any documents you wish to save on a separate storage drive or to the cloud. Then use the Windows reset options to scrub your data and restore the factory-supplied software.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I now own 4 of these Acemagic mini PC between home and office. I bought this Matrix M5 Mini PC (Intel i5 version) to use as a compact desktop for work and general home use, and so far it has exceeded my expectations. I wanted something small that could replace a traditional desktop tower, and this machine has handled everything I’ve thrown at it.Setup was very easy. I connected a keyboard, mouse, and two monitors, powered it on, and was up and running within minutes. Windows booted quickly and the system felt fast immediately.Performance has been great. The Intel i5 HX-series processor is much more powerful than what I expected in a mini PC. I regularly run multiple browser tabs, Office apps, streaming video, and other programs at the same time without any slowdown. Everything feels very responsive. For productivity tasks, coding, general work, and media consumption it’s more than enough power.The 32GB RAM and 1TB SSD are a big plus. Programs open instantly and the system boots in seconds. The large amount of RAM also helps when multitasking heavily. I also like that the storage and memory can be upgraded later if needed.The size is another big advantage. This PC is incredibly compact and barely takes up any space on my desk. It could easily be mounted behind a monitor if you want a very clean setup. Despite the small size, it still includes a good selection of ports, including multiple USB ports, HDMI, DisplayPort, Ethernet, and USB-C.Noise levels are low. During normal use the fan is barely noticeable. Under heavier loads it becomes audible but still much quieter than most full-size desktop computers.Graphics performance is what you’d expect from integrated graphics. It’s perfectly fine for everyday computing, watching videos, and lighter games. I’ve tested a few casual games and emulators and they run well. It’s not meant for high-end gaming, but that wasn’t my goal with this system.Overall, this mini PC offers excellent value for the price. You get a powerful processor, lots of RAM, fast storage, and a very compact design. It’s been a great choice for a home office setup and everyday computing.If you’re looking for a small but capable desktop computer for work, school, programming, or media, this is definitely worth considering. I’m very happy with the purchase.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I originally bought this mini PC because the specs were too good to pass up for the price, especially that 32GB of RAM. productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Windows is preinstalled!  Good for most use common cases.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: First, something that wasn't obvious to me at time of purchase (June 2025):  Yes, this system comes with Windows 11 preinstalled!  I bought the 32GB/512GB/7430U configuration.  Note this is a DDR4-based system, which is becoming obsolete and is slower than the more common DDR5.Quite happy so far.  As per other reviews, the Wifi card is not compatible with Linux and I installed a WiFi 6E AX210 NGW Wireless Card for $21 without issue.  Disassembly was straightforward.  Interesting to find two NVMe SSD slots: one SATA (which they populated, likely for cost reasons) and one PCIe NVMe.  SATA is slower, but gives acceptable levels of performance for the casual user this system is targeted for.  Installation of Ubuntu 24.04 Desktop was typical - no surprises - on my own NVMe SSD (removed the stock SATA one just to be sure I wouldn't hurt it).  Wired networking worked fine.  All USB ports tested and working well.  RAM tested perfectly with MemTest86+.  Of course, the upgraded Wifi card worked great and as expected, works well in Windows 11 too.So while this system hasn't had a lot of hours put on it, it's quiet and performs well enough for the typical 60% browser,  30% Thunderbird, and 10% LibreOffice needs.  The mother-in-law will be happy and surprised to replace the large desktop with this little box!Hoping reliability won't be an issue!
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on September 28, 2025

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Terrific deal, with one big caveat.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Linux Mint installed instantly, everything except wifi was 100% immediately.Big caution: the wifi chipset is the (infamous) RealTek RTL8852BE. It's slow, prone to disconnects, and is not a good fit for linux. I'm not sure if it's better under Windows, but I'd avoid it everywhere.To get it to work in linux requires a bunch of  tweaking & compiling - and once it's working with wifi the bluetooth will be disabled.I disabled the builtin wifi and used a TP-Link AC600 USB wifi adapter that's based on the RTL8811AU chipset. Instant blazing speed, completely reliable.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Stays cool and is power efficient.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I was careful to pick the right mini-pc that would have decent everyday performance and good cooling. So far THIS computer has done great. I ran several handbrake encode tests and saw no throttling from overheating. Playback of media files all the way up to 4K x265 and AV1 works great. Occasionally I'll find a file where the bitrate is just too high but this is rare. For just a few dollars more I could have upgraded to a faster CPU and more ram but again my worry was too much heat. I found a good promo code on techbargains so I was able to score mine for $219. I tried having a strong fan blowing across the vents to see if I got a boost in fps during my encode tests but saw little difference. At this price point you are getting older generation laptop hardware but that doesn't mean it won't perform well provided you have at least 16GB of ram. Just to be safe I placed the box on a passive laptop cooler and bought an extended warranty. The PC is the size of a small paperback novel with good transfer speeds over USB 3.0 of around 300 MB/s using windows explorer. Running Teracopy slows transfers down greatly to 65 MB/s but you get the CRC check. I often back up my movies to HDD to watch later without adding wear and tear on my UB820. This little computer plays the files just fine. Costs the same as a Nvidia Shield but has way more functionality. Finally I have not had one problem with W11 Pro or any updates. Not a fan of some of the W11 changes so I installed classic shell.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Pretty good computer for the price

This means you can enjoy Tri 4K@60Hz displays without a single stutter, perfect for productivity setups, home theaters, or even light photo/video editing and casual gaming. While the Intel N95/i3-10110U struggle to run a single 4K display without lag, The KAMRUI AMD 4300U Mini PC handles Tri 4K effortlessly, turning your workspace into a high-efficiency hub or your living room into a premium entertainment center.

【Large Storage Capacity, Easy Expansion】KAMRUI Pinova P2 mini computers is equipped with 8GB LPDDR4 for faster multitasking and smooth application switching. 512GB M.2 SSD ensures fast startup, fast file transfers and plenty of storage space,eliminating slow loading times and ensuring fast responsiveness. the two storage slots (1x M.2 2280 SATA/NVMe PCIe3.0 slot, 1x M.2 2280 SATA slot) can be combined to provide up to 4TB of total storage(Not included). This gives you enough space for all your projects, media and data.

【4K Triple Display】KAMRUI Pinova P2 4300U mini desktop computers is equipped with HDMI2.0 ×1 +DP1.4 ×1+USB3.2 Gen2 Type-C ×1 interfaces for faster transmission, Triple 4K@60Hz Display, KAMRUI P2 mini computer is ideal for visual home entertainment, home office, conference rooms, etc. USB3.2 Gen2 Type-A port ×2 with a transfer speed of up to 10 Gbps (21 times faster than USB 2.0) for efficient data transfer. Ideal for seamless multitasking between spreadsheets, browsers and presentations, or for an immersive entertainment experience.

【USB3.2 Gen2 Type-C 10Gbps, Versatile connectivity】KAMRUI P2 mini desktop pc fast and versatile connectivity! The USB3.2 Gen2 Type-C port offers a data transfer rate of 10Gbps and simultaneously supports DisplayPort 1.4 video output. The P2 AMD Ryzen 4300U Mini PC is complemented by Gigabit LAN, WiFi and Bluetooth, so nothing stands in the way of a productive working environment.

【Save space & High efficency cooling system】The portable small pc features a silver case and can be stored in a bag and carried with you at any time, ideal for business trips. Save space by supper mini size(5.05x5.05x1.73 inch) and a VESA mount to install it on wall or monitors. The shape of the P2 has been recently improved, improving heat dissipation and enabling continuous and stable operation of the micro pc. The cooling fan is practically silent at light load and even under load, the fans remain fairly quiet; minimal or inaudible fan noise is perfect for concentrating on the task at hand!

【Why KAMRUI? Reliable Technical Support & Warranty】We offer lifetime technical support and 12 months satisfaction service. For all our KAMRUI products, please contact our professional service if you have any problems, KAMRUI will do everything to provide satisfactory service.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I've been waiting patiently for it to be released and MSI didn't disappoint. This is a beautiful machine. I really like the understated look of it. It lives up to it's namesake.I've not had a chance to put it through it's paces to test it's performance yet as I only received it yesterday. But just sitting here doing everyday things, it is a very quiet laptop. I fired up a couple of games to test out the gpu, but the fan remained silent.The OLED screen is simply gorgeous. It's very bright and crisp, and the colors pop with nice dark blacks. The speakers are loud, surprising for a laptop that is so slim. The music is crisp with no distortion, though the bass isn't quite as deep as one might want.It's a bit pricey due to the recent spike in memory prices, but I think it it's worth it as I'm replacing a 12 year old gaming laptop.
