productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Easily the best and most fun 4/5 star item I've used
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I am a PC gamer with 35+ years of experience gaming and 20+ of building my own PCs. I have worked in the field as well and am generally an enthusiast user of these devices.I will start with the "great" of this device.1) Really "tight" build quality and feel. My other laptops in recent times have included Dell XPS13 9360 , XPS15 (same gen), Dell Latitude 7490, Latitude 2-1, a Lenovo Slim, and my current daily use Thinkpad P14s. I would compare the feel of the build quality as being similar so far to the XPS series of dells, which is better than I expected. There is no wobble or real flex. Excellently done for a consumer machine.2) Shockingly good speakers, although my expectations were comically low. But still they're good!3) The screen is really nice for gaming. It seems to handle text alright as well, I just simply do not use this device in that way much. I have had no complaints at all about the screen for general use.4) General hardware specs and potential are good. 32gb of ram and a mobile 5070ti 12gb isn't anything to laugh at. I appreciate that there are two m.2 nvme slots for hard drives, with one remaining available as configured for me.The "good":1) The keyboard is good, but I'm not wowed by it. I don't hate it either. For general use it is actually nice, for gaming I don't really like it. It would do ok in a pinch but I'd still probably use an external keyboard if this was my only device to game on.2) Port selection is completely adequate. Two USB-C and you don't have to use either for charging if you don't want, because there is a third "main" charging port. I do not think average users will need more ports than this has. Ethernet, HDMI, two USB-A, headphone as well.3) Overall size/feel of the device, besides the good build quality, is very good. It is "possible" to sit there in bed with it to browse on if you needed but it is kind of large for doing so. It clocks in at ~4 lbs though, which isn't too bad.4) Battery life seems decent enough. I didn't run any tests on it other than to see if it "went down" while I was plugged in and gaming, which I got mixed results on in the same game during different sessions. It went down a few% after maybe 30 minutes during my first test, but not at all during the second test. It is possible it was also background downloading at that point, since it was fresh-er out of the box.The "mediocre":MSI's software package. It isn't terrible, it is actually on par or better than some other ones I've used. But that isn't saying much. It's ALMOST terrible. It is functional though, so at least theres that. I could not see a way to set a custom fan curve even though reading about the software suggests you should be able to. I don't think its necessary out of the box to change the fans, but I did look and see what it let me change. The biggest "useful" part of it is probably that you can change the RGB on the keyboard.The "bad":1 TB hard drive on a $3100 gaming computer. Yes, its a sign of the times. No, I don't care. It is still a reality that many people would logically need to purchase/add additional storage to this device to get the full functionality out of it. It is already difficult to judge value in this category and this doesn't help, because it is difficult to not feel like you need to invest another few hundred dollars to take advantage of this machine.I checked to see if this unit supported m.2 SATA as well as m.2 NVME and so far my research indicates no, but I have refused to open this device up yet. I try to keep my reviews based on what is possible/probable for average users- ie, no modification. It is ok that it doesn't support SATA but it would have been nice and alleviated some of my issue with the storage.Now in terms of gaming performance, I have tried 3 games (all at the 2500x1600 screen native screen res).Game 1 was Barotrauma, a 2d simulation game that is more CPU intensive than GPU and it ran flawlessly, which I expected. My main computer is a 16 thread / 64gb/RTX4080S desktop and it matched that with no issue. But that game was more to establish a baseline that it performed as expected.Game 2 was 2021's Chivalry 2, a somewhat poorly optimized UE4 engine game. This game can chug along on decent spec computers if you max the settings and try for high FPS. I was able to get ~180 fps sustained with DLSS performance mode using a mix of "good" to "epic" level graphics, with shadows turned to medium. I switched to quality mode and was still getting good fps but it was noticeably dipping up and down, so I capped it to 120 and it more or less pinned at 120 on those settings.Game 3 was Baldur's Gate 3, running around the "lower city" area, which has a lot of buildings and textures etc to load. I would actually rank this as the most "stressful" of the 3 I tried in terms of how much heat the laptop was generating (and doing a decent job of venting). I ran it on Ultra preset with DLSS Quality mode enabled and while I did see one dip down to 60 fps, it spent more time above 100 than below it. This is not really a game you need high FPS for, so it was basically as good as you would realistically ever need this game.I should note that for all 3 games, I tried it in a room with ambient temperature of 80F. Normally I game in climate controlled room but I specifically wanted to test this in a sub-optimal place. Fans were of course running but the laptop maintained performance. I was impressed. I tried a cooling pad as well and it seemed to prolong the point at which fans came on loudly. You should expect that you will need the provided AC adapter to game with for anything intensive- I tried using my 135w USB-C and it was the only time the laptop struggled. I'm not sure if the USB-C on this unit is even rated that high, or what its rated for. Either way, USB-C charging will not provide enough for strenuous tasks on this unit- at least not the ones I tried.All in all I was very pleased with the opportunity to receive and review this model, it is a beautiful and performant laptop. You can adjust the keyboard so it isnt at all "gamery" and the laptop itself looks like a normal premium home use laptop. It was able to cool itself adequately.  The only true letdown is the 1TB hard drive, it simply won't be enough for somebody using this device for its intended purpose I think. Similar to a porsche with a 1 gallon/4 litre gas tank.Any of the other issues I had with this laptop were mainly due to the annoyance of Windows 11 or came down to personal preference (ie, the trackpad, which actually feels great and works very well, is not my preference). I would also prefer if the USB-C was on the other side or one on each side but there are electrical engineering reasons for this.If you found this review helpful please mark it as such, I don't get anything out of it but it lets me know that I talked about something useful and will try to keep doing that if so.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: A decent 16" laptop wrapped around an RTX 5070Ti. If you need that GPU it's a good value.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This MSI Stealth AI+ has a sleeker aesthetic in my opinion than earlier MSI laptops and other laptops with similar specs. While still relying on stepped regions rather than proper tapering, the design nonetheless has the appearance of looking thinner than it is. The eased angles and massive trackpad are distinctly… well plainly… MacBook Pro. That’s fine: great artists steal and all. We’re not cheaping out here, but still it’s nice to see the 240 Hz QHD+ 16” screen actually looks and feels like those numbers suggest it should. Aside from some Elegoo inspired line art on the top lid, this looks respectable. Considering the performance, this runs fairly quiet... Obviously cooling fans kick in more when performance is being used.  Overall, build quality and design first impressions: this is a premium experience.Of course, wake the beast and that 4 zone RGB keyboard kicks any sense of muted sophistication (or stealth, for that matter) right out the window. I know, I know - this a gaming laptop, and some gamers like tacky lights on their keyboard, but when my $15 tablet case keyboard has this, it loses some appeal. But is this a gaming laptop? Is this an AI laptop… wait is it an AI gaming laptop? With the MSI Mystic Light Windows app, you can adjust this to a normal static color. I haven’t checked if this setting sticks in ROM, but since mine will be running Linux, this matters to me - the process of booting to windows only to change the keyboard lights would be annoying, but not being able to change the keyboard lights at all would be worse.My model has a series 3 Panther Lake Core Ultra 9 386H. That’s a lot of letters and numbers. Simply put, Intel highest end mobile processors are starting to catch up to the standard entry level M series both in power consumption (25W / 80W Turbo) and performance (well… multicore anyway), while also continuing to lift Apple’s codenames from 23 years ago. With roughly 10-11 hours of standard use from the large 90 Whr battery, we aren’t in impressive territory for a portable, but this isn’t like the gaming laptops of yesteryear that had a glorified internal UPS. Notably, you can’t enable full power “Apex Mode” on battery, likely because discharging that battery in 30 minutes would make for bad press.What is a bit disappointing is the meager 1TB PCIe 4.0X4 NVMe drive. Luckily this laptop features a second empty PCIe 4.0X4 m.2 slot, but utilizing the ultra 9’s dedicated 5.0x4 NVMe lanes would have been nice… even if it was wired to the empty slot. I imagine this was a thermal decision given this laptop’s thinness - cooling over performance. I know times are tough, but a 1TB 4.0x4 drive is hard to swallow at this price point. A lot of gamers and AI coders will probably keep this as a system drive, and that’s kind of a waste.This does have honest to goodness TB4. With this, (some) USB4 or (most) TB 3-5 enclosures can tunnel up to 4 lanes of PCIe 3.0 to external drives. TB4 is a bit outdated in this class, but it’s something. That’s not MSI’s fault; Intel doesn’t support TB5 on their newest flagship mobile processors almost 3 years after Intel released the standard. That’s odd.Here’s the thing, if you’re considering paying this much on something that isn’t a MacBook Pro, you’re buying this for one reason - the RTX 5070Ti. If that’s not true, stop here and find better options at half this price. If you are part of the target audience, a gamer who needs RT cores or a coder who needs tensor cores or CUDA acceleration in a portable package, this is for you. You’re paying a premium for mobile use, and paying a 30-40% performance tax along with that (almost certainly worse than that on battery), and that RTX is (and being an 8 lane PCIe 5.0 accelerator in a slim laptop - probably needs to be) soldered to the board, so you can’t resell this component or upgrade later.That makes this an excellent laptop for the price, but only if you need a high end Nvidia dGPU in a reasonably thin and portable form factor (I wouldn’t call it a laptop with Apex Mode on), with a good screen and decent - but underwhelming for the price and application - components and connectivity. If you don’t need all of that, you’re paying a premium for depreciating hardware that you don’t need.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Packs a lot of powerPacks a lot of power
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This is definitely geared toward gamers, but it’s also perfectly capable of handling everyday use. You can browse, stream, work, edit photos, multitask, and do all the normal laptop stuff without any problem. The difference is that when you want to game or run something demanding, you have all that extra power available.The QHD+ 240Hz OLED display is probably my favorite part. Everything looks incredibly crisp, colors are beautiful, and the high refresh rate makes the screen feel exceptionally smooth. With the RTX 5070 Ti, Core Ultra 9, and 32GB of RAM, performance is excellent and there’s plenty of headroom for demanding games and applications.It’s also nice having a 1TB NVMe SSD and Wi-Fi 7, and despite being a powerful gaming machine, the design is fairly sleek.Pros:* Beautiful QHD+ OLED 240Hz display* Excellent gaming performance* 32GB RAM for easy multitasking* Powerful Core Ultra 9 processor* Fast 1TB SSD* Wi-Fi 7* Can easily handle everyday tasks in addition to gamingCons:* 1TB may not feel like much if you install a lot of large games* Fans get noticeable when the laptop is working hard* Battery life isn’t going to match a lightweight productivity laptopOverall, this is clearly a gaming laptop first, but that doesn’t mean it’s limited to gaming. It works great as an everyday computer too. The price makes much more sense when you consider the high-end gaming hardware, OLED display, and 240Hz refresh rate you’re getting. If you want one laptop that can handle normal daily use but also has serious gaming power when you need it, this is a great option.

features: 🏆 [Proven PC Expertise, Now in GeekBook] Backed by years of design innovation, GEEKOM has established itself as a leader in the mini PC market, earning international honors such as the 2026 Red Dot Award for Product Design and Best Value Desktop System at the 2025 European Hardware Awards. Now, we’re bringing that same proven expertise to the GeekBook series. Every GeekBook laptop undergoes rigorous thermal, drop, and hinge durability testing for reliable everyday performance. For added peace of mind, the laptop includes a one-year limited warranty and 24/7 U.S.-based technical support.

🪶 [Featherlight, All-Metal, All In] At just 2.2 lbs and 0.23 inches thick, the Titanium Gray GeekBook X14 Pro slips easily into your bag and won’t weigh you down—even when you’re on the move all day. Its chassis is made from aerospace grade magnesium alloy, and the precision-milled CNC unibody gives it a clean, solid feel. A careful multi-step coating adds a smooth, warm finish (not the cold, harsh feel of many metal notebook) and helps reduce smudges and fingerprints. Every line and curve is thoughtfully refined, so it looks clean and modern on your desk and feels just as good in your hand.

✨ [Every Pixel, Perfected] The GEEKOM GeekBook X14 Pro delivers exceptional clarity with its 14-inch 2.8K OLED display. Self-lit pixels produce true blacks, rich contrast, and naturally vibrant colors. With 100% DCI-P3 color coverage, it reproduces a cinematic range of hues with impressive accuracy—ideal for creators and movie lovers alike. A smooth 120Hz refresh rate keeps scrolling and animations fluid, while up to 450 nits of brightness helps keep the screen clear even in bright, sunlit spaces. It’s more than a display—it’s a more immersive way to see your world.

🔋 [Go All Day, Pack Light] With its 72Wh high-density battery, the GeekBook X14 Pro is built to go the distance—up to 16 hours on a single charge. Whether you’re bouncing between meetings or working on the go, it keeps up without constantly hunting for an outlet. When it’s time to recharge, the compact 65W GaN charger delivers fast, efficient power in a package about 30% smaller than a typical laptop adapter—and can charge the battery to up to 80% in about an hour. Toss it into any bag and you’ll barely notice it until you need it.

💪🏻 [Power That Thinks With You] The GEEKOM GeekBook X14 Pro is built on Intel’s latest Meteor Lake architecture and features a Core Ultra 9 185H processor with 16 cores, 22 threads, up to 5.1 GHz, and 24MB of Smart Cache. Intel Arc graphics adds modern capabilities like XeSS, ray tracing, and AV1 encoding, giving creators smoother workflows and more efficient hardware-accelerated performance. A dedicated NPU works alongside the CPU and GPU and integrates with Copilot to deliver truly on-device AI—from eye tracking and background blur to intelligent noise reduction and more.

❄️ [Strong and Quiet] The GEEKOM GeekBook X14 Pro delivers the power you need while staying cool. Its advanced IceBlade 2.0 thermal system keeps performance steady during demanding tasks—at whisper-quiet levels. High-efficiency heat pipes pull heat away from the CPU and GPU quickly to reduce thermal throttling and maintain smooth performance over long sessions. The result is a laptop that stays responsive and ready for whatever your day brings. And when it’s time to focus or unwind, dual speakers with DTS:X Ultra audio deliver rich, immersive sound—so you hear more of your content and less of the fans.

🍀 [Command Every Connection, Own Your Privacy] Two 40Gbps USB4 ports with Power Delivery and DisplayPort 2.1 let you charge devices, move large files, up to three 4K displays. You also get HDMI 2.1, a USB 3.2 Type-A port, and a 3.5mm audio jack. And unlike many thin-and-light laptops, you don’t have to rely on dongles—the included docking station makes it easy to plug in and get to work. Privacy is built into the way you use it. The GEEKOM GeekBook X14 Pro includes fingerprint unlock and a dedicated physical camera shutter. Slide the switch and the camera is completely cut off—you always know when it’s off.

🚀 [Fast That Keeps Up] The GeekBook X14 Pro laptop Windows 11 is built to stay fast under real-world workloads. With 32GB of ultra-fast LPDDR5x memory at 7500MHz, it keeps demanding apps and stacks of browser tabs moving without breaking a sweat. A 1TB PCIe Gen4 NVMe SSD gives you the space and quick load times big projects need. Wi-Fi 6E opens up the 2.4, 5, and 6GHz bands for higher throughput and lower latency on crowded networks. And with Bluetooth 5.4, pairing your headphones, mouse, and other devices feels more reliable, responsive, and power-efficient.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Fantastic machine for anyone's use case. Good screen, great specs, runs cool, and is very light and easy to carry. I often have an ungodly amount of chrome tabs open along with some work programs and occasionally a virtual machine. This things just chugs along and handled it. I love the keyboard, it's nice and tactile. The trackpad kinda sucks but that's doesn't hinder my 5 star opinion as I use a mouse anywhere I use it and that wouldn't change if I had a different machine. Great value and quality. Love the machine and hope to get many years of faithful serving out of it!
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on July 5, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: This Machine Hits the Sweet Spot!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I was lookin for a notebook that was around 13-14 inches. I saw a review from Action Retro on YT. Geekom was the sponsor and sent him a Geekbook to review.. Action Retro gave an honest review of the Geekbook 14. He did not let the fact that they were sponsoring his video influence his review. I was pleased with what sounded like a decent notebook. I also liked the fact that he installed WINUX (A Linux flavor) on it. That made me pull the trigger and I was pleasantly surprised. This machine is designed well. Built tough and no Windows 11 bloatware!. I booted up the first time using windows. It boots quick and the screen is sharp and clear. It's nice and light. The battery is also good. I've left it sleeping for three days. opened the lid and still had 80%. I left it playing YT videos for about four hours and only used 25% of the battery. Battery usage obviously depends on what you do with it.  It can game pretty well although not like a true gaming machine. But, that's not what it was made for. Since I bought the 2TB model I split the storage and installed ZorinOS 18 Pro alongside of Windows. Dual boot works perfect. Zorin Linux and Windows (without bloatware) run very well.To sum up, This is a great choice for a daily driver. A durable machine that handles most tasks with ease. Another plus, lots of memory. You get 32Gig  and 1TB or 2TB of storage out of the box. Also a dongle with extra ports to plug in.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on March 20, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Geekom X14 performs well, camera issue with Windows Hello sign in not a deal breaker
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I purchased this as a lightweight travel computer. It was on sale and had very good reviews. So far, it has been a good travel computer, is fairly quick, has a great keyboard with good tactile response on the keys. It has a bright and very clear screen (be aware that it is not a touch screen) and the track pad works very well - one of the best I've ever used such that I don't really feel the need to use a mouse or trackball. The battery life is pretty decent since I can use it, leave it in sleep mode and come back to my work working off and on all day. I've been verry pleased with it. The only quibble at the moment is that Windows Hello facial recognition sign in option is not available because it doesn't find a compatible camera. The camera is recognized by Windows when I look at the camera options - though it calls it a USB camera, and it works with Zoom so I'm not too bothered. The noise and heat levels are excellent. So after 1 month - I'd say that it was definitely worth the price.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on April 27, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: First time having an ultra-light laptop, everything feels phenomenal, I can literally bring it and use it anywhere. Display is beautiful, runs decently well for coding tasks, and battery lasts me the day. Audio, touchpad, works great too for me. Definitely worth it for its price.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on August 10, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Fantastic laptop with 14" OLED, 32gig ram, 1T storage for just over $800 sale
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Nice unit. Have had for a month now. Only a little larger then my old 13 ASUS ZenBook, but almost a full pound lighter. Reason for purchase, battery life on ZenBook is down to about 30-40 minutes. Wanted to take to Bible Study meetings.Now the Good about this unit.1. Beautiful OLED display, crisp and bright. Have at about 70% and brighter than old LED.2. 32g Ram and 1T storage is quick and should last long time.3. i5 ultra is really quick can handle anything I have given it so far. Old i7 8th gen. could handle everything, but slower.4. Has stayed pretty cool to the touch so far. Old i7 even on cooling fan pad, gets pretty warm inch.5. Only about 1/4 inch wider and 3/4 inch front to back longer, but 1/2 thinner and almost 1LB lighter.Still fits on old backpack got  for 13" laptop, after my 15" laptop died years ago.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on August 3, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I reluctantly returned this item after a few days. At first, it seemed like a great value for the money, despite the older generation CPU and lack of an IR camera (required in addition to the regular camera to support Windows Hello face login, for those wondering why that doesn't work). The fingerprint reader in the power button works great and to my mind is better than face recognition. The display is wonderful and plenty bright enough for indoor use, though I would have preferred a matte finish because of the reflections. Fan noise is mostly absent and the unit is almost lighter than air :)The main reason I returned mine was that the keyboard was unacceptable because some of the keys make an ugly scraping noise as they are depressed. Perhaps the key mechanism is slightly misaligned for some positions, I'm not sure. Yours might not have the same issue.Also on the keyboard, but definitely not a deal breaker, the back-lighting through the keycaps is a bit uneven across keys even though it looks like all the LEDs are lit.The touchpad works very smoothly for touch, but as other reviewers have noted, physical clicks are only practical near the bottom edge due to the type of mechanism used.With a higher-quality keyboard build, this would have been a keeper.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on August 5, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Lightweight, fast, and great battery lifeLightweight, fast, and great battery life
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I’ve been really happy with this laptop so far. It’s light and easy to carry around but still has plenty of power for what I need.Performance has been great. It boots up quickly thanks to the SSD and mine came with 32GB of RAM, which definitely helps keep everything running smooth. I’ve had Fusion 360 open along with 15 to 20 Chrome tabs and it handled everything without slowing down. Overall it feels fast and responsive.Battery life is also very good and it charges quickly with the included charger, which has been a big plus for me.One thing I didn’t expect to like as much as I do is the fingerprint reader. It’s fast, reliable, and honestly works better for me than Windows Hello facial recognition. I also haven’t had any issues with heat. Even under load it stays cool, which is impressive for how thin and light it is.A couple small downsides. The touchpad just isn’t my favorite. It doesn’t feel as smooth as I’d like and sometimes doesn’t pick up clicks as well as it should. The speakers are also a bit underwhelming, but that’s pretty typical for a laptop this size.Overall, if you’re looking for a thin, lightweight laptop that still performs well, this has been a great option.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on April 29, 2026Reviewed in the United States on April 29, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Overall I am impressed with the quality, storage, RAM, and the value for the price. While this is not really enough of a reason for me to return and as I use it, would probably occur anyway, it is a bit of a shame that it came with a chip brand new, especially for over $1000.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: Ich war zunächst skeptisch, ob ein Notebook mit dieser Ausstattung zu diesem Preis wirklich überzeugen könnte.Aber dieses Notebook hat mich wirklich auf ganzer Linie beeindruckt und zählt für mich zu den besten Geräten, die ich bisher genutzt habe.Es vereint eine erstklassige Verarbeitungsqualität mit einem erstaunlich niedrigen Gewicht, wodurch es sich nahezu mühelos überallhin mitnehmen lässt. Gerade für unterwegs ist das ein riesiger Vorteil.Trotz der kompakten Bauweise wurde bei den Anschlussmöglichkeiten nicht gespart, und mit der beiliegenden Dockingstation sind selbst umfangreichere Setups problemlos realisierbar.Auch im täglichen Einsatz zeigt das Gerät, was in ihm steckt: Die Performance ist durchweg souverän, alles läuft schnell, stabil und ohne spürbare Verzögerungen.Ich nutze das Gerät für meine tägliche Arbeit – das Notebook meistert jede Aufgabe zuverlässig.Besonders hervorzuheben ist außerdem die Ausdauer des Akkus, der locker über den gesamten Tag hinweg durchhält und somit maximale Flexibilität bietet, wo namenhafte Hersteller mich oft schon nach wenigen Stunden wieder am Netzteil hängen ließen.Ein absolutes Highlight ist das brillante OLED-Display mit 2.8K-Auflösung. Die Darstellung ist schlichtweg beeindruckend: intensive Farben, knackige Kontraste und eine Schärfe, die sofort ins Auge fällt.Absolut kein Vergleich zu einem LCD oder IPS-Panel wie es in vielen anderen Geräte verbaut wird.Auch bei der Ausstattung lässt das Gerät keine Wünsche offen: Mit satten 2 TB Speicherplatz und 32 GB modernem LPDDR5-Arbeitsspeicher ist es mehr als großzügig dimensioniert und bestens für zukünftige Anforderungen gerüstet. Gerade in Zeiten steigender Hardwarepreise ist diese Kombination ein echtes Argument und unterstreicht das hervorragende Preis-Leistungs-Verhältnis.Unterm Strich liefert GEEKOM hier ein rundum überzeugendes Gesamtpaket, das Leistung, Mobilität und Ausstattung auf beeindruckende Weise vereint. Ein Laptop, der nicht nur überzeugt, sondern in seiner Klasse heraussticht.Ich kann das Gerät jedem empfehlen, der ein Notebook sucht, dass für einen absolut fairen Preis eine Hammer-Performance, ein hervorragendes Display und eine grandiose Akkulaufzeit liefert!

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: 32 GB DDR5 RAM, 2 TB SSD, OLED, LEICHT & KOMPAKT – unschlagbar für den Preis
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: Ich bin insgesamt sehr zufrieden mit dem Laptop. Besonders überzeugt hat mich die hochwertige Verarbeitung sowie das extrem geringe Gewicht, das Gerät ist wirklich angenehm leicht und ideal für den mobilen Einsatz. Genug Anschlüsse gibt es auch. Falls diese aber nicht reichen sollten, gibt es als nettes Extra eine Dockingstation dazu.Die Leistung ist für meinen Alltag völlig ausreichend und läuft zuverlässig. Auch der Akku hält problemlos einen ganzen Tag durch, was im Studium oder im Arbeitsalltag ein großer Vorteil ist.Ein absolutes Highlight ist das wunderschöne 2.8K-OLED-Display. Die Farben sind kräftig, das Bild ist gestochen scharf, hier merkt man sofort den Unterschied zu herkömmlichen Displays.Mit 2 TB Speicher bietet das Gerät mehr als genug Platz, sodass kein Nachrüsten notwendig ist. Auch die 32 GB schnelle LPDDR5-RAM sind in der heutigen Zeit, insbesondere bei steigenden RAM-Preisen, ein großer Pluspunkt und sorgen für ein sehr starkes Preis-Leistungs-Verhältnis.Insgesamt hat mich GEEKOM mit diesem ultrakompakten Gesamtpaket voll überzeugt. Ein leistungsstarker, leichter Laptop mit hervorragender Ausstattung zu einem fairen Preis.

Der GEEKOM X14 Pro ist in der Tat klein, leicht, und damit sehr handlich - dabei ist die hohe Auflösung des scharfen OLED-Bildschirms ein Asset. Das Setup war einfach, vor allem da GEEKOM auf das Ausliefern massenhafter Bloatware verzichtet, die sonst das erste Einrichten von Marken-Laptops zur langwierigen Angelegenheit machen.Positiv: alle komponenten funktionieren out of the box, auch der Fingerabdruckscanner. Das System bootet sehr schnell, das Mousepad reagiert schnell. Die beleuchtete Tastatur hat einen angenehmen Anschlag, man kann damit auch bequem längere Texte tippen. Die Batterie hält zwsar nciht die angegebenen 16 Stunden durch, aber das wäre auch zu viel erwartet. Ich bin auf eine Laufzeit von 11 Stunden bei starker Last gekommen, aufgeteilt auf 3 Sitzungen mit Runterfahren des Geräts dazwischen. Dann hätte ich laut Anzeige theoretisch noch 2 Stunden gehabt, aber das war mir zu unsicher. Es war ja kein Test um des Tests willen, sondern tägliche Anwendung unterwegs.Negativ: die Belegung der Tasten < und > als AltGr-Umschaltung zu Y und X ist für mich beim gelegentlichen Programmieren lästig - aber man gewöhnt sich auch daran.Ich hatte vorher einen Microsoft Surface Pro 9 - eine Spur kleiner, aber an Speicher und SSD nur spärlich ausgestattet. Vergleichbare Hardware ist bei MS nicht erhältlich und würde bei Hochrechnen der Preise auf vergleichbaren Speicher und SSD erhablich mehr kosten.Das GEEKOM X14 Pro macht einfach Spaß.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: Leichtes Reisenotebook mit guter PerformanceLeichtes Reisenotebook mit guter Performance
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: Ich suchte nach einem leichten, nicht zu großen Notebook, den ich auch auf Reisen verwenden kann. Die Performance sollte ausreichen, um auch schon einmal unterwegs Bilder zu bearbeiten.Ich stieß auf den Geekom X14Pro U9, den ich jetzt seit 3 Wochen verwende und mit dem ich sehr zufrieden bin.Die Größe und das geringe Gewicht von ca. 1kG sind optimal für meine Zwecke. Das Display hat eine recht hohe Auflösung, weshalb ich die Windows-Skalierung auf die empfohlenen 200% eingestellt habe. Mit der Tastatur komme ich gut zurecht. Was mir manchmal fehlt, sind die Pos1, Ende und Druck Taste. Naja, Gewohnheit. Man kann sich auch anders helfen.Neu für mich war die Copilot-Taste, die man zum Aufruf desselben konfigurieren kann.Wenn man Copilot fragt, ob das Notebook für Ihn geeignet ist, erhält man zur Antwort:"Dein Rechner ist ein echtes Copilot‑Monster. Mit Intel Ultra 9 185H, 32GB RAM, 2TB SSD und Windows 11 Pro hast du ein System, das für Copilot‑Funktionen weit über dem Durchschnitt liegt. Das ist nicht nur „gut genug“ – das ist High‑End‑Laptop‑Hardware, die Copilot in allen Varianten locker stemmen kann.". Scheint also ok zu sein.Beim surfen bleibt das Gerät leise, bei hoher Last hört man das Lüftergeräusch. Man kann mit Fn-p zwischen 3 Performancestufen bzw. Geräuschstufen umschalten. Das steht in der Beschreibung bei Amazon. Im kleinen Handbuch habe ich die Information nicht gesehen.Ich habe die meisten Schnittstellen ausprobiert:HDMI zum 4k-Monitor, kein Problem. Über USB-C auf Display-Port Adapter, den ich noch hatte, auch kein Problem.Das Aufladen erfolgt, wie heute in der EU vorgeschrieben, auch über USB-C. Entweder direkt an den USB-C Buchsen am Gerät oder über den beiliegenden USB-Hub. Über den schließe ich das Notebook auch an das kabelgebundene Netzwerk an. WLAN war auch kein Problem. Verbindung mit einer Bluetooth Maus ging direkt. Mit einer Maus, die einen USB-Adapter benötigte, auch.Kopfhörerausgang auch ok mit meinem 30 Jahre alten Beyerdynamic Kopfhörer.Den Fingerabdruckleser finde ich praktisch zum einloggen.Nach drei Wochen habe ich noch keine Probleme festgestellt und bin sehr zufrieden. Bin gespannt auf die erste Reise mit dem Geekom.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: Sehr gutes Gesamtpaket, starker Performance, Top Preis-LeistungSehr gutes Gesamtpaket, starker Performance, Top Preis-Leistung
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: Ich nutze das GeekBook X14 Pro jetzt seit einiger Zeit im Alltag und bin wirklich positiv überrascht. Besonders die 32 GB RAM machen sich deutlich bemerkbar, selbst mit vielen geöffneten Anwendungen und Browser-Tabs läuft alles durchgehend flüssig. Genau das war mir wichtig und hier liefert das Gerät wirklich ab.Auch das Gehäuse ist hochwertig verarbeitet. Das Notebook ist angenehm leicht und kompakt, sodass es sich problemlos mitnehmen lässt. Das OLED-Display ist scharf, kontrastreich und wirkt insgesamt sehr hochwertig.Für den Preis bekommt man hier ein rundes Gesamtpaket mit viel Leistung. Ein kleiner Punkt wäre noch die fehlende Gesichtserkennung, aber der Fingerabdrucksensor funktioniert zuverlässig und schnell.Insgesamt bin ich sehr zufrieden mit dem Gerät und würde es wieder kaufen.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: Leistungsstark, hochwertig und absolut überzeugend – Ein echtes Top-Gerät!
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: Der GeekBook X16 Pro ist für mich ein echtes Spitzenmodell und hat meine Erwartungen in jeder Hinsicht übertroffen. Schon beim Auspacken überzeugt das hochwertige, elegante Design. Alles wirkt absolut premium.Die Leistung ist beeindruckend – egal ob Multitasking, Office, Bildbearbeitung oder anspruchsvollere Anwendungen, alles läuft flüssig und zuverlässig. Der große SSD-Speicher (bis zu 2 TB) bietet reichlich Platz.Besonders hervorzuheben ist das brillante, hochauflösende und entspiegelte Display. Die Darstellung ist gestochen scharf, Farben wirken kräftig.Der Laptop ist angenehm leicht und damit ideal für mobiles Arbeiten. Der Akku hält tatsächlich bis zu einem ganzen Arbeitstag durch.Unterm Strich bietet das Gerät eine starke Ausstattung zu einem sehr fairen Preis und kann sich problemlos mit etablierten Marken messen.Klare Kaufempfehlung und volle 5 Sterne!

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: Super Notebook, für den Preis meiner Meinung nach unschlagbar...Super Notebook, für den Preis meiner Meinung nach unschlagbar...
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: Normal bin ich nicht derjenige der ein Produkt bewertet, allerdings hat mich das Notebook komplett überzeugt. Obwohl ich nur "die kleine" Version davon bestellt habe ist es echt Fix und gut ausgestattet. Was mich sehr überzeugt ist das Mega gute Display und der Fingerabdruckscanner im An Schalter, den hingegen zu vielen Mitbewerbern auf dem Markt, funktioniert der Fingerabdruck Scanner 1A. Wenn ich Das Notebook einschalte, meldet er mich sofort an. Ja das Display spiegelt bei direkter Sonneneinstrahlung, aber welches nicht. Da sind mir die Farben und das satte schwarz lieber wie ein schlechteres Display und es spiegelt nicht. Die Akku Performance ist ausreichend, kommt man locker mit durch einen Arbeitstag und Abends kann man auch noch ein wenig Filme schauen. Dann gab es vom Hersteller auch noch einen super Preis, ich würde mal behaupten für den Kurs gibt es im Moment nichts besseres auf dem Markt ( auch auf dem Gebrauchtmarkt nicht ). Die Qualität des Gehäuses ist schon fast angenehmer wie vom Apfelmann :-). Wo ich mich erschrocken habe, wie leicht das Gerät ist und trotz des Gewichtes kann man das Display mit einer Hand öffnen. Auch zu erwähnen finde ich die Hintergrundbeleuchtung der Tastatur, da ich mich an sowas gewöhnt habe. Nice ich kann dieses Notebook nur weiter empfehlen und wenn ich noch ein 2 bräuchte würde ich auch ein 2 davon bestellen.
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewedIn: Reviewed in Germany on February 25, 2026Reviewed in Germany on February 25, 2026

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: GEEKOM GeekBook X16 Pro Laptop, 1299g Metallgehäuse, 16" 2.5K, Intel Core Ultra 5-125H, 32GB LPDDR5x 7500MT/s, 1TB SSD, USB4, Fingerabdrucksensor, DTS:X Ultra, bis zu 17h Akku, Copilot, Windows 11 ProIch hätte ehrlich gesagt nicht erwartet, dass mich ein Laptop so überzeugt – aber das GeekBook X16 Pro hat mich komplett überrascht!Extrem leicht, super edles Metall-Design und dabei richtig leistungsstark. Das Display ist einfach wunderschön – scharf, flüssig und perfekt für Arbeit und Entertainment. Alles läuft schnell, leise und zuverlässig.Was ich besonders liebe: Ich kann den ganzen Tag arbeiten, ohne ständig ans Ladekabel zu müssen. Genau so sollte ein moderner Laptop sein!👉 Für mich ein echter Geheimtipp – würde ich sofort wieder kaufen!

Schnelle Lieferzeit: 2 Tage.Auspacken, einschalten und mit dem Internet verbinden.Nach automatischem Update war das Gerät sofort betriebsbereit.Die Leistung und der Bildschirm des Geräts sind Spitzenklasse.Ob Streamen, Surfen, Multitasking oder anspruchsvolle Anwendungen, der Laptop arbeitet flüssig und ohne Probleme.Auch die Bildbearbeitung macht mit diesem Gerät richtig Spaß.Der Bildschirm mit seiner hohen Auflösung zeigt brillante Farben und gestochen scharfe Bilder. Da bekommt man auch beim Filme schauen keine müden Augen.Was mir an diesem Laptop auch noch gefällt ist das elegante, hochwertige Design und das erstaunlich leichte Gewicht.Der Laptop hat ein sehr gutes Preis - Leistungsverhältnis.Ich bin vollständig zufrieden.Deshalb 5 Sterne.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I'm loving this laptop so far! I wanted something primarily for lighter work and entertainment, and for those purposes it has been exactly what I needed.I don't use it for gaming, so I can't really comment on its performance there. My typical use is work, web browsing, and watching shows, and it has handled all of that very well. For everyday tasks, the performance has been perfectly adequate and I haven't felt like I needed anything more powerful.One feature I've especially enjoyed is being able to connect it to my desktop and use the laptop essentially as a remote screen and input device. That gives me the best of both worlds: my more powerful desktop can act as the workhorse doing the heavy lifting, while I can still use the laptop from somewhere more convenient.For entertainment, it has also been great. It's easy to grab when I want to watch something without sitting at my desktop, and it fits nicely into the role of a lightweight secondary computer.Overall, this has been an excellent laptop for my needs. If you're looking for something for everyday work, browsing, streaming, and similar lighter tasks rather than serious gaming or other demanding workloads, I've been very happy with it.The only big downside is the RAM is soldered in so you can't upgrade it.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Remember the old cheap netbooks? The ones you could get for a couple hundred bucks at the local big box store. This is essentially the same thing, but for modern users. You wouldn't use this for gaming, and if you keep your expectations low as far as multitasking, you'll be fine. I needed a laptop that I can move around the house with for writing and web browsing and maybe streaming some music on at the same time. This checks those boxes easily. It hasn't gotten overly warm and it's still in the break-in period so that may change but so far I'm satisfied.The screen is not as good as I was hoping. The viewing angles are not particularly good in front of a window, and the speakers are very very quiet. My pixel phone has louder speakers. Keep all this in mind when you are looking into this PC. It's a little heavy, but it feels solid. The performance is good enough with the AMD CPU which is nice and delivers enough speed for processing simple tasks but a huge con for me is not being able to add to the RAM or upgrade it (it's soldered in) and it's certainly a large enough case to accommodate a spot for adding extra storage but they didn't do that either. I'm giving this a solid 3.5 out of 5 stars for these reasons. If it had those upgrades or at the very least free included software to be able to clone and replace the hard drive, I would give it a 4 out of 5 stars and you'd get much more value for your money. As it is, the price should be lower.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This laptop isn’t bad for the price. It’s got a clean sleek profile, it boots quickly, opens programs quickly, and runs them smoothly. It’s far from being a powerhouse, but if you’re just looking for an affordable, lightweight option for work or school, this is a great choice.The screen is only HD, but it’s bright and clear, and looks great. The built-in speakers are not that great, but they work.Comes with a few ports on the back of each side. Enough for a small amount of accessories, or you can hook up a port hub to it. Does not come with an Ethernet port though so you’ll need an aftermarket plug in if you need to run cable.Really this is just a budget computer that does a good job at the basics (Office suite, research, video playback). It’s nothing fancy, but if you don’t need a ton of power and need to save money, this is a reliable option.The only thing I would’ve liked to see differently is a backlit keyboard. It kind of seems like that should be a feature on every modern computer, but Acer didn’t include it in this model for some reason.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I was in need of an extra laptop, and this Acer Aspire Go-15 is the perfect choice. productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Nice budget laptop with modest processing power and battery life
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: For those with very basic needs (using this almost like a Chromebook or a very large tablet e.g.) this is a very nice budget laptop with a generous screen size. A major strong point is that it has a full complement of ports, unlike many other thin style laptops which limit you to USB-C ports. This one has two full function 3.2 USB-C ports, two USB-A ports, a 2.1 HDMI port, and it even has a physical 3.5mm audio jack, as well as a Kensington type lock slot. Couple this with a full sized keyboard with full sized numeric keypad and a very nice thin profile, and you could have a virtual traveling desktop computer. HOWEVER, as this is a budget laptop, you should temper your expectations. This laptop came with only 8GB of RAM and 128GB of memory, What limits this the processing capabilities/speed of the CPU. This is great for relatively simple tasks (most of what most of us do on a computer anyways on a daily routine basis, but it does get bogged down when multi-tasking with several windows and search tabs open. In addition, the full sized keyboard, while quite spacious and very desktop like in size, is fairly mushy and does not give much tactile feedback, making it less than ideal and somewhat frustratiing until you really get used to the feel of it. Also, despite a relatively large 15.6 inch display, it is only full HD at 1920 x1080 but with a nice matte anti-glare screen. Surprisingly, despite a relatively modest processor (and one that is supposed to be energy efficient, the battery life is meh IMHO. Connectivity supports Wi-Fi 6 and Bluetooth 5.1/5.2. Hardwire Ethernet requires an optional cable that incorporates a USB to LAN converter. It conveniently came loaded with Windows11 Home Edition. So, overall, a nice budget friendly option for those that do not require heavy duty processing nor graphics power but wish to have a thin but full sized laptop for basic tasks (web browsing without going wild with tabs, streaming, and basic office work) when not performed all at the same time. While this might be a good basic computer for those on a budget (think students etc), keep in mind that this is quite a large laptop at 14.25” x 9.5”, IMHO not really backpack friendly despite Acer naming it the Aspire GO.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought this for my husband for Father's Day.  He was overdue for an upgraded chromebook.  After researching and comparing, I chose this device.  I ordered it on June 3rd, it arrived June 9th and I set it up today, June 11th.  I was feeling good about this purchase, and was pleased with my decision, until I tried to access the camera, one of the features that attracted me, it was an included app.  I could Not get the "Mirror Preview" to turn off.  I didn't want selfies, I wanted pictures.  I spent nearly 1 1/2 hours online with support, with no resolution.  As it turns out, my Issue falls under the category of SOFTWARE, NOT HARDWARE, which conveniently is NOT covered by WARRANTY or INSURANCE.  I am sorry, but I am having difficulty accepting that rationale due to the fact that item purchased and described ( camera) was not 100% operational, but was, rather, defective due to the fact that it did accommodate all of my required parameters for choosing this device.  But ultimately, and herein lies the real kicker:  I can have this issue addressed and possibly fixed by "purchasing" a "service upgrade" entitling me to 1(one) 30 day Single Incident - Lenova Live Assistant - Set-up.  Part #5WS1J63373.  Oh, but that's not all, I get this for a mere $69.00, with an ISSUE DATE of June11 and an EXPIRATION DATE of June 25th.  What does this even mean?  I either have to accept or decline (or just let it go).  Will this option be availabe later?  Will it cost me more?  Welcome to the life of a consumer. productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The MacBook Air M5 13-inch is absolutely the best purchase I have made in my entire life. It is so light that it doesn't make any difference in my backpack. It is fast and absolutely great to handle everyday tasks. However, I am extremely disappointed with the way Amazon handled my case.On June 25, 2026, I purchased an Apple MacBook Air M5 during a promotional period for $949.00 plus $6.99 shipping, for a total of $955.99. My order was subsequently affected by Amazon's account-security and payment-verification procedures and was canceled. I complied with multiple identity-verification requests, submitted the documentation Amazon requested, and eventually had my account and identity verification successfully restored.The problem became much worse afterward.Because Amazon would not reinstate my original order, I contacted Customer Service and escalated the matter to a supervisor. I was specifically instructed to purchase the same product again at the higher price, wait until it was delivered, and then contact Amazon for a reimbursement of the difference.This was not something I assumed or interpreted myself.The supervisor calculated the difference using the original total of $955.99 and the replacement price of $1,298.00:$1,298.00 − $955.99 = $342.01I was then given the same information again by another Amazon representative, and Amazon subsequently sent me a written confirmation stating that the $342.01 difference would be reimbursed after the replacement order was delivered.Additional escalation contacts also confirmed that Amazon could honor the promised reimbursement.I therefore relied on Amazon's instructions and purchased the replacement MacBook at the substantially higher price. The replacement order was delivered on July 27.Only after I had followed Amazon's instructions and completed the purchase did Amazon change its position and refuse to provide the $342.01 reimbursement.What makes this particularly frustrating is that Amazon later attempted to treat my case as a normal "price matching" request. It was not.I did not buy a product and later ask Amazon to match a lower price. I had already purchased the product at the promotional price. Amazon's own security procedures resulted in the original order being canceled, and Amazon representatives then instructed me to make a more expensive replacement purchase with the specific assurance that the difference would be reimbursed afterward.I followed the procedure Amazon gave me.Instead of resolving the matter, I have experienced contradictory explanations, repeated transfers, and a situation in which the promised solution effectively disappeared after I had fulfilled my part of the agreement.This experience has seriously damaged my trust in Amazon's Customer Service. A customer should be able to rely on a specific resolution provided by a supervisor and subsequently confirmed in writing. If Amazon can tell a customer to spend hundreds of dollars more and then simply refuse the promised reimbursement afterward, it raises serious questions about the reliability and accountability of its Customer Service system.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: BEST LAPTOP IN THIS PRICE RANGE !!BEST LAPTOP IN THIS PRICE RANGE !!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: After a long wait of trying to get my hands on the neo & watching tons and tons of reviews about it, I've BEEN wanting a MacBook for years, especially since the touchbar and when the M2 came out 😭 and also not being able to afford one before because its expensive in my country... this MacBook Neo was the perfect opportunity for me to finally get one & it filled the gap.Honestly, it did NOT disappoint!!I’m actually so confused by all the negative reviews?? I’ve been trying SO hard to find something I don’t like and I genuinely can’t find a single thing 😭, like I genuinely dont see a problem with all the limitations/ problems everyone's mentioning, it literally doesnt bother me.I’ve been a Windows user my whole life too, so this is my first ever MacBook.The Color: I got the Blush one because I love pink and it’s so pretty 😍. It’s literally gorgeous; I’m in love with it. It’s not childish or super pastel, it’s more of a pink with a silver-ish hue. It’s an "adult" pink that you won’t get tired of seeing.Heating: so far… no overheating at all 🤷🏽‍♀️The Speed: Right out of the box, it was a little laggy, I’m not even gonna lie 😭. But as soon as I updated to the latest macOS, it got super smooth. For 60Hz, it feels fast and the lag completely disappeared.The Build: Stunning. Chefs Kiss. Quality!!!! 😍. The quality speaks for itself: sleek, clean, aluminum body, and very aesthetic. It looks and feels so premium that I find myself looking at it in awe like, "Damn, this is really mine!?!?" 😭 If this is so well-built, I can only imagine the Air and Pro models?? 😍Screen & Display: 13 inches the size is perfect, not too big, not too small. The display is EXCELLENT, sharp, crisp, clear and so clean & very close to 2k quality. its like a mid-range laptop but apple style premium experience.The bezels are a bit thick, but you get used to them quickly. The 500 nits brightness is great, but since I wear glasses, I changed the settings from default to *scaled* so it’s much easier for me to see. Plus, it supports 4K video (& also output to a monitor), which is a big win for YouTube and streaming.Speakers & Weight: The speakers are good, they aren’t the greatest ever, but they are loud and clear enough to hear it. Its enough for the neo. Regarding the weight, it’s about 3 lbs. It does have a little weight to it & it’s not as lightweight as some people are making it seem, but it’s not super heavy either. It’s a nice middle ground. its solid.Value: Well worth the money!!! 🤏🏽🤏🏽 A MacBook Air was way too expensive for me 😭, & as a 1st time mac user i didnt want to just throw out over 1k usd on a laptop so I got the Neo 512GB version because this is going to be my main laptop for years and I don’t want to stress about storage.Battery/Charging: My ONLY downside is not really knowing when it’s fully charged 😭. Since there’s no MagSafe light, you don’t get that green indicator, but that is my only complaint.Overall: This is literally one of the BEST laptops in this price range. Its NOT comparable to a Chromebook at all, (lowkey offensive to the laptop) they are not even close to equivalent at all and it’s definitely not an "iPad with a keyboard" 😭a laptop can do so much more. I’d consider myself a heavy user and I still don’t need crazy specs or the best and latest tech to be satisfied at all.I can definitely see this being the perfect first MacBook for a lot of people, imo the target audience is every and anyone, especially if you’re coming from Windows like me. Id choose this over a windows laptop in the same price range any day. And honestly… in THIS economy??? BUY THE MACBOOK NEO 😭 1000/10 WOULD HIGHLY RECOMMEND, especially the 512GB version. It is VERY impressive, it almost feels like a steal.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Perfect Laptop for Me!Perfect Laptop for Me!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: **MacBook Neo Review – Perfect for My Workflow After Switching From iPad Pro**I haven't owned a laptop in over 10 years, and honestly I wasn't sure what to expect when I bought the MacBook Neo. For the last several years I did everything on a 1st Gen. iPad Pro, and while it worked, I always felt like I was fighting the device when trying to do real file management or any kind of serious organization.After using the MacBook Neo, I can honestly say this is exactly what I needed.I'm not what you would call a power user. I don't do heavy video editing or programming. My main use is organizing large photo collections, doing light photo editing, managing files, writing, web browsing, and general everyday tasks. For that kind of workflow, this machine feels perfect.The biggest upgrade for me was simply having a real desktop operating system again. Being able to organize thousands of photos in Finder folders instead of dealing with the Photos app structure alone has made a huge difference in my productivity. Tasks that felt complicated on the iPad now feel simple and fast.Performance has also been excellent for what I do. Photo editing is smooth, everything launches quickly, and I never feel like I'm waiting on the computer. It feels responsive without being overkill for my needs.Another thing I really appreciate is how quiet and efficient it is. It just gets out of the way and lets me work. Battery life has been great, and I don't feel tied to a charger like I expected with a laptop.Switching from an iPad Pro to a MacBook Neo also changed how I work in a good way. The keyboard and trackpad make longer sessions much more comfortable, and multitasking is far easier. I didn't realize how much I missed having a traditional computer until I started using this again.For someone like me who just wants a reliable computer for photos, organization, light editing, and everyday tasks, this feels like the sweet spot. It doesn't feel like I'm paying for power I'll never use, but it still feels fast and modern.If you're coming from an iPad and want something more capable without jumping into a complicated professional setup, I think this is a great choice.For my needs, the MacBook Neo has been a perfect fit. Absolutly love my MacBook!

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I have been working in I.T. for about 15 years now, and Apple products have been known to have a rep for being non-repairable, and lacks the ability to really upgrade it.  While some of this is still true, you cannot upgrade this after purchase, what they have made is the easiest laptop to recommend to anyone.1. This is a sturdy laptop.  It has the same fully metal case that defines the Apple look. This is going to protect the internal really well with no flex to any. The downside, this thing will get every finger print on it ever, and likely some from another dimension2. Battery Life is amazing. If you open this sucker up, the actual system is the small board near the hinge.  THIS IS AN IPHONE. It literally is last year's iPhone Pro board. The rest of the case is devoted to battery and speakers. During normal use (web browsing, email, watching movies, playing music), the screen brightness will be the biggest drain on battery life. If you are ok with a slightly dimmer image, then this thing will last you well past your work/school day.3. ...but can it game?.... Yes within reason.  Look you can go onto youtube and hear any number of tech influencers talk about how it "is not a gaming laptop".  Gonna have to call BS on that.  It can run MOST of the Steam Library, with the exception of some of the latest most demanding titles.  I have successfully played the following with 30+ frames per second: DOTA 2, League of Legends, Ultrakill, Rocket League, Bioshock Remastered, and Persona 5 Royale.  YES these games are in the 10+ year old range or require just a really ambitious potato to run, but I have had a great time playing. DOTA 2 I would say is the most demanding game I have tried (released in 2013), but I was able to get 2-3 matches in before the Macbook Neo dropped below 50% charge.  If you can handle remote gaming through stuff like GeforceNow, Xbox Game Pass, or even Steam Remote Play, then you are going to be really happy.4. YOU CAN FIX IT!!! Ok so you cannot upgrade it, but the ram dies.  You can replace the system board with no prior experience and have a working laptop with in an hour.  The whole laptop is like 7 parts, the case, mouse, speakers (x2), battery, the screen, and the keyboard.  A part number, an IFIXIT kit, and a youtube guide can get you back up and running. Even laptop brands that market themselves as "User serviceable", are impressed with this thing.This laptop isn't meant to be anything more than the easiest way to get into Apple, and it is.  Apple processors harness some black magic to get the performance they get. You can find cheaper laptops, absolutely, but you will be having to make some compromises that will make your purchase age quicker than you think. This is a product that is sold as a product, not a product sold to make you pay a subscription fee month after month after month.  This is a durable computer perfect for kids in school, college students, your mom, and your grandma.  Look at this laptop 1st, then compare all others to it for your wants and needs.This is what is called a "Market Disrupting Product"but damn it is a finger print magnet

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Not Perfect But Better Than Windows Laptops
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I’ve been retrofitting Macbooks since the blueberry, tangerine and lime notebooks series from 2000 or thereabouts (usually from Apple’s OS to Linux) but my computing experience goes back to the 70s era of flowcharting and punchcards.Although I desired a new MacBook, I wasn’t willing to pay the exorbitant high costs associated with buying one new, or refurbished, from Apple (hence the oft-used term, “Apple tax”).Along comes the Neo.  An Apple laptop for $700 or less?  That’s nearly $300 less than the cheapest Air.  Qualify for the educational discount and you get an additional $100 off.Hyped as a Chromebook killer, this is undoubtedly a hit for Apple.How do I know this?  The first batch sold out within a day and current backorders are reaching well into April.  I got mine delivered in two days via Amazon but was limited to indigo, indigo and indigo.  Bummer, I wanted citrus but that sold out first and the remaining colors (except silver, go figure) were in low or no supply.And, as you can see, I got the upgraded 512GB model with touch ID.As a comparison tool, I’m using my Samsung Chromebook Plus with 8GB RAM, 512GB SSD, high resolution webcam and a 15 inch OLED screen all powered by an Intel i3 processor.  New, these cost around $800 but I got mine as an open box with a defective micro-SD slot for less than $400.I won’t bore you with the Neo specs - you already know them.  Instead, I’ll inundate you with my results and answer a few complaints I’ve heard.First, the complaints:* No MagSafe charger.  Whoopee.  It uses USB-C which means I don’t have to carry yet another charger just for this.  Chances are you’ve got bookoodles of USB-C cables and chargers hanging around anyway.On that topic, it comes with a 20 watt slow charger but the charging port can handle a 65 watt charger and possibly charge a little bit quicker.* The trackpad has no haptic feedback.  Double whoop.  Since my MacBook conversions used Linux, that doesn’t matter.  You’ll get used to it.  The nice thing is, you can click anywhere on the trackpad.The bad news?  It’s no better than any other trackpad out there and pressing down will expose gaps in the sides.* No backlit keyboard.  Okay, I’ll agree on this one.  Fortunately, the Neo comes with keys that are lighter in color than the casing, so I really haven’t had too many difficulties here, plus I know my keyboard layout after 55 years of typing.* Two USB-C ports with one that’s old school.  Still faster than my 2017 Air that was still hooked on the fatty USB-A ports.As a test I hooked up my Macbook double C external port dongle (the type that hangs from the side.  Works like a champ, contrary to what some online critics state.* It’s a glorified iPad Air.  Hmmm, I checked.  The iPad Air with 512GB SSD and a keyboard costs $1,168 from Apple.  While it may come with the M4 chip and 12GB RAM, it still has just an 11 inch screen and a $468 price premium over the Neo.  No comparison there, especially given one is iOS while the other is OSX.* The speakers aren’t up to Apple standards.  That’s why I have bluetooth speakers at the ready for rocking out to Zeppelin or Floyd.  Otherwise, I listen to jazz and the included speakers do just fine.* It uses a phone chip (A18).  Yes, and so what?  So does your iPhone and I don’t hear you complaining there.* No privacy shade for the webcam.  You can buy a stick on version for a couple bucks or do like my neighbor and use a small sticky note to block it.On the negative end, it doesn’t have a light to tell you when it’s activated.  That should be standard.* The Apple logo on the cover doesn’t light up.  That’s an issue?  Really, c’mon now, Apple stopped that design feature about a decade ago.* The battery peters out too quickly.Well, if you consider about 8 to 10 hours to be too quickly, then you’re right; however, I come from an era when laptop batteries lasted maybe all of 2 hours.Now on to the good points, in my observations.* It’s aluminum, just like its bigger MacBook brethren. No cheap junk plastic here.* Not a lick of bloatware, unlike Windows computers that often load up with anti-virus and other assorted gimmicks you didn’t ask for.* The battery is user replaceable.  Yep, it has just 4 screws holding the battery in (not counting the ones holding the back cover on).  Even the motherboard is replaceable, according to a couple reviews I’ve seen (I won’t be trying either the battery or motherboard replacement for a few years, at the worst).* That is one vivid screen, even at just 13 inches.  The resolution is tight and bright, as one observer noted.  Even my 66 year old eyes have no problem with this.* For such dinky speakers, the sound is surprisingly good, in my opinion.  Again, I’ve got bluetooth speakers to help along as necessary.* It’s faster than you might think.  That phone chip goes a long way to make sure it keeps things humming along.So, does this beat the Chromebook Plus?Well, it does allow for apps Chromebook can’t duplicate and it’s not internet reliant, in most cases.However, in the overall scheme of things it depends upon your needs and the level of use or abuse you plan to heap on whatever you get.Ten years from now this will probably sell on the used market for around $200 while the Chromebook will be in a dump somewhere.It’s not perfect but it’s a step forward for Apple and I’m sure it’ll be a hit just because it’s inexpensive compared to other MacBooks.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: Honest Student Review: 8GB Ram Is Fine
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: If you’re hesitant about buying this laptop, this is the brutally honest review I wish I’d found before I bought it.I’m a university student, so my laptop gets used constantly for essays, research papers, online textbooks, downloads, and what feels like a million tabs open at once. I was really hesitant because it’s significantly cheaper than a MacBook Air, and I kept seeing mixed opinions online. Google and ChatGPT both gave me conflicting answers, and I was especially worried that the 8GB of RAM wouldn’t be enough or that the laptop would start lagging as soon as I had multiple things open.I’m happy to say that, at least so far, none of those concerns have been an issue. It handles everything I throw at it without slowing down, and I haven’t experienced any lag. If you’re using it for school, browsing, streaming, writing papers, research, and multitasking, I honestly think it’s more capable than people give it credit for.I couldn’t justify spending the extra money on a MacBook Air, so this felt like a bit of a gamble. Looking back, I’m really glad I took the chance.My only real complaint is the colour. I ordered the yellow, but with a clear case on it, it honestly just looks green. It’s not a huge deal, but it’s worth mentioning if colour matters to you. I was also a little disappointed that the keyboard isn’t backlit, but after using it, I’ve realized it doesn’t affect me at all. I don’t normally use my laptop in the dark, so it’s never actually been an inconvenience.Overall, I’m really happy with this purchase. If anything changes as I continue using it, I’ll absolutely come back and update this review.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Fast and light for productivity tasksFast and light for productivity tasks
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I reviewed the HP Omnibook 3, model 16-by0499nr, with 8GB memory and a 512GB hard drive. For its price this is a good laptop that is acceptable for web browsing, email, word processing and the like. It can easily handle regular productivity tasks for school or work. It would be good for light gaming with entry-level or older games, but more modern games require at least 16GB ram.It has a nice feel, and seems sturdy and well made. The full keyboard, which includes a numeric keypad, has a good feel when typing. It is backlighted which is a huge plus for those of us who arise early and login before turning on the lights. Graphics are very good for the 2K resolution (1920 by 1200) and it has a touchscreen that responds well.The cpu is pretty good. The Ryzen 5 40 cpu benchmarks at 9995 (Passmark score), with a single thread rating at 2592. It has 4 cores and 8 threads, and would be good for normal tasks. You won't be doing major video editing or running modeling software, but daily tasks are fine. With so many things cloud-based now, there's not a great need for powerful cpus except for specific tasks (like gaming or local AI).  The product description claims over 14 hours of battery life, but I estimate that it is not near that.  I used up about 50% in about 3-4 hours, which would give it about 5-8 hours, but I was doing the install and testing with heavy use that entire time, so moderate usage may make it last longer.  Even so, that's better than my current laptop by far.Microsoft has removed the option during setup to install without WiFi and a Microsoft account, but you can get around this if you search for the method (Alt <F10> to open a CMD window and then some commands) if you are worried about privacy. The installed software takes up about 55GB of hard drive space, but memory usage is minimal, so the 8GB provided is fine. I understand that the memory cannot be upgraded, as it is soldered onto the board, but I don't know about the hard drive. From first power-up to being able to open a browser and surf the net took me about 1 minute of setup and 10-15 minutes of waiting around for updates - about average.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I own a lot of hp products. I love hp because they’ve really have made some quality stuff over the years and they’re also pretty easy to upgrade. This is the Omnibook 3. I’ve heard it compared to the Hp Pavilions which I also have. So I will give my pure opinion based off that.This Omni book is a good mid level laptop. Lots of speed from the Ryzen 5, huge 16” screen, its touch screen and the battery life is much much longer than my pavilion which is its biggest weak point on the pavilion. The Omni book also look amazing as it has a nice compact redesign. It’s missing the finger print id and the usb c or lightening ports that I think should be standard on all computers. It has back lit keys that you can see very nicely. The keypad is a bigger upgrade from the pavilion where the keys are not backlit on mine and also hard to see. Performance wise the omnibook 3 runs just about everything well. It browses no problems and it sets up WiFi on startup. It will run the usual windows programs no problem. This is an excellent business or casual use laptop. Maybe if you want to play a few games the ryzen 5 will help you no problem but this is not a gaming pc it’s a business casual laptop. That sometimes becomes the unfair comparison for computers and laptops when they’re compared to high performing gaming computers. This is everything the average person I think will need. I’m running Protools on it and that is resource heavy and it is flawless with no hiccups at the highest audio rates. I can record lots of musical tracks and play them back with no problems. This is really a great laptop. I’m very satisfied with it.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I’ve been using this ZAQTG 15.6” laptop for a while now, and overall I’m very satisfied with it. The micro edge design provides an impressive 88 percent screen to body ratio, while the anti glare coating and 300 nits brightness ensure clarity even in well lit office environments. Perfect for creative professionals and students alike, this vibrant display supports intuitive touch gestures for effortless navigation, making it ideal for detailed photo editing, streaming your favorite content, or collaborating on visual presentations with precision.

[FUTURE PROOF CONNECTIVITY] Stay connected at the highest speeds with cutting edge Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6.0 wireless technology, providing ultra stable and fast internet access even in crowded networks. This versatile laptop features a comprehensive array of ports including two USB Type-C 10Gbps ports with Power Delivery 3.1 and DisplayPort 1.4 support, allowing you to connect multiple 4K monitors and peripherals with ease. With an additional two USB Type-A 5Gbps ports and an HDMI 2.1 output, you have all the flexibility needed for a professional desktop setup or a mobile workstation, ensuring you can link up with external storage and modern docking stations.

[ELITE VIDEO CONFERENCING] Elevate your remote work experience with the integrated 1080p FHD camera featuring HDR auto switch and temporal noise reduction for crystal clear video calls in any lighting condition. The dual array digital microphones and AI based noise reduction technology effectively filter out background sounds, ensuring your voice is heard clearly during important business meetings or virtual classes. For enhanced privacy and security, this laptop includes a physical camera shutter and a dedicated microphone mute key with a visible LED indicator, giving you complete control over your workspace and peace of mind during your most sensitive communications.

[MAXIMUM MOBILE EFFICIENCY] Designed for the on the go professional, this lightweight 3.61 pound laptop features HP Fast Charge technology that powers your device from 0 to 50 percent in approximately 45 minutes when powered off. The full size keyboard with a dedicated numeric keypad is perfect for rapid data entry and complex spreadsheets, while the Windows 11 Pro operating system provides enterprise grade security features and advanced multitasking tools. With a long lasting 3 cell 41 Wh battery and a compact 45W USB Type-C GaN power adapter, you can remain productive throughout your entire workday without being tethered to an outlet, making it the ultimate tool for mobile performance.

aPlusContent.title: From the manufacturer
aPlusContent.rawText:
From the manufacturer
Dell 16 Laptop 

Compact 16-inch laptop with a modern design and Intel Core processors and graphics that power effortless productivity and captivating entertainment. 
16.0-inch 16:10 FHD+ (1920x1200) Anti-Glare Non-Touch 300nits WVA/IPS Display with ComfortView
Intel Core 7 150U Processor (10 cores, up to 5.4 GHz)
Intel Graphics
1TB M.2 PCIe NVMe Solid State Drive
16GB, 1x16GB, DDR5, 5200 MT/s Memory
Windows 11 brings you closer to what you love 

Family, friends, obsessions, music, creations - Windows 11 is the one place for it all. With a fresh feel and tools that make it easier to be efficient, it has what you need for whatever’s next. 
Edge-to-edge clarity 
Enjoy crisp, expansive visuals on a 16" screen with FHD+ resolution, and a 16:10 aspect ratio - delivering a wide, immersive viewing experience. 
Ready for business 

Flip between effortless productivity and captivating entertainment on a large, immersive screen powered by Intel Core processors and graphics. 
Built to last, this laptop features military-grade durability, a hardware security chip to protect sensitive information, a wedge-shaped lock slot, and Dell BIOS software - ideal for small businesses or passion projects. 
Built for virtual connection 

Bring your connections to life with an FHD camera, designed with wide dynamic range and temporal noise reduction to deliver crisp, sharp images, no matter the lighting conditions. 
Ensure your voice is captured with clarity and precision using built-in dual microphones, effectively reducing background noise for flawless sound quality. 
And a built-in mechanical privacy shutter for added privacy and peace of mind. 
Inspired by sustainability 

Design innovation: Designed with 50% recycled aluminum in the top cover, and 50% low emission aluminum in the palmrest, with an etched logo on the lid that reduces manufacturing waste and is a more durable design. Thoughtful material and design considerations help lower environmental impact. 
Based on internal analysis, April 2025. 50% recycled aluminum in the top cover and 50% recycled low emission aluminum in the palm rest. 
Elevated standards 

This product is certified ENERGY STAR with Climate+. 
Based on internal analysis, April 2025. 
Packaging innovation 

Ships in 100% recycled or renewable packaging. 
Contains up to 95.7% recycled content and up to 4.6% renewable materials. Renewable materials in the form of sustainably forested materials. Percentages may vary slightly by region[and formfactor]. Excludes optional items added to order and included in box. 
Windows Copilot Key 

With one click, you have instant access to Copilot in Windows – Your own personal AI assistant. Get real answers, inspiration and solutions at your fingertips. 
Timing of Copilot feature delivery and availability varies by market and device. Requires Microsoft account to log in. When Copilot in Windows is not available or enabled on the device, pressing the Copilot key will launch Windows Search. 
All-day comfort 
Dell ComfortView Plus helps reduce harmful blue light emissions while preserving true-to-life color, keeping your eyes comfortable even during prolonged screen time. 
Fingerprint reader 

Fingerprint reader for quick secure sign-in. 
High-capacity battery 

Enjoy long-lasting battery life featuring ExpressCharge that minimizes the time you spend tethered to an outlet, recharging your battery 80% in 60 minutes. 
ExpressCharge must be enabled within Dell Power Manager software. System must be powered off or in hibernation mode for ExpressCharge feature to function. After charging has reached the stated capacity, charging speed will return to normal speed. Recommended for use with the provided Dell power adapter. 
Adaptive thermals 

Built-in technology allows your PC to sense when it's on a stable surface and adjusts its power and thermals to run more efficiently. 
Keyboard 

Full size backlit keyboard with number pad for ease of use and enhanced productivity. 
Ports and Slots 
1. Universal Audio Jack | 2. USB 3.2 Gen 1 Type-A | 3. Wedge-shaped lock slot | 4. Power jack | 5. HDMI 1.4 | 6. USB 3.2 Gen 1 Type-A | 7. USB 3.2 Gen 1 Type-A | 8. USB Type-C with Power Delivery 3.2 (10Gbps) and DisplayPort 1.4 
3.5mm Audio Jack functionality varies by model configuration.
