productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I wanted a new laptop for personal use as well as mostly moderate gaming, and this laptop is great for all my purposes (i9, 32GB RAM, 1TB storage). I consider the price I paid ($1746) reasonable compared with similar laptops, but it does go on sale sometimes.The laptop is a little on the heavy and slightly bulky side for casual use, but I wouldn’t have minded if it was even bigger than it is if that meant better cooling, less cost, etc. It really not too bulky for a gaming laptop. Size aside, it looks great. Stylish and sleek, and the customizable and dimmable keyboard backlighting is a nice touch. I like the keyboard layout for typing as well as gaming, I find it to be very functional. The number pad is small but usable. The function keys are well thought out (function keys for screen brightness, keyboard backlighting brightness, enable/disable touchpad, mute mic, etc.), which I find to be rare with laptops. There’s a light for function lock and mic muting. WASD are a different color for gaming.The laptop runs Windows 11 well and seems very fast and powerful (although I haven’t done anything yet to truly push its limits). The BIOS is pretty reasonable, based on my experience (IT professional). The MSI app with designated function key lets you quickly change the power mode for your purposes, although my limited experience with the AI mode has not been great so far (it throttled the power down when I needed it, reasons unknown, and it turned off the keyboard backlighting at night). I’ve only played a few games on it so far, but it handles Fortnite like a champ without needing its full capabilities (power setting on “balanced” works perfectly). I haven’t run into any major issues with other programs or OS yet. Worth noting, the laptop does not always shut down properly. I’ve had to disable sleep and hibernation in Windows, as the laptop frequently does not resume from those states gracefully. Sometimes the laptop does not shut down completely at all, and the Embedded Controller keeps the fans running indefinitely, until I hold down the power button to manually power it off. That’s not ideal, but for me it’s not too big a deal either.The laptop also runs hot when in performance power mode or when gaming. I would never use a gaming laptop without a cooling pad, but if you’re new to gaming laptops, take note. The laptop seems to manage its built in fans well (and there’s a keyboard function key to let you immediately turn all the fans on to max speed), but again, I advise a cooling pad with fans to ensure you don’t overheat it during any use more intensive than watching videos. Definitely don’t ever put this down on a soft surface (like a bed or couch) without a hard flat surface under it or you’ll probably melt it.The power supply is bulky, as you would expect for a laptop that needs extra power for gaming, and the power supply also gets hot. Best to keep it where it can easily cool when in use. The power cord has a third prong/ground.All around, a great gaming laptop for a reasonable price.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Absolutely a beast for gaming, but loud on Fan Boost.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I am a gamer that likes to play both modern and older games. The computer has no compatibility issues with older games so far, and runs all the modern games with no issues. I have it attached to an external 32" gaming monitor and play games like 7D2D on the highest settings. The screen is bright and the laptop hinges for the lid to the body seem well made.The battery life when playing heavy games last about 45 minutes, but lasts about an hour and a half when playing only music. I take the laptop with me everywhere I go. The sound quality is impressive and can get pretty loud, however it needs to be loud for my next point.The only negative feedback that I have is part of a double-edge sword. When doing normal activities, the laptop runs cool to warm. There is enough air speed in the fans to keep the laptop from getting real hot when heavily gaming, however you would need to use the Fan Boost to do that. The trade off is the sound from the fan sounds like a mattress air pump. It does push a LOT of air, so I guess there has to be a trade off.Would I buy this laptop again? Absolutely!

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Boyfriend and I needed new laptops after our old ones were dying, so I bought two.At first it ran great. Screen was adjustable. The battery life lasted like a good couple hours if you're not doing gaming. Dies fast within hour if you are doing anything intensive.It does run a bit hot, but I got one of those USB fans for underneath for my bf and it ran fine. I haven't gamed lately since I purchased it, and so mine didn't run hot at all. Battery box though - watch out for that since that does get burning.I like the RGB colors on it. Having a numpad was bonus. Touchpad is a bit hypersensitive. I seem to keep triggering it when I type but that can probably be adjusted/turned off.Didn't have issues with Wifi connection.But after 4 months, my background started flickering on and off. Again, I wasn't doing anything intensive. Updated drivers and everything. But that didn't solve the issue. Things started lagging. But mine wasn't as bad as my boyfriend's. His games started lagging, constant disconnects. Whole computer freezes every now and then and just shuts off. I suspect it's a GPU problem. But two laptops having issues is not a good sign.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Absolutely fantastic!! Great specs, great price!Absolutely fantastic!! Great specs, great price!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: MSI is hit or miss for me. This Katana 15HX is a 100% a hit! A beast of a machine at a very affordable price.The i914900 is super fast, the RTX 5070 is very strong! Every game I tested runs at max settings, with very high FPS. Resident Evil 9, Cyberpunk, Final Fantasy VII parts 1 & 2, and several other games tested all work with no stutter. 1440p resolution on all games I tested. It’s awesome.You get 32GB DDR5 ram. It’s efficient and quick. Of course you can upgrade to faster memory speed and size. 64GB is maximum.The laptop fan will get loud during heavy use, but the CPU and GPU temps are well within safe temps. The built in MSI software works good at monitoring, and making changes. There are several obnoxious apps installed as bloatware. I uninstalled all of them and it’s been great.This comes with 1TB Gen 4 NVME SSD. It’s very quick at 7000mb/s. You could upgrade the SSD to Gen 5 with extra space. It’s costly, but worth it if you play a lot of modern games. Many of them take 100GB and more.I bought an upgrade to make Windows 11 the Pro version. Windows 11 Pro offers more options for your choosing but for some, Windows 11 Home is ok. You can buy a legit, genuine Windows 11 Pro key for less than $20 online. Do not use those Pro activation hacks. Some are malware and you could have serious issues. Besides, Microsoft does updates that verify the authenticity of your Windows key. Buy the legit key and change it in Windows settings. It’s very fast and simple.The screen is smooth at 165hz. I wish it were OLED but the quality is still very high. The screen gets nice and bright plus antiglare.Battery life is about 2-3 hours when playing games. I keep mine plugged in and the battery does not drain during gameplay like some claim. I keep the max battery charge at 80% to extend the life.It’s a bit heavy but that’s to be expected for a gaming laptop.The speakers are pretty good, but like any setup, I use headphones.Overall I am very happy with this gaming laptop from MSI, and I should get 5-6 years of use before upgrading again.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Powerful and Reliable – A Great Value for Serious Gamers
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: As someone who’s been building and using gaming PCs for years, I picked up the MSI Katana 15 HX B14WGK-016US primarily for portability without compromising performance—and I’m impressed with what this system delivers.First off, the Core i9-14900HX and RTX 5070 combo is no joke. This laptop chews through modern AAA titles without breaking a sweat. I’m seeing 100+ FPS on high to ultra settings in titles like Cyberpunk 2077, Hogwarts Legacy, and Call of Duty MW3, and it stays consistent even during long sessions. MSI did a solid job with thermals—kick on Cooler Boost and it stays cool enough without thermal throttling. The 165Hz display really helps the experience feel fluid in competitive titles.Stability is another strong point. No weird crashes, no blue screens, no random freezes—just reliable, smooth performance. And coming from a brand like MSI, that doesn’t surprise me. I’ve used their graphics cards and motherboards in my builds for years, and they’ve always delivered.  MSI overall I’ve had a good experience with their products That same engineering shows up in this laptop.That said, there are some things to be aware of. Battery life isn’t great—maybe 4 hours max under light use, and much less if you’re doing anything demanding. For some this laptop could be heavy for a 15-inch laptop, but others will say its not. I didn’t pick this laptop for its light weight design. It was about performance and portability. The chassis is plastic but metal feel and pretty basic clean design, though it feels solid enough. The RGB keyboard looks great, but the number pad layout is cramped and takes getting used to.Out of the box, expect sometime to setup— Windows updates, and drivers, etc.Bottom line: if you’re a gamer who prioritizes performance and value, this is a fantastic machine for the price. You’re getting high-end GPU and CPU power without paying $2K+. It's not a luxury laptop—it’s a focused, performance-driven tool for gaming and heavy workloads. Highly recommend for experienced users who want desktop-like power in a mobile form.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought this to replace a 6 year old Eluktronics laptop.  Worked perfect until it kept crashing multiple times per day for no reason.  After doing a lot of research, this seemed like a solid choice for a gaming laptop.  Not high end super-duper intensive gaming, but it works for my gaming needs.Obviously, like most new computers, set-up can be tedious, and some people may try to rush the process.  My suggestion is to let Windows do ALL of their updates before you start installing your apps.  Let your other onboard hardware do the same.  Then, after everyone is all happy and up-to-date, you can install your stuff.  It went error-free for me.  After a few days of additional tweaking, I got this new laptop to "feel" like the workhorse it replaced.  Plus, I have the reassurance that I should get several years of dependable service.Now, the unhappy discoveries that I made:1.  The built in webcam is not "Windows Hello" compatible.  I hadn't really thought about this ahead of time.  My OLD laptop's built-in camera worked just fine with Hello.  I got used to using this login feature.  I miss this feature.2.  There really aren't enough USB ports.  I am now using 3 of 4 ports.  One is for a fingerprint device (see above complaint).  It would be a cool feature if a corner of the built-in mouse pad had fingerprint technology...  Another port is being used for a laptop cooling riser.  Yes, this laptop has pretty good cooling, but adding more comes in handy with heavy usage.  The 3rd port in use is for a portable hard drive.  This leaves 1 port for available use.All in all, it's a really affordable laptop for better-than-just-basic gaming as well as general duty use for everything else.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I needed a laptop that can handle my accessibility needs.  I use Magnifier and a screen reader, which can be rather taxing on a system.  When I was researching this product, one of the first YouTube reviews that came up was some guy bashing this product.  But I kept watching other reviews and reading.  I wound up by giving it a chance.  I'm glad I did. The first video review I saw where the guy was bashing it, was comparing it to something twice the price or more... which is not fair to do.This laptop is actually VERY nice.  It's sturdy, not flimsy, which was a big selling point for me, since my school-age daughter and I aren't the most graceful people on the planet.  It's got a 16 inch nice crispy display, with a full keyboard, including a numpad.  The key travel isn't quite that of an external keyboard, but MUCH better key travel than many other laptops.  I can actually type on this thing.  It's got plenty of USB ports, an HDMI out, combo headphone/mic 3.5mm port, etc., and even has an Ethernet port.If you're going to get this, I would suggest a couple things:Get an extra 8GB of RAM for it.As soon as Windows is done installing and setting up itself, remove the bloatware like McAfee and most of the ASUS services.  They're completely unnecessary, and only serve to take resources away from what you want to be doing instead.  You can always re-install the ASUS stuff later if you need to modify or diagnose stuff.Go to Windows Update and get the latest drivers for the chipsets.So far, I don't have any major complaints.  It runs everything I've thrown at it, including games like ESO and Star Wars: Outlaw.Is it a $3000 Alienware uber-spec'ed wet dream?  No.  It's a fully capable, well built gaming laptop.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: TLDR: ASUS laptops have been solid for me. Do your research though!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The ASUS computers have been solid computers for mid tier gaming and designs. We have got several over the past few years. When choosing which one Get the CPU/GPU, graft a card, and screen size you want. You can upgrade memory and SSD to fit your goals.Based on others reviews I had seen some of the models sold by 3rd parties can potentially have some defects. But those seem hit or miss as any mass production item can have some faulty hardware.My recommendation: I prefer the GPU over CPU with 5-7 cores. And a decent graphics card. I usually go NVIDA for the card. Unless you want to get the best get one that is a year or two older. They can still crank up graphics pretty well and save you some money. I can’t say for sure what the sweet spot is for model numbers as those change frequently.Windows 11 is the best long term choice even though I’d stay Windows 10 If that was feasible. But it’s not.I’d recommend getting at least 32Gb of Ram  for gaming. Whether you desire to spend more now or save now and upgrade later. The choice is yours. 16gb will let you play games but not have the beat graffiti settings.As for the SSD if your laptop doesn’t have an additional slot. You can clone your SSD and replace it. I just replaced my 500gb to go to 2tb. I’d say don’t go less than 500gb to start.  If you do like to download a lot of games and have videos or video editing the more space you have is always better.  SSD cards have a read write speed. The better that speed is the quicker apps and games load up and process.I hope this helps!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Compact and Powerful—An Excellent Choice for a Home Office Setup
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: **Dell OptiPlex 7050 Micro Computer, Intel Quad Core i5-6500T****Compact and Powerful—An Excellent Choice for a Home Office Setup**I recently upgraded my home office with the Dell OptiPlex 7050 Micro Computer, and it has been an outstanding addition to my workspace. This compact yet powerful machine handles all of my daily tasks with ease, making it perfect for anyone needing a reliable and efficient computer for work or personal use.**What I Liked:**- **Compact Design**: The first thing that stands out about the Dell OptiPlex 7050 is its incredibly compact size. It takes up minimal space on my desk, which is a big plus in a home office where space can be limited. Despite its small footprint, it doesn’t compromise on performance, making it a great option for those who need to maximize their workspace.- **Strong Performance**: Powered by an Intel Quad Core i5-6500T processor with speeds up to 3.1GHz, this micro computer delivers excellent performance for everyday tasks. Whether I’m multitasking with multiple applications, browsing the web, or handling office work, the system runs smoothly and efficiently. The 16GB of DDR4 RAM ensures that everything runs quickly and without lag, even when working with demanding software.- **Fast SSD Storage**: The 256GB SSD provides fast boot times and quick access to files and programs. I noticed a significant improvement in overall system responsiveness compared to my previous setup. The SSD is also more reliable and durable than traditional hard drives, adding to the longevity of the computer.- **Windows 10 Pro**: The inclusion of Windows 10 Pro 64-bit is a great feature, offering enhanced security and administrative features that are ideal for a professional environment. The multi-language support (English/Spanish/French) adds flexibility, especially if you work in a multilingual setting or need to switch between languages.- **Easy Setup and Connectivity**: Setting up the Dell OptiPlex 7050 was quick and straightforward. It comes with all the necessary ports, including USB 3.0, HDMI, DisplayPort, and Ethernet, making it easy to connect to peripherals like monitors, printers, and external storage devices. The built-in Wi-Fi also ensures that I stay connected without needing extra adapters.- **Renewed, But Like New**: I was initially hesitant about purchasing a renewed product, but the OptiPlex 7050 exceeded my expectations. The computer arrived in excellent condition, with no visible wear or signs of previous use. It functions just like a brand-new machine, offering great value for a fraction of the cost.**What I Didn’t Like:**- **Limited Internal Storage**: While the 256GB SSD is fast and reliable, it might be on the smaller side for those who need to store a large amount of data or run multiple large programs. However, this can easily be mitigated by using external storage or cloud solutions. For most home office tasks, though, the storage capacity should be sufficient.- **No Dedicated Graphics**: The computer uses integrated Intel HD Graphics, which are fine for general office work, web browsing, and video streaming. However, if you need to perform graphics-intensive tasks like video editing or gaming, this system might not be the best choice. That said, for typical office use, the integrated graphics perform adequately.- **Basic Accessories**: The computer doesn’t come with a keyboard, mouse, or monitor, so you’ll need to have or purchase those separately. While this isn’t unusual for a desktop setup, it’s something to keep in mind if you’re starting from scratch. However, this also allows you to choose accessories that best fit your needs and preferences.**Bottom Line:**The Dell OptiPlex 7050 Micro Computer is a compact, powerful, and reliable option for any home office setup. Its strong performance, fast SSD storage, and efficient multitasking capabilities make it an excellent choice for professionals who need a dependable computer for daily tasks. While the internal storage and graphics capabilities might be limiting for some specialized uses, the overall value and functionality of this renewed system are hard to beat. If you’re looking for a space-saving, high-performing computer that handles typical office work with ease, the Dell OptiPlex 7050 is a fantastic choice. I’ve been very satisfied with its performance in my home office, and it has made my workday much more efficient and enjoyable!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great value, minor flaws, TV streaming with HDMI and DisplayPort connectivity
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Mine arrived in excellent packaging with a generic wired keyboard, mouse, and USB 2.0 "n" network dongle. It didn't have the internal wireless system. Not ideal but works just fine.There was some damage to the finish on the housing at the back where it wasn't noticeable. It was covered up with some black permanent marker. Also, at this price point, not unexpected for a refurbished item.I'm using mine as a media station at my 4K TV. I was disappointed at how noisy the fan was but went into the power settings and found that limiting CPU to 70% and changing cooling scheme from Active to Passive in the Windows power settings makes it effectively silent. Even at 70% it has way more CPU performance than the laptop it replaced and has no problem processing video at 4k and the cheap WiFi works just fine for streaming 4k video. The HDMI passes audio through my TV to my 5.1 receiver just fine making for fantastic sound.Paired with an Air Mouse remote control https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0DXFPSSSK it's just about perfect for a home media and internet surfing setup. I went from 3 remotes with my Roku to just 1 and ditched the ads while gaining the ability to surf in a real browser.It uses a SATA SSD and has a free M.2 SSD slot and a free M.2 WiFi slot if you wanted to upgrade or ditch the dongle and use something more modern with an external antenna. I get full bars and it's plenty of storage for me, so I probably won't bother with upgrading anything.Over-all I'm extremely happy with my purchase. If it were more expensive, I might knock it down to 4 stars, but for this price you can't ask for much more.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Not refurbed, reboxed. Broken, dirty and wrong power supply.Not refurbed, reboxed. Broken, dirty and wrong power supply.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Update: I received a replacement and it is in much better shape. Still cheap 100mb wireless n usb. This one is much cleaner and has the correct power supply. Another thing I forgot to mention was packing. The box is twice as wide as the insert to hold the machine, so it and the power supply are surely smashed around inside the box as neither was in the padding upon arrival. I'll keep this one as it runs, but this experience has me questioning Amazon Certified Refurbs.Very poor refurb. Looks like it was just reboxed and nothing of refurbishing occurred. The video port didn't work, the case was sticky and the case screw looked like it was rusted or had coffee poured on it. Being an IT guy, I opened the case and was shocked. The board was broken and was covered in dust. And it was loose dust that could have been blown out, but wasn't. The video port cable was broken off the board and just hanging. The power supply was the wrong one, under powered and it had a dongle adapter to make it fit. But even worse, the DC plug was bent out of the jacket and definitely a fire hazard. There was no on board wifi, but they included a 20yo technology N usb wireless adapter.I'm not sure who is remanufacturing these, but it's time to find another company because they are not doing anything but maybe wiping them off and reboxing. Not even qualified to include the right power supply. I've purchased many refurbs before from Amazon, but this by far was the worst. No QC at all.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Solid little PC, good value. Refurb job was meh. Replace the wifi dongle.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: NOTE: While I am a Vine reviewer, I bought this PC with my own money. This is not a Vine review.Overall, this is a decent little PC. I've had it for a month and am happy with it as my desktop daily driver. The size is very convenient, though the chonky AC adapter takes away from the compactness. It runs quietly, even under load, and is unobtrusive. It is a fairly good value for the cost, especially considering the 16GB of RAM and 256GB SSD.The refurb job was OK, 3 stars for that. They missed dusting the CPU heat sink under the fan shroud, which is concerning, but I'm not seeing any overheating issues so far. The insides were otherwise fairly clean.The included janky Wifi-only USB dongle was flaky and slow. I replaced it with a TP-Link Nano Wifi/Bluetooth dongle, which is much faster, doesn't flake, and provides Bluetooth. Strongly recommend that buyers consider a similar upgrade. For the computer's price, that quality of dongle should have been included instead of the janky one.The RAM and SSD both seem OK so far.There was an option included to "recover" / install Windows, but I installed Linux Mint instead, which runs very happily on it, zero compatibility issues seen to date. 16GB of RAM is way plenty for Mint, which typically burbles along at under 4GB used. However, when running World of Warcraft via Crossover, it can get close to 14 or 15GB used, so yeah, bloated huge MMORPG unsurprisingly needs all the RAM.It's an Optiplex, which means that it has plenty of connectivity, is built to be reliable, and is modular. Individual parts are relatively easy to source and replace. But it is a 15+ year old PC. Kind of hilarious how this is still fairly mid-performance for a sub-$500 Intel-based system. I had a similar one on my desk at work a decade ago, so it's a known quantity, low-drama and just works.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: I LOVE LOVE LOVE this tiny computer!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The machine arrived in great condition and fired right up.  The first thing I did was create a dual boot for LINUX and windows.They even included a WiFi dongle to get by with until I could install a card internally.  I have the larger 7050 desktop tower version, and my first thought was that this would not perform exactly the same as its larger sibling, but this thing is every bit as good!I quickly upgraded the processor and memory and now have a great machine that I can place below the desk on a side shelf, giving me back the top of my desk for the other things I use.This thing sips power like a squirrel, making almost no noise and just running happily as I game away. Still, the stock memory capacity is more than enough for general use, lending itself to more demanding tasks.The other thing I really love is the sturdy, all metal construction of the chassis. productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great for office uses, but not all resellers are equal.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: For those considering this machine, please read carefully.  I selected a reseller with a price higher than the lowest offered.  Why?  Because at the time of my selection, the lowest price seller had 71% satisfaction rating, but for $6 more I selected another seller with a 90% satisfaction rating (TekRefurbs.com).  This is especially important with a renewed computer!  Many reviews reflect problems due to the differences in resellers, so it pays to select carefully.The first thing I did on receiving the computer was open the case and remove the new 256 GB ssd, and install a 1 TB nvme ssd into the m.2 socket, and a 2 TB ssd into the hard drive caddy and reinstalled the caddy and closed the case.  The computer was spotless inside and out.  The next step is very important.  I went to the Dell website and downloaded the BIOS update.  I run linux on a multi boot system, but linux cannot install the new bios so I booted into windows for the bios update.  Just follow the on screen instructions and the update takes just a few minutes.  It is crucial to update the bios as the machine is vulnerable until it is done.  The machcine is capable of running Windows 11, but apparently the Windows 10 Pro that comes with the computer will not allow updating.  Since I did not install Windows 10, but moved my existing drives into the computer, I was all set with Windows 11.  Many users prefer Windows 10.I recommend before buying or receiving the computer that the user/owner manual in pdf format be downloaded from the dell site as it is really mandatory if you are going to get your newly renewed machine set up properly.  Curiously this computer will run with either the 65 watt or the 130 watt power supply cord;  mine came with the 65 watt power supply and it works flawlessy.  There are also two other m.2 sockets on the motherboard for WLAN and WWAN cards as shown in the manual for those who want or need them.  The cards and cables and antenna are available on Amazon.I hope this information is useful to any who take time to read it.  The machines are not for gamers as they do not have the graphics horsepower for that use, but are great for other applications if you choose the reseller carefully. productPageReviews.reviewTitle: It's good, but it could be better
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I've been using this computer for a while now, it works very well, but there are times when it stutters, the FPS drops to 0, which usually takes less than 1 second, but it's still very annoying. The screen's 165Hz refresh rate is spectacular, but I did an online test and I'm almost certain it has ghosting, which is also quite annoying. Also it's a bit slow when performing various tasks, such as opening the browser or simply changing categories on Steam.I'm going to add more RAM since the 8GB it has doesn't seem enough to me; I even think that might be the root of the problem I mentioned. So, I'll try to upgrade to 32GB of RAM.But despite all of the above, it's still a very good computer. I like that it comes with the Nitro Sense application and also with Intel's graphics software, since it allows for some customization. The camera looks good and works smoothly in good lighting, but the computer doesn't have anything to cover the camera.You have 3 fan options: silent, balanced, and performance. Expect a lot of noise from the fan in performance mode. Also, another bad thing is that when I connected my headphones with a built-in microphone, the computer only recognized it as audio output, not as both audio input and output, so I had a lot of problems with that. I even had to restart my PC in safe mode to reset everything because I had no sound anymore, so be careful with that, If you experience the same issue, simply open the Realtek Audio Console application, then go to advanced device settings and program it as an input and output.So I think it's a very good computer. You have to do a couple of things beforehand to be ready to use it for gaming or anything like that, but I don't think I'll be changing it for a long time. Just add more RAM and you'll probably be good to go. I'll update this review when I add more RAM to let you know if there are any changes to the stuttering.So my final thoughts on this laptop are that I wish it were more of a turn-on, ready-to-use thing, but I guess you can't expect that at this price. Despite that, I give it 5 stars

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Almost perfect for a limited budget
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The computer has been quite a ride. When I purchased it, the price was $679, which was more than reasonable considering everything it offers. Of course, at that price some might expect a poor product, but that’s not the case here. Still, I would say this is more of a “project” laptop, as upgrading the RAM is absolutely necessary if you plan to use it for demanding tasks.Performance:With the limited RAM, it handles basic and relatively simple tasks well. For more demanding tasks, performance is just average. The system runs fast overall, Wi-Fi speed is solid, and the graphics are decent as long as you’re not too demanding. As mentioned, this computer shines as a base to upgrade, especially by adding more RAM.Display:The screen looks good. Since it’s an LCD panel, you can’t expect extremely vibrant colors, but it still delivers a pleasant experience and the refresh rate is more than sufficient.Cons:1. The spacebar does not have backlighting.2. The RAM is very limited.Issues Experienced:1. The pre-installed Windows was defective. After transferring files from my old computer, it started deleting data and even erased my entire user folder. I basically lost almost everything, recovering only a few files I had on another SSD. I had to reformat and reinstall Windows, which was a chaotic first experience. However, after installing a fresh copy of Windows 11, I haven’t encountered the same problems again.2. RAM limitations are significant. Just being on the desktop consumes around 80% of the available memory. I strongly recommend purchasing additional RAM to avoid these restrictions.Overall, it’s a good value laptop for the price, but keep in mind that adding more RAM is essential to get the most out of

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I purchased this laptop expecting a smooth, reliable experience, but unfortunately it has been faulty from the start. The most serious issue is with the keyboard:• The spacebar types random numbers (like “6”) instead of creating a space• The J key types “J5”• The K key types “K8”• The period ( . ) types “.m”• The X key types “,x”…and there are likely more affected keysThis problem even happens in the BIOS, which confirms it’s a hardware defect, not a software issue.I tested an external Bluetooth keyboard and it works perfectly, so the problem is clearly with the internal keyboard. This makes the laptop extremely frustrating and almost unusable for normal tasks like typing, studying, working, or even browsing the web.To be fair, the laptop does perform decently for casual gaming and light use, but the keyboard issue completely ruins the experience for everyday productivity.I would recommend buying a different brand instead, and personally I do not recommend purchasing through Amazon for a big item like this. If you do decide to buy on Amazon anyway, it’s better to wait for Black Friday deals instead of Amazon Prime subscriber deals, since Black Friday discounts are usually much better.Overall, this has been a very disappointing experience and I cannot recommend this product.The laptop is great for the buck if you are a casual gamer but a defective keyboard on a new laptop and not being able to return after just one month makes me not want to buy laptops on Amazon ever again.

Precision cooling for maximum efficiency 

The new Cryo-Chamber design optimizes airflow, cooling and performance. 
Intentional airflow: Air is strategically pulled in above the keyboard and in the Cryo-Chamber, and out four exhaust vents on the sides. 
Quiet and cool: Expertly designed fans keep the system running smoothly and quietly. 
Built to last: Efficient thermal design protects internal components and extends the life of the system.

Advanced thermals for extended play 

Our advanced cooling technology, Alienware Cryo-tech, is designed to maintain system stability even during the most demanding sessions. 
Dual fans 

Two fans with ultra-thin blades pull cool air in from the top and bottom; exhaust hot air out 4 vents to help enable higher performance. 
Copper heat pipes: Three copper heat pipes dissipate heat from the CPU and GPU ensuring seamless gaming. 
Blend into any environment 

Activate Stealth Mode with F7 to switch performance to Quiet Mode for a more subtle, covert experience. 
Quiet mode lowers noise produced by your system's cooling fans when possible. While your computer's performance might be slightly impacted, this option may also reduce both CPU and GPU power consumptions.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Premium Power and Performance in a Sleek Gaming Package.The Alienware 16 Aurora Gaming Laptop is an absolute beast and lives up to the Alienware name in every way. From the moment it boots up, you can tell this machine is built for serious gaming and high-performance use. Everything about it feels fast, smooth, and premium.The 16-inch display is gorgeous, with sharp visuals, rich colors, and fluid motion that makes games feel immersive and responsive. Fast-paced action looks incredibly smooth, and the larger screen size is perfect for both competitive gaming and cinematic single-player experiences. It’s just as impressive for everyday tasks, streaming, and creative work.Performance is where this laptop truly shines. Games load quickly, run smoothly, and maintain strong frame rates even during intense moments.Multitasking is effortless, whether you’re gaming, streaming, or running demanding applications. Cooling is well-managed, keeping temperatures under control during long sessions without excessive noise.Build quality is excellent. The chassis feels solid and durable while still looking sleek and modern. The keyboard is comfortable with great key travel, making long gaming sessions easy on the hands, and the customizable lighting adds a nice touch without being over the top. Ports are well-placed and plentiful, making it easy to connect accessories and external displays.For a gaming laptop, battery life is surprisingly respectable during lighter use, and overall reliability has been excellent. The Alienware 16 Aurora strikes a great balance between raw power, design, and usability.If you’re looking for a high-end gaming laptop that delivers outstanding performance, a beautiful display, and premium build quality, the Alienware 16 Aurora Gaming Laptop is absolutely worth it. A true five-star experience.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I recently purchased the Alienware 16 Aurora Gaming Laptop AC16250, and it has exceeded my expectations in every way. The WQXGA display is absolutely stunning—crisp, vibrant colors with incredible sharpness that make both gaming and everyday use a joy. Playing fast-paced titles feels smooth and immersive thanks to the high refresh rate and excellent brightness levels.Performance-wise, this machine is a beast. The combination of cutting-edge graphics and a powerful processor handles demanding games effortlessly, with no lag or stutter. Even when multitasking—streaming, editing, and gaming simultaneously—the laptop remains responsive and reliable.The design is sleek and modern, with Alienware’s signature build quality that feels premium and durable. The cooling system is impressive too; even during extended gaming sessions, the laptop stays cool and quiet compared to others I’ve owned.Battery life is solid for a gaming laptop, and the keyboard is comfortable with customizable lighting that adds a nice personal touch.Overall, the Alienware 16 Aurora AC16250 is a fantastic investment for gamers who want top-tier performance, a gorgeous display, and a machine that looks as good as it performs. Highly recommended!

Usually though, they are pricy - whereas this one was perfectly within budget.My partner doesn't use the system enough on battery to really say anything about battery life, but it would seem to be average as to what is expected.The display looks nice and high quality, and it functions as it should. productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Been using this laptop for a few months. In general it does great with the games I play, runs Civilization 7 and several other games I have tried pretty well, battery life isn't great but thats pretty typical for this sort of laptop. Its more than fast enough for all normal productivity tasks. I travel for work and so I bought it mostly to use for work when I travel but I like to play games in the hotel. It can be a bit loud if the fan is running full out, but under most conditions its fairly quiet and can get pretty warm on your lap if you are say playing games on the couch. Overall I have been very happy especially at the price I paid back in NOV.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on February 13, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This thing is extremely slick.  Even though looking right at a picture, I still didn't expect it to be so futuristic looking, it's very cool.  Booted through all the usual welcome junk, established account etc, and imported all my settings and bookmarks no problem.  Then immediately disabled all the M$ bloat i could and chained that monster to the wall in shackles.  Running on chrome, disabled the blinky keyboard in settings (now its just solid backlit a sinister red).  And we're off to the races.  The response is very immediate and "buttery" as they say, and the screen is very sharp - I went to check out some 4K nature stuff, and it's incredibly sharp and vivid in fullscreen.  I don't know how it games, I didn't buy it for that.  I bought it so I can have multiple tabs open, a movie, and still browse other things and open new tabs without it getting bogged down, which it is more than adequate for.  Good price for this powerful of a laptop, it's obviously trying to compete with some really high end machines and doing a pretty good job of it.  But beware, it is BIG.  This is a portable battle-station, doesn't make for a very sleek backpack laptop to lug around as a daily driver.  I normally don't buy for looks, so i would've walked right past this in the store, but the guts came in this cool package and I admit, I like the sci-fi appearance - even if I'm not their target audience.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on November 24, 2025

ASUS won’t let me exchange the laptop with the same model for some reason which I think is completely valid because the laptop is DEFECTIVE. I’ve been messaging back and forth with support about fixes and updates that they said would fix the problem and it hasn’t. If you get a laptop like mine with ANY touchpad issues AT ALL immediately return it! This is absolutely ridiculous for a $1000 laptop.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: False Advertising - Received Significantly Lower Specs Than DescribedFalse Advertising - Received Significantly Lower Specs Than Described
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I am disappointed with this purchase. The product description clearly stated that this HP Victus gaming laptop would feature an Intel Core i5 13th Gen 13420H processor, an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 with 6GB of GDDR6 memory, and 16GB of DDR4-3200 RAM. The listing also highlighted these specifications as key features for 'fast and efficient performance' and 'excellent gaming visuals.'However, the laptop I received is the HP Victus 15-fa0033dx, and the actual specifications are significantly different and inferior to what was advertised:* Processor: Instead of the 13th Gen i5-13420H, it has a 12th Gen Intel Core i5-12450H. As the description itself acknowledges, this is a weaker processor.* Graphics Card: While it does have an RTX 3050, it only has 4GB of GDDR6 VRAM, not the advertised 6GB. This is a crucial difference for gaming performance.* RAM: The received unit has only 8GB of DDR4 RAM, half of the 16GB that was promised, impacting multitasking and potentially gameplay smoothness.The other specifications, such as the 512GB SSD and the 15.6" FHD 144Hz display, appear to be consistent. However, the discrepancies in the processor, GPU VRAM, and RAM are substantial and completely undermine the performance level I expected based on the product description.This is a clear case of misleading information and false advertising. Potential buyers need to be aware that the listed specifications are not what they might receive. The seller absolutely needs to include the specific model number (HP Victus 15-fa0033dx in this case) in their product description to avoid this kind of bait-and-switch.I will be seeking a return/refund due to this significant misrepresentation."

Je voulais remplacer mon Lenovo yoga qui venait de rendre l’âme.Je me suis intéressé à la gamme “chromebook” plutôt par curiosité au regard du prix.Après avoir lu des dizaines de classements je me suis lancé sur ce modèle.Il est tout à fait adapté à mon usage basique pour le moment : bureautique, navigation sur le web et creation/maintenance d’un site web.Si vous avez d’autres usages, ce n’est pas le modèle adapté (pas assez de memoire, puissance, et installation de programmes de retouches vidéo/image est impossible)Cerise sur le gâteau : 100go offert sur G Drive à l’achat du produit.Donc maintenant j’ai migré tout mon contenu sur G.Drive et ca me suit partout.En plus sa batterie tient bien le choc et vous pouvez l’utiliser de longues heures avant que celui ci ne vous lacheQuestion perf, l’ordi supporte sans problème la navigation avec une dizaine d’onglets ouverts.La lecture de vidéo YouTube, Netflix ou autre ne pose aucun problème : pas de ralentissement, belle image et son clair avec l’équipement Bang et Olufsen.Encore une fois, attention les puristes. Je suis dans un usage de fort nomadisme, je juge donc en fonction de ce critère également.La dalle tactile répond bien.Bémol mon casque Bluetooth Sony n’est pas reconnu :(Sur le fond, je ne regrette pas l’achat. Sur la forme non plus.Bon le look fait un peu plastique fragile et son format carré est assez inhabituelLe clavier est assez petit et demande un petit temps d’adaptation mais les touches sont confortables et la rédaction de documents ne pose plus de problème.Il est léger et donc facilement transportable.Dommage que HP livre cet ordinateur avec un chargeur traditionnel légèrement plus petit que ceux d’un pc mais ils auraient pu aller au bout de la démarche en miniaturisant cette partie la également.Donc produit idéal pour les nomades et si vous n’avez pas un usage autre que bureautique/ web … gamer et apprenti videaste/photographe, passez votre chemin :)

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Excellent for the home officeExcellent for the home office
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This all-in-one PC is awesome - even though it’s got a big screen, it saves a lot of space on my desk.  Love the 24” (well, 23.8”) curved screen and even though it’s more immersive working or watching videos, it doesn’t feel like it’s crowding me.  The screen quality is very nice and clear with great colors. Performance is very zippy with the Core i7 and 16GB RAM.  I see zero lag for things like working on documents, browsing, and watching videos (from the HDD or streaming). With the 512 GB SSD, it boots up quick and apps open fast, along with plenty of storage. Sound quality is also good even with the speakers facing backwards - it’s loud enough and clear. There are plenty of ports including 6 USB ports, HDMI, ethernet, headphone and mic ports, it’s even got a VGA port if you’re stuck in the 2000’s!  The wifi is very stable with excellent speeds up and down. The stand has one screw to secure it and it’s very stable when upright.  And it has a tilt option so it can adjust to your eye level.One weird quirk, the system keeps going to sleep after about 10 seconds when a keyboard is plugged in.  This is true with the included keyboard as well as another one I had and tried. Some software glitch that I couldn’t solve.  But this isn’t a big deal for me as I have a wireless keyboard/mouse combo that I use.Overall, I find this machine to be a good value for the money

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I purchased this laptop in January, and by March, it was already showing major issues. Using it has been incredibly frustrating.Unfortunately, I didn’t dig deep enough into reviews before buying and was misled by overly positive ones. After running into these problems, I did more research and discovered that this model is widely known for poor performance and reliability.I called HP and they told me that Amazon or 3rd party sellers modify the laptop from the original 4 GB RAM to 16 GB. This laptop is not compatible with 16 GB, and that's why this is a piece of garbage.HP also informed me that there are many customers who are experiencing the same problem, but because the laptop was modified by a third party, they can’t honor the warranty or provide technical support for the device in its current configuration.I strongly recommend avoiding this laptop. productPageReviews.reviewTitle: A lightweight, fast Windows laptop with a great screen, but it runs hotA lightweight, fast Windows laptop with a great screen, but it runs hot
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: TL;DR: This HP OmniBook 3 is light, fast for everyday tasks, and has a genuinely impressive OLED display with fast charging and solid battery life. The keyboard and trackpad feel great, and I haven't run into any app compatibility issues despite the ARM-based processor. My main complaints are that it runs hot enough to need propping up for airflow, and I had some wifi instability during the initial setup.I chose this laptop to use as a family laptop for everyday tasks like homework, browsing, and light gaming, and so far it has handled that well.Out of the box, the build quality is solid and the laptop is noticeably lightweight, which makes it easy to move around the house. The silver finish looks clean and not overly flashy.The display is the standout feature here. It does appear to be a true OLED panel, with excellent brightness and color in normal indoor lighting, and no glare issues. Typing is comfortable with good key travel, and the trackpad tracks well with a satisfying click.Performance for everyday use, browsing, email, documents, and multiple tabs, has been fast and smooth. I haven't run into any app compatibility problems so far, which is worth noting since this laptop uses a Snapdragon (ARM) processor rather than a traditional Intel or AMD chip. Roblox, which is our household's main game, has run without issue. Heavier or less common software may still see occasional friction on this platform, so it's worth checking compatibility for anything specific you rely on.Setup was fairly quick and easy, aside from repeated wifi disconnections while trying to log into my Windows account. I'm not certain if that was the laptop or my network, since none of my other devices had issues during that same window, but it's worth flagging in case others run into it. Wifi has been stable since setup finished.Battery life has been strong so far. After a few hours of use, it was still above 70 percent. Fast charging lives up to the claim too, charging noticeably quickly.Ports are generous for a laptop this size: two USB-C, two USB-A, one HDMI, and a headphone jack. I tested all four USB ports and everything worked without issue.The one real downside is heat. This laptop runs hot, and because the fans are on the bottom, I've found I need to prop it up to keep airflow going and keep the temperature manageable. If you plan to use this on your lap for extended periods, that's worth knowing going in.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Strong Battery Life and Vibrant OLED Display, But Upgrades Are LimitedStrong Battery Life and Vibrant OLED Display, But Upgrades Are Limited
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I replaced an aging, premium Google Pixelbook C0A with the HP OmniBook 3 14 inch Next Gen AI PC (Model 14-hz0288nr.)  The display is a very nice 14”  OLED panel. While its 2K resolution (1920x1200) is lower than my former laptop's high-resolution screen, I noticed a slight screen-door effect and odd text if I look closely. Running ‘cttune’ helped the text to look much better.This model is not a convertible and does not feature a touchscreen. It may take a few days to break the habit of touching the display to pinch and zoom or scroll. Additionally, while the OmniBook 3 series offers backlit keyboard options, this specific configuration lacks one.In terms of physical layout, USB-C ports are located exclusively on the left side. Because my couch setup has the charging cable coming from the right, I have to route the cord under the laptop while plugged in. However, because the battery easily lasts 3 to 4 days on lightweight tasks, it rarely needs to stay plugged in. The included tiny GaN charger is a great touch.Performance and thermals are solid improvements over my old setup. My previous Google Pixelbook ran very hot, but the Snapdragon X ARM processor in this laptop stays much cooler during use.I use a Wi-Fi 7 mesh router at home, but this laptop is equipped with a Qualcomm Wi-Fi 6E module. As a result, it connects to the 6GHz spectrum, but it cannot support Multi-Link Operation (MLO) or connect to multiple frequency bands simultaneously. This is still fine for my use-case which is mostly browsing.While this laptop lacks a fingerprint scanner, it does have IR Facial Recognition along with a physical slider to cover the camera. Having a built-in 3.5mm audio jack is also a welcome feature.Windows 11 ARM generally works fine with existing installers, but I did run into issues with a few apps that needed a specific ARM download instead of the x64 download. That is just something to be aware of.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Fast, Efficient, and Incredible Battery LifeFast, Efficient, and Incredible Battery Life
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Just a fantastic all-around speedy little laptop! Excellent display, fast performance with the Snapdragon processor, and the best battery life I've ever had on a laptop.  Great alternative to the MacBook Neo and at a cheaper price on Windows 11 ARM (just like the regular Win11).  I'd give this a strong recommendation for any student going back to school this Fall as it should provide everything they need and will last for many years to come.  RAM is uber-expensive these days and this configuration provides an adequate 16gb of it, so that should be plenty for schoolwork and most games.Upon receiving this laptop, I charged it overnight and it's still at 60% battery after nearly a full week of very light use w/o having to charge it again.  This battery is legit.  Our last laptop lasted like 3-4 hours and now needs to be permanently plugged in to function, so this is an incredible upgrade.  As far as setting up, it was easier than expected.  Laptops of the past had so many pre-installed bloatware, but this only had McAfee AV.  That took about 30 seconds to uninstall, and it was replaced by another app I already owned (Malwarebytes).  There wasn't much more to do other than that but to install iCloud and setup the Edge browser with my usual favorite bookmarks.As far as being an "AI PC", that's more marketing speak.  Any laptop can run AI in the cloud and the more ram you have, the quicker it is to run AI locally.  With the speedy components this laptop provides, I guess you can call it AI-Ready.  They mention Otter.AI in the details, but all they do is give you a 30-day free trial.  Stick with CoPilot or whatever AI tool you are already paying for.  Get this laptop if you're on a budget, want the best value laptop, and one that should last for several years and still keep up with the latest software.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Entry level Windows laptop, good starter for students or people just getting into computers.Entry level Windows laptop, good starter for students or people just getting into computers.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This is a solid entry level laptop if your demands are just web browsing, word processing and light productivity.  I bought this laptop for my daughter going into 4th grade as she has been learning coding, typing, amongst other computer related things in her school.  The 14" 2K display is sharp and the extra vertical space with the 16:10 aspect ratio, makes a difference for browsing and working versus a standard 16:9 screen. While I am personally an Intel person with a little dabble in AMD when I was younger... the Snapdragon X processor handles daily tasks smoothly with no noticeable lag and battery life while varies with usage, it was pretty close to advertise in terms of the hours.  A negative though with the battery, is that it would have been great if HP provided software that threshold charges the battery like my Lenovo Thinkpad X1 does, unfortunately HP does not have this software.  The battery goes to 100% all the time.  The build quality feels very plasticky.  The cover is able to open with 1 hand, but requires slight effort.  The touch pad is large and has gestures.  There is also an option to enable the gesture to adjust screen brightness and sound volume with the sides of the touchpad.  It takes some getting used to, but not difficult by any means.  The keyboard is not backlit and does not feel soft.  The keys feel very average tier to me and the font used on the keys looked kind of weird to me.  Its like HP was trying to make the key fonts edgy and techy.  For example X looks like ><.  Anyways, the keyboard will work, but if you have used better keyboards, you will definitely notice the difference with the feedback.Because there isn't much on the internet on this OmniBook 3 and I like to tinker with computers.  The first thing I did after taking it out of the box was opening up the laptop from the back to see what kind of guts we are dealing with.  There are 4 easily stripped screws that hold this laptop together (so be VERY careful).  Unscrew the front 2 screws and then the rear right screw first.  The screw on the rear left does not come off of the shell (there's a small washer that keeps it in place).  When that one is unscrewed it kind of pops the rear shell cover up.  Now comes the hard part.  The cover is made of plastic and it feels exactly how filmsy plastics feel.  I carefully pried with my finger nails open from the back first.  Then made my way to the sides.  Once all the sides were loose, its time to just pop the front.  The plastic shell clicks and clacks into and out of place and really did not want me to be messing around with it.  Once I finally got the rear cover off there really wasn't much to see here (check my pictures).  The 16GB RAM is onboard with no slots to expand.  The only part that is worth while to upgrade whenever prices come back down to Earth is the NVME.  That at least is upgradeable.  The included NVME is a FORESEE Gen 3x4 XP1100 256GB.  To be honest, I have never heard of this brand even though they have been around for almost 3 decades.  I would have thought HP would have just used their own HP NVME drives (I guess they were trying to cut costs here).  Anyhow, I will be switching that out with a Samsung or SK Hynix 2TB NVME as soon as there's a good sale.Once I put everything back together, I started the laptop and went through the usual Windows 11 setup.  I had to create my admin account first before I created and linked my daughter's Microsoft child account through the family setup.  There were several updates that had to be done during initial boot and as soon as my account was setup, so it took about 40 minutes or so (maybe an hour) until I really was able to use the laptop.  When I was able to start looking through the programs and applications, as expected, there are bloatwares that came with this laptop.  I removed the majority of the crap that I would not be using.  Hey, I only have 256GB, I can't have these bloatwares taking up the valuable storage space!  Going through Windows, browsers, and apps, the laptop was snappy and responsive.  The only thing that slowed me down was getting used to the touchpad.  I watched a few Youtube videos and thought the speakers, which are located on the bottom of the laptop where your hands would rest when typing, was just okay.  It sounded a bit hollow.  Maybe I can tweak it, but honestly, I really don't think my daughter cares how the speakers sound.  For watching Youtube videos and what not, the speakers are fine at this price point.  I think the placement could have been better, instead of under the laptop where the sound bounces off the desk.  I'm sure HP thought about it and some analysis they ran told them this was the most optimal speaker position for this laptop frame ¯\_(ツ)_/¯.I do have to give HP credit for the port arrangement of this OmniBook 3.  There are 2 USB-C ports (1 will be taken up by charging unless you use a USB-C hub with PD), 2 USB-A ports (1 on each side at the rear of the laptop), 1 HDMI port and 1 3.5mm headphone jack.  The reason why I say HP deservers credit for the port placement is this.  The HDMI and 2 USB-C ports are all on the same side (left side).  This allows better cable management for people running a vertical laptop setup and using an external monitor via HDMI, and a USB-C hub where they can connect their external keyboards, mouse, ethernet cable etc. and keep the all the cabling behind the desk.  And because the HDMI and USB-C ports are on the left side, when placing the laptop vertical, fans are blowing off to the side and not towards me.  I can slot the laptop down in a stand and then hold it up and power it on and slot it back down easily.  I have had experience with a Dell laptop where the ports are HDMI is on 1 side, USB-Cs on the other side.  It made it very annoying for a vertical laptop setup with needing extension cables running and in plain sight.  I have OCD with cable management so it triggered me every time I saw it. It was a work laptop and I had to use it temporarily.  I could not run back to my personal Thinkpad setup fast enough once I was able to get back on it.Before I decided on getting a Windows laptop for my daughter; my wife and I deliberated on whether to get my daughter the Macbook Neo.  Since my daughter has an iPad Air already, she is familiar with the Apple ecosystem.  Apple's entry level MacBook Neo, starts at the similar price point at $599.  The Neo only comes with 8GB of non-upgradeable RAM and a smaller 13" display, versus the HP OmniBook 3's 16GB and larger 14" 2K screen.  So spec for spec, the HP wins on paper for the same money, more memory, more screen real estate, and a higher resolution display.  The thing with Macs though, is that the MacOS is optimized in a way where it can run similar apps to a Windows without utilizing the same amount of RAM.  So in the end it really comes down to personal preference if you are deciding between the two operating systems.  I decided to just go with a Windows laptop, because my daughter's school teaches with a Windows laptop.  Had her school taught with a Mac, I would have gone that route.At the price of $579 (at the time of review), that 256GB NVME size feels cheap in 2026.  Between Windows updates, apps, and a media library, you'll be managing space constantly or rely on cloud storage (OneDrive, Dropbox etc.) or external SSD drives.  A 512GB option should really be the standard at this price, not an upsell.  It is worth noting that the MacBook Neo has the same 256GB starting point, so this isn't unique to HP, but it's still a fair complaint at this price.  Another beef I had was how scary the plastics all felt and sounded when I was trying to take the back cover off to see the internals.  I really hope I do not break anything the next time I go in there to change out the NVME for a 2TB.  Anyways, the HP OmniBook 3 model HZ0288NR is fine for an entry level basic laptop for people who do not demand much from their computer.  If your use is just web browsing, light productivity, non-graphic intensive games and media consumption (Youtube, Netflix etc), this laptop will perform well for that purpose.  The 2K screen is bright and clear.  The Snapdragon X processor performed with no issues.  I did not try to run any benchmarks, I think that's a bit excessive for this kind of laptop at this price point.  In real world use for the kind of person I described above who would be a user of this laptop, none of those numbers matter.  All that matters is there's no lag when moving from app to app, website to website and video to video; this OmniBook 3 does that.  I am certain my daughter would be happy with her first laptop.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Amazing 4k display quality. Excellent battery performance. Lightweight compact design.Amazing 4k display quality. Excellent battery performance. Lightweight compact design.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I find this HP Omnibook 3 an awesome personal laptop next to my work HP ZBook. The size is excellent at 12.75" wide and 9" deep. The thickness is between 0.82" and 0.75", which is still thin enough to stack on top of my large 16" work laptop in travel bag. The weight is very light at 3 lbs 1 oz. I often find myself wishing I could use this laptop for quick work tasks as so much more convenient.To the point of convenience, the battery life is excellent, reminding me of tablets where charging constantly not a concern. In my test, I conducted about six hours of continuous use within a 26 hour period. The battery status showed 40% life remaining. The night before, the battery was at 41%, thus has a great standby. I used continuously another two hours and finally received a low power mode prompt at 30%. Another hour of use and turned off at 20%. Charging back up with the included 65 watt charger was fast, taking about two hours. I noted zero heat concerns from both the charger and battery area. The included USB-C cable is really thick and not very flexible. I prefer to use my own high wattage braided cable with no problems. I did notice wattage stays at about 55 watts with an occasional spike near the 65 watt mark. The max wattage on the power meter peaked at 62.4 watts.The available ports is your typical HP with two USB-C, one HDMI and one USB-A on the left side. The right side has one USB-A and surprisingly one headphone jack. Has always drove me crazy not to put a USB-C on the right side for devices like external monitors with ports on one side vs the other. In my case, I have to have a cable that runs to the other side of the monitor, which means more long cables to carry. The USB-C powers up my external display, at ~3.3 watts, with my own cable - the included charge cable does not pass display data.I did have a problem after first navigating through the initial setup to include using Co-Pilot a few times. I charged the laptop overnight and would not turn on. The charge light was white (between the two USB-C ports) indicating full charge. I pressed the power key but was slow blinking white. I forced shut down by holding power until light went off, waited 30 seconds, and powered on fine after. I then had message that updates were underway, which rebooted again and everything fine. I immediately noticed the packaged Mcfee virus software committing 0.188 GB of memory at idle, 0.7+ GB during scan and a total of 8.5 GB for the duration. At the end of the scan, I received a HYPERVISOR ERROR blue screen at the end of said scan. I always uninstall these packaged scanners anyhow which triggered Defender to kick automatically. I have not had any problems since. The included OS is Win 11 Home 25H2 with build 26200.9168. After removal, the total usage is idling at 6.5 GB. There is no keyboard backlight which is bit of a bummer for compact laptop. The touchpad does mistakenly minimize all windows when scrolling with two fingers but this could be a setting I need to adjust. The SSD drive and USB-C data transfer is your standard 1 GB max transfer rate. The hard drive is not the greatest size at 250 GB (237 actual). With the decent transfer rates and cloud storage services these days, I don't have any concerns with it. I appreciate the display camera has a little switch to cover the lens as other HPs also have.The display brightness is the greatest I've ever seen. So much so that nearly blinded me in a dim lit room. After using Edge, Chrome, and G Drive, the total memory idles at 10.4 GB of the 8 available CPUs. Only two of those CPUs are typically used. I did stream an 8k video (actual 4k max) and bumped memory up to 12.5 GB usage. I noticed definite strain with 1-2 second delays in loading up video and minimizing / maximizing window. More CPUs kicked in ranging from 4-5 but never had any major strains and no where close to the 100% total. The video was amazing and one of the most beautiful I have seen on a laptop. The colors were vibrant, HDR amazing and detail extremely sharp. The sound is very good for such a compact laptop, much better than my ZBook. I would have no concerns cozying up in bed and watching a full movie on this.I am extremely happy with this laptop once everything configured to my liking. I feel the price is great and an excellent value.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I came from the world of Thinkpads to fall for this Legion. I had (still have) a Lenovo Thinkpad X1 Extreme 2nd with i7-9750H, 64GB of RAM, 3TB of storage, 4K OLED touch panel and the GTX 1650 max-Q. I purchased this laptop in 2019 when it was announced (very pricey, but it was one of the best). It was very good at the beginning, but his thinness was a major flaw because it was overheating like hell with time passing. Since my work requires a powerhouse laptop with both the CPU and GPU, my laptops couldn't handle the workload anymore. I use a lot of virtualization labs and video rendering and it takes too much time to render one video session. So I looked for a replacement and found this Legion and I was quite impressed but a bit disappointed. Here are the pros and cons:Pros:- Very light: almost the same weight as my older Thinkpad- The OLED screen is amazing (The thinkpad was a bit better because of its 4K panel, but less bright than the Legion)- The CPU is sooo powefull and everything is snappy. The GPU is also very good for my needs (I'm not a hardcore gamer, just a casual one)- The laptop is quiet all the time, but the fans kick like a jet taking off when I run some heavy tasks (video rendering) lol. I don't mind the noise for performance.- The lid can be opened with one hand, not like my old Thinkpad- The webcam quality is way better than my Thinkpad's- You can switch between performance modes using Fn+Q shortcut- You can overclock the GPU and undervolt the CPU (haven't tried it yet)- the HDMI and power port are located behind the laptop- Webcam switch to enable/disable itCons:- Only 16GB of RAM for this price, which make it pricier- No fingerprint scanner or Windows Hello compatible Webcam- Typing on the Legion's keyboard is quite good, but not as delicious as the ThinkPad (1.5mm key travel vs 1.8mm for the Thinkpad)- in my opinion, the numpad keyboard wasn't necessary since by adding it, they had to shift the keyboard to the left which needs you to get used to it.- The black color is a fingerprint magnet.- The battery life is average. Coming from my Thinkpad that had less than 2h of battery life, I can squeeze more than the Thinkpad if I enable the Quiet mode and reduce the screen's brightness. But it's more than enough for me since I'm plugged in almost all the time- No SD card reader and not enough portsRegarding the delivery, Amazon used the " Lenovo Legion 5i Gaming laptop...." instead of "Lenovo Legion 5 15IRX10", which is the accurate name of the product, and that created an issue with the customs. Please Amazon, next time use the real name of the product because there are many models and generations of the Legion 5.I received the laptop 2 weeks ago, so I'll wait to see if there are any other issues.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: What a nightmare. I've had this laptop for nearly 7 months and nothing but problems. I've replaced the bottom cover three times due to the rubber feet coming off. I replaced the fans and the heat sink after the fans went and couldn't find fans alone. Now, my spacebar is busted, and keycaps are nowhere to be found. The spacebar is the first warranty claim I've put in simply because I cannot find the parts without replacing the entire keyboard and armrest. The plastic coating is already starting to wear significantly, too.Basically, this laptop looks and functions as though it were already several years old. Not worth it. I regret this laptop purchase enormously. Don't make the mistake I did. Unacceptable build quality. Once I have the spacebar sorted, I'm selling it immediately and getting a different laptop.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on March 17, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: It's cool. Still overpriced but what isn't these days
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Looks fine so far(probably update more later). Confused as to why it didn't come with some type of owners manual or paperwork at all (that's why it's 4 stars) also FYI this model tends to get stuck on a massive BIOS update for over an hour so be patient and wait it out.Update: gaming is excellent. Well compared to my Series S it's great. Don't know if that comparison qualifies or not but yes it's better. BUT I'm into streaming movies as much as I game and the streaming quality (to me) isn't great. I do have a brutal OCD with movie quality so it's probably better to everyone else than it is to me but still. I can't get passed the brightness "rings" that happen in dark areas. Brightness/contrast adjustment does nothing and I'm sure I'm not the only one who thinks Windows HDR settings are junk. Actually, speaking of,I tried the HDR and the black borders that surround widescreen movies end up with "bleach" glitches or strands that pop out at you. I turned it off they went away but the rings in shadows still is very present. This was my last serious purchase before I slave it out for the next 2 years to make the money back and I don't think its worth it at all. Maybe 8-900$ but 1500! Hell no. Never again. Oh and for some reason Youtube only allows me to stream at 480p nothing higher at all on this 15 hundred dollar device. I get 1080p off my 6 year old kindle. So wtf with that...
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on March 26, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Review after had the laptop about two weeks
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I paid about $1,700 after tax for this Lenovo Legion 5i, and honestly, it’s beyond my expectations. The performance is smooth across everything I’ve tried — from everyday tasks to heavy gaming. The build feels solid, the cooling does a great job while keeping the fan noise really low  and the display is sharp and immersive.At this price point, I feel like it’s absolutely worth it. The only area I’d suggest for improvement is RAM — the system is strong out of the box, but with more RAM it could unlock even more potential, especially for multitasking and future-proofing.Overall, I’m very satisfied and would definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a reliable, high-performance gaming laptop.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on September 23, 2025

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This laptop for gaming is excellent. I was having issues with frames per second in Diablo IV and 7 Days to Die. It is also nice that there is another slot to upgrade the storage in the future, but I find 1TB is enough for my use. I mainly use this to game when I go on a trip. I have a desktop PC for gaming at home.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: ive had this for about 3 days now, and after all the updates i can say this is a pretty good starter laptop. the battery life with the gpu on eco and battery saver on and everything on power saving mode can get you about 5.5-6 hours on one charge, which is more than enough. even if the battery runs low throughout the day, you can bring the charger and plug it in and be goood to go in about an hour. the speed is pretty instantanious. when i open a tab or search something up it pops up almost immediantly. the screen quality has been good for the games i play and so is the cooling. the only game ive really tested is roblox but roblox has some intense games that spawn a lot of things on your screen at once, and this laptop didnt crash at all. i am yet to test any AAA games but i am almost certain it can handle those too. when gaming the fans cant be heard through a headset and they provide really good airflow throughout the laptop. the keys or touchpad never really get warm and it never overheats. for 990, this laptop is basically a steal. between the build quality, large screen, backlit keyboard, and amazing cooling, 990 is great, not to mention the battery doesnt just drain when its off the charger, even without battery saver on and all the graphics card on standard so it might activate sometimes, you can still expect 3.5-4 hours out of this laptop. i would recommend buying this if you just want to dip your feet into the gaming laptop scene and also if you want to have a laptop that can run some AAA titles and take notes/run certain coding programs or engineering programs.
