features: 【Powerful AND Ryzen 7 7735Hs Processor】Unleash elite responsiveness with the robust AMD Ryzen 7 7735HS processor, engineered on advanced Rembrandt architecture with a high-performance 54W TDP. Effortlessly compile code, run resource-heavy business software, or handle complex spreadsheet macros with rapid processing speeds that optimize daily workflow efficiency for college students and business professionals.

【Ultimate 17.3" Widescreen Laptop For Max Productivity】 Experience desktop-level viewing on this premium 17.3-inch Full HD laptop, featuring a crisp 1080P resolution and a classic 16:9 aspect ratio. Ideal for professional data analysis, split-screen multitasking, or immersive movie streaming, this expansive workspace drastically reduces eye strain during long hours of remote work, online learning, or casual entertainment in your home office.

【Next-Gen Expandable DDR5 Ram & Dual PCIE 4.0 SSD】Maximize system response times with high-speed dual-channel DDR5 SO-DIMM memory and dual M.2 2280 PCIe 4.0x4 solid-state drive slots. Enjoy near-instantaneous boot times and rapid application loading, while the expandable storage architecture provides ample space to store massive project assets, media libraries, and heavy software local files without lag.

【Integrated AMD Radeon 680M Graphics & Rich Audio】 Harness stunning visual processing power with integrated AMD Radeon 680M graphics based on advanced RDNA 2 architecture. Perfectly tailored for light gaming, smooth casual photo editing, and high-definition video playback, beautifully complemented by dual premium 2W stereo speakers that deliver crystal-clear audio during virtual business meetings or home entertainment.

【Next-Gen Blazing-Fast Wifi 6E Connectivity】 Stay seamlessly connected anywhere with cutting-edge WiFi 6E technology, supporting the ultra-fast 2.4GHz, 5GHz, and 6GHz bands alongside Bluetooth 5.2. Experience ultra-low latency, stable cloud data syncing, and buffer-free 4K video conferencing, making this office laptop perfect for congested home networks, dynamic workplace environments, or campus cafes.

【Versatile Dual Type-C Ports & 100W PD Fast Charging】Power through demanding schedules with the 58Wh smart Li-polymer battery, fully compatible with modern workflows. Package includes a premium 100W PD fast-charging adapter, while dual fully functional USB Type-C ports supporting Power Delivery and DisplayPort allow you to rapid-charge your portable device and connect external dual 4K monitors simultaneously.

【Ultra-Slim Metal Body & 180-Degree Flat Hinge】Crafted with premium double-sided A/D metal panels, this clamshell laptop boasts an upscale textured chassis. Weighing under 2.1kg and only 18.8mm thin, it slips easily into backpacks for on-the-go transport. The flexible 180-degree lay-flat hinge lets you conveniently share the screen with colleagues and classmates during group projects and meetings.

【Premium Backlit Keyboard & Secure Touchpad Fingerprint】Enhance input efficiency in dim environments with the premium full-size US-layout backlit keyboard, designed for comfortable, tactile typing. Safeguard your confidential information instantly with the secure fingerprint reader integrated seamlessly into the touchpad, enabling secure, password-free biometric login via Windows Hello in public spaces.

【Integrated HD Webcam With Privacy Shutter & Security】Take full control of your digital workspace privacy with the built-in 2MP HD front-facing web camera, featuring a physical camera privacy shutter. Together with an integrated Kensington lock slot and hardware-based SPI TPM security encryption, this business laptop provides reliable data protection against physical theft or unauthorized virtual access.

【Multi-Scenario Adaptability & 2-Year Warranty】Experience ultimate peace of mind with our dedicated American customer support and a premium laptop tailored for diverse modern lifestyles. Your purchase is fully backed by an industry-leading 2-year warranty and a hassle-free 90-day return or exchange policy, ensuring complete product reliability and long-term brand confidence.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: With a toddler, I grab laptop time in tiny windows. My old machine groaned through boot-up, but this Ryzen 7 fires up in seconds. Windows setup was breezy; I was inside apps before the kiddo finished his juice box. The fingerprint reader on the touchpad logs me in instantly, and the backlight helps when I’m typing in the dark during naps. Connectivity is a relief too—WiFi 6E stays solid even when the baby monitor and a tablet are hogging the network. The dual USB-C ports let me plug into my 4K monitor and charge at the same time via the included 100W adapter, so my workspace expands without swapping cables. The 17.3-inch 1080P screen is bright enough for small text and split tasks, and the Radeon 680M handles light editing without stutter. No spills yet, but the palm rest feels sturdy enough to survive sticky fingers.

From the manufacturer
Dell 27 All-in-One 

Get the performance you need and impressive visuals with a space-saving all-in-one desktop. 
27-inch FHD (1920 x 1080) Narrow Border Infinity NTCH Display with Wide Viewing Angle
Intel Core 5 processor 120U (12MB cache, 10 cores, 12 threads, up to 5.0 GHz)
Intel Graphics

Windows 11 brings you closer to what you love 

Family, friends, obsessions, music, creations Windows 11 is the one place for it all. With a fresh feel and tools that make it easier to be efficient, it has what you need for whatever’s next. 
Stunning display. Sleek design. 
Incredible visuals: The FHD IPS display features 99% sRGB within a narrow border so you can enjoy true-to-life colors and crisp resolution as you work, learn or stream. 
Eye comfort: This All-in-One display features Dell ComfortView Plus to help reduce harmful blue light and a flicker-free panel to optimize eye comfort. 
Optimize workspace: Keep your area clutter free with an innovative stand that has the perfect keyboard parking space underneath the display. 
Immersive audio 

Immerse yourself in a rich audio experience that's loud and clear with dual 5W speakers and Dolby Atmos spatial sound. 
Made for video chatting 

Put your best face forward, even in high-contrast lighting, with Wide Dynamic Range, on 5MP camera with a tilt feature that's adjustable from 0 ~ 20 degrees. And, when you're ready for privacy, simply push the pop-up camera down to hide it. 
Versatile functionality 

Enjoy a seamless experience with the Intel Core Processors and 512GB SSD. 
Connect multiple accessories with WiFi 6E capability and five USB ports. 
Expand your productivity with HDMI-in/HDMI-out ports that allow you to connect to a separate PC and use this one as a secondary monitor. 
WiFi 6E requires Windows 11 Operating system and compatible router. Router requires a separate purchase. WiFi 6E connectivity is only available in select locations. Check availability with your service provider. 
Availability depends on local government regulation. 
Environmental Standards and Design 

Your All-in-One is designed with sustainable materials including post-consumer recycled plastics and recycled steelwith an etched logo that reduces manufacturing waste.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: This is a very nice all-in-one computer
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I'm very happy with this Dell 27 All-in-One desktop. It offers excellent performance for daily tasks, multitasking, and even some light gaming thanks to the powerful Intel Core i7 150U processor and the NVIDIA GeForce MX570A discrete graphics. The 27-inch Full HD non-touch display provides bright, sharp visuals with good color and viewing angles, making it great for work and media consumption.The design is sleek and modern, and the all-in-one form factor saves a lot of desk space by integrating all components behind the monitor. Setup was straightforward, and all the included accessories like the keyboard and mouse work well. The only minor hurdle I encountered, which relates to Microsoft rather than Dell, was clearing out OneDrive software to enable backup to my NAS, but once configured, the system runs smoothly.Overall, this machine balances power, style, and convenience for home and office use perfectly. Highly recommended for anyone looking for a responsive, clutter-free desktop with ample RAM and storage for demanding applications.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Wow! So far so good. Delivered last night and just set it up today after acclimating from cold to warm. Easiest thing I’ve ever hooked up-basically plug n play. I have to get better acquainted with windows 11 because presently I’m feeling a bit lost. It’s like stumbling around in the dark! Well, actually it’s brighter and crisper than my old hp-both the desktop and laptop.Anyway, it’s a classy, beautiful set up and quite the change from the previous desktop menagerie. I’m not a gamer and just a retired person with less computer needs these days…so far. I didn’t think I’d like the keyboard and mouse but I actually do now that I’ve used them for awhile. The sound quality is good with dialogue and not good with anything but soft, mellow music perhaps.Anyway, let’s hope this lasts as long and as well as my oldies but goodies-that still work, they’re just not as fast or sprite as they once were…like me, I suppose.After using, I’ll add one caveat-I hate Windows 11! . What I’ve learned about this OS after purchasing this classy desktop has really upset me. I’m done with windows. We’re roped in because we’re used to their os and it was easy for them to implement all this garbage that most of us don’t understand and without extensive research will likely never know or understand.Here I come Linux!

features: Equipped with an Intel i3-N305 processor and robust memory capacity, the Lenovo A100 All-in-One (AIO) desktop simplifies everyday tasks with lightning-fast performance. Enjoy seamless video calls with crystal-clear audio, thanks to the optional 5MP webcam and dual-mic setup.

Relive cherished memories on this AIO desktop — view photo albums and videos on a stunning 23.8″ (24) Full HD (1920x1080) IPS Anti-glare 250nits, 99% sRGB display. The expansive, nearly borderless screen transforms every visual into a masterpiece, showcasing colors with great accuracy. Get pulled into an immersive world, combining clarity and vibrancy to enliven treasured moments.

Equipped with up to 32GB DDR4 memory, ensuring seamless multitasking across spreadsheets, web browsing, and business software. The up to 1TB PCIe M.2 SSD enables ultra-fast boot-up, quick file access, and efficient data transfers—perfect for handling large files, presentations, and daily workloads. Ports include 1x DC power in, 1x Ethernet (RJ45), 2 x USB-A (hi-speed USB), 2 x USB-A (USB 10Gbps), 1x HDMI-out, 1x headphone / mic combo.

With multiple ports, the Lenovo A100 AIO desktop provides versatile connectivity, keeping you ready for work, play, and everything in between. Expand your workspace with the HDMI output for dual displays, while fast WiFi 6 keeps you connected at every turn. Plus, enjoy a streamlined setup as you pair your devices via Bluetooth 5.2.

This A100 AIO desktop boasts a sleek design, blending elegance and functionality that suits any room. Adjust the stand from -5° to 25° for your ideal viewing angle and comfort. Moreover, the chic Cloud Grey finish gives it a stylish appeal, adding sophistication to your work area.

The original seal has been opened solely for upgrading purposes. A 3-year coverage on the upgraded RAM/SSD is provided by PCOnline US, while the remaining components retain the original 1-year manufacturer's coverage.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: 5⭐️ for what it is and is not
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Ok, so I got this as a portable option when I can’t or just don’t feel like using my PC. For the price the CPU (i5) and GPU (Nvidia 3050) is a pretty good combination for playing most games. I tested it using Cyberpunk 2077 which is known for eating up resources and it plays well on medium settings and does admirably on high settings with some lag in high graphically demanding areas with the occasional random lag. Playing less demanding games like Fallout 4 I have encountered no issues. The screen is decent for the price. If I had a complaint it would be I wish it was a bit brighter but for the price that is something I can easily overlook as an issue but put it out there in case it is something important to anyone reading this. The colors are pretty good…better than expected at this price point. For daily computing (web surfing, email, watching videos, and work/school) I won’t waste much time other than to say…nothing to worry about there and I would highly recommend this machine to students or professionals that want something that can handle gaming, basic use, and work/school use on a budget. Works well with wired/wireless controllers as well as other peripherals and again (for the price point) there are a generous amount of places to connect. Physically this laptop doesn’t look like some other brands that were clearly designed for gaming. I personally like that. I’m in my forties and don’t particularly love most of the gaming laptop designs especially when using it in a professional or academic environment. The build is primarily plastic but it doesn’t feel thin or cheap by any means (was expecting it too at this price). That being said, if you are taking this on the go it might be wise to pick up a carrying case with some padding to avoid damage if dropped, bumped, banged, etc. The battery life is OK. (Tip: Battery can be upgraded with an 80v Lenovo Legion battery) and you can add RAM pretty easily. I would recommend doing a bit of research if you are new to poking around inside of devices but as someone who is tech savvy and has a degree in cybersecurity and networking, I would say this is a pretty easy device to swap out components as far as that goes. Another nice feature is being able to physically block the web cam and the slider bar that does this is very discrete (nice little design touch). The weight of the device isn’t too bad and definitely much lighter than most gaming laptops I have used in the past. The cooling is pretty solid but like any laptop it can warm up under high demand usage but so far nothing concerning and I have not yet had to use a cooling pad out of concern (I do use them as a standard practice though). So in summation for an entry level gaming device, a multipurpose device (gaming/school/work) with a modern but classic look that is well built (physically) and has pretty solid hardware I would feel comfortable recommending this device. Great buy and would be a good buy for college students, professionals, parents who want to buy a multi purpose device for kids/ young adults.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: There's a learning curve with the ARM architecture
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This laptop has incredible features as it is designed to combine the capabilities of Windows with the convenience of a smartphone. It is showing itself to be ideal for me to have an organized system for research notes, online business, and helping the people around me, and being informed and prepared for daily accomplishments and relaxation. The design, features, and extras provided in this purchase are impressive. All the pros mentioned in the reviews and video unboxings I've seen around the web for previous years models are in this one. There is also significant effort to make more apps run natively on ARM, making the cons less con.Tradeoffs take place for those of us that take the option to switch out of S-Mode and use Windows 10 Pro. It takes educating ourselves about app compatibility. Specifically when downloading, if an app is expected to run natively or in emulated mode, or should it not be downloaded due to incompatibility. Once installed and running it's also possible to verify compatibility and make further adjustments and assessments.Be prepared to improvise a bit if you buy this PC. Expect to use Edge or Firefox browsers initially as they run ARM64 natively, and to set aside Chrome and Adobe for a while as they will noticeably lag. The need to use the Web version as well as the UWP version (from the Windows store) of common apps is emphasized, as most will run natively. Accessories which may be needed include a MicroSD card, a universal silicone gel case (when apart from the keyboard, the tablet can easily slip out of one's hands), a USB hub with pass-thru charging (there is only one USB Type C port on the device), a flash drive, and an external USB hard drive for backups.This is a great laptop for someone ready to innovate. I've only had to give up two apps due to lag or incompatibility, and the increased convenience is very noticeable. Although the ARM architecture eliminates some of the versatility enjoyed by having an Intel or other x64 chip, for me it seems to be a move in the right direction.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great value and it’s huge. Love it.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Great price, great quality. The stand is a real steel stand. I was surprised. Way more than I expected. It took just a few seconds to screw in the 3 screws. It’s well built.I’m not using this for gaming. I’m using this as a second screen for my IMac. It’s also how I want to watch YouTube videos when I’m taking a break but mostly I use it to play video and put a ton of different windows on this screen while I use my iMac screen for video editing. Works great for my needs.It’s running at 60hertz at 2560x1440 which is what I run on my iMac. It can go up to 3840x2160 if you want. For $180 it is well priced and offers a great value.The only negative is the on-screen menu which you really only need once. Unlike a joystick which you see on many monitors you have a series of buttons that have multiple functions and have to keep trying to navigate the menus. That was painful. But once I took it off ECO mode (which is on by default) and set the light on the back of the screen to a red glow I basically never have to use this again. The one pain point isn’t worth overlooking this monitor. It’s a great value in every other way, especially for its size.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Mixed Feelings on the SCEPTRE 32-inch IPS 4K UHD Monitor - Great Picture, Quality Control Issues
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Rating: ★★★☆☆ (3 out of 5 stars)Purchase Date: April 15, 2024Upon unboxing my three SCEPTRE 32-inch IPS 4K UHD Monitors, I was immediately concerned due to the rough condition of the packaging. Thankfully, none of the monitors appeared physically damaged at first glance. However, my relief was short-lived after setting them up.Positives:The image quality of these monitors is nothing short of stunning. The resolution of 3840 x 2160 delivers crisp, vibrant visuals that are a pleasure to look at. When it comes to screen clarity and color accuracy, these monitors certainly set a high bar when compared to others in the market. They offer a great viewing experience whether for work or leisure.Negatives:Unfortunately, the quality control seems to be lacking. Out of the three monitors, two arrived with noticeable dead pixels. These are not just minor imperfections; there are black streaks across the screen that are quite distracting and make the affected areas of the screen functionally useless for detailed work or enjoying media. This issue significantly detracts from the otherwise excellent display quality.Given the mixed experience, I am currently in the process of requesting replacements for the defective units. The potential of these monitors is clear, but the frequency of quality checks might need improvement, perhaps reflecting the lower price point and manufacturing compromises.Overall, if you're considering this monitor, be prepared for the possibility of having to deal with returns due to quality issues. When they work as intended, they are absolutely amazing, but it seems a bit of a gamble at this point.Recommendation:Buyers should be aware of potential quality control issues and prepare for the possibility of needing to request replacements. However, when the monitors are free from defects, they are exceptional in performance and value.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on April 19, 2024

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Incredible picture and quality for the price without wasted frills.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Since HDR isn't really all that great without like 1000nits anyways, and I'm using this for my mac studio as a work screen, I don't care about gaming or refresh rate (though 70hz is nice). I expected less than what this monitor gives. The stand is very sturdy and has a smaller footprint than the LG Ultrafine 27UN850-W it replaces. Picture is brighter and clearer after some basic adjustments. Color is perfectly -fine- if you're not a designer, especially at this price point. I will never test the speakers. I'm using a thunderbolt to display port adapter and everything works great. I love that there's not a bunch of gimmicky random features no one ever uses that usually aren't very well implemented in the first place like my other monitors, so it feels like I'm simply paying for a solid, reliably 32" 4k monitor and that's what I got. Had it for a few days now and as for it's sturdiness, I accidentally let this slip out of the box as I was opening it and it fell onto my polished concrete floor about a foot and a half and had zero cracks or anything. I was worried but no dead pixels or anything at all.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Nice Monitor for the Money, but with a Dead Pixel...
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The monitor itself is nice, the stand, while not height adjustable, really is robust and worked well. Picture quality is first rate...BUT, it has a dead pixel. I expect a new monitor to not have dead pixels. I have used many different bands over the years, Samsung, Dell, Viewsonic. Basically, the big boys of monitors, premium units. Never had a dead pixel. I have Dell monitors 10+ years old and no dead pixels in any of them. I decided to roll the dice with Sceptre. Unfortunately, it had a dead pixel right out of the box. I debated returning it and decided to just live with it, but it doesn't bode well for the future. IMHO, you get what you pay for and if you buy a bargain brand you get a bargain product. Not always the case but that seems to be the case here. I gave it three stars. I would probably not purchase this brand again, despite it having a lot of other positive attributes. At the end of the day, all the pixels have to work or you have failed in your mission to make a good monitor.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: And they say size doesn't matter...
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I've been using 4K screens since 2016, when i took a bet on a QNIX monitor. That lived long enough, and 4 years later, i had to replace it. But the only thing that was on my price range was a 27'' AOC monitor. Wow, i really missed the size. And then this one got a decent discount to $200, and i have no regrets at all. Color-wise and brightness-wise is better than the AOC monitors, and it is bigger.My unit came with three stuck pixels, but they're each on one corner, and the advantage of 4K is that pixels are tiny until you get into 60'' class screens, so they being stuck doesn't get noticeable at all. Also, my unit had no IPS glow at all.The second factor that made me buy this is the port selection. Most monitors have two, maybe three ports, usually one DP and two HDMI. HDMI is nerfed too, with only one 2.0 port and the other one being 1.4. To me it doesn't matter that one port is 1.4 since i just use that to connect my PS4, but usually i need to connect my laptop and a second PC via HDMI, so i've been using an HDMI splitter and leaving a rat's nest of cables behind the screen. Now, this monitor has TWO DP and TWO HDMI ports, so i can connect both my desktops, my laptop and my PS4, and everything gets 4k60 (except my PS4 because the mere idea of 4K makes it sound like a jet turbine), and even the PCs get 4K70 over DisplayPort.The 70 Hz thing... well, that's my issue with this monitor. It is too low to be really useful over 60 Hz (maybe 75-80 HZ would've been better) and even if some people can notice the difference, the fact that this monitor has no adaptive refresh (like Freesync) makes that feature almost useless as a concept. The only saving grace this has, and the reason i am not annoyed with it, is that it is not a heavily marketed feature. Yes, it appears on the Amazon description, but unlike most other El Cheapo monitors, Spectre doesn't oversell this feature. Hell, they market this more for productivity than for gaming, so yeah, i can live with this.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on November 2, 2023

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: Excelente relación calidad precio, si sabes que compromisos tienes que tomar.Excelente relación calidad precio, si sabes que compromisos tienes que tomar.
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: UPDATE: A los dos meses y medio de uso, prendí la computadora y hay un problema de imagen. No se ve tan claro en las fotos, pero la imagen está como duplicada/partida, además de tener algunos artefactos y en todo el monitor se veían líneas delgadas como tipo "scanlines".Apagar el monitor y prenderlo no ayudó.Desconectar el cable display port y volverlo a conectar no ayudó.Se arregló cuando desconecté de la corriente el monitor, apagué la computadora, reconecté ambos extremos del cable tanto al monitor como a la computadora y volví a prender la computadora.Espero que solo haya sido algún error extraño de drivers o algo por el estilo y que no sean inicios de algún fallo mas grave.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------Apenas llevo un par de días utiliándolo y hasta ahora todo bien. Tuve la fortuna de que no llegara con pixeles muertos y el famoso "ips bleed" muy bien controlado y el "ips glow" creo que es muy poco. Pero en una marca de esta gama la verdad es que eso va a ser muy de suerte. En general los colores se ven muy bien sobre todo para juegos y algo que me sorprendió muchisimo, es que tiene unos negros muy pero muuuuy buenos a pesar de ser IPS.Espero que no falle, ya que hay varios comentarios que pues por la marca no tienen tan buen control de calidad y parece que a algunas personas les ha fallado en menos de un mes (toca madera). Pero supongo que eso son los riesgos de comprar tan barato, así que si algo pasa actualizaré el review. La verdad es que ya es difícil encontrar buenos monitores duraderos, este lo compré porque mi monitor original un MSI comenzó a fallar en menos de 4 meses :c.Ahora si, vamos a ver quienes se beneficiarán de este chulo monitor.Es para ti si:- No tienes varo :'v.Lo conseguí en poco más de 5k, en la página oficial está en 400 dlls. Hombre, un monitor 4k, de 32" y además IPS!!!! A este precio no vas a encontrarlo, no hay, no existe. Todos los de 32" ya son puras porquerias con panel VA.- Lo quieres para trabajo/productividad, ver peliculas, o simplemente quieres saber que es el maravilloso mundo del 4k pero no quieres gastar mucho.Por este precio no te vas a conseguir nada mejor, los 4k mas baratos que he visto son de 8 mil para arriba, suponiendo que encuentres de 32", con paneles VA que tienen problemas incluso de que se queme la imagen en la pantalla.Las pelicular se ven increíbles, si usas tableta gráfica para escribir cosas, se siente super natural con una tableta de tamaño de mediano, caben mil cosas en la pantalla, la verdad es genial trabajar en 4k.- No eres jugador profesional, competitivo, tryhard.El monitor es de 70hz y tiene un tiempo de respuesta de 7ms oficiales pero seguro es mas. A ver yo juego shooters y pues está jugable, pero mi segundo monitor era 144hz/1ms y si se nota mucho el cambio, peeeeeeeeeero era 2k y este es 4k paps. La verdad no juego mucho y pues si extraño los 144 pero no me arrepiento de tenerlo como monitor principal (no puedo jugar en el 2k 144hz porque lo tengo en vertical y no caben los dos en mi mesa si lo pongo en horizontal jeje), pero si tu espacio te diera para tener uno para jugar y al lado este, la verdad estaría genial.Si se puede jugar shooter, y si no has tenido un monitor de mas de 120hz y menos de 5ms de respuesta, no creo que sientas algo tan raro. Los juegos que son de historia pfffffff.... pues es 4k a 32", se ven hermosos.Si tu tarjeta no da para correrlos en 4k y quieres los máximos fps, bajale a 2k, y la verdad es que se ven super bien, los juegos mas pesados como cyberpunk los juego en 2k y a la distancia que lo hago se ven muy bien.El fornite con nanite me da creo 65-70 fps en 4k, el overwatch es la cosa mas optimizada del mundo así que sin problemas, el farlight igual, no estoy seguro del cod, pero en defintiiva si te da problemas solo bajale o a la calidad o a la resolución y juega en 2k.- No eres fotógrafo, diseñador, videografo/cinematógrafo PROFESIONAL (mas adelante por que lo pongo en mayúsculas). Si eres uno de estos, solo te lo recomendaría como una pantalla secundaria.Si no te dedicas a nada que tenga una necesidad de calibración, no creo que notes nada raro, la verdad sus colores son buenos y en juegos muchas veces si te dejan como WOW!!!Ahora, si tu SABES calibrar un monitor y además has usado monitores con buenos paneles, sRGB, adobeRGB, has calibrado para impresiones y cosas así, entonces vas a notar que los colores son... raros. A veces tienen ese factor wow pero en otras ocasiones se ven deslavados donde no deberían verse deslavados. Is the 512GB M.2 SSD durable enough for 24/7 industrial or office use? 
Yes. The M.2 2280 SATA SSD features Wear Leveling and Bad Block Management to prevent data loss. Designed for high MTBF, it handles continuous CNC/ATM logging and business tasks with sustained speed and commercial-grade stability. 
Is it easy to add more storage for industrial logs or large databases? 
Very easy. Along with the 512GB SSD, we include a SATA cable for the 2.5" bay. Directly add to 2TB HDD/SSD for databases or logs—no extra parts needed. A truly ready-to-expand commercial storage solution. 
Can this mini PC be installed inside a tight ATM cabinet or CNC control box? 
Yes. The compact VESA-ready design fits tight ATM cabinets, kiosks, and CNC boxes. Its rugged PC+ABS chassis and full-copper thermal module ensure peak performance in constrained commercial environments with limited airflow. 
Is the cooling fan loud during heavy multitasking or video meetings? 
No. It operates at under 38dB via an upgraded fan. Even when driving dual 2.5K displays for multitasking or meetings, the C3 remains whisper-quiet, ensuring a distraction-free environment for professional or educational use. 
Does this support dual monitors and professional commercial software? 
Yes. Dual HDMI ports support two 2.5K monitors simultaneously. Fully compatible with Windows 10 Pro, but not support Windows 11, and it runs POS systems, ERP software, and 3D slicers like Cura with smooth, professional-grade reliability.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: amazing! not going back to Beelink anymore!amazing! not going back to Beelink anymore!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I used to buy all computer parts separately for motherboard, memory, hard disk, case, and even cooling fans to build my own custom PCs back in the days.  About 5 years ago, I started replacing my customer desktop PCs with Mini PCs because of the form factor and price.  My first few Mini PCs were Beelink brand and I did like them so I got one for my daughter and my son. I bought Beelink GT-R model for my son and Beelink SER5 model for my daughter but my daughter's SER5 model started having problem just after a year and a half of using it.  At first, the WiFi controller stopped working so I had to buy a USB WiFi receiver to get wireless WiFi working, which had significant speed issue.  Then it started making screeching sound, which I didn't want to take the chance of hard drive failure so I decided to replace my daughter's Mini PC.  Around that time, my son graduated from H.S. and went to a college so my daughter moved into his bedroom, which is much bigger and I asked her if she wanted to use his Beelink GT-R Mini PC but she asked me to buy her a new Mini PC that has very fast CPU and WiFi connections as her new bedroom is furthest away from our router in the basement.  After doing some research, I got this origimagic A2 MiniPC and I was mind blown by its specs and actual performance!It not only has super fast i9 processor but with 32GB of memory and 1TB of solid state drive on board, this is one top-notch Mini PC that can compete with any desktops or laptops.  I surely don't have to worry about my daughter ever running out of disk space and 32GB of memory will allow her to use 2 monitors and play games or watch videos without any lags.  In fact, this beast can connect up to 4 monitors and I just had to try out for myself and I was really impressed with the result.  It has DP, HDMI, VGA and Type-C ports for connecting 4 monitors, which worked flawlessly.What's also amazing is how quiet this Mini PC is and even when connected to 4 monitors and watching videos, I never heard the sound of fan spinning or the surface of the Mini PC got hot.  Looks like it has really good cooling and air circulation design inside.  It also came with 2 antennas that connect on the back, and now my daughter has the fastest WiFi speed with this Mini PC, which is really impressive as well.  She absolutely loves this beat and minimalist look.  Oh, she didn't have to plug 2 USB Hubs that she used with her previous Beelink Mini PC because this beast has so many USB-A 3.0 and 2.0 ports, which is awesome since some wireless devices such as keyboard and mouse works much better with USB 2.0 ports.This Mini PC is such a great bargain for its price and you won't regret getting this.  I don't think I can go back to Beelink Mini PCs anymore and I'm now really tempted to buy this origimagic A2 Mini PC again for myself because I'm so jealous and mind blown with it.  Highly recommend it without any reservation!

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Great value for a great monitor. Picture is terrific 4K, w good color and contrast. The BEST? Nope. But at this price, this pretty great screen becomes a bargain. Plus I can use my VESA arm. Also, I got mine “like new” and got a nice discount on what appeared to be a brand new monitor.No one ever bought a computer monitor for the speakers, but these are essentially nonexistent, so much so I had to turn the volume up all the way and then put my ear right up to the screen to even find them (on the bottom edge btw, presumably intended to bounce sound off the desk). My iPhone speakers sound better. Again, not a big deal since no monitor speakers are good, but some can at least add some fill to your setup. Not these.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Bought this to replace 1 of 3 monitors I have on my desk. Monitor is good and matches the Philips i have. The only problem is Philips put the on/off switch on the back of the monitor. It is 6" up from the bottom and 4" in from the right side. this is a ridiculous location. Plus the on/off is also a 4 way toggle for other functions, like volume, picture and other things. Ok I would have to memorize the other functions or paste a picture on my desk. productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought this to replace an earlier, non-HDR version that I dropped. I'd just upgraded my video card anyway. I can't emphasize enough the quality of this monitor at the price point. It may not have the ultra-crisp look of monitors costing two or three times this (or more) but it certainly does the job(s) I want from it at this price point.Gaming: Elder Scrolls Online doesn't necessarily challenge the combination of RX760XT and this monitor, but the game looks great with the auto-HDR function.Photo Editing, the more important aspect for me, has taken on a new "flavor". Between upgrading from a RTX3060 to RX7600 XT and this monirot, images in Lightroom have a depth on this monitor that makes me want to try out some "crazy" editing functions that didn't look very satisfying on my old monitor.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: El tamaño, la imagen, es buenísimo. Muy recomendable para el trabajo creativo.
Excelente imagen con resolución 4K
Llego con pequeñas rayaduras en la pantalla...

Funcionó bien 6 meses. La luz de fondo o backlight filtra un poco de los lados y esquinas pero tenía  buen color así que lo probé. A los 6 meses comenzó a parpadear la parte central y ese parpadeo en dos días terminó como un gradiente negro. Falla de la luz de fondo. El monitor contó con todos los cuidados y precauciones electromagnéticas (regulador de voltaje con supresión de picos y no break, buen cable DP 1.4 sin interferencias, todas las actualizaciones debidas), así que fue claramente falla del producto.Al contactar a Philips para validar su garantía (36 meses en monitores), me hicieron hablar con 10 personas diferentes hasta que una reconoció que no era válida mi garantía porque Amazon no es un distribuidor autorizado de Philips. En este momento espero el reembolso que Amazon prometió ya que me permitieron devolver el producto, pero Philips como compañía quedó mal conmigo y su producto era de pobre calidad. No lo recomiendo.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I have various 4k budget monitors currently for doing office work.  The Asus ones I have are nice but lack the ability to mount them, and the Samsung ones have the mounting capability but have a very noticeable image retention/persistence issue, meaning if you're viewing high-contrasting contents and open something with a pale background (like a "dim mode" website), you can see ghosts of the previous thing you were looking at.Since the Asus doesn't have this issue, I know it must depend on the actual panel manufacturer, so I used a LLM to research the likely panel manufacturers of common budget models, and LG stood out as being known to not have the image persistence/ghosting that some others do, so I purchased two, and am very pleased so far.For me, the extra ~$40 for the 27UP850K-W (compared to the 27UP650K-W) was worth it.  They apparently use the exact same panel, but there are more ports and OSD configuration options (picture controls, etc.) and speakers with the 850, plus you can connect a modern laptop directly to the monitor with USB-C to both display stuff and get a charge.  I don't have a need for this currently but it's nice to know it's there.  And of course, it doesn't have the image persistence issue like my Samsung ones.I see that some other people have reported a crooked stand, but since I'm using a dual mount I'm unable to test that.  If I could go back in time, I would have gotten all 27UP850K-W models since they meet all my needs.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: Good monitor for office and light multimedia work
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: This is my first 4K computer monitor, but not my first 4K screen. A few years ago, I bought an LG 4K OLED smart TV, and I was happy with the experience. Enjoying my photos in high resolution and on an HDR-capable screen was definitely something that stayed with me ever since. But I wasn't ready to go 4K OLED on my computer yet. The price tag of such a monitor is beyond my acceptable level for everyday use. I'm not in the creative media business to justify the costs. But for the office and light multimedia work (at the amateur level), a decent 4K monitor became a necessity, and one of my old monitors needed an update.I found the LG 27UP850K a good compromise between price and quality. The image is sharp and with good colors out of the box. But for critical work, I have a calibrator that makes it even better. I had some issues in the first weeks of use, but it wasn't the monitor. I hate thick and sturdy cables, and I bought some really thin and flexible ones. Well... don't go for the cheap ones because you will notice problems (mostly derived from the inability of such poor cables to handle the bandwidth required by 4K resolution, combined with the best frame rate you can get and HDR. I replaced the cable with a good brand, and the problems went away.I'm not going to comment on the sound quality. No TV or monitor can deliver the quality of sound I expect using their own little speakers. But the availability is useful for regular work, where audio is just to provide more context to what you see and to immerse you in the story or the emotion of a good musical piece. No, for this kind of experience, I use a pair of good-quality cans, an external DAC unit, and a dedicated headphone amplifier.The USB ports are nice. Not that I use them a lot. But I know I have some extra ports if I expand beyond the regular peripherals. As an electronics engineer, I experiment a lot and USB gives you the ubiquity of communicating with your gadgets and instruments.So far, so good. Once properly set up, the monitor is stable, works as expected, and I hope it will last as long as my old Dell U27813HM (still in service today). As always, YMMV. Enjoy!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: My HGFRTEE B320BZU06 computer monitor is a better than my previous Samsung S7 monitor.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: My HGFRTEE B320BZU06 computer monitor is a better than my previous (old, outdated model) Samsung S7 monitor. Both these monitors are 32 inch diagonal as advertised (yet the actual diagonal display size is 31.5 inches), and both these monitors are UHD.The drawback of my Samsung S7 monitor is the viewing angle is very narrow for a good picture, and the colors looked washed-out on the left side and on the right-side.  The HGFRTEE monitor doesn't have washed-out colors on the left side or right side.The supplied mounting stand for the HGFRTEE monitor is more stable than the smaller footprint stand for my Samsung S7. Neither of these monitors have adjustable heights, yet the HGFRTEE has a little bit of tilting capability built into it, yet my Samsung S7 cannot adjust its tilt.The colors of the HGFRTEE is much more vibrant than my Samsung S7.  The HGFRTEE default settings were much too vibrant in colors that resulted in oversaturation, and browns and tans looked orange.  I was able to adjust the oversaturation partially with the HGFRTEE's "M" button located on the back on the monitor and then stepping through the mini-display popup screen that appeared in the bottom right corner of this monitor.I did further fine-tuning of the display's colors and contrast and brightness and gamma & digital vibrance by using my desktop computer's NVIDIA GPU graphics application.--> A 2nd comparison: The LG 32UN650-W 32'' monitor is height adjustable and it has a more stable stand (base) than the HGFRTEE, yet the LG costs a lot more $.  I have the 27" variant of this "LG" monitor that I mentioned, and the text size is too small to read at 3840x2160, but text size is OK (tiny yet OK readable) in all the 3840x2160 32 inch monitors that I've used.--> So why didn't I buy LG 32UN650-W 32'' monitor? Answer: cost.  The HGFRTEE is an unbeatable value $, yet it has less-than-ideal stand (base) and no height adjustment and the display quality not top of the line (it required a lot of fine tuning using my NVIDIA GPU display settings).--> DISCLAIMER: I've only used this display for a few hours spanning 2 days, so I cannot comment on longevity or reliability, and I cannot comment on whether the screen glitches in any way since it's too new to review those details.--> NOTE FOR NEW BUYERS: The power "on" button is located on the back of the monitor and it's tiny (the size of a narrow pencil eraser).  Once I pressed the power button, then the monitor turned on if ("if") my computer is also on.  When I turned my computer to "sleep" mode, then the monitor automatically turns off after a few seconds - that's a nice feature.--> CONs: The only drawback I noticed with this monitor is the refresh rate is only 60 Hz, so if you do competitive gaming or if your eyes need a higher refresh rate, then look for monitors that advertise a higher refresh rate.  I didn't subtract a "star" for this drawback because this monitor is specifically advertised as 60 Hz and that refresh rate is OK for my eyes.

The 4K 60Hz output produces a crisp, sharp picture on compatible displays, making videos and presentations look excellent.I was also impressed by the incredibly small footprint. It takes up virtually no desk space and can easily be mounted behind a monitor for a clean, clutter-free setup. The build quality feels solid, and the Windows 10 installation was ready to use right out of the box.If you’re looking for a compact computer for everyday tasks, media playback, office work, kiosks, or digital signage, this mini PC stick offers excellent value for the money. It won’t replace a high-end desktop for gaming or demanding applications, but for its intended purpose it performs exceptionally well. Highly recommended!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Good monitor for content creatorsGood monitor for content creators
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The Samsung 27" ViewFinity S7 (S70H) is an excellent productivity-focused monitor for anyone who wants sharp 4K resolution, accurate-looking colors, and a comfortable viewing experience. The 27-inch IPS panel provides plenty of screen real estate while the 3840x2160 resolution makes text, images, spreadsheets, and detailed content look impressively crisp. It also offers useful connectivity and Samsung's Display Manager software for improving workflow.Positives:- 4K UHD resolution delivers exceptionally sharp and detailed images, making text and fine details easy to see- High pixel density provides a noticeable upgrade over standard Full HD displays, especially for office work and creative tasks- IPS panel offers consistent image quality and a wide 178° viewing angle- HDR10 enhances contrast with deeper blacks and brighter highlights for more engaging compatible content- Wide viewing angles make it easy to share the screen or work from different positions without significant changes in brightness- HDMI and DisplayPort connections provide convenient compatibility with computers and other devices-- Eye Saver Mode helps reduce blue-light exposure for more comfortable extended viewing- Flicker-reduction technology helps minimize visual fatigue during long work sessions- Samsung Display Manager adds useful productivity features, including split-screen setup, brightness adjustments, KVM, PIP/PBP, and calibration controls- 27-inch size provides a good balance between desk space and usable screen area- The high-resolution display is particularly well suited for documents, spreadsheets, multitasking, photo work, and detailed applicationsNegatives:- The 4K resolution can require display scaling on some operating systems to make text and interface elements more comfortable to read- Users looking primarily for competitive gaming may prefer a monitor with a higher refresh rate and gaming-specific features- HDR performance is useful for compatible content, but this is primarily a productivity monitor rather than a dedicated HDR entertainment display- The 27-inch screen may feel somewhat small for users who prefer a larger workspace for extensive multitaskingFinal VerdictThe Samsung ViewFinity S7 S70H is a very capable 27-inch 4K monitor that prioritizes productivity, image clarity, and comfortable long-term use. The sharp UHD resolution, IPS panel, HDR10 support, wide viewing angles, and Eye Saver features make it a strong choice for office work and everyday computing. Samsung Display Manager is another nice addition for users who regularly multitask and want more control over their workspace. Overall, this is a polished, high-resolution monitor for professionals, students, home offices, and anyone who values a crisp and comfortable 4K display.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: UPDATE: I have continued issues watching movies on Amazon and Netflix. I've had to lower the resolution yet again. It is now 2048x1152. In terms of watching movies, this is way worse than previous lower resolution monitor. Samsung still hasn't provided an updated driver. If this continues, I may have to go back to my LG Monitor.Previous review:This monitor is a photographer's dream! The display is sharp and detailed. The colors are not just accurate, but subtle. I was able to put the monitor together without reading the instructions, though I think it is best if you do read them. The screen comes with both HDMI and DisplayPort cables. There is also a USB-A port on the back. I'm surprised how lightweight the unit is. I can easily carry it in one hand without straining anything. It has a single rocker button interface that controls all the settings. Out of the box, I think the colors were good and brightness was set to a reasonable level. I use a Spyder densitometer to set accurate colors for photo editing. After I had done that, the color has shifted only slightly. The reading indicated that the monitor is about 110% of the sRGB spectrum which is the most standard for general photo editing. It comes in respectfully on the AdobeRGB spectrum as well, but I don't use that as it is too hard to get that standard to translate to prints off my printers. The monitor gets plenty bright if you want it to. I use TwinkleTray to adjust brightness on the fly. For general use, I have it set to only 17% which is amazingly low. The anti-flicker tech on this monitor is great too. I have zero eye strain even after staring at the monitor for hours on end. And last, is the resolution. This is my first 4K monitor, and it is almost too detailed. I've had to change settings on a number of apps as the text is too small to see easily unless I lean in.However, there are some issues. First, there is some light falloff at the corners. This becomes less apparent the further away from the monitor you get. I am using this monitor with an Intel NUCI IDBBi7. Despite having a moderately high-end computer with 64GB or RAM, there are problems with Samsung's driver. Some videos and web pages cause screen jittering. This is really annoying! Trying to access Text can appear ghosted. I lower the resolution down to 1080P to get stable results. When I removed the driver and went back to a generic display driver things settled down. I hope Samsung reads this and releases a new version of the driver soon so I can update this review. In the meantime, I haven't encountered any new issues using the generic driver.Overall, I'd say this is a fantastic monitor as long as you have a good graphics card and don't run into driver issues. For the price, it makes editing photos a joy!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Bright, Vivid Monitor With Great Productivity Features and Surprisingly Fun PIP/PBP Use
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This Samsung monitor has been a fantastic addition to my personal setup. I’m using it for a mix of light gaming, project work, and general productivity, and the jump to a 32‑inch 4K panel from a pair of 12 year old 23-inch monitors is immediately noticeable. The screen is super bright and vivid, with crisp text and excellent clarity across the entire display. For everyday use, coding, browsing, and media, it’s a huge upgrade in comfort and workspace.The VA panel delivers deep blacks and strong contrast, especially in HDR10 mode. It’s not an OLED, but for the price range, the color richness and contrast are impressive. Viewing angles are solid for a VA panel. Straight‑on looks fantastic, and even slight horizontal shifts hold color well. Vertical angles show more of the typical washout, but nothing unexpected. When my toddler is in the office, it's usually what will be playing music for him and the winamp style equalizer bring both of us joy.One of my favorite features is the Picture‑in‑Picture and Picture‑by‑Picture functionality. I’ve been running Forza on the main screen while keeping my phone connected as a PIP window for music or videos. It’s a genuinely cool experience and makes the monitor feel more like a multi‑device hub than just a display. The multiple connectivity options help with that too: HDMI and DisplayPort cover everything I need, and an HDMI‑to‑USB‑C cable lets me plug in my tablet, phone, or Switch with no hassle. The Samsung Display Manager software is another strong point. Splitting the screen, adjusting brightness, or switching between inputs is quick and intuitive.Physically, the monitor is lightweight and easy to mount. I have it on an arm, and it’s surprisingly impressive in portrait mode. It's been perfect for reading, editing documents, or vertical workflows. The stand itself is basic and lacks height adjustment, but the VESA mount makes it easy to work around that.Gaming at 60Hz is fine for casual play (personally am running it through a cloud environment, so no complaints here). It’s not built for high‑motion competitive gaming, but for racing games, RPGs, and general entertainment, the picture quality carries the experience. Ghosting is minimal on the panel, and HDR adds a nice punch to visuals.For productivity, the 4K resolution gives a massive amount of usable space. Running multiple windows side‑by‑side feels natural, and text is sharp enough that long reading or editing sessions don’t strain the eyes. The brightness adjusts well to ambient lighting, and the anti‑glare coating keeps reflections manageable.If these go on sale, I’d absolutely pick up a second one to replace my work setup and blend everything I do at the desk into a single unified layout. At it's current price, it's a great value, but not until one of my existing monitors kicks the bucket...a sale though, would swap them immediately :)  Between the vivid display, flexible connectivity, and genuinely useful PIP/PBP features, it’s a great monitor for anyone who wants a large, bright, versatile 4K screen without overspending.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Samsung 27" ViewFinity S7 (S70H) High-Resolution Monitor - 4K UHD (3840x2160), IPSSamsung 27" ViewFinity S7 (S70H) High-Resolution Monitor - 4K UHD (3840x2160), IPS
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Preamble: I currently have 4 DELL S2740L Super Glossy Monitors and love them. Recently, I purchased 3 of Samsung's 32" Odyssey G5 G50F QHD as future replacements when these begin to go (I bought them in 2013 and so far, they are still perfect as day 1, just had to replace on power adapter.) My G50F review is here:  https://www.amazon.com/gp/customer-reviews/R6BZE4PXUWKAMRegarding this Samsung 27" ViewFinity S7, it's a fairly standard IPS monitor that I would expect at the price point of around $250 today, currently at the time of review: $249.99. With that said, let me list my initial impressions of it:1. AG Coating is acceptable, I've seen a lot worse, especially from Dell. Is it's like Samsung TV's? Unfortunately no, it's shows that it has a AG coating compared to their TVs. Initially out of the box, it actually looks nice/slightly glossy like a TV, but that's due to the protective film (excitement was short lived.) I would have kept the protective film on if it wasn't for the writing they put in the bottom left hand corner, especially since with AG coated screens, fingerprints and saliva (yes, saliva, some people spray the screen when they talk) is very difficult to remove compared to a glossy screen, they come right off with a microfiber towel and some distilled water.2. Colors are less saturated unless you bump that up in the settings (out the box, the Odyssey G5 G50F QHD is more saturated and more color eye pleasing,) however, some people may want more color accuracy compared to more color saturation by default.3. Doesn't have speakers, but does have a headphone output that you can plug into desktop speakers next to the power input. I haven't tested it yet, but that's a nice touch for cases where you may want to plug in a device like a roku in the HDMI port and watch with audio.4. This model also uses a rear settings control joystick which I don't like, very bad ergonomics.5. The stand is fix in positioning unlike the  Odyssey G5 G50F which can swivel and has height adjustment.6. The photos were taken with a S24 Ultra playing the Samsung QLED demo video using a Roku stick in the HDMI port.7. Only has 2 ports, one for HDMI and one for a DisplayPort. This model only comes an HDMI cable, the G5 G50F comes with both, HDMI and DisplayPort cables.8. Design wise, it'll fit into almost every office/home setup and is lightweight if you need to move it around.9. Auto HDR is nice! There's also quite a few a preprogrammed display settings to choose from, in the photos, I took pictures on each mode, however, it's more obvious in person that with the photos to see the differences.10. Standard IPS glow...didn't observe any anomalies like blooming/clouding.Bottom line, it's a fine deal for a 27" IPS Monitor. If you're looking for an AWESOME deal on 32" 2K Samsung Monitor with out-of-the-box nicer color saturation (I got mine for $219 each,) take a look at this: https://www.amazon.com/Samsung-Resolution-Compatible-FreeSyncTM-LS32FG502ENXZA/dp/B0G1DZM5QW They also make a 27" model of the Odyssey G5 too, but I have no personal experience with it.

features: PREMIUM GAMING PC MINI COMPUTER - The Nucbox M7 Ultra Mini PC is a small form factor Desktop Micro Mini Computer with an AMD Ryzen 7 PRO 6850U (8C/16T 2.70Ghz Base speed with Turbo speed up to 4.7Ghz) processor. The GPU is integrated with a powerful AMD Radeon 680M 12 Cores Graphics Card; performance is almost close to that of a full NVIDIA GTX 1050 Ti. Coupled with the support of FSR 3.0+ technology, the computer can handle heavy computing tasks and AAA gaming

MINI PC COMPUTER SUPPORTS QUAD SCREEN 8K DISPLAY - Nucbox M7 Ultra gaming pc is equipped with Dual USB4 USB-C Video output. The latest HDMI 2.1 port can connect to large screen TV and Display Monitors and output up to 8K@60Hz resolution. The Type-C DisplayPort Video output can connect to the latest monitor displays utilizing 4K@144Hz. Features simultaneous four screen display

OCULINK PORT - The M7 Ultra Oculink port enables higher bandwidth capabilities, better frame rates and lower lag. The standard also operates at PCIe x4 speeds, compared to Thunderbolt's x3. Gamers and content creators can benefit from OCuLink's higher bandwidth, resulting in better performance and lower lag for eGPU setups

UPGRADED DUAL COOLING FANS - Our new Hyper Ice Chamber 2.0 design uses larger top and bottom cooling fans with 360 degrees in and out air flow. The copper base keeps the fan cool and we have lowered the fan noise down to 35dB in Quiet mode

THREE PERFORMANCE MODES UPDATED UEFI - The M7 Ultra mini computer features an all new BIOS update with three performance modes (Quiet 35W, Balance 50W, or Performance 65W-70W). VRAM Allocation is also possible with Auto Power On, Wake-on-LAN options available

DUAL NIC 2.5GbE + WiFi 6E + BT 5.2 - Dual Intel NIC 2.5GbE LAN port design provides more applications, such as firewall, multichannel aggregation, soft routing, file storage server, etc. WiFi 6E provides a faster internet experience for browsing, streaming and gaming. Built-in Bluetooth 5.2 is more stable and efficient to connect multiple wireless devices such as projector, printer, monitor, speakers and etc

32GB DDR5 DUAL CHANNEL RAM & 512GB PCIE SSD DUAL SLOT EXPANSION - Installed with DDR5 32GB RAM 4800MHz (Dual Channel 2x16B), the Nucbox M7 Ultra mini pc support expansion to 128GB RAM. Featured with 512GB M.2 2280 PCIe 3.0 SSD, supports dual slot expansion to 2*PCIe 4.0 2TB SSD up to 4TB. (Upgrades not included)

PREMIUM PC BUILD DESIGN - The M7 Ultra mini gaming pc has a beautiful metal chassis and matte top cover. Easy to remove cover lid, simply rotate the cover counter clockwise and remove. The top cooling fan is custom built and the bottom cooling fan has been upgraded with a copper base

GMKTEC WARRANTY - GMKtec offers a 1-year limited warranty for each mini PC, starting from the date of the purchase. All defects due to design and workmanship are covered. With a professional after sales team always ready to attend to your needs, you can simply relax and enjoy your mini PC

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: (K12 - Ryzen 7 H 255) Great value, exceptional hardware and connectivity
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This is specifically for the K12 with the Ryzen 7 H 255.Honestly, not a bad deal.The CPU is pretty good for its class, and has very acceptable integrated graphics. The H 255 is seemingly only sold to the chinese market, has no real documentation officially (as of the time of writing), and is essentially a recycled die from better chips that didn't meet the cut so to speak (at least as far as I can find), but I don't see any of those as a real problem; die recycling is perfectly fine if it actually works and is stable, and AMD is usually pretty good at the latter... and it makes me feel a little better that AMD can save something that would otherwise end up being e-waste. Despite the borderline unofficial nature of the CPU, I have not experienced any performance issues, instability, or crashes of any kind after a few weeks. Note that I updated the BIOS and microcode immediately after receiving the unit, and I suggest everyone do the same.The unit itself is from GMKtec, which is a chinese company. However, there were some (good) surprises in the box that tells me they actually cared about the end user experience, though possibly only just enough to make sure that the average joe blow didn't immediately return it because they got pissed off at something that would honestly be Microsoft's fault (eg. the horrendous OOBE for Windows). I choose to believe they actually care though, and somewhat reinforcing that, my email to them was answered the next day (I'll get to what the contents of that was later).The specs of the unit, aside from the CPU which is pretty good itself, are actually darn incredible. OCuLink is a quasi-rare connector, but an *extremely* welcome one! That significantly improves the unit's lifespan and enables mostly modern gaming, provided you genuinely do the research into how to use it (remember, don't plug or unplug it when the PC is on!), though it can already handle light-medium gaming with just the integrated graphics. Though I have not tried the OCuLink port yet, I have no reason to believe it doesn't work or anything like that. USB4 is also extremely welcome, and I can confirm that it not only works, but it follows best practices of how to implement the protocol. Since the port does do PCIe tunneling, it should work with all Thunderbolt 4 appliances out of the box. GMKtec could have taken the cheap way out and omitted this detail, but they did not. Absolutely incredible to have both of these available.There are also, seemingly (I have not opened the unit up yet, no reason to), three M.2 slots, one at Gen4x4 and two at Gen4x2, which is perfectly fine in terms of speed and great in terms of how many slots they offer. I cannot think of any other mini PC with this level of overall connectivity. You lose out on some external USB connectors that would otherwise be present, but USB4 seriously more than makes up for it. The dual 2.5G LAN ports are just the whipped cream on top of all this.Though, not all can be as good. There is no S3 power state support in the firmware, so you're stuck with shutting down the computer, hibernating it, or relying on Microsoft's absolutely abysmal "implementation" of sleep in the form of modern standby (S0). This was confirmed in my aforementioned email to GMKtec's support. Oh well, I have the whipped cream but miss out on the cherry. This may be an oversight on GMKtec's part, but it may also be difficulty getting S3 implemented with OCuLink. Don't know exactly how that works. I'm tempted to knock a star off for this, since S3 is a very, very nice power state to have available, but it's something I'm personally not terribly concerned about, especially with everything else so good. Please, if you're reading this GMKtec, add it in a BIOS update! Would love to see it!There may also be an issue with the TPM, specifically in regards to when the firmware tells the OS to initiate S0 sleep (eg. from the power button short pressed). In such an event, when the computer resumes from S0 the TPM will either fail or lock up. This may be an issue with Windows, or with the TPM, or with just my unit, and it requires a reboot to clear it up. Either way, my way around it is to leave the unit turned on or to just shut it down, but again it's not a concern for me personally, and YMMV.Overall, I would recommend this unit. Though I have not opened it to inspect the internals, nor tested the OCuLink connector yet, I see great value in this unit, and I imagine I will keep it around for a very long time, getting significant usage out of it. I would give it 4.5 stars if that were possible, but for Amazon I will leave it at 5.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great deal, but mine came with a used SSDGreat deal, but mine came with a used SSD
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Pros:- Small- Powerful (8 Zen4 cores, 16 logical CPUs, Radeon 780M graphics, HX power spec)- (Relatively) low power consumption from being a laptop CPU (Though the HX is not as efficient as the U version)- Comes with a good amount of good quality RAM from a name brand- 2x 2.5G nics- USB4 port (haven't tested it out yet, other reviewers had issues)- Good cooling- Quiet at idle (YMMV)Cons:- Came with a moderately used Lexar SSD- Windows 11 (wiping that put even more write cycles on the SSD)- A U power spec option or BIOS support for lowering TDP would have been nice for lower power consumption- No SATA support- Ethernet controllers are Realtek, not Intel- Wifi also not IntelThis is just an initial review, but out of the box I noticed that the 1TB SSD that was included in this GMKtek K6 mini PC had logged about 86 hours of usage in SMART, as well as over 8TB written and 7TB read on this 1TB Lexar SSD.  That seems like a lot more than initial imaging and burn-in to me.  Over 8 full write cycles for every memory cell will have an impact on the SSD's lifespan.  I am only using the included SSD as a supplement to my main SSD, so it's not a big issue, but buyer beware!  Also, the SSD did come with an extra heatsink pre-installed.  That may improve the longevity of the disk enough to compensate for a lot of the usage.  I removed it from the included drive and installed it on my 3rd-party drive instead since I use that one more.Overall, this system seems to work well.  I wiped Windows 11 and am using proxmox on it.  The Ryzen 7840 CPU is really great for my purposes as a VM server / AI host.  In July 2024 I got this for $509.  With the 32Gigs of ram and a 1TB SSD that is functioning, at least, it's a really amazing deal.  Similar machines from other manufacturers cost hundreds more without the RAM or SSDs, so I'm not going to complain too loudly.  In fact, I think it's a great deal from Amazon and GMKtec.Time will tell how well this machine holds up, but the construction seems solid, the cooling seems to be well-designed for this form factor with a fan for the CPU being pretty standard, but a second fan for cooling all the other components is a nice addition that you don't see in some competitors.  I will update this review with any developments.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: GMKtec K12 Gaming Mini PC: A C&C Generals Fan's Compact Powerhouse
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: As a PC enthusiast since the dial-up era, I’ve built my share of rigs to fuel epic Command & Conquer: Generals and Zero Hour sessions. I’m not chasing high-end FPS titles—give me base-building and Shockwave tank rushes at 60fps any day. The GMKtec K12 Gaming Mini PC, with its AMD Ryzen 7 8745HS, 32GB DDR5, 512GB SSD, and Radeon 780M graphics, has become my go-to for strategy gaming and everyday tasks. Here’s why this tiny titan earns my nod.This thing is small—think hardcover book size—yet it’s a beast. Setup was a breeze; Windows 11 installed without a hitch, dodging Microsoft’s TPM 2.0 roadblocks. I went local user mode for privacy, and it just worked—no workarounds needed. The K12’s quiet operation is a standout; even during intense Zero Hour GLA campaigns, the fans barely hum. It’s a far cry from the roaring towers of my past, perfect for late-night gaming without disturbing the house.Performance? Stellar. The Ryzen 7 and 32GB DDR5 chew through Generals and Zero Hour at 1080p, delivering silky-smooth battles and fast load times thanks to the NVMe SSD. The Radeon 780M handles particle-heavy Scud Storm effects flawlessly. I’ve also dabbled in Age of Empires II Definitive Edition—high settings, no lag. Multitasking is effortless, with browser tabs and Discord running alongside game sessions. Three M.2 slots and dual 2.5G NICs scream future-proofing, though I’d grab a USB hub for extra peripherals.Downsides? The port selection (HDMI 2.1, USB4, etc.) is solid, but heavy peripheral users might need a dock. Thermals are great, but place it in a well-ventilated spot for marathon sessions. At roughly $500, it’s a steal for the power.For C&C fans like me who want a compact, quiet rig that crushes strategy games without the hassle, the K12 is a winner. Five Stars—ready to command and conquer.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Good (and fast) product, however ... if you are installing a Steam Deck alternative like Bazzite then expect to get down in the weeds with a little Konsole work. Actually, everything is quite simple. It just needs tweaking. The biggest problem  ... of all things ... was the 3.5mm jack! Note: it is TRRS 3-ring. Most likely you will get no audio there, even on a TRRS jack! I went down a rabbit hole of alsactl settings only to find out my USB 2.0 mini-DAC fixed the no audio through headphones issue. I could only tap the HDMI digital audio through my monitor speakers! Now, it's good through the mini-DAC. Bazzite installs GREAT! No problems. Setup your BIOS first. I Clonezilla'd the disk with Win 11 and tossed in drawer. Bazzite runs great and if I need an upgrade, most things are possible with the OcuLink and spare memory and hd slots. Also note: the front ports are electronically noisy for BT and 2.4G. You might have issues. Move to the rear ports. BT is out for my mini-keyboard but 2.4G works fine.All in all, a good buy. I was skeptical of the 'ease' of installation claims. Not the easiest and not the hardest. Typical weird Linux stuff. Bypassing and configuration usually fixes things. Is it the best solution all the time? No, but it gets you into Steam just fine! Runs fast in Performance Mode. Fan runs constantly, so switched back to Balanced Mode. We'll see how some later games play.Recommended!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Perfectly capable little computer, great form factorPerfectly capable little computer, great form factor
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This is a very neat little box of a computer, and if you know what you plan to do with it, I think it's a pretty good value.Basic setup is extremely simple, literally just plug in your mouse/monitor/keyboard and the power supply and turn it on. It booted with zero issues into the normal Windows 11 setup. For some reason the manufacturer recommends that you do not use a LAN cable when you first start the computer, but I was never planning on using it on anything but wifi, and it worked fine over wifi, so that is not a problem for me.Although I am planning in the future to install Linux on this machine, I was grateful that it came with minimal Windows 11 bloatware (just the windows standard stuff). Although initial setup was very fast, as soon as it connected to the internet it discovered that it had a year's worth of Windows updates to install, which takes a while, so the second time you restart the computer, expect it to go through a long update process (10-15 mins).I had no trouble hooking up Bluetooth peripherals (in my case a controller).If you are planning to use this computer for general purpose web browsing/word processing/light home server use/etc, you will have zero problems. For general purpose tasks, this computer is great. It's extremely snappy when browsing the web, downloading files, and running programs like Steam or Discord.I think advertising this as a gaming PC is a bit of a stretch-- there's only so far integrated graphics will get you, and I suspect this computer will suffer if you try to run any truly top of the line games on it. It is great for older games, or lighter indie games. I tested it on Fallout New Vegas and Celeste and it had zero issues whatsoever. I ran a benchmark test and it performed predictably poorly compared to computers with dedicated graphics cards. You can get a little more juice out of this machine by changing the allocation of VRAM in the BIOS. It's by default set at 3GB, but I went in and bumped it up to 8 (see the options in the pictures). After doing that, I didn't notice any performance dips from reallocating away the regular RAM. The 32GB this machine comes with is very generous.Even when I was trying to stress-test this machine, it was very quiet, and putting my hand on the top of the case, it never produced a ton of heat. The best way I could describe this machine is unobtrusive-- it's really small and could easily be mounted beneath a desk to completely hide it away. The power supply it comes with is almost the same size as the computer itself. The computer comes with a mounting bracket that I think is intended to be used to mount it to the wall.My one grumble is that the 1TB of onboard storage will run out pretty quickly if you're a person with a large media library like I am. I am not sure how upgradable the storage is, but I guess I can always just attach an external hard drive if I need more storage.The display options are HDMI and DisplayPort, which is fine. I wish the audio jack were on the back of the box rather than the front, but it is what it is.It comes very well packaged, works right out of the box, and performs exactly as expected. If you have a need for general purpose computing in a small form factor, this will serve that need.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Better than expected, but you need realistic expectations
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I definitely recommend this mini PC, but it is not for everybody. I spent several weeks watching videos of testing and gameplay in different devices before selecting this device with this APU, because I am a gamer and also a developer. For an average user who does not play the newest, high-spec games, this should be more than enough.I got what I expected and a bit more -- it performs better than I expected. It has not failed to meet my expectations in the 3 months I've used it, and I use it every day for many hours.The device is reliable, and the 7840HS APU is exceptional. I have played games on this which have higher requirements than this device offers, and it has done well despite being "below spec", (ymmv). The fan is as noisy as I would expect from a laptop-type fan, so beware that if you put this under heavy load you will notice the fan noise, but it isn't any different than a laptop fan running at full speed. They have online access for updates like BIOS, which I've not updated yet but seems relatively simple.The only complaint I've got is, I'm struggling to reach the BIOS menu. My monitors are 75hz and on most desktop PCs that's not a big deal, but on mobile processors with integrated graphics you can encounter issues reaching BIOS when using monitors over 60hz, as it is not built by default to accept higher monitor refresh rates. I have found multiple sources online which state you can get around this by using a different cable such as VGA (I use HDMI and Display Port), but I have not had the opportunity to try yet. However, I have seen recent YouTube videos where people have successfully reached BIOS on the GMKtec K6, so it is an issue on my end and not the device.I typically will have a lot of things going on, usually streaming videos, plus many browser tabs, plus a game of some kind, plus some apps, and this device really handles it all very well. I treat it like a normal PC, and it does truly rise to the challenge, despite being small lower power -- it is a significant change in power consumption from my gaming PC, which is quite nice, because I haven't really sacrificed anything significant to go smaller!Overall, I'm very impressed. I have been telling everybody about it now that I've had a chance to really feel it out.It will play games like Cyberpunk 2077, but you may need to tweak the settings to get the most out of it. Do not expect it to run heavy games like an actual full gaming PC with a dedicated GPU. Have realistic expectations, but don't be surprised if this little device exceeds them.10/10, would buy again, no doubts.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: On the first day of use this monitor has many lines of pixels that infrequently lose power. It reminds me of antenna TV static except it is organized across approximately 15-lines of pixels that span the screen. The locally failed display persists for a few seconds, then fades away and returns to a normal monitor. A few minutes later the cycle repeats. The distraction makes it impossible to use the monitor for work. The other issue is the monitor's power cord. The cord is less than 36-inches so unless you have a power outlet on, or immediately on the underside of the desk, you'll have a problem. The power transformer integrated into the plug and covers 3-outlets on your power bar. Replacement aftermarket power transformers will cost you an additional $25 to $35 to compensate for this problem they've forced on you. The monitor itself struggles to display accurate colors. White can be tan and muddy or blue, and is only truly white when you have the brightness approaching 100%, which can be hard on your eyes after many hours. Lastly, the monitor does display 3840x2160 but automatically reduces the refresh rate down to 30hz, which is the final disappointment. I purchased a 27" Dell S2725QS, which uses the same LG panel but 1) has a higher refresh rate, 2) has a standard (and longer) power cord, and 3) has integrated speakers for only about $20 more.
