productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I’ve been using this Acer 27-inch monitor for a couple of weeks now and I have to say — it’s tremendously nice. As someone who spends long hours in front of a screen for both work and gaming, this display has been a fantastic upgrade.What I love about it:•  Smooth 120Hz refresh rate – Everything feels noticeably more fluid compared to my old 60Hz panel. Scrolling, gaming, and even just moving windows around feels buttery smooth. The 1ms VRB and Adaptive Sync make fast motion look crisp with very little tearing or ghosting.•  Excellent picture quality – Colors are vibrant (especially with that colorful abstract wallpaper shown in the product images), and the flicker-free technology really helps reduce eye strain during extended use.•  Great size for productivity and entertainment – 27 inches is the sweet spot for me. Plenty of real estate for multitasking without feeling overwhelming on my desk.•  Solid build and stand – The monitor feels well-made, and the stand is stable. Setup was quick and straightforward right out of the box.•  Value for money – For the features and performance, this Acer delivers outstanding bang for the buck.Helpful Tips:•  Tilt adjustment: The stand allows for easy tilt. Gently hold the top and bottom edges of the screen and push/pull to find your perfect viewing angle. It’s very responsive once you get the feel for it.•  OSD menu navigation: The buttons are located on the bottom edge. Take a few minutes to explore the picture modes — I found the “Standard” or “Gaming” modes worked best for my needs, and adjusting brightness/contrast to your room’s lighting makes a big difference.•  Cable management: The included cables are good quality. I recommend using the DisplayPort cable if your graphics card supports it for the full 120Hz experience.Acer has done a wonderful job with this monitor. It’s reliable, performs beautifully, and looks modern on the desk. I’m genuinely impressed and would happily recommend it to friends and family. Thank you, Acer team — keep up the great work!If you’re on the fence, go for it. You won’t regret it.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I was definitely a little nervous about ordering this, I’ve never owned a mini pc and was not sure if a generic mini pc at this price would be any good. After using it the last couple of days I am actually pretty impressed…especially for the price. It came packaged very nicely and it boots up almost instantly, so far I have zero complaints. If your someone who has no idea how to set up a computer you might run into some trouble because the owners manual is pretty hard to follow but for anyone that has set up a pc before there will be no issues at all. I’m very satisfied with this purchase and it does everything i need it to and it does it well. The thing is insanely quiet as well, it makes literally no noise at all. I really like that it came with a little bracket so that you can mount it to the back of a monitor. The price is very competitive given the specs and I would for sure recommend it to anyone looking for a good computer for work, school, surfing the internet, etc. I would not be surprised recommend it for gaming however…im not saying you can’t play any games on it but it def can’t handle AAA gaming.

features: MINI PC COMPUTER OFFICE LIGHT GAMING - GMKtec Nucbox G10 Series is equipped with the Ryzen 5 3500U, a 64-bit quad-core mid-range performance x86 mobile microprocessor. This processor is based on AMD's Zen+ microarchitecture and is fabricated on a 12 nm process. The 3500U operates at a base frequency of 2.1 GHz with a TDP of 15 W and a Boost frequency of 3.7 GHz. This APU supports up to 32 GB of dual-channel DDR4-2400 memory and incorporates Radeon Vega 8 Graphics operating at up to 1.2 GHz. 20% Multi-core Performance increase over previous Ryzen 3 models such as 4300U. 35% performance increase over the Intel N-series N95/N97/N150.

RYZEN 5 3500U vs RYZEN 3 4300U COMPARISON - Why Choose Ryzen 5 3500U: Better multi-threaded performance: More threads, better suited for multitasking and demanding applications. Better graphics: With Vega 8, it's superior for casual gaming, video playback, and GPU-intensive tasks. Overall higher performance: Higher boost clock and better ability to handle a variety of workloads, from light gaming to productivity tasks. So, if you're looking for a more balanced processor with stronger multitasking capabilities and better GPU performance, the Ryzen 5 3500U would be the clear choice.

16GB DUAL CHANNEL DDR4 + 512GB SSD - Installed with DDR4 16GB SO-DIMM RAM Dual Channel (2x8GB) and a 512GB SSD, the Nucbox G10 mini pc supports memory expansion to 64GB RAM. Featured with Dual M.2 2280 PCIe 3.0 slots, supports dual storage slot expansion to 16TB SSD (2*8TB). (Upgrades not included) This model supports a configurable TDP-down of 12 W and TDP-up of 35 W.

UNLEASH RAW PERFORMANCE MODE 25W - Dominate demanding tasks with the AMD Ryzen 5 3500U processor. When switched to Performance Mode in the BIOS (press "Esc" key repeatedly during boot, save then exit), this mini PC delivers superior multi-core processing power, significantly outperforming Intel N-series chips in CPU-intensive applications, multitasking, and creative workloads.

MINI DESKTOP COMPUTER WITH TRIPLE DISPLAY SCREEN - Nucbox G10 integrates AMD Radeon Vega 8 1200 MHz GPU to deliver powerful graphics processing power to easily handle video editing, and playback, or casual gaming. And it can connect to 3 display screens simultaneously via HDMI 2.1 TMDS/ DPv1.4/ TYPE-C.

ULTIMATE PORTABILITY WITH TYPE-C CHARGING: Power the mini PC effortlessly with a common 65-70W (19V-20V/3.42A) USB Type-C PD charger. This versatility allows you to ditch bulky power bricks and even run your system on-the-go using a high-output portable power bank, making it perfect for mobile offices, presentations, or entertainment anywhere.

2.5GBE ETHERNET FAST NETWORK SPEEDS - Enjoy up to 2500Mbps data transmission speed without worrying about lagging. Ideal for working, gaming, and surfing the internet. Great for Untangle, Pfsense or as a server office PC.

FAST WIRELESS INTERNET WIFI 5 + BT5.0 - Enjoy blazing WiFi 5 & Bluetooth 5.0 alongside a powerhouse selection of ports - dual USB 3.2, USB 2.0, stunning 4K@60Hz HDMI 2.1 TMDS, Full Function USB-C (PD/DP/Data), dedicated DisplayPort, 3.5mm audio, and PD Power Supply for seamless multitasking and premium connectivity.

GMKTEC WARRANTY - offers a 1-year limited warranty for each mini PC, starting from the date of the purchase. All defects due to design and workmanship are covered. With a professional after sales team always ready to attend to your needs, you can simply relax and enjoy your mini PC.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Best Cost to performace ratio ive seen so farBest Cost to performace ratio ive seen so far
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Been using this for my Arch setup, and everything is easy to tweak and install.The quality of the edges are better than most I see on other nucboxes, and I use it with no  problems with latency with my display playing Starcraft on max quality.  I've also been using it as a NAS, and its been working. The windows 11 comes preinstalled, so it was very little at time consuming for any of the initial setups. The size was enough to punch it inside my room corners, and takes very little power from the previous models that uses n100.The compatibility is top notch, as it's easy to install a new ssd or ram by popping up the title cover, and add away to your heart's desires. I added an extra 1TB to dual boot, but it's definitely managable with just 512 gb of storage. The fans are pretty much silent. never knew they were even running until I was halfway on my cyberpunk with max resolution. The front two usb 3.0 ports are fast for booting and reading, while the bios is fast and secure boot disabled, which saved me from having to troubleshoot why my grub wasn't loading for 2 hours.  Would recommend for a general purpose PC to run steam, use as a distro tester, or just have one to add to your NAS.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Fast, low wattage, and powerfulFast, low wattage, and powerful
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Really happy with my purchase, the M8 is a little workhorse. I can confirm it comes with an activated Win 11 Pro. Even though GMK has never seen an issue, I have a ritual - I boot from USB and image the NVME fresh (after getting the Windows key from a command line just in case), then wipe the mini pc's NVME (deleting all partitions) and install Windows 11 fresh. Windows picked up the BIOS key automatically on install and launched right into a fresh Windows 11 Pro. Network and sounds drivers were missing, but I grabbed them from the Europe site (Google it) and ran the .bat file. Without a reboot, everything picked up and no yellow exclamation marks in Device Manager. Windows Update took about 20 mins, as I fresh installed the newest Win 11 version (25H2 as of this writing).So the PC itself is rock solid, no blue screens, streams OBS 4k just fine, and have no random crashes or reboots. It's a great Docker server or workstation PC if needed, runs Office just fine. I notice no loud fan noise. Can’t comment on Oculink, I don’t use it.If you're looking for an all-in-one on the Ryzen platform, this one is a good bang for the buck.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I would have given it 5 stars, if it had not became inoperable within a week.  The problem was most likely due to a Windows update that removed necessary hardware definition files.  With the help of GMKtec people, I was able to get it working again using their link to download a rescue utility. I created a bootable USB (ISO) on another computer.  I re-booted the GMKtec with the Microsoft USB ISO starting with the least intrusive tool, then continuing on to the next level recovery tool within Microsoft "advanced utilities", until the problem was solved.  I lost no files or programs or settings.  This is a great little computer.  I purchased this unit to run a once-a-year program that requires Windows 11.  I added a second NVMe drive then installed the operating system that I trust for daily, efficient, flawless, and spy-free operation... Debian 13.  Installing a drive on this computer is so easy...just pop off the top and insert it.  This computer is as strong and functional as a Intel i5 series 8.  For those who prefer an uncluttered desk, install this powerful, little box to the back of the monitor.  Processing speed, graphics and storage are more than enough, even for power users.  I am very happy with my purchase and I would buy it again.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: It's decent for the price but it's way too late I would have bought it 2 months ago..
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: It's a good PC.  Windows 11 does not do it any justice. It will work for gaming. But not for large games in ultra quality if you're gaming on this you're going to be in 1080P at low or ultra low quality with all of the cool stuff turned off that makes your game look nice. If you want a game in low quality there you go.. this is the perfect device for you. However if you put it into performance mode it runs uncomfortably Hot for me. 90° + c is a little too hot for my comfort and then the nvme starts throttling.. so if you wanted to work keep it in balanced mode it will still game in that mode. productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: Very capable mini PC, Good for any office workVery capable mini PC, Good for any office work
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: I bought the GMKtec G10 mainly as an everyday office and home machine, and after a few weeks of daily use I'm impressed by how much computer you get for this price. With 16GB RAM and 512GB SSD, it's at a very good price in this RAMpocalypse.This combination of hardware makes a real difference in day-to-day responsiveness. Windows boots in seconds (keep in mind that it comes with Win 11 Pro, not home, so extra features are unlocked), apps launch instantly, and there's none of the lag you'd expect from a machine this small and affordable. For the kind of work most people actually do: email, Word, Excel, big spreadsheets, PDFs, a browser with a dozen-plus tabs open, plus Teams or Zoom running in the background, it just handles it.The thing that genuinely surprised me is the multitasking headroom. I regularly have multiple HD video streams going at once. A YouTube video in one window, a webinar in another, and a video file playing on a second monitor, all while I'm typing in a document and flipping through browser tabs. The integrated graphics plays the video smoothly, no stutter, no fans screaming. Even the integrated speakers are, while not great, very usable.Connectivity is excellent for the size. I was very surprised to see 2.5GbE LAN port in a machine this small. The triple 4K display support via HDMI, DisplayPort, and USB-C let me run a multi-monitor setup without any docks or adapters. Plenty of USB ports up front and back, so peripherals were a non-issue.A few honest notes: this is a 15W mobile-class chip, so it's built for productivity and media rather than serious gaming or heavy video rendering. If you go in expecting an office and daily-driver machine, you'll be delighted; if you expect a gaming rig, that's the wrong tool. It runs cool and quiet under normal load, which I appreciate on a desk.Bottom line: for the price, this is one of the best value office mini PCs I've used. As a fan of mini PC's, this is not my first time buying from GMKTEC and they did not disappoint. Easy recommendation for a home office, small business, or anyone who wants a tidy, capable everyday desktop that fits under or behind their monitor.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: One dead ram slot, loose heat sink and something was stuck to a pin on the cpu.One dead ram slot, loose heat sink and something was stuck to a pin on the cpu.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Seemed good at first but when I put 2 good matched sticks of ram in it so I could run dual channel and it wouldn't boot. I discovered slot 2 was dead after much ram swapping and testing. I also noticed the fan was loose so I checked the heat sink and it had 3 loose screws too. I took it off and there was hardly any paste either. I then decided to check for bent pins and didn't find any but one had something black stuck to the base? Used an old soft toothbrush and got the black thing off but slot 2 is still dead after putting it back together. Going to try and exchange it and see if the next one has 2 working ram slots after I find a pin map and find out if that pin had anything to do with slot 2 maybe there's more of it stuck in the slot.Yep after much searching the pin with the black spot is ma_clk_h[3] DRAM Channel A DIMM 0 Differential Clock. So I bet there is more black stuff that slot on the motherboard or the one next to it that is the other channel.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Decent machine quickly with some issues.Decent machine quickly with some issues.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: So the shipping was quick and the listing was mostly accurate. Drive size, RAM, and CPU were all accurate to the listing. There was a loose 2.5 inch drive tray in the case and the speaker was also hanging loose. Those were easy fixes. There were two major issues. One, no WiFi antenna for the built in wifi card, the instead sent a USB wifi dongle. That was just tacky. I happen to have some SMA connectors and antennas sitting in a drawer so I solved that issue, but for others beware you may have to grab a cheap one or cannibalize something else to use the onboard WiFi. The bigger issue was the locked BIOS. After booting in had the displeasure of having it ask for a password to get into the BIOS. After some searching this particular model you can wipe the BIOS by jumpering 2 pins on the MoBo (see pictures), turning it on and waiting for 2 beeps, turn off then putting the jumper back. Not all Think centres are like this, so got lucky here and I want to call out the seller in that they really shouldn't sell it like that.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The Samsung 27" ViewFinity S7 (S70H) is an excellent productivity-focused monitor for anyone who wants sharp 4K resolution, accurate-looking colors, and a comfortable viewing experience. The 27-inch IPS panel provides plenty of screen real estate while the 3840x2160 resolution makes text, images, spreadsheets, and detailed content look impressively crisp. It also offers useful connectivity and Samsung's Display Manager software for improving workflow.Positives:- 4K UHD resolution delivers exceptionally sharp and detailed images, making text and fine details easy to see- High pixel density provides a noticeable upgrade over standard Full HD displays, especially for office work and creative tasks- IPS panel offers consistent image quality and a wide 178° viewing angle- HDR10 enhances contrast with deeper blacks and brighter highlights for more engaging compatible content- Wide viewing angles make it easy to share the screen or work from different positions without significant changes in brightness- HDMI and DisplayPort connections provide convenient compatibility with computers and other devices-- Eye Saver Mode helps reduce blue-light exposure for more comfortable extended viewing- Flicker-reduction technology helps minimize visual fatigue during long work sessions- Samsung Display Manager adds useful productivity features, including split-screen setup, brightness adjustments, KVM, PIP/PBP, and calibration controls- 27-inch size provides a good balance between desk space and usable screen area- The high-resolution display is particularly well suited for documents, spreadsheets, multitasking, photo work, and detailed applicationsNegatives:- The 4K resolution can require display scaling on some operating systems to make text and interface elements more comfortable to read- Users looking primarily for competitive gaming may prefer a monitor with a higher refresh rate and gaming-specific features- HDR performance is useful for compatible content, but this is primarily a productivity monitor rather than a dedicated HDR entertainment display- The 27-inch screen may feel somewhat small for users who prefer a larger workspace for extensive multitaskingFinal VerdictThe Samsung ViewFinity S7 S70H is a very capable 27-inch 4K monitor that prioritizes productivity, image clarity, and comfortable long-term use. The sharp UHD resolution, IPS panel, HDR10 support, wide viewing angles, and Eye Saver features make it a strong choice for office work and everyday computing. Samsung Display Manager is another nice addition for users who regularly multitask and want more control over their workspace. Overall, this is a polished, high-resolution monitor for professionals, students, home offices, and anyone who values a crisp and comfortable 4K display.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: UPDATE: I have continued issues watching movies on Amazon and Netflix. I've had to lower the resolution yet again. It is now 2048x1152. In terms of watching movies, this is way worse than previous lower resolution monitor. Samsung still hasn't provided an updated driver. If this continues, I may have to go back to my LG Monitor.Previous review:This monitor is a photographer's dream! The display is sharp and detailed. The colors are not just accurate, but subtle. I was able to put the monitor together without reading the instructions, though I think it is best if you do read them. The screen comes with both HDMI and DisplayPort cables. There is also a USB-A port on the back. I'm surprised how lightweight the unit is. I can easily carry it in one hand without straining anything. It has a single rocker button interface that controls all the settings. Out of the box, I think the colors were good and brightness was set to a reasonable level. I use a Spyder densitometer to set accurate colors for photo editing. After I had done that, the color has shifted only slightly. The reading indicated that the monitor is about 110% of the sRGB spectrum which is the most standard for general photo editing. It comes in respectfully on the AdobeRGB spectrum as well, but I don't use that as it is too hard to get that standard to translate to prints off my printers. The monitor gets plenty bright if you want it to. I use TwinkleTray to adjust brightness on the fly. For general use, I have it set to only 17% which is amazingly low. The anti-flicker tech on this monitor is great too. I have zero eye strain even after staring at the monitor for hours on end. And last, is the resolution. This is my first 4K monitor, and it is almost too detailed. I've had to change settings on a number of apps as the text is too small to see easily unless I lean in.However, there are some issues. First, there is some light falloff at the corners. This becomes less apparent the further away from the monitor you get. I am using this monitor with an Intel NUCI IDBBi7. Despite having a moderately high-end computer with 64GB or RAM, there are problems with Samsung's driver. Some videos and web pages cause screen jittering. This is really annoying! Trying to access Text can appear ghosted. I lower the resolution down to 1080P to get stable results. When I removed the driver and went back to a generic display driver things settled down. I hope Samsung reads this and releases a new version of the driver soon so I can update this review. In the meantime, I haven't encountered any new issues using the generic driver.Overall, I'd say this is a fantastic monitor as long as you have a good graphics card and don't run into driver issues. For the price, it makes editing photos a joy!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Bright, Vivid Monitor With Great Productivity Features and Surprisingly Fun PIP/PBP Use
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This Samsung monitor has been a fantastic addition to my personal setup. I’m using it for a mix of light gaming, project work, and general productivity, and the jump to a 32‑inch 4K panel from a pair of 12 year old 23-inch monitors is immediately noticeable. The screen is super bright and vivid, with crisp text and excellent clarity across the entire display. For everyday use, coding, browsing, and media, it’s a huge upgrade in comfort and workspace.The VA panel delivers deep blacks and strong contrast, especially in HDR10 mode. It’s not an OLED, but for the price range, the color richness and contrast are impressive. Viewing angles are solid for a VA panel. Straight‑on looks fantastic, and even slight horizontal shifts hold color well. Vertical angles show more of the typical washout, but nothing unexpected. When my toddler is in the office, it's usually what will be playing music for him and the winamp style equalizer bring both of us joy.One of my favorite features is the Picture‑in‑Picture and Picture‑by‑Picture functionality. I’ve been running Forza on the main screen while keeping my phone connected as a PIP window for music or videos. It’s a genuinely cool experience and makes the monitor feel more like a multi‑device hub than just a display. The multiple connectivity options help with that too: HDMI and DisplayPort cover everything I need, and an HDMI‑to‑USB‑C cable lets me plug in my tablet, phone, or Switch with no hassle. The Samsung Display Manager software is another strong point. Splitting the screen, adjusting brightness, or switching between inputs is quick and intuitive.Physically, the monitor is lightweight and easy to mount. I have it on an arm, and it’s surprisingly impressive in portrait mode. It's been perfect for reading, editing documents, or vertical workflows. The stand itself is basic and lacks height adjustment, but the VESA mount makes it easy to work around that.Gaming at 60Hz is fine for casual play (personally am running it through a cloud environment, so no complaints here). It’s not built for high‑motion competitive gaming, but for racing games, RPGs, and general entertainment, the picture quality carries the experience. Ghosting is minimal on the panel, and HDR adds a nice punch to visuals.For productivity, the 4K resolution gives a massive amount of usable space. Running multiple windows side‑by‑side feels natural, and text is sharp enough that long reading or editing sessions don’t strain the eyes. The brightness adjusts well to ambient lighting, and the anti‑glare coating keeps reflections manageable.If these go on sale, I’d absolutely pick up a second one to replace my work setup and blend everything I do at the desk into a single unified layout. At it's current price, it's a great value, but not until one of my existing monitors kicks the bucket...a sale though, would swap them immediately :)  Between the vivid display, flexible connectivity, and genuinely useful PIP/PBP features, it’s a great monitor for anyone who wants a large, bright, versatile 4K screen without overspending.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Preamble: I currently have 4 DELL S2740L Super Glossy Monitors and love them. Recently, I purchased 3 of Samsung's 32" Odyssey G5 G50F QHD as future replacements when these begin to go (I bought them in 2013 and so far, they are still perfect as day 1, just had to replace on power adapter.) My G50F review is here:  https://www.amazon.com/gp/customer-reviews/R6BZE4PXUWKAMRegarding this Samsung 27" ViewFinity S7, it's a fairly standard IPS monitor that I would expect at the price point of around $250 today, currently at the time of review: $249.99. With that said, let me list my initial impressions of it:1. AG Coating is acceptable, I've seen a lot worse, especially from Dell. Is it's like Samsung TV's? Unfortunately no, it's shows that it has a AG coating compared to their TVs. Initially out of the box, it actually looks nice/slightly glossy like a TV, but that's due to the protective film (excitement was short lived.) I would have kept the protective film on if it wasn't for the writing they put in the bottom left hand corner, especially since with AG coated screens, fingerprints and saliva (yes, saliva, some people spray the screen when they talk) is very difficult to remove compared to a glossy screen, they come right off with a microfiber towel and some distilled water.2. Colors are less saturated unless you bump that up in the settings (out the box, the Odyssey G5 G50F QHD is more saturated and more color eye pleasing,) however, some people may want more color accuracy compared to more color saturation by default.3. Doesn't have speakers, but does have a headphone output that you can plug into desktop speakers next to the power input. I haven't tested it yet, but that's a nice touch for cases where you may want to plug in a device like a roku in the HDMI port and watch with audio.4. This model also uses a rear settings control joystick which I don't like, very bad ergonomics.5. The stand is fix in positioning unlike the  Odyssey G5 G50F which can swivel and has height adjustment.6. The photos were taken with a S24 Ultra playing the Samsung QLED demo video using a Roku stick in the HDMI port.7. Only has 2 ports, one for HDMI and one for a DisplayPort. This model only comes an HDMI cable, the G5 G50F comes with both, HDMI and DisplayPort cables.8. Design wise, it'll fit into almost every office/home setup and is lightweight if you need to move it around.9. Auto HDR is nice! There's also quite a few a preprogrammed display settings to choose from, in the photos, I took pictures on each mode, however, it's more obvious in person that with the photos to see the differences.10. Standard IPS glow...didn't observe any anomalies like blooming/clouding.Bottom line, it's a fine deal for a 27" IPS Monitor. If you're looking for an AWESOME deal on 32" 2K Samsung Monitor with out-of-the-box nicer color saturation (I got mine for $219 each,) take a look at this: https://www.amazon.com/Samsung-Resolution-Compatible-FreeSyncTM-LS32FG502ENXZA/dp/B0G1DZM5QW They also make a 27" model of the Odyssey G5 too, but I have no personal experience with it.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Fantastic productivity monitor for those who can’t go back to 60hz.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: After upgrading to a 360hz 1440p OLED and giving away my old 144hz 1440p IPS, I needed another monitor primarily productivity and programming as a CS student. But after trying other 27 inch 4k monitors with 60hz refresh rates, it didn’t feel like home. it just made everything feel slower and made me feel less productive. But this monitor ticks all my boxes, it reaches 350 nits brightness which is on par with my old monitor but with noticeably better contrast. You wouldn’t think 1000:1 to 1500:1 makes a difference if you own an OLED that can literally reach infinite:1 but yes, it makes a big difference. Colors look good to me when just eyeballing it next to my 2019 MacBook at a comparable brightness. The resolution at this size is fantastic text and every part of the UI is ultra crisp like my MacBook (honestly even more so, I think ClearType makes a big difference). Viewing angles are great. The matte coating does produce some grain which is noticable if you are in a dark room viewing full white screen within a foot away but it’s by far not the worse i’ve seen and with dark mode I legitimately cannot notice it and the reflection handling is pretty great.Now the refresh rate… wow. 4k on 27 inches with 120hz is just, stunning. Just feels like the way navigating a desktop is meant to feel. It honestly feels like a crime we use 60hz for literally anything, it makes everything just feel way more responsive. Response times are okay, absolutely fantastic for a productivity however for gaming with a mouse it wouldn’t be my first pick. It’s not my use case but I feel I should mention it. There is quite some noticable ghosting in games but I am coming from an OLED so I am probably particularly sensitive to noticing it. It’s FreeSync compatible which is just great but I would spend a bit more to get faster pixel response personally if you are going to ever play FPS games with keyboard and mouse on it. But if you are getting it for playing on a controller or console then you’ll probably be pretty happy and I would choose it over a another gaming focused monitor with 1000:1 contrast even with it’s relatively slower response time (it’ll be lightning fast compared to any LCD TV). People recommend getting and gaming on much slower VA MiniLED panels all the time so that’s worth mentioning.My only true complaint for my use case is there is a slight amount of vignetting on the right side of the panel which is only noticeable if I purposely move a light mode window to the edge and back again, watching it closely. I literally never notice it during actual work since I use dark mode but even if I used light mode I doubt it would bother me much if at all. No noticable flicker, IPS glow is very minimal with no noticable hotspots. Overall pretty great panel for the price and I couldn’t imagine wanting much more out of a productivity monitor.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Started out great, really impressive, then it died, but customer support was excellent
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: For the first 24 hours, I was really impressed. Really snappy performance, 8 GB of RAM was plenty for simple tasks, and the SSD was capacious at 256 GB, considering the price. The inclusion of Windows Pro made the box almost free! However, after updating to Windows 11 Build 22H3, during the process of applying updates, the computer locked up. After 60 minutes with the computer no longer visible on the network and the keyboard and mouse non-responsive, pulled the power cord. Upon restoring power and turning on the computer, the PC was stuck for hours at the spinning circle during boot.Two more power-cycles and Windows repair interface appeared. Selected Windows Reset, Local Source (wouldn't work with cloud source), Windows began resetting. However, after a restart, computer back to the infinitely spinning circle. :-(If this had proved reliable, I'd have bought a dozen or more as remote monitoring PCs for client networks. But given that I've had good luck with the similarly priced AWOW models, I will not be investing any more money or time in the GMKTek offerings.Update 01-07-2024-----------------------Fortunately, GMKTek provides a download for a Windows 11 re-installation ISO. With this and leveraging a fair amount of knowledge of Windows installation options, was able to re-image the SSD. Unfortunately, the product key is invalidated and I had to use a spare Windows 10 product key to re-activate Windows. Unfortunate the GMKTek hasn't worked out the same relationship with Microsoft that Dell has, whereby any Windows 11 ISO used to load Windows onto a Dell OptiPlex results in an automatically activated Windows 11 installation.Bottom line is that after recreating and updating all apsects of the re-installed Windows 11 OS, the PC is back to running normally. I know to steer clear now of some driver updates. The PC has been running for about 36 hours and I'll post an update if that changes in the near future.When this PC works, it represents a great value for the money in terms of hardware specs and a Windows 11 license. However, taking into account the time issue remediation takes and the expertise required, the TCO (total cost of ownership) rises significantly. If I never have to do brain surgery on this device again, I'll still feel the cost was justified based on the performance of this sub-$200 device.P.S. I now make a complete image backup before running/installing ANY updates so I can simply restore the image backup rather than running into yet another Windows 11 re-installation process and the requirement to use/purchase another Windows product key.P.P.S. The WIndows 11 re-installation ISO download was 11 GB and was not a standard Windows 11 installation ISO. This had to be burned to a flash drive (I used a 16 GB USB3 model; I used Rufus to create the bootable UEFI flash drive) and then the GMKTek PC booted with it. Upon boot, I was faced with a terminal window and a couple of choices. The one I chose led to an image/sysprep process that fortunately got the PC bootable once again with Windows 11 Pro.P.P.P.S. Highly recommended --> As soon as you boot the device for the first time, find a tool such as ProduKey by NirSoft and extract and save the Windows 11 product key. Ideally (although I didn't have a chance to test), this key would work if a re-install was ever required. The other option, that I was waiting for until the PC was fully updated, is to create an image backup using any number of tools, including the image backup tool in Windows. Thus, if any of your update processes results in a non-bootable PC, you can simply re-image from the backup and avoid having a non-activated instance of Windows 11.Update 01-12-2024-----------------------Vendor reached out proactively and offered some assistance, although I'd resolved the corrupt Windows 11 issue independently. However, that level of customer support is remarkable considering the price of this product and the lack of such support from other vendors with much pricier offerings. Due to this, upgrading the rating to four stars.Update 01-13-2024-----------------------Customer support proactively reached out and provided a product key so I could activate Windows 11 and free up my personal product key. GMKtec's proactive reaching out to a customer with issues is almost unparalleled in my experience over 40 years, so despite the issues I encountered, I'm raising my review to five stars. For a product this inexpensive but with excellent performance, providing this level of customer support is laudable.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Didn't waste time setting it up since it is Windows 11. Took a while but finally had all the updates installed. The first test was 4k video on YouTube - no issues. Network speed on fiber was almost 400mbs. The green color plastic case is nice, and wife thinks it's cute. Pretty snappy for what it is - paid $137 and it is well worth it. Basically, as much as a Raspberry Pi but $37 dollars more for memory and a hard drive. Loaded some GIS software to test performance and didn't see any issues there either. Loaded a fancontrol program for more refined control. Will test more but am very satisfied👍FEW DAYS LATERI bought this little PC ($135) for streaming TV and web browsing from a hotel. In the past I purchased a travel router and a streaming TV dongle, and it worked OK. This G3 is substantially better, is a great deal with all the hardware and Windows 11. The TVs picture is substantially better than the Chromecast while running the same YouTube TV app on the same TV.There were a number of settings I had to figure out but it's well worth it. First I like using a Bluetooth mouse with Windows accessibility virtual keyboard. The fan was a little loud but go to GetFanControl and read what their software does. The bios is very functional also with many settings but didn't change any yet. Had to change settings on my Samsung TV for the way the TV monitors USB connections. Turned it all off to work properly.It's a PC so it has all the same issues - updates, power settings, etc. but WOW! Connect to TV, log into Wi-Fi and you're up and running. Purchased an air mouse with keyboard and track pad but a regular mouse works well and less complicated. I didn't know my TV could look this good. You will need to figure out how to use the power button to hibernate and turn on. Once I turn it on I have to move the mouse to get a picture but as I mentioned - ITS A NICE NUC👍 for a TV streaming and web browsing from a hotel. productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Perfect gift for anyone whos not a tech invalid
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I love this thing. Easily one of the best purchases I've ever made. It's super portable with accessible and sufficient ports. productPageReviews.reviewTitle: This was a replacement for my older machine that was not upgradeable to win 11.  It worked well
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: My GMKtec arrived on time and booted up into windows 11 pro without any problems.  I used 2 monitors to test if it would run both simultaneously.  I went to best buy to add a cable to go to my old monitor which did not have the correct connections.  They both worked well together.I found one problem after a week or so that I could not solve. productPageReviews.reviewTitle: PC N100--reliable, powerful solution for office & home needs. Good factory support.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I am writing this after using a Mini PC N100 for eight months, and I can report that it has more than met my expectations.  Most of the setup was done automatically, but if you want to avoid it, you can start loading your own software before allowing the computer to check for updates.  My software consists of a word processor, Skype and Zoom, schematic and PWB editors (I'm a retired engineer), software for controlling radios and lab equipment, and software that helps me manage our home network.There are USB ports on the front and the rear of the enclosure.  I have two monitors on my desk, and I used the dual HDMI outputs to spread out projects and avoid having to page in and out of screens I was working with.The troubles came after my wife and I put our house on sale and moved to a smaller home in a retirement facility.  In the new setup, audio, streamed or from movies or online conferences, was accompanied by short buzzing sounds at roughly 1-second intervals.  I struggled with this for a few days and finally swallowed my pride and filed a trouble report with GMKtec.  This where many of the offshore PC manufacturers disappoint their customers.  I was in for a pleasant surprise, though, because a reply arrived in less than 24 hours.  A lady answered my request for help and promised a referral to a support person.  This gentleman offered a list of things to check--several of which I hadn't thought of--and then asked for a recording of the sounds.I provided the recording, and after more discussion, which didn't produce a solution, I was offered the option to replace the computer with a new bare bones unit.  Eventually, I chose to remove the memory and SSD and send my unit back to GMKtec.  I never got a chance to find out how quickly they would send a new PC N100, because shortly before printing a UPS label, I decided to clean up the area where the computer had been sitting, and I noticed that the power supply was a 19.5 Volt unit.  To shorten the story: I had packed things a little too carelessly when we were moving, and I mixed up the power supplies for the computer and another piece of equipment.  (The PC N100 uses a 12 Volt supply.)  When I connected the correct supply, the PC N100 worked perfectly.  No problems from then on.  I sent profuse apologies to my contact at GMKtec.  Appreciation and best wishes came from his end.So what can I report about the PC N100?  I does what I need from a computer.  It was easy to set up.  And even while it was struggling to overcome my mistake, it ran all of my software perfectly.  Factory support? Couldn't be better.  Thank you, GMKtec!  (Full disclosure: I was not offered any compensation for this report.  I've just summarized my experience with the company and one of its products.)

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Size Does Not Matter In This Case
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: So far this tiny PC is working well. I purchased it as a low cost solution to my 2014/2015 Acer Chromebook that was very outdated.This product was very easy to set up. You just plug it in and attach your monitor, mouse, and keyboard. It is that simple. They recommend not updating it at first if you want to explore its functionality, but I went ahead with all the Windows updates, which took a while and there were a few download failures. After working through the updates, I began loading the software that I need on it. As a note, this product does not come with a bunch of Google products pre-installed, which is a bonus. Microsoft Edge does come with it. It is bare bones for any added software, which I also find refreshing in this era. So far it is humming right along for what I need it for.The cons: there are limited USB ports (4) and two HDMI ports. You may need to invest in a USB hub for the long run if you have multiple external drives or other needs that require USB connectivity. The product does not feel as rugged as I had hoped but it does come with a bracket so you can secure it to a wall or table. After about an hour I could feel the heat pumping out the sides of the PC so I grabbed my other laptop's dual fan USB platform just out of precaution. I would recommend giving it a little boost if you can. For the low investment cost, I am very happy that I purchased this item. I bought the two year protection plan so I know I am going to get at least two years out of it. I find that worth the investment.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: Small form factor Windows 11 desktop with great energy efficiency.Small form factor Windows 11 desktop with great energy efficiency.
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: I received this package from Amazon last Monday, superfast delivery even without Prime. The packaging was sealed and already small, and the box is even smaller, all the content is shown on the photo. The G3 is very light weight and there's a metal clamp, I believe this is to attach and hide it behind a screen, however the box takes so little space that I simply place it even on a really small desk.The box's plastic material feels like good quality and the colour is a nice, maybe dark-olive green, I prefer that over white which often gets yellowish over time, black collects dust and grey looks boring. It is replacing a bulky old Omen gaming PC in the living room area that was 8 time more in height and about the same difference is true for the surface area, the photo gives you an idea. The old PC was used mainly for internet researches, some homework related uses, some attempts in coding and writing emails etc. A Steam client was running on it with quite a collection, but more casual games. One issue was that the old PC was on 24/7 and a gaming PC is drawing a fair bit of power and I don't need the heat it produces now in summer, the Omen must have used at least 10x more energy than this G3. The tiny charger that came with the box says in small font I believe 36W, but I suppose the G3 is running on a lot less on average, so at 20 Watts it costs just about 3 cents a day to run permanently. The box is slightly warm but definitely not hot. The other issue with the Omen was that it didn't allow an upgrade to Windows 11 although the specs on that gaming PC are not bad. The G3 comes with Windows 11 preinstalled and that was very is easy to set-up. I recommend to take a backup with a 16/32 GB USB stick immediately once you've installed your browsers and any additional software. It takes about a night to run a Windows backup but it is just good practice because you don't want to be forced to buy an expensive Windows licence if ever something happens, even if it feels unlikely with a fresh Windows 11, which in my experience is a stabile OS and has become fairly secure, make sure you don't disable the updates.I've been running the G3 now for a week with three different browsers (Edge is preinstalled), countless tabs open. I had no problems connecting the Samsung screen via HDMI, a USB keyboard (even has French has second layout), a USB mouse and a headphone (cinch). My Wifi printer worked without much hassle, very easy to add it in Windows 11.  This purchase fully meets my expectation and use case.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: The Nucbox G3 is a great mini-computer especially at its price point.The Nucbox G3 is a great mini-computer especially at its price point.
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: I’m someone who’s used to working with a traditional desktop setup, and so, I was skeptical about how well a mini-PC like the Nucbox G3 would work for me. However, after having it for a few weeks, I can say with confidence that this little box has blown me away with its performance, especially considering its price-point.SetupInitially after I opened the box, I was impressed with its compact size and sleek design. Setting up this computer was a breeze; it comes pre-installed with Windows 11 and the SSD allows for the booting of the computer to be very fast. Overall, the computer was extremely easy to get up and running, just plug it in, boot it up, and go through a quick Windows 11 setup and you’re ready to start using the computer.Price-to-PerformanceWhat sells this little computer for me is the price-to-performance ratio. The cheapest option is only ~$266CAD (8GB RAM 256SSD) and the most expensive option is ~$350CAD (16GB RAM 1TB SSD) at the time this review was being written. Wifi and BT is integrated. You can connect two 4K screens and run 4K videos on both at the same time. The noise from the cooling fan is negligible since it throttles according to load. Generally, in this price range, you wouldn’t find a computer nearly as good and especially not within such a small and compact size. The fact that is comes pre-installed with Windows 11 is just the cherry on top. This is great computer that costs less than some smartphones, yet I feel not any compromise.SizeThe Nucbox G3 is incredibly small, which makes it great for creating a “hidden” setup. You can just stick it to the back of your monitor and create a “hidden” PC setup and if you have a wireless keyboard and mouse, you can also create a “wireless” setup. As well as being great for creating a “hidden” setup this computer is also great as a media computer. Stick it to the back of your TV, connect a wireless media keyboard and you got yourself a media setup. Another great thing about the small size of this computer is its portability, taking this computer somewhere else and setting it up is just so easy compared to a regular computer because of its size. This computer is a great middle-grounds between a laptop and a regular desktop PC. Overall, the small and compact size of this computer fosters many benefits and allows for a variety of different setups you can create.ConclusionHonestly, if someone had switched my PC with the Nucbox G3 and didn’t let me know, I probably wouldn’t even notice a difference in my day-to-day use. It’s a really great computer and I have nothing bad to say about it at this point because it is serving me very well. You’re likely not going to be doing intense gaming on this (although you could do some casual, light gaming pretty well on this thing). From its quick and easy setup to its compact size I was delighted all the way through.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: My unit has a weird bug where if it goes to sleep, it will hard reset when it wakes up. (Kernel 41 error). Not a HUGE deal, as I just turned the sleep function off, but certainly makes me wary of other potential hardware fails or glitches.GMKtec did get right back to me about the issue through customer service - they suggested I edit something in the system registry - but I didn't want to mess with that.All in all though, I'm very happy with this. Machine is quiet and fast. The last PC I bought was in 2013, so you can imagine how far the tech has come since then.This thing is just blazingly fast with 32GB of RAM. I have no complaints about the quality of the build - it's sturdy and easy to use.I don't use the WiFi, I use an ethernet cable, so I can't comment on the WiFi issues some people experience.I would buy it again, to be totally honest. I'm excited for the future of mini PCs. I use it for some light gaming - CS2, guild wars - but it handles CS2 like a champ so I'm sure it can handle most games on low to mid settings. Older games run on high, obviously, no problem.EDIT: 6 Months///////////////I have had instances where I need to use the WiFi and it has worked fine for me in those scenarios. Nice!Would still recommend it to someone who is maybe on the savvier side of PCs. I definitely still don't trust it 100% to not fail on me, and I back everything up on an external.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Wow, very fast for just 15 watts of power.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Edit update again 01/10/2025: I fixed my fan issue and as promised raised the score back up to 5 stars. It is a good, fast little computer but does get hot when you are gaming. I recommend popping the top off and exposing the top fan to the outside as this really helps in keeping it cool. When you put the top back on, when your finished, don't snap the top back in place so it will be easy for you to remove when needed. I know this would bother some people but I am not bothered by it as it helps keep it cool. Still five stars for what it can do for it's size. Still highly recommended.Edit up date 01/09/2025: I had to reduce the GMKtec M5 Plus from five stars to three stars because the little top cooling fan will not work all the time. I have the lid on but not snapped in because I have to take it off to force the fan to run. A quick spin with my fingers gets it going but I got to keep an eye on it other wise the little computer will over heat even though it's only fifteen watts. This is serious and the reason for only three stars. I am going to try to contact them and if they help I will improve the review back to five stars.*Next is another concern that has a lot of YouTube press and that is, Mini PC's shipping out with Malware or viruses. Let me make clear that GMKtec has been cleared so far and I tested mine forward and backwards with zero positives but you should be made aware of this. The most offending company (watch YouYube to get the companies name as it is all over) still has not completely cleaned their computers and are being very sneaky in the way they hide the Malware. One buyer replaced his M2 SSD and loaded a fresh copy of Windows 11. If you are one of those people who are sensitive to computer security then you need to know what you are getting into with Mini PC's. I didn't know this before I bought mine. Please check out the problem on YouTube before you buy. If you do buy, do not connect to the net till you have run a complete check. I recommend the very long but important Windows 11, full virus scan and download the free version of Malwear Bytes and run a test with that. I hope Amazon allows this review update to be printed as this is an important issue that everyone should be made aware of before they buy a mini PC.First off, it worked right out the box. Early setup could not have been any easier, a smart 8 year old could have set this mini computer up. That's not stretching it either. However setting up all the drivers from AMD and getting Windows 11 up to date did take time and requires someone a little more knowledgeable.I bought this as a novelty but now using it all the time. My big gaming computer has taken a back seat to this amazing little mini computer.Pros: Very quite, Very fast, Yes it plays games but more on the casual level. Beautiful eye popping monitor visuals, It uses only 15 watts of power. That means it runs very cool. The AMD processor the 5825U is designed to run on 15 watts.Cons: Terrible instructions with tiny print. Example, they send you a piece of black metal with some black screws that looks like it might be some sort of mounting bracket but the instructions give you zero information on what it is for. It uses only 15 watts of power. I know I had that as a pro but it could also be a con if you want to play more powerful AAA games. But who would use a mini computer to play AAA games like Cyber Punk 2077 or Hogwarts. Come on, use common sense.I will end this by saying do your research. Not all mini computers are only fifteen watts like this one. And if you look you will find the newest mini computers are AM5 platform and use up to 70 watts. But those units run from seven hundred and fiftly to almost a thousand dollars. You start spending that muchmoney you might as well buy a full size gaming rig.Highly recommended

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I am not a gamer, but I decided to buy this PC for one of my workstations primarily for business as I had slowness issues with other devices.  I wanted horsepower, but a small form factor which I didn't think would exist until I discovered this machine.I have been blown away by the speed and responsiveness of this device.  It is lightning fast and responsive to running many memory intensive business applications.  I also have 3 monitors connected to the device since there are 2 HDMI ports and one USB- C port that can be used to support a 3rd monitor.  It is definitely worth the price and adding the coupon code makes it even more of a value.  There is no bloatware like other PCs out of the box have.If you want a high performing PC at a 1/3 of the cost of other well known devices to handle business applications, then look no further.  This hidden gem is definitely worth it!Update 2 months later:  This little device is still going strong without issues.  I have been pleasantly surprised with its speed and the ability to handle multiple applications at once without performance degradation.  This is such a great machine that I give my highest recommendation.Update 5.5 months from original purchase:  Over the course of the past few weeks, I have experienced some major issues with this device.1.  Network Intranet Speed:  I just added fiber internet to my home at a very fast speed tier.  All other hardwired devices are reporting appropriate speeds, but this device is showing a download speed significantly lower.  I have changed the cables multiple times, but still get lower speed.  The only way to resolve this has been to completely disconnect the cable and reconnect it.  But after a few hours, the issue returns.  Because I rely heavily on video conferencing for work, I have have found this aspect to be unreliable.2.  AMD Processor Errors:  As mentioned above, I do a lot of video conferencing for work.  About 2 weeks ago, I began receiving fatal errors about the processor as I use Zoom or Google Meet for these calls.  The computer froze and I had to restart the Zoom session.  This was not a good experience as I missed critical information communicated on the call.I'm likely going to put my old computer back in place since it was far more reliable than this.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Surprising performance in a little packageSurprising performance in a little package
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: In my real life, I am a Technical Writer and Knowledge Manager for the company I work for, so if this review seems a little long or maybe too detailed, I wanted to make sure you got as much information as possible as I started using the computer.  At home I am an avid movie and personal video collector and I just completed rebuilding my video server.  It is in a tower case and is occupying the only space I have in my office for such a computer. As part of the rebuild, I intended to separate the serving and processing functions, so I was searching for a compact solution that would allow me to render video content for the server.  This computer has provided everything I was looking for and more.These are the criteria I used in deciding on a replacement computerHigh speed processingI needed a computer that would help with video rendering.  I am not a gamer but the performance of a gaming computer would speed up the video work I do.  With the initial testing, this design is completing the rendering tasks about 20% faster that my previous computer.A compact Design.I have limited space on my desk for a PC.  This mini PC was great as the size gave me options on my already crowded desk.  Its size allowed me to place it behind a monitor, but there were also 2 mounting screw holes in the case so I decided to mount it to the back of  my desk.Convenience of Several connection options.With 4 USB A ports I was able to connect my printers, keyboard and mouse and still had USB C connection options for my USB monitor and an External SSD device.  See the picture Exterior Pictures Showing Ports and Top RemovalAlong with that connectivity there are options to connect wireless networks and to use Bluetooth top connect audio devices like headphones.ExpandabilityIn this small package I could still add an additional standard sized SSD.  The surprise expandability is found in the Oculink Port this port gives PCIe connectivity speed for external devices.What Came in the BoxThe computerIntroductory Booklet (Unfortunately not an English Page, but other picture have some English labels.)Power Supply and Power CordHDMI cable (Must boot first time on HDMI)Mounting Bracket (No instructions on the exact uses. I mounted mine using the mounting holes on the back of the case.)See the Picture What's In the BoxSetting up the ComputerUnpacking the computer was straight forward. There was no assembly required.  The only things needed to get started is a monitor to connect the HDMI cable (provided), a keyboard & mouse and to plug in the power supply.I followed the instructions on the yellow notice over the network ports advising that the system would set up much more quickly without Windows attempting to update during the initial boot up.  This worked great and I will use this process on any other computer I will build.  Within a few minutes, I was at the windows desktop. I was in a position to start installing software.  See picture Original Desktop.I then connected a network wire and I was able to install my software and connect to my Microsoft account.There was a bit of disappointment, as there were no instructions in English supplied. There were about 10-12 languages in a pamphlet included in the box but none were English. The drawings were labeled well enough to identify the details of the ports well enough for my trained eye, but the standard user may be left with questions about a few of the ports.I decided to add a second SSD to the computer and found the access inside very simple. Turned the top shield a quarter turn to the left and it unlocked exposing 4 screws that held the top fan in place. Once those were removed, the fan lifted out easily (be careful of the wire connecting the system board to the fan.)See the picture Disassembly with SSD 2 Slot IdentifiedAs part of the final setup, I had to decide where the computer would be on my desk.  I had a option to put it behind my monitor See Picture Behind the Monitor, but instead, I took advantage of the mounting holes on the bottom of the computer to hang the computer from the back of my desk.  See the picture Desk MountBIOS NotesI did look at the BIOS.  I was curious about how configurable it was as I have found with other units that the BIOS is very focused and not designed to allow tweaking. While the interface was not very fancy (very DOS like) it appeared to have several settings to adjust memory and processor. See the picture BIOS Advanced There are many drill down options.SummaryOverall this computer provides a significant performance boost over the equipment I had. In my research I found that the AMD products provide better performance for the dollar, combined with integrating the GPU into the chip design it made the unit compact while still providing enough horsepower to drive 3 monitors effectively. In the few days I have worked with this unit, I still find myself marveling at how fast bootup times are and how quickly applications launch and web pages load. If you are looking for a gaming computer I would give this one a chance, I think you will be surprised at the speed of this computer and its ability to keep up with some of the most demanding games.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Bought this last year because I wanted to try downsizing some of my systems. I didn't use the Windows 11 install that came with it and instead installed Ubuntu -- everything was detected just fine and I was up and running pretty quickly. The system was pretty snappy, although I wasn't pushing it super hard, just regular browsing, video watching etc. If you push the system, the fans ramp up and they can get a bit noisy at full tilt. When I bought it was also before the rampocalypse, so I got a great deal on it, too.A few months ago, though, the CPU fan started making a grinding noise. I turned off the system and emailed support since I was till in the one-year time window. I have a technical background, so I didn't need a full replacement or anything and let support know all I needed was a CPU fan via their web support form. A few days later they got back to me and after a bit of back and forth they asked for my address and shipped me a replacement fan. When I got the package, I was pleasantly surprised that they sent me both a cpu fan, and the system fan, along with some sealing tape to ensure airflow with the heatsink and a screwdriver which was super nice of them. The fix was pretty easy and I was up and running again after about a half hour.Overall mostly pleased, knocking a star off since the fan died in the first place and the system in general isn't really designed to be run at full load, but I think the support response was great.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great device! But... If you want to add in a 2nd SSD, you can't!Great device! But... If you want to add in a 2nd SSD, you can't!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The GMKtec M5 Plus performs well for its size — Tiny case, huge cyber-size! It's quiet, fast and more than capable for most workloads. However, once I opened the unit to upgrade the SSD, I discovered a design issue that buyers should be aware of.I was delighted to discover that the GMKtec had TWO SSD slots! But the delight was short-lived. It turns out, there's a design flaw that makes the 2nd SSD slot impossible to use!The internal layout places the second SSD directly under the fan shroud that’s molded into the inner top cover. If you install an SSD with even a low‑profile heatsink (the kind that comes pre‑attached on many drives), the fan cowling cannot be reinstalled. There simply isn’t enough vertical clearance.This means the second SSD slot is only usable with a completely bare drive, and even then, thermals may be questionable because the fan housing sits right on top of it.Copilot confirms that GMKtec doesn’t mention this limitation anywhere in the product description.If you only plan to use a single SSD, the system works fine. But if dual‑SSD support is important to you, be aware that the physical design of the case prevents standard SSD drives from fitting under the fan above the 2nd SSD slot.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Impressive engineering at a very reasonable price.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The short form: I wanted a small form-factor computer for general work and light-duty gaming. This machine provides it admirably.The longer form: I chose it because it promised a decent level of gaming performance for the one game I play, World of tanks, at a decent frame-rate without its having a to have a noisy, secondary fan to handle the kinds of heating that the additional performance needs.What I have, and what I'm writing this review on, is a machine that handles world of tanks with low medium graphics settings at a frame rate of 40-60 fps with a highish ping which fulfills my basic needs, and it can do more if I turn it's graphics settings to low, at which point its frame rate goes to over a hundred-and-ten fps which works to make up for my senior-citizen reaction speeds.For the general work requirement, it is more than adequate, as in "much more."I can run multiple applications on multiple desktops and stream video (Amazon, Netflix, etc.) with no problems. Although I am transitioning from Mac to Windows in order to use it, I found its set up was a fairly simple process.One very pleasant surprise of the thing is just how quiet it is and competent the thing has been. Right now, I'm running several different, none-too demanding apps, and the fan is barely audible. And, even when I run my gaming app, the top of the box has never gotten more than perceptibly, but not uncomfortably, warm to the touch.The artificial intelligence app built into the operating system is a surprisingly good knowledge-base that greatly extends the power of search engines to answer general knowledge and technical questions. It was particularly useful when the computer started crashing when I played YouTube videos. The suggestions it provided got me back normal function in minutes.Considering how internet integrated modern operating systems are,  I think it is imperative that you buy and install antivirus software as your second act with this or any computer.The bottom lineI am perfectly happy with this computer.I would like a smidgeon of additional graphics power for gaming, but, considering my needs and the price, and after a month of use, I am very satisfied with my purchas,  and I would definitely recommend it to someone like a college student or a light-duty gamer who was willing to trade a small amount of graphics power for noise-heat-and-hassle-free operation.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Handles just about everything you need...with some caveats.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I got this one 2 months ago upgrading from an old beelink ser4 and it is leaps and bounds better than that for sure. I've played videos, edited some videos played retro games and modern games. it won't play them at very high settings but at medium, the games still look pretty good with high frames (depending on the game of course)...as an example, i played spiderman remastered at medium settings running at about 80 frames....i'm more than satisfied playing at medium settings but it's nice to have the oculink port should i ever want to upgrade with an external gpu.As for the pc itself, it's extremely quiet. i can barely hear it. I like that you can open it from the top and that it has normal size screws for easy access. my previous mini pc came with extremely small screws that i had to buy a special screwdriver kit for. i like the translucent top as it lends itself to adding some rgb lighting if you want to customize it a bit...  A few minor issues to point out though...Mine came out of the box in the Quiet setting in the bios. Changing it to Balance or Performance made no difference. After asking in the reddit forums it turns out that windows has it's own power settings and will ignore anything you change in the bios if not enabled in windows 1st...so i had to go into the windows setting, dig through some settings trees to find the power setting to enable and accept the change in the bios. After that, it was smooth sailing. Odd that it came disabled to begin with...(use free monitoring software you can download to check if your pc is in the right settings).i also had to buy a usb hub as i found the usb ports it comes with weren't enough for all my accessories (mouse, keyboard, mic, camera, flashdrives, lights, etc.)...Another small gripe...the power button blinks on and off if you put the pc to sleep which can be very distracting...however, if you set it to hibernate there is no blinking light...It's only been 2 months but i think this mini will last me a few yrs without needing to upgrade. I will upgrade this review should any problems arise. So far i think it's the best 8845hs mini pc on the market when it comes to price to performance.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: A Simple Display Box, But Not Built for Speed
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I picked up this mini PC stick mainly because I needed a cheap way to power a touchscreen monitor and run a web-based dashboard. The setup was pretty straightforward, and once it was plugged in, the 4K display output looked sharp on my screen. For its size, it’s got all the basic connections you’d expect—WiFi, Bluetooth, and an Ethernet port. If you just need a small box to plug into a screen and keep a few browser tabs open, it does exactly what it’s supposed to on paper.The downside is how slow it feels once you actually use it. The processor and 4GB of RAM struggle with anything beyond light browsing, so switching between apps or loading a dashboard takes noticeably longer than it should. My biggest concern is the heat. Since it doesn’t have a fan, it gets pretty warm during normal use, and I’m honestly worried about how long the inside parts will last with that kind of constant warmth. It’s not a dealbreaker for occasional use, but if you leave it running all day, I’d pick a spot with good airflow or expect to replace it sooner rather than later.Overall, I’d call it a niche gadget rather than a real desktop replacement. It’s fine for digital signage, a light office task, or keeping a single dashboard visible on a touchscreen. Just don’t expect it to handle heavy multitasking or fast performance. If you know exactly what you’re using it for and can live with a slower system that runs warm, it’s an affordable option. If you want speed or plan to push it hard, you might want to spend a little more on something with a fan or better cooling.
