productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Best value 4K monitor on the market
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: After 3 days using this monitor, I continue to be amazed how good it is. IMO, it is the best 4K monitor value for the money. The color, contrast and sharpness are excellent. It is a great combination with my M4 MacMini. The monitor allows me to connect up to 3 computers with it's dual HDMI connectors and a DP.I love that the OSD buttons are on the front and you can set the menu size to large so you can see it easily. It allows you to turn the power indicator light off while the monitor is in use so the blue LED doesn't distract you. I wish all monitors could do that. Sometimes it is the little things that make a product stand out. This Viewsonic monitor is a good example.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on June 15, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I picked this up as a second monitor for my system to extend the display and have some work tabs open while doing other things. The setup was fairly easy and the entire unit seems to be fairly robust. The graphics and color displays seem to be on point. Since I'm a photographer, I did a little color calibration to be sure, but it didn't take much time or work to get things right. The response time for menu entries seems fairly snappy and the system seems easy to navigate. There are lots of port options for HDMI (2), Display Port, Mini Display Port, and one audio out if you don't want to use the built in speakers.I'm not much of a PC gamer, so I can't speak to that aspect, but overall, I'm happy with the purchases. For the money, it seems to be a really good quality monitor that offers good connectivity and great on-screen performance for the specs. Seems to be a good value overall.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on December 16, 2025

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I got the 4k model. I bought it used from Amazon for $240. It was like new with no issues. It came in a plain box.For business or programming applications the 4k monitor is the best. Don't get a curved screen. With 4k your screen can fit four 1080 p screens.Mine has the power & settings buttons on the lower front corner of the display instead of behind the display as pictured. I like it much better with the buttons on the front where it is easy to access. My model was exactly the same as the one pictured. So, I don't know why my buttons were on the front.The manual is useless. I had to figure out the settings buttons by experimenting.  It wasn't too difficult if you are technically inclined.I had a 2 yr old LG 32 in 4k monitor that fell over during the CA earthquake and broke the screen. The Viewsonic has a more stable base and I like the picture better than the LG.The LG had a thinner monitor screen than the Viewsonic, but it is not bulky. Unless you look at it from the side all the time you wouldn't notice it. They seemed to weigh about the same.I had a Viewsonic around 30 years ago and loved the screen quality back then. So, I bought one now and the quality is still great for business or photo editing applications. I probably wouldn't recommend it for gaming because there are faster monitors available at a much higher cost.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on May 12, 2025

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I have owned two of these, the 2K and the 4K, and I cannot believe they share the same model numbers. The 2K monitor is absolutely fantastic and I am still using it now after 5 years. Perfect regular use computer monitor.The 4K version is completely different, and I'm not sure why it shares the same model number. Other than the stand everything else is completely different. The picture is so dull, colors are absolutely horrendous and washed out. Also mine arrived with a vertical line on the screen, so the QC isn't up to par. I'm telling you the colors and picture was so bad, unlike anything I've ever seen before, I decided to take time out of my day to write about it. I wouldn't even buy it for $99. If you are looking for 4K, this is definitely not the one.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on April 30, 2025

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Don't let the negative reviews get in the way.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Display is sharp, bright, and color is perfect. This monitor is paired with a 2K display that is in portrait mode. Using Nvidia Desktop Manager or Fancy Zones as part of Windows Power toys I can split the the display into 4 - 1080p displays, smaller ones for email, etc... Or use the whole display for video and photo work. Some of the comments said the stand was not stable. I don't have that problem. The stand appears to be cast aluminum, very attractive. I put it together, and used loctite blue on the threads of the screws, and have had zero vibration issues. Very pleased with this display. Typically I prefer Benq or ViewSonic displays, and the price and quality is perfect for my professional use.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on August 24, 2023

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: 4 Inputs - HDMI x2, Display Port, Mini-Dispaly Port
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Updated: Lots to like about this monitor, however after only two days it has a flicker. See attached video.  Its most pronounced on the windows login splash screen. I don't know if its broken or its simply trying to self adjust and is in some weird loop, but either way its not working properly. Its not always as pronounced as that screen, but that screen has a lot of black on it. I have a GeForece GTX 1060 6GB video card, not top of the line, but no slouch either.Original Review:It has 4 inputs and that super amazingly awesome! I connect three different computers to it, so having at least 3 inputs is super important. 4 is way above average on monitors.  However the interface to switch inputs is via a crappy menu system and not a single button like others. This could drive you nuts. Also if an input is no longer there it will auto switch to something with an input. I cannot find any way around this in the menus. The information I was able to find before I purchase "implied" that it was a single button to switch inputs.  So that part sucks when switching between computers.The screen is okay. There isn't anything bad about it. I find flesh tones are too red saturated. I would not use this for Photo/Video Editing. This is not that monitor, don't even attempt it, you will be disappointed.On the other hand for the price point, web-surfing and office type work is great. Compared to my 2k (1920x1200) monitor this is quite the upgrade and you will love real 4k and all the space you have. I bought the 32" and not a 27" and I think that was a good move. On Windows 10 you can scale everything on the desktop so it's not super tiny small. I found 150% is my sweet spot.  32" gives you a bit more room to maximize the zoom vs amount of desktop space in use. I might have needed 175% on a 27" monitor to get things to look the same size. Even though the pixel count is the same you need to factor in the actual size of icons and whatnot. 32" for me gives me more space. Text from applications is crisp sharp, there are no pixels that I can easily see. Compared to my old 2k monitor this is amazing!This is not an IPS panel, but instead, its MVA technology. The screen is really large, which is awesome, but its so big in fact that the viewing angle becomes important. The left and right if I'm sitting center is no longer 100% perfect because of the viewing angle. Not outrageously bad, maybe 10% worse to the right or left of what you are working on. I suspect IPS is better, but I didn't read up on it so I don't know.Finally it has VESA mounting holes (100mm x 100mm) and I was able to mount it on my monitor arm. I added the spacers since it could bump into their bracket if used without the spacers. There were no specs on the screws (it would be nice to put a sticker or put it in the manual so you knew what max length was supposed to be).  I used M4x16's (x4 of them) (which is 16mm long) and that seemed to work just fine. That was through my VESA backing plate and spacers and it didn't seem to hit anything on the inside.  It would have been super nice if they included 4 screws.Other than that its a good price for a brand name monitor, but there are plenty of monitors in the price range. I'm happy I have it, but I probably should have splurged for a more expensive display. If you are doing Office work you will be very happy once you get the settings adjusted to your liking. The thing that held me back from other brands was the lack of a dedicated input select button, which in the end this one doesn't have.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: Viewsonic VX3276-4K-MHD (32 Zoll, 4K UHD)Viewsonic VX3276-4K-MHD (32 Zoll, 4K UHD)
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: Hab nach einem guten 4K Monitor für mein MacBook Pro (Mid 2014) gesucht und mit dem Viewsonic VX3276-4K-MHD (32 Zoll, 4K UHD) einen gefunden.+ Design / Material / Konstruktion:Auf jeden Fall einer der coolsten Displays, die ich bisher verwendet hab. Durch den schmalen Rand kommt die Größe richtig zur Geltung, Der Rahmen ist Oben und an den Seiten effektiv 9 mm dick. Durch den schwarzen Bildschirmrand und der silbernen Fassung optisch jedoch viel dünner. Eine kleine rechteckige LED rechts unten leuchtet beim Betrieb blau, im Standby orange. Den Standfuß hab ich ehrlich gesagt nie ausprobiert (hab den Bildschirm direkt an die Wand gehängt), sieht aber sehr hochwertig aus und liegt auch schwer in der Hand. Der Monitor ist an der dicksten Stelle etwa 4,5 cm breit, sodass er sehr nah an die Wand montiert werden kann. Die Kabelanschlüsse befinden sich auf der Unterseite und etwas vertieft, sodass sowohl von Vorne, als auch von der Seite nur die Kabel sichtbar sind, nicht deren Stecker. Außerdem ist in dieser Vertiefung genug Platz, um die Kabel zur gewünschten Stelle zu führen - sehr minimalistisch also, gefällt mir gut!+ Funktion:Das IPS Panel sieht super aus. Bin begeistert von den Farben und der Schärfe. Auch der matte Display ist genau so, wie ich ihn mir vorgestellt hab. Selbst bei schönem Wetter, wenn die Sonne voll ins Zimmer scheint, spiegelt nichts. Auch ist die Bildschirmhelligkeit in einer solchen Situation immernoch sehr gut. Der Monitor besitzt viele Einstellmöglichkeiten, die sich alle über die 6 Tasten auf der Rückseite bedienen lassen. Dadurch, dass man diese Tasten nicht sieht, sondern nur erfühlt, ist die Bedienung etwas umständlich, jedoch muss man dort im Normalfall selten was ändern. Ich hab einige Einstellungen und auch die Game-Modi ausprobiert, komme aber immer wieder auf die Standardeinstellung zurück, diese ist bereits wunderbar kalibriert!Wenn man nicht gerade das Ohr an den Monitor legt, ist er völlig lautlos. Selbst wenn der Computer mal nicht lüftet, ist das Gerät absolut geräuschlos, konnte kein Surren oder ähnliches feststellen. Die verbauten Boxen sind absoluter Schrott. Selbst Systemtöne werden mit einem leichten Rauschen ausgegeben, die Tonqualität von den Lautsprechern von Smartphone oder Laptop sind um Welten besser - aber ganz ehrlich, wen interessiert der Ton bei einem externen Monitor?Nach dem Einschalten erscheint kurz das Viewsonic-Logo in Farbe in der Mitte des Bildschirms, dann erst das übertragene Bild. Zum Hochfahren braucht der Monitor insgesamt nur 5 Sekunden.+ Zubehör / Anschlussmöglichkeiten:Beiliegend ist das Netzkabel und ein HDMI-Kabel. Das Netzteil ist im Monitor verbaut.Auch die VESA-Kmpatibilität ist sehr gut - die 4 Gewinde für die Schrauben (mit einem Abstand von 100 x 100 mm) liegen auf der hinteresten Ebene des Monitors, es müssen also keine Abstandhalter verwendet werden. Auf der Unterseite befinden sich neben dem Anschluss des Netzkabels links des weitern 2x HDMI Ports, 1x Mini-DisplayPort, 1x DisplayPort, 1x Audio Out rechts.Fazit: Top 4K-Monitor! Kaufen!So und jetzt zum Thema mit den 4K bei 60Hz an einem alten Mac:Um mit dem MacBook Pro (Mid 2014) einen 4K-Monitor bei 60Hz zu betreiben gibt es nur eine einzige Möglichkeit - über ein Mini-DisplayPort zu DisplayPort Kabel !!!!!!!!!! Diese Kabel gibt es von verschiedensten Herstellern in vielen unterschiedlichen Längen - ich persönlich verwende eines von iVANKY um 10 Euro.Auf den Bildern sind die beiden Grafikkarten des MacBooks Intel Iris Pro und NIVIDIA GeForce GT 750M zu sehen. Das Bild des Monitors läuft bei mir automatisch auf der NIVIDIA-Karte. Seit ich dieses Kabel verwende, gab es bei den 60Hz keinen einzigen Aussetzer mehr. Ein weiterer Vorteil beim Verwenden des Mini-DisplayPorts (bzw. Thunderbolt-Anschluss) ist, dass sich das MacBook die Größen und Positionen der geöffneten Programmfenster auf dem Monitor merkt, das klappt sonst nicht.Selbstverständlich ist es auch möglich, das Bild direkt über das HDMI-Kabel oder einen Thunderbolt auf HDMI Adapter zu übertragen, jedoch nur bei 30Hz. Ich würde absolut niemandem empfehlen, den Bildschirm bei nur 30Hz zu verwenden. Man kann vieles schön reden, aber das ist einfach nur unerträglich mit der Zeit. Auch wenn man den Monitor nicht fürs Gaming verwendet, sondern nur zum Arbeiten, ruckelt der Mauszeiger, das Scrollen von Websites ist anstrengend, Videos sehen furchtbar aus, alles wirkt verzögert - tut euch das nicht an und investiert die paar Euro für das richtige Kabel.

From the manufacturer
ProArt Display PA279CRV 
All the Essentials for Pros 
ProArt Display PA279CRV is a 27-inch 4K HDR monitor designed for professional video editors. This Calman Verified display boasts a wide color gamut with 99% DCI-P3 and 99% Adobe RGB coverage and is factory pre-calibrated to Delta E < 2 for exceptional color accuracy.

aplus content video
Filmmakers & Video Editors 
Ultrahigh resolution and wide colour gamut for 4K HDR video production. 
Designers & Photographers 
Truly precise colour reproduction to bring out the details in photographs or digital artwork. 
Previous page
Impeccable 4K HDR Imagery 
The 4K UHD (3840 x 2160) panel of PA279CRV delivers four times the pixel density and three times more onscreen space than similarly sized FHD displays. 
Enjoy True-to-Life Color 
PA279CRV goes beyond industry color standards, providing 99% DCI-P3, 99% Adobe RGB, and 100% sRGB coverage. In addition, 10-bit color depth enables more than 1.07 billion onscreen colors. 
Class-Leading Color Fidelity 
Each ProArt display is factory pre-calibrated using a new three-scale process for incredible color fidelity. 
True Color, Out of the Box 
Color professionals rely on their displays to ensure that their creations look exactly as intended. PA279CRV is Calman Verified & tested to ensure smoother gradation for color-accurate viewing. 
Next page
Previous page
The USB-C That Does it All 
The included USB-C port enables superfast data transfers, DisplayPort connectivity, and 96-watt power delivery to charge laptops and other devices―all via a single cable. 
Expansive Connectivity 
In addition to USB-C, ProArt display offers a myriad of connectivity options including HDMI, DisplayPort (with daisy-chain support), USB Type-A, and additional USB-C downstream port. 
Connect to Your Devices Easily 
A built-in USB 3.2 hub at the bottom of PA279CRV includes one USB Type-A port and USB-C, allowing you to easily connect a variety of devices and peripherals, as well as charge compatible devices. 
Ergonomic Stand 
Each ProArt display features an ergonomic stand with tilt, swivel, pivot, and height adjustments for comfortable viewing.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Great quality photography editing monitor that requires troubleshooting out of the box.Simply put, it is a wonderful high quality screen but the default settings need to be changed to make it useable.  The picture quality is great and needs no changes, but the power settings make it “not wake up” and have trouble connecting to your computer.Here’s what worked for me:Set Power Saving to Normal.Disable anything like eco mode, deep sleep or auto standby.Turn off auto detection (this means you have to manually select the input if you switch between connection ports)I only recommend this product if you are willing to tinker with the settings.  That being said, now that it actually connects, I love it.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Defective from time of sale, and ASUS customer service dodging warranty repair/replacement
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This item was defective from the get-go. The USB-C that's meant to charge my laptop while also delivering visual to the display never worked consistently. Within a few months it went from failing periodically to failing consistently. I would have to wiggle the cable until it was just so to get a connection, and then heaven forbid I accidentally nudge my laptop or need to reposition the display, as it would mean starting the whole process over. Now, it never detects the laptop without all of this nonsense (and the ports are all on the back, making it that much harder). Tested it this morning, and it turns out it's not just the USB-C port: it's -all- of the ports. So there's no way to make it work reliably - and at this point, pretty much at all. It supposedly came with a warranty. Asus said over the phone they would ship me a replacement if I would authorize a hold for $100 to be refunded when they received my defective unit shipped back to them. But then they sent me a text message saying they had "forgotten" to collect my email over the phone to begin the paperwork. Once I supplied it, they sent over an invoice for $472.97: more than the original cost of the display. When I told them the hold was supposed to have been $100 according to the original representative, they denied it. Also, different representatives would respond to the case without any explanation for the handoff and without replying to previous emails--defeating threading in what felt like a very intentional effort to make the conversation hard enough to track and manage that I would give up or forget the facts. I thought I had done my research when I made this purchase: others seemed very happy with the display. I had not, however, researched their customer service or more specifically, their warranty service. Apparently they are notorious for this sort of thing. Others have reported that when they have requested a warranty repair, ASUS has responded with charges near the cost of their device for issues they didn't have originally or request service for.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on June 4, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Glorious, glorious beams of light directly into my eyes
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: TLDR: fantastic. Color accurate, flickerless, and beautifully smooth. The stand it comes with is premium as well.I work in graphics and presentations for business. It’s important we have color-accurate monitors to prevent things we think are navy from printing out purple and whatnot. This works beautifully.It is plug-and-play essentially. The directions are simple (although these dudes are heavy and awkward to hold if you’re a smaller person, so be ready for that) and it goes up pretty simply.I did have issues with getting it to connect but those were issues with the LAPTOP and not the MONITOR. *THE MONITOR WORKED GREAT* my laptop sucked.Once plugged in properly, you can use the handy dandy buttons on the bottom right to navigate to the correct input channel and boom. The blinding image quality of a thousand suns beaming directly into your retinas. Beautiful. (You can adjust the brightness in the monitor settings using the buttons in the bottom right if you want to keep your retinas.)The size is nothing to sneeze at either. Look, I like having multiple screens, but I basically just use this one now (my laptop screen serves to keep outlook open and basically nothing else).I need these dudes to put one of their screens on a Wacom… my pen display tablet looks so Blegh in comparison.I did purchase a monitor arm with the intent of putting this on there. The display mounted to that effortlessly. I hated the monitor arm. It was so bulky and awkward and weird. Put this thing back on the stand it came with and I loved it so much better. It rotates, tilts, moves up and down and whatnot easily but sticks exactly where you put it when you leave it. There’s also a good little spot for running all your cords through to manage them so you have less electrical spaghetti on your plate.10/10 no notes, standing ovation

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Tiny Budget PCs are great again!Tiny Budget PCs are great again!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: At first I was skeptical.  I've had low-budget hardware before and had always found the experience inadequate.  But I've been nothing but impressed with this cute, tiny little box and would highly recommend it to anyone looking for a budget-friendly general-purpose computer.  It's no good for 'modern' gaming (which if that's what you're looking for, you wouldn't be looking at these kinds of computers anyway), but for everything else typically done at home it's perfectly fine.Boot time:  So fast my monitor actually takes longer to turn on than it takes for the computer to be ready to log in.Gaming performance:  About what I expected.  Console-grade Unreal Engine titles from as far back as 2015 generally run unacceptably badly, requiring reduction to minimum detail levels at low resolution to reach even a minimum standard of playable.  But as a *kids* gaming device?  Sure.  Minecraft requires a bit of tweaking to get it to run well ('Fancy' graphics, reduce resolution to 900p, 3x3 textures and 8 chunk render/simulate distance) but it is workable and looks fine.  Even the most demanding Roblox experiences are reasonably playable at medium detail levels (automatic is fine).  Mobile-class games like various Tower Defense games, including ones with low-detail 3D graphics, run perfectly well.  Load times are really quick except in Minecraft.Web browsing:  Everything is fast and responsive enough that your internet connection is likely to be the sole frustrating thing about it (oh and btw the WiFi chip/antenna is of pretty decent quality so it's your ISP that will be the pain, not the box itself).  Even the text editors with built-in grammar checking will be 100% responsive -- a surprise given that this was a significant pain point in the last low-budget computer I got (I had to disable grammar checking in order to keep it responsive on previous devices -- but not on this one).  Endless scrolling and loading of images on social media are as fast as your internet connection will allow, which for me meant scrolling Facebook literally as fast as my mouse wheel could go and not experiencing any noticeable hitches.(Note:  I have a Pi Hole on my network that eats up ads, and ads are always a pain point in internet loading).For good measure I loaded up YouTube videos in 4 different windows and forced them to 1080p/60 quality mode.  All four windows were rendering the video at full resolution and full frame rate with no visible hitching.  Stream decoding is fast enough for any kind of video streaming a reasonable person would be doing.I only did a cursory check of Office productivity capability.  For this I found some decently large documents and loaded them with LibreOffice.  I didn't notice any hitching as I scrolled through the documents, edited them and even tossed in some typical use-case spreadsheet calculations.  While I can't say if it'll be ideal for, say, an accountant or author or artist who will want to use absurdly large sheets with complex calculations or thousand-page drafts with dozens of revisions that the document tracks, or massive Photoshop jobs, I *can* say that if your use case is such that you're even considering a low-end PC, this one will suit your needs well enough.Color me impressed.  10 years ago I bought a 'mid-range' CPU that all by itself cost more than this box, not counting everything else I had to buy for the PC that CPU went into.  This box, for less than the price of that CPU, substantially outperforms it, and does so while being dead silent and consuming no more power than an LED lightbulb.  I'm sold.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Massive performance in a tiny, quiet package!!Massive performance in a tiny, quiet package!!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I am incredibly impressed with the sheer multitasking power packed into this compact chassis. The AMD Ryzen V2748 processor is a total workhorse, featuring 8 cores and 16 threads that handle heavy workloads, massive Excel spreadsheets, and 4K video streaming simultaneously without any stuttering. Unlike many other mini PCs that struggle with heat, the thermal management here is top-notch; even under a heavy load, the fan remains a low, unobtrusive hum, and the unit stays remarkably cool to the touch. It comes pre-installed with a clean version of Windows 11 Pro and the 16GB of DDR4 RAM provides a very snappy user experience right out of the box, making it a perfect primary desktop replacement for anyone looking to reclaim their desk space.The connectivity and upgrade potential are where this machine truly shines as a long-term investment. Having the ability to run a triple 4K monitor setup via the HDMI, DisplayPort, and full-featured Type-C ports is a game changer for productivity and creative work. I also appreciate that the internal layout is accessible, allowing for future RAM upgrades up to 64GB or swapping in a larger SSD if the 512GB NVMe drive eventually fills up. The build quality feels premium with a sleek, textured finish that doesn’t attract fingerprints, and the inclusion of a VESA mount allowed me to hide the entire PC behind my monitor for a completely wire-free look. For the price point, the performance-to-value ratio is simply unbeatable for a home office or a high-end media center.Edit- After some tinkering, I came to the conclusion that the stock Sata SSD is too slow. I added an 500GB NVME for extra storage. This definitely helped the write speeds.  I also ditched the Realtek RTL8852BE wifi card, and replaced it with an Intel Ax210. My wifi speeds DOUBLED, I went from 231mbps to 461mbps. My Bluetooth went from 5.3 to 5.4, a nice bonus. I added another 16gb of DDR4, to 32GB total. This is now a proper speed demon, capable of heavy multitasking. Don't get me wrong It was pretty good out of the box, BUT NOW IT'S GREAT!!!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: A great tiny PC to gift to the technologically resistant elderly relative in your life
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: My grandma hates computers. She has refused to buy a computer newer than 3 years out of date and always picks the absolute lowest tier of big name PC makers. It will work great at first. It doesn't take long until I then get to play tech support as it quickly becomes slower and slower until it finally makes it to the big scrap heap in the sky. Yes, I'm the family computer geek.This most recent time... well, she needed a new computer but wasn't going to buy a new computer until the one that I lent her died. It started begging for the sweet, sweet release of a big blue screen right around the time that she decided to move 5 states away to be closer to her son (my uncle) and her great-grandkids (his grandkids). I decided that it was time to just get her one (and get her a GOOD one) instead of letting her drag a 10 year old, dying brick of a computer 1000 miles away. Plus, that was my 10 year old, dying brick of a computer, thank you very much. I had plans for it before I lent it to her and buying this was cheaper than buying new parts for my project. Seriously, this little PC is CHEAP in the best way possible. It's very solid, has an amazingly small form factor that impresses everyone who sees it, and this little thing RIPS. It's fast. It's not top tier parts but it's far from bargain bin either. It's light-years beyond anything that she's used before.She doesn't need it for much. She just needs to check her email about once a month, search for a nearby business or address, and maybe order gifts for her great-grandkids every so often. (Honestly, this PC is more powerful than what she needs but the one thing that she hates more than computers is cell phones.) She's 87, does not understand computers, and does not WANT to understand computers. She actually likes this little PC. She has an old 22" Dell monitor that she loves and refuses to get rid of. How old is it? 1 VGA port only, no HDMI, much less Display Port. One of the big selling factors for choosing this as her gift was the VGA. I paired it with a tiny VGA cable, got a little VESA mount/adapter for the monitor, and let her have her pick of my old keyboards and mice. She's now got a tiny little PC attached to her tiny monitor that stays out of her way but is there when she reluctantly has to use it. It's got my anti-virus on there under a "parental control" account so that even from opposite sides of the Gulf of Mexico, I can serve as tech support lol.If you've got an aging family member who hates PCs but needs one, I recommend this whole heartedly. I also think that it could make a great home theater PC, a kid's first school work PC, a smart home hub, a travel PC that can plug into hotel TVs, a garage workshop PC/projector/TV and so much more. Once I finish with my current projects, I'll absolutely be buying at least two more of these for other projects.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on November 25, 2023

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Buyer Beware – BIOS Failure After Only 90 Days
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I would strongly caution anyone considering purchasing these PCs.This is now the second computer we have purchased that has experienced a BIOS error and will no longer boot up. Unfortunately, the problem occurred outside of the manufacturer's extremely limited 30-day return/replacement window.A computer should reasonably be expected to last far longer than 90 days. Having two separate computers experience BIOS-related failures is extremely concerning and makes me question the reliability and quality of these PCs.Once you are outside the 30-day replacement window, you are left dealing with a computer that will not even boot, despite being only a few months old.Based on our experience, I would not recommend purchasing these PCs. There simply does not appear to be enough assurance that the BIOS and system will continue functioning properly beyond the short return period. Buyers should be aware of this risk before spending their money.

breadCrumbs: Electronics > Computers & Accessories > Monitors
description: Bring your gaming to the next level with the Samsung 32 Inch UJ59 UHD 4K Gaming Monitor (LU32J590UQNXZA) that offers breathtaking picture quality like you’ve never seen before, greatly enhancing PC viewing, gaming and more. Thanks to over 8 million pixels that support a rainbow of colors (over one billion shades!), this 32-inch UHD computer monitor gives you widescreen 4K gaming that makes this PC monitor more of a gaming TV. Samsung’s 32-inch computer monitor offers immense power, letting you connect not one but two devices to your 4K monitor while maintaining the optimal quality in each, thanks to two HDMI 2.0 inputs. Watch your favorite shows, sports and more while not missing out on a second of your gaming thanks to split screen function like Picture-by-Picture viewing. You can resize the second source up to 25% of the screen and position it wherever you like. True gamers will love great features of Samsung’s 4K monitor like Game Mode, which optimizes your monitor to offer you the edge you need during competitive gameplay. Game Mode boosts contrast, letting you see details in dark areas like you never have before. Spot your enemies faster and win the match, thanks to Samsung’s 32-inch 4K UHD monitor.
features: WIDESCREEN UHD: With 4x the pixels of Full HD, get more screen space (vs 16:9 screen) and UHD images; View documents & webpages w/ less scrolling, work more comfortably w/ multiple windows & toolbars, and enjoy photos, videos & games in stunning 4K

A BILLION COLOR SHADES: Supporting a billion shades of color, the UJ59 delivers incredibly vivid and realistic images; Its color accuracy means colors appear true to life, making the UJ59 ideal for photo, video and graphics applications
SEAMLESS UPSCALING: Samsung’s UHD upscaling technology includes signal analysis and detail enhancement that seamlessly upconverts SD, HD and Full HD content to near UHD-level picture quality

WIDESCREEN 4K GAMING: With 8.3 million pixels supporting a wide range of colors and resolving every image with astonishing clarity, UHD gives you a wider view for a truly thrilling and immersive gaming experience

SMOOTHER GAMEPLAY: AMD FreeSync synchronizes the refresh rate of your graphics card & monitor to reduce image tear & stutter; Low Input Lag Mode minimizes the delay between mouse, keyboard or joystick input and onscreen response for smooth gaming

GAME MODE: Game Mode instantly optimizes screen contrast to give you a competitive edge during gameplay; By selectively boosting contrast in scenes, Game Mode reveals more detail in dark areas to let you spot your enemies faster

POWERFUL MULTITASKING: Picture-by-Picture (PBP) lets you connect to 2 devices to the monitor and maintain their original quality; With Picture-in-Picture (PIP) you can resize the second source to up to 25% of the screen and position it anywhere

SLIM BEZELS: Framed by slim screen bezels and finished in stylish matte black, the UJ59 sits elegantly on virtually any desktop; And its Y-shaped stand provides a firm footing and a refined metallic touch

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great for office work, etc. I would not say a great gaming monitor
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I don't play too many games on the PC this is on. But it's not the fastest refresh, so I probably would not buy one for that.That being said, I'm not putting this down at all! It's an awesome monitor. I HAD a great gaming monitor with a curved screen this replaced. I don't need 240 Hz refresh rate or whatever. I play drums, and this is the monitor I use to play along to sheet music on the screen mostly. But my eyes weren't what they were. I run it at half the resolution it is capable of, because I want everything LARGE. I need to see the music notes clearly. I also need nice big clear text. The visual difference when I got this monitor after using the last one for 2+ years for this, was astonishing. Everything was clearer and sharper. Text is crisp. Video play back is awesome. This isn't the best of the best in monitors, but in this price range, this size, well I'm glad I picked this one. Sturdy as hell. You can see and feel the build quality. Colors are vibrant but not (to me) inaccurate. And I'm sure it works great for gaming! But not what I would pick for gaming, as I would want a faster screen refresh rate. productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought this to replace my current 32" Samsung monitor with a UHD monitor.  The first problem occurred after swapping out the monitors using my existing DisplayPort cable.  The computer wouldn't boot.  It beeped 5 times which is its way of saying "I don't have a graphics card".  The monitor had actually managed to hang the Nvidia card.  I switched over to the included HDMI cable and after leaving the computer unplugged for a while it booted.  I streamed some HD content and the first thing I noted was noise in my speakers that wasn't there before the swap.  Digital noise was somehow making it through my USB DAC and into my reference monitor speakers.  Then the flickering started - not the whole screen, just a part of it.  Not really flickering, there was a large geometric pattern appearing that caused the underlying colors to wash out.  Then it started randomly going into power save mode (or just turning off) for intervals from a few seconds to a few minutes, and this was while it was playing streaming video.  The audio continued so the computer was still running, I guess the monitor had just decided to take a break.  I put the old monitor back in place on DisplayPort and the noise is gone and so is the blanking.  Back into its box and back to Amazon this hot mess goes.  EDIT:  As I was repacking it for return, I realized that there was no protective film anywhere on the monitor.  Also after writing this review, I checked the manual and the monitor had arrived with the OSD in lock mode and I was unable to get it out of that mode.  Add to that the extra layer of tape on the box and I begin to wonder if what I got was a "refurbishment" of someone else's problem.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on October 31, 2022

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Stunning visuals, versatile connectivity options, and eye-friendly features.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The SAMSUNG UJ59 Series 32-Inch 4K UHD Computer Monitor is a visually stunning and feature-packed monitor that elevates your viewing experience. With its impressive 4K UHD resolution, versatile connectivity options, and eye-friendly features, this monitor is designed to meet the demands of both work and entertainment.The standout feature of this monitor is its breathtaking 4K UHD resolution. With a resolution of 3840x2160 pixels, it delivers crystal-clear images and vibrant colors, providing exceptional detail and clarity. Whether you're working on graphic design projects, editing photos and videos, or simply enjoying movies and games, the UHD resolution enhances every visual element on the screen.Connectivity is never an issue with this monitor. It features both HDMI and DisplayPort inputs, allowing you to connect a variety of devices, including laptops, desktops, gaming consoles, and more. The multiple inputs enable seamless multitasking and make it easy to switch between different devices without the hassle of constantly reconnecting cables.The eye-saving features of this monitor are highly appreciated. The Eye Saver Mode reduces blue light emissions, which can cause eye strain and fatigue during extended periods of use. This mode helps to minimize eye discomfort, allowing you to work or enjoy content for longer periods with less eye strain. Additionally, the Flicker-Free technology ensures a smooth and flicker-free viewing experience, further reducing eye fatigue.For gamers, the inclusion of FreeSync technology is a game-changer. FreeSync synchronizes the monitor's refresh rate with the frame rate of your compatible AMD graphics card, eliminating screen tearing and stuttering. This results in smoother gameplay and an enhanced gaming experience overall. Whether you're playing fast-paced action games or immersing yourself in detailed RPGs, the UJ59 monitor delivers responsive and fluid visuals.The 32-inch screen size is ideal for productivity and entertainment. It offers ample screen real estate, allowing you to multitask efficiently and comfortably. Whether you're working with multiple windows or enjoying immersive multimedia content, the large display provides an immersive and engaging viewing experience.In terms of design, the UJ59 monitor boasts a sleek and modern appearance. The slim bezels and clean lines give it a sophisticated and professional look, making it a stylish addition to any workspace or gaming setup.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on July 10, 2023

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Wished I would have liked this much more than I do
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought this to be a decent monitor to use at home for working from home as well as for surfing.  I love Samsung and wanted a 4k monitor.  I read endless reviews and specs on this and all the other monitors in the same price range and specs.  I loved the color capabilities and the price point was where I wanted to be.This rated the best and I felt it would be amazing.  Unfortunately I can't say I am very impressed with it overall.  Other reviewers seem to love it though.  First I wanted something that I could use at 4k as a multi-monitor display.  This does have great colors and can do 4k.  The inputs are finicky as stated in other reviews.  Only one input is capable of doing 4k at the highest refresh rate.  The multifunction power button is disappointing at best.  It serves as the power button and will let you flip between monitor modes and inputs.  It seems to work only most of the time.  Sometimes when you try to use the button it does nothing.  The lack of options with the stand is also disappointing.  It's lackluster and is fixed.  I have loved Samsung products and have several TVs and they do not disappoint.  This display did though for the price.  The colors are amazing though for certain.  Sometimes it gets caught in a loop of trying to go to sleep and flipping between inputs and flashes when my laptop goes to sleep and it's annoying. productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Fantastic sale price, gorgeous picture quality, a snap to assemble
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: My previous monitor died suddenly, and I happened to need a replacement as October Prime Days was starting. I found this monitor, a 4K upgrade, for an excellent price. My Asurion protection plan paid for it, basically.It shipped quickly. When I got it, I was afraid that it was a return, not a totally new monitor. The box had been opened, the accessories were not well repacked, and there was no warranty card. I decided to set it up anyway rather than insist on a replacement.Assembly was a snap, and the mount can be removed easily if needed. There were USB-C and HDMI cables included; I use Display Port instead, but I had a cable already. It was truly plug-and-play: switched it on, my laptop recognized it instantly. The monitor was already set up for great color, brightness, and contrast. I had to dink around with resolution, text size, and icon size to get the finder set to the appearances I'm used to, but that's expected going from a 2K to a 4K monitor.If I have any complaint, it's that the menu buttons don't function as I expected and the explanations are not detailed. I got used to them.No bad pixels or damage. Gorgeous picture quality. Terrible sounding speakers, but I have some Basics small speakers on order. Simple assembly. Already well-calibrated. I'm very happy with this monitor, and when I'm able to get it registered under warranty I'll be totally happy. I would gladly buy this again.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on October 13, 2024

This single cable effortlessly handles display, data transfer, and even powers my MacBook and other Mac computers, drastically reducing cable clutter and simplifying my workspace. The convenience and efficiency this offers cannot be overstated.Adding to its appeal, the included default Mac computer color calibration is a thoughtful touch that saves time and ensures optimal performance right out of the box. It’s clear this monitor was designed with professionals and discerning users in mind, offering a premium experience without the need for additional tweaking.In a market flooded with options, this monitor stands out as a clear winner. It's an investment in unparalleled visual quality, effortless connectivity, and a truly satisfying user experience. Highly recommended for anyone seeking the pinnacle of display technology.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Purchased for portrait mode as a second monitor.  Sharp image quality and brightness.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I usually don’t buy cheap computer components, but when I saw this monitor on sale I decided to give it a try.  This thing sits in portrait mode next to my 32” Alienware gaming monitor.  Except for some glow of black images the INNOCN’s color and sharpness compares well with the far more expensive OLED Alienware plus the brightness exceeds the OLED so much so that I turned it down.  It’s great to view web pages while playing a game, whether I’m looking up info, on discord, watching the stock market, or all of the above.  Reading the news in portrait is especially cool because it's like looking at a full page news paper.  The monitor will rotate left or right so that you can easily hide the cables behind another monitor.  It comes with a HDMI cable, but no DP; however for my purposes the HDMI provides plenty of band width.  I suppose the speakers maybe better than nothing, but not good.  Get a good speaker system, it will last forever, or some headphones.  I think this would be good for a single monitor budget system, but as a second monitor it’s great.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on August 1, 2024

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Purchased this monitor for my daughter's freshman year of college in the dorm.  Ordered it early so I could test it.  The idea was that I could plug a fire stick into the HDMI so she could watch TV or she could plug her laptop into the USB-C to use as a second monitor.  Assembled it at home and tested it, and by switching between inputs, I could switched between laptop and firestick.  The screen itself was very nice looking.On moving day, I reassembled the set-up at her location.  Low and behold, the HDMI post stopped responding.  No matter what I plugged in there (the external display of laptop or the firestick) I got no input signal.But since the USB-C post still worked, I decided I'd troubleshoot next time I visited her at school.Today, she says the monitor will not wake up with the laptop either.  It still powers (charges) the laptop, but no signal.The is monitor is a lot more trouble than it's worth.  I must have owned 10 monitors in my lifetime (including a couple of docking station monitors), and never had these kinds of issues.  I would recommend passing on this monitor.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on September 3, 2024

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I was using a 27" iMac with a 5k screen. Thinking that moving to a 4k screen would be a big step down, I ordered the Asus 5k screen for $800. Did not like it at all. Weird green ghosting when scrolling text. Very dark. So I sent that back to Amazon and got this screen (my wife has had one for years). It cost about 1/3 as much, and for my money, is perfect. It charges my laptop, provides crisp text, great colors. It's a little slow to wake up, but I can wait a few seconds in the morning. I'm not editing videos or photos, so I can't comment on the color calibration, but everything looks good to me. For a reliable, sharp, reasonably priced monitor, this seems a great choice.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Way faster than specs would tell you. Windows 11 upgradable. GREAT little PC!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I got this new a couple of years ago, to replace a terribly old Mac that couldn't keep up anymore. I've been astonished at how fast this little PC has been. The specs don't really tell you the whole story. The folks at HP managed to optimize this machine so that it's just blazing fast compared to other computers I've had that were closer to top of the line in their day. It may not hold up well for instensive things like video procesing or bulk graphic editing in Illustrator, but for the vast majority of productivity type tasks, this tiny PC is perfect. You'd never know you're on a mini PC except the fact that it's stone cold quiet and doesn't have great HD space (just get a 500GB flash drive, they're cheap). With 7 USB ports and a 2 DisplayPorts, even the lack of HDMI isn't a very big deal. Thunderbolt would be nice but there are workarounds.  I've got this thing hooked into a 43 inch 4K monitor and everything looks beautiful. Mouse is a bit slower on the big screen, but that's it.Upgrading to Win 11 was as easy as upgrading the TPM to 2.0 w/ HPs official tool, and using MSFT's registry override published on their site with instructions how to install Windows 11 on machines deemed incapable (Windows will tell you the CPU on this machine isn't up to par, but that's ridiculous). Then during the ISO ugprade you need to selected advanced and turn automatic updates during installation OFF or the install will cut out. Also, all the warnings about how if you upgrade on a machine deemed incapable will make you ineligible for future Windows updates are totally bogus - updates work fine. Windows 11 is way better than 10, especially for multiple monitors. I ran the Performance Monitor app in Windows 11, and not only did this machine pass with flying colors, it scored an 8.7 in the CPU area - where 5 is a passing score. So not only can the CPU handle Windows 11, it handles it a lot better than plenty of the machines deemed capable of Win 11.Buying one of these for $110 refurbished for office, home, or school is a no brainer.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: So I picked up one of these to use as a Raspberry Pi alternative for some small IoT services around the house. I had a NVMe SSD in another system I should be able to drop into this and boot, which mostly seemed to work, but I was having some strange issues that took a while to figure out.So, out of the box, I went ahead and opened it up and unplugged the SSD included. I don't need Windows for my needs and would rather not have it numerated in Linux or anything, so I just unplugged it. I plugged my prepped NVMe in and it all seemed fine.Booted into the BIOS, went thru resetting some things, and upon save & resetting the BIOS... it wouldn't boot. I kept getting "RESET SYSTEM" messages and it just kept rebooting. I couldn't get it back into the BIOS either.At first I figured I did something wrong in the BIOS and tried to reset the CMOS, but that didn't really do much either. I was able to get into the BIOS once, didn't change anything, and it immediately started back into a RESET SYSTEM loop.I took it apart completely and noticed the Wifi antenna were seemingly damaged. It looks like there are a couple of places where the antenna has been stripped on purpose, exposing the inner metal shielding to the bare metal of the chassis. I didn't think it was likely causing a short but I did see some others reporting such a problem. I'm not using the wireless so I went ahead and removed it. Problem persisted.After a bit more troubleshooting I figured out if I plugged a second keyboard in and spammed F12 on both I was able to get into the BIOS, and from there I set the boot delay timer to 5 seconds... and it boots into Linux very consistently now.I say all this to hopefully help anyone else that picks up one of these for homelab type things: Ensure the boot delay timer is set, because it seems like the HP BIOS can't kick over to GRUB otherwise. Super weird, but hey, it ends up working fine.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Update 3-1-23: Another computer just died. Hard drive failed. Avoid purchasing from this seller because he NEVER responds and sells junk.  Again, Amazon won’t do anything about. Now I have two computers on my desk.I purchased 4 of these computers for our office. One of them did not work upon arriving. I immediately had amazon replace it. Out of the four, one has stopped working (only used 5 months). It keeps rebooting, asking for drivers to be reinstalled because they have "failed." My IT people told me they could not do much and to request a replacement since refurbished computers come with a one-year warranty.I am giving this a 2-star review simply because I contacted the seller last week and I still have not heard back (1-star for the inconvenience, 1-star for not hearing back, 1-star for causing me the extra expense of being down a computer). I will update the star rating once I hear back from the seller. I am hoping for their customer service to be great.UPDATE 1-17-23 I still have not heard back from the seller. The second computer (2/4) has stopped working. It was not even been a year since I purchased all four. The hard drive fell out of the blue. It was working find the day before yesterday.UPDATE 2-22-23 Amazon had informed me about a week ago they could not do anything for me and that I needed to contact HP customer service for support and replacement. When I called HP they stated my WARRANTY HAD EXPIRED BACK IN MAY 2019. Their 1 year warranty is not valid. I would avoid purchasing from this seller as he's never responded to my messages.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I spent the last few work years developing automation using raspberry pi, so it made sense to have it as my daily drive and desktop. Now retired, I wanted to see how the rest of the Linux world was doing. I looked through my motley collection of old computers and decided I needed something more modern, nothing crazy, I'm not a gamer or video producer. I just needed a commodity desktop. On that front, not much has changed for years. I looked at what I could get new locally or online and wasn't impressed. But I did see huge numbers of these on sale at attractive prices. Off lease doesn't scare me I have the tools and knowledge to build PCs if needed. So, I found what seemed the best deal, Amazon renewed so I could send it back if hopeless. For $100, these old business models are pretty much on par with the new budget models I was looking at.So, what did I get? Slightly more than I ordered, this one had a 1tB ssd and it does have WIFI and Bluetooth internal. The ssd had been running for 5 years and was down to 9% life according to Crystal Diskinfo. But, it had Windows 10 Pro on it and works fine. The external antennas were missing but both WIFI and Bluetooth work OK. I didn't really have to do anything. But I added a nvme M2 ssd and put LinuxMint on it. I left the Windows on the original drive and if it fails eventually, no big deal, I don't use it anyways. But, it's a great deal for what I needed and more than fast enough as a Linux desktop. I am pleased, and as someone who has been in the game since before PCs, that's saying a  lot. I would recommend if for someone who just needs an average desktop.

I also liked the pop-out USB-A and USB-C ports below the monitor, which I used for Keyboard/Mouse dongle and headphone dongle. productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Serious USB-C/dock failures and extremely frustrating Dell support
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought the Dell S2725QC mainly because of its USB-C/docking functionality: one cable for video, charging, and peripherals. Unfortunately, that core feature stopped working reliably after only a few months.I tried the obvious troubleshooting steps: different USB-C cables, confirming the correct USB-C input, power cycling the monitor, and using HDMI as a workaround. HDMI works, but it does not solve the problem, because the USB-C/dock function is one of the main reasons this model is attractive.The support experience has also been very disappointing. I contacted Dell under case 227018992 and was told that, because the product was bought abroad, I needed to transfer/register the warranty in Brazil. I followed the instructions, but the transfer was denied because the “previous owner” information did not match Dell’s internal records — information a retail customer has no way to know. I then contacted Dell again with the Service Tag, purchase context, denied transfer request ID, and problem details, but received no useful follow-up for several days.Instead of a clear warranty path for a relatively new product with a serious defect, I was sent into a maze of emails, webpages, unclear responsibilities, and dead ends. I contacted the channels I was directed to, but still ended up with a faulty monitor and no practical resolution.I cannot recommend this monitor, especially for anyone buying it because of the USB-C/docking feature or expecting straightforward international warranty support from Dell. After this experience, I am very unlikely to buy another Dell product.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Comparing this to the Apple Studio Display isn't fair (it's 5x as much money), but I'm going to do it anyway because I bought this to see if it can replace a Studio Display. The resolution and Mac compatibility of the Dell monitor are quite good, they get close-ish to the Studio Display, but where the Dell really falls short is in color. The color on the Studio Display is way better, shockingly better, but how much money is that worth to you? If you don't have a Studio Display, this Dell is a perfectly fine monitor.  For 1/5 the money, the Dell is a good deal, and works great as a monitor for a Mac.The build quality on the Dell is okay. It's a standard plastic monitor. The ports are nice, the Mac Thunderbolt port works fine when connected to the USB-C port. If you turn on "HDR" in your Mac's settings (which is odd because I don't think this monitor does HDR) you can control the monitor's brightness from your Mac, which is cool. This Dell is highly adjustable in terms of height, rotation, angle, all that stuff. You might need to break out a level to properly level this monitor, I fiddled around with leveling it a bit and never seemed to get it quite right. Obviously the build quality doesn't even remotely compare to the Studio Display, but you knew that already.Compared to other monitors (aside from the Studio Display), this is a good monitor, especially for the money. It's better than any of the Viewsonic monitors that I have, and it's way better than a 4K LG monitor that I have. The image quality looks pretty good right out of the box with no setup. 120hz works fine. You can set it to variable refresh rate on a Mac which is nice. It just works and looks good for the price. I would recommend this over other monitors at this price.If you're reading this far, I want to get back to color. The color on this monitor is just okay, but if you care about color, you need to go with a more expensive monitor. It looks fine if you're just a casual user, but you should not be using this monitor for anything where accurate color is required (eg: serious photo or video editing or art). It looks fine for watching videos or looking at photographs, but when you compare it against something like the Studio Display, it's not even in the same ballpark. If you're a casual user, you're not going to notice, but if you care about color, get something more expensive. Going back and forth between this and the Studio Display makes the color on this Dell look really bad in comparison, but you're talking about a $1600 monitor vs a $300 monitor.Also, 120hz is anything special. I know you might think "the base Studio Display doesn't do 120hz," but trust me when I say that unless you're a gamer, you're not going to notice or care 99% of the time. I've owned a number of 120hz displays, often side by side with 60hz displays, and the 120hz is not noticeable or important most of the time. You'll forget that it's even there. Color and resolution are always just as impressive as the moment you first saw them, but refresh rate is not. So don't make a big deal out of the 120hz, because you get used to it real fast, and it stops being impressive after a very short time.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: The Monitor That Earns Its Real Estate on My Left!The Monitor That Earns Its Real Estate on My Left!
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: Let me be clear: I didn’t need a third monitor. I needed a third monitor that could rotate into portrait without making me feel like I was looking at a grocery receipt stapled to a wall. This is that monitor. And regardless of orientation, the display is bright, even, and does not disappoint.The Setup:Look-left slot. Portrait mode for SQL result sets, log tails, and ABAP stack traces that scroll like the Dead Sea Scrolls. Flip it landscape when I’m doing side-by-side field mapping or need to stare at a 200-column staging table and question my career choices.The Random Bits:The integrated speakers exist. They are monitor speakers. Manage your expectations accordingly. I use them for Teams calls when my headset is charging and the experience is “functional in a conference room with no dignity” which is exactly what Teams calls are anyway.Ash White color is clean and doesn’t look like a hospital equipment clearance sale, which some white monitors absolutely do.The integrated sound is solid, much better than the crappy average of most panels, but you aren’t buying this monitor for the sound. Check out my EDIFIER MR5 review for the desk cans I bought to pair with my Data Ninja battlestation.What May Annoy You (but it’s ok..):OSD navigation is four physical buttons on the back-right-bottom edge. Even more annoying on a third monitor, but you will (hopefully) not have to reach for it often.Dell has been doing this since we told them it was a bad idea, and yeah, they still do it. I do get it, I mean who doesn’t love a sexy thin and buttery smooth bottom…bezel. We all love those. 🫣Bottom LineI’m a data engineer. My left monitor is a working tool, not décor, but the wife likes it, and it breaks from the plethora of tech black-attack. I’m happy with the panel, and after 90 days of 70 hour weeks of solid service, I am glad I pulled the trigger on this premium-adjacent purchase.

With dual HDMI outputs, you can connect two 4K@60Hz displays simultaneously, enabling efficient multitasking for work and entertainment.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: A desktop space-saver that completely exceeds performance expectations.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: My first impression upon receiving it was how compact it is; mounting it directly behind the monitor instantly decluttered my entire desk. Despite its small size, the performance is impressive—it handles large Excel spreadsheets, dozens of open web pages, and even occasional short video editing in Photoshop with perfect smoothness and absolutely no lag. productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Powerful, great value, but not a gaming machine!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This is my 2nd BMAX mini-PC purchase after 5 years, and I am absolutely a fan of mini-PCs in general.  BMAX stands out from the rest of the mini-PC offerings in that they incorporate recent chipsets (AMD or Intel), dual NVMe support, and all the connections (USB-C, DisplayPort, HDMI, etc) you would expect on an up to date PC today.  In short, this is not system comprised of a hodgepodge of generations old surplus components.  Although maybe the 'surplus' description is still applicable.My first basic and very affordable mini PC still works today, but due to my extremely positive experience, I decided to upgrade to one of their most powerful offerings today.  The BMAX B8A Pro runs a current AMD Ryzen 7 8745HS released July 2024.  When it comes to mini-PCs using generations old chipsets, this is pretty much as good as it gets.The B8A Pro touts itself as a gaming mini-PC but here's the reality.  Call of Duty Warzone runs at the lowest settings, and struggles with 30fps at 1080p.  The bottleneck is not so much with the internal Radeon 780M graphics but with the memory.  The single 16GB DDR5 4400Mhz memory module is great for home office, streaming and browsing, but not for gaming.  For gaming, 2 memory modules are recommended.  4400Mhz DDR5 is also on the slower end when there options up to 6400Mhz today.  This gaming bottleneck applies to other BMAX offerings also as the 24GB or 8GB are also single memory modules.So in short, this is not a FPS capable mini-PC out of the box (unless you want to run it at super low resolution and frame rates).  You would be better served purchasing a PS5 or Xbox instead.  If you keep these expectations in mind, then the BMAX mini-PC then becomes an incredible system that delivers great value and is blazing fast for everything else.Lastly, one thing that is obvious but not mentioned often in reviews is that laptops are just not great at being a static home PC.  Biggest issue with long term reliability is cooling and wearing out the USB-C connector.  So if you are primarily using your PC at home, this is where the compact form, power saving, and most of all....value of a mini-PC shines.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Met expectations - good valueMet expectations - good value
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I had this monitor in my Amazon wish list last year. When it was discounted on a Prime Day, I bought it. I'm pleased with this monitor, especially at the price point. I haven't had any problems with its function. Its resolution is better than the older monitors it replaced.I had been using a setup of two older 25" monitors. Now I use this this 31.5" monitor sitting next to my Macbook Pro's screen, and that's fine for my needs.I don't play sound through the monitor speakers, so I don't know how good they are as monitor speakers go. I use a Bose bluetooth speaker for better sound quality than I would expect from the speakers in a monitor or a laptop.My only negative comment about this monitor: its power cord is stupid short. It wouldn't reach from the monitor - sitting on the desktop of course -  to the power strip on the floor below. I've never had a computer peripheral with such a short power cord. productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great screens if they stay on
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought two of these monitors. So far the screens have been good to look at. The resolution is great and the colors are sufficient for my needs. The only problem that I have had is one of these screens is now going off while I am using it. It just randomly goes black. It doesn't actually turn off and start all over but it will go blank and wait a second to flicker back on. I really like the screens but now the return window has closed so I guess I am going to do a warranty claim on it and have to go down that route to get something done about the one. It wouldn't be really bad but I do graphic design on these monitors and I can be drawing or making adjustments to photos right when it goes off. Then I have to wait and see if what I was doing right in the middle of the screen turning off was what I wanted to happen. If not then I have to undo and start whatever I was doing all over. It gets pretty annoying working on stuff when the screen goes dark. I have tried not to use the screen while I was trying to figure out what is going on but I bought the second screen to have the real estate to do my graphic design and video production.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on March 6, 2025

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Buyer beware!  Pray to fail fast or not at all!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I purchased two of these, and one had no issues.  The other however, is flakey as anything.  It doesn't always wake up from screen timeout, it randomly starts going dim and then returns, and this is started after Amazon's return window, but well within ASUS's warranty period (just shy of 3 months actually).  If you have an issue with an ASUS piece of equipment, pray it manifests in Amazon's return window as ASUS will make you wait for a refurb to become available before they will ship you a replacement.  They will not ship a new model to replace it and your only other option is to surrender your equipment to a repair center and wait for them to either repair or replace (up to 10-14 days I was told).  As I use my equipment for work, I was not willing to be down for up to 2 weeks.  It seems like a horrible policy as I've now been waiting for over 3 weeks for a replacement since erratic behavior is better than doing completely without.  Do better ASUS!
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on June 10, 2025

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: The best in it's class. Grab them while you can, there are popular!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This is the third ASUS monitor, two 31.5-inch. Extremely high quality and easy on your eyes with the Blue light filters. Compared to price, but with better quality than most brands, ASUS is the only brand of monitors I will ever buy.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on June 20, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This monitor isn't going to break any records, the image quality is what you'd expect from 4K, it looks sharper than anything with less resolution and this monitor has a decent color gamut. It's bright and easy to do work on. I do play games on this monitor but also program and consume entertainment. It's a little heavy too, but I like having the large square base for it to rest on. This is where the positives end.Minus one star for finnicky firmware - I have experienced on at least one occasion where the HDMI port stopped working and I had to grab a DisplayPort cable to be able to access the firmware settings and reset the settings. If the monitor attempted to use HDMI, it would constantly power-cycle. I would at least have expected a fail-safe to detect invalid settings. This monitor is unforgiving to novice users but at its price-point that seems to be its target market.Minus another star for being a 2023 monitor using outdated DisplayPort 1.2 (2010) and HDMI 2.0 (2013). There is zero doubt the VP327Q is NOT aiming to be a high-refresh gaming monitor; however, newer ports offer better versatility and bandwidth. They have been out for over a decade since this monitor was manufactured and should have been implemented in its design. I don't believe that the value proposition for this monitor necessitated using extremely outdated built-in video-in ports.Overall, it's a decent monitor and a good start for those looking to see if 4K is right for them. However, it's not going to impress in its video-in ports, unforgiving firmware and it's definitely nothing close to a proper 4K OLED monitor. Even my old 4K/Pantone Color Calibrated ThinkPad P71 from 2017 had better color accuracy.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on November 30, 2025

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great display, but the OSD settings are changed by using the on/off button as a joystick
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This is a nice monitor at a great price.  The ability to change settings via the on screen menu is NOT intuitive.  The manual illustrates using directional arrows, like those on a keyboard.  The only button on back is the on/off button.A brief call with their excellent customer service informed me that the on/off button functions like a joystick.  That means after entering the OSD menu you need to make/change setting by pushing the button up/down or right/left.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on February 11, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Poor colors and dark sides, returned
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought this monitor as what I thought would be an upgrade of my current monitor, a 24" Dell ST2421L (from 2010). I found this ASUS monitor to have very poor color quality, which looked washed out, and just "off". Also noticed on the left and right sides of the screen were darker than the center -- which I believe to be just what the eye perceives when viewed from that angle.. if I moved my entire body to the left or right, those areas then appeared normally lit.Also I will note that when I bought the monitor, and currently which is a few days later, the Amazon description says this is an IPS panel. It is actually a VA panel. I've since read that VA panels can suffer from color issues, which might explain what I noticed.I played with the color settings a bit on this ASUS to see if it could be adjusted away, but within 10 minutes it was back in the box and is heading back. It was definitely a downgrade from my cheap 2010 Dell 24".

How do I access the BIOS? 
Press the "Delete" key to access the BIOS settings. Press the "F7" key to access the boot options menu (press it repeatedly immediately after the system starts up). 
What should I pay attention to when using this mini pc for the first time? 
To avoid initial setup issues, the first time you use this mini pc,don't connect network or wifi until the windows system of your mini pc is running. 
How is the performance of this mini PC, and what games can it run? 
The integrated Vega 8 graphics offer approximately 60-70% of the performance of a GT 1030 GPU. It smoothly runs retro-style games like Stardew Valley and well-optimized online titles such as League of Legends. 
What I/O ports does the C4SE have? 
C4SE includes USB 3.2 Type-A x2 (Gen2 10Gbps, 5V/2A, Front), USB 3.2 Type-A x1 (Gen2 10Gbps, 5V/2A), USB 2.0 Type-A x1 (480Mbps, 5V/2A, Back), RJ45 Gigabit Ethernet Port x2 (RTL8111H), HDMI 2.0 x1, DP x1, USB Type-C x1, and a 3.5mm combo audio jack. 
What operating systems are supported? 
C4SE supports Win 11 and Ubuntu.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought this to replace my older GMKTech computer used as a router/gateway running IPFire. The GMKTech did not fail - I just wanted to have fresh gear powering my network. Now, the GMKTech is a backup in case the C4 fails. I have a fully-qualified domain in my house, all of my devices have names, I have firewall rules for forwarding ports to various machines, and firewall rules that block my 2 LG "smart" TVs and a Reolink PoE doorbell from any access to the Internet.I like my privacy. My phones are de-Googled with GrapheneOS, and all of the computers on my network run Debian Linux with the Cinnamon desktop environment. My phones and computers don't spy on me because they just don't. My TVs don't spy on me because they don't have Internet access. I also have a couple of Pi-Holes for DNS, and these have rules to block a lot of Internet activity from smart TVs, and I can add rules as needed. The firewall on this machine prevents what the Pi-Holes miss.The TVs are on the network so that I can automate some functions in Home Assistant, but blocked from Internet access because I don't want them spying on us. The TVs have tiny PCs running Debian/Cinnamon on them attached to an HDMI port, and we stream Hulu, Netflix, Paramount+, and Prime Video on them in isolated Chrome browsers. For Peacock, we have Fire TV sticks, because Peacock is not supported on Linux.For my use case, I suspect that the noise level will be permanently minimal. I'm running an Internet appliance, and not a gaming machine, so I can't comment about that. The machine is about a thousand times faster than necessary for my application and, at 700 or so MB, IPFire is not going to tax the storage capacity.Installation and set up were a breeze. This device is probably severe overkill for my use case, but I'm very happy with it so far.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on May 31, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Bought on a whim, very happy!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I'd never heard of this brand, but read something positive about this model on the MiniPC Reddit, which led to an Amazon search, where this model was on sale at a price I couldn't resist. I've had it for a week or so now and so far it's been pretty great, though like all minis it has its idiosyncrasies.I have a decent level of experience with these tiny computers by now, having bought a few Beelink models, both of which have been great for the most part, and a Geekom, which was not so great and was returned. I also had a poor experience a few years ago with a Chuwi Larkbox X, which was garbage. There seems to always be some little thing that isn't as perfect as it could be on these things, even the pretty great ones.I like how Beelink does things. They run cool, have logical Windows partitioning and account setup, and run Linux well, which is what I use mainly. But even with them it seems that their AMD graphics implementation can trip up certain Linux versions, though they are catching up. It's cutting edge tech, some of this, therefore it may take the Linux people a minute to get drivers sorted. The more up to date distros like Arch do fine, the older 'buntus not so much, and a few won't even boot the live USB (Alma, a Red Hat derivative that has fairly ancient software).Anyway, this particular OrigiMagic Nebula N2 model shares many of the attributes that make Beelink good - the low temps, the solid and sturdy engineering - and also the AMD graphics thing, though in a different way. The symptom on this one is that every so often the graphics kinda go wacky, before an OS is even loaded. One time even the bios setup screen was distorted and discolored, something originally noticed with Linux's bootloader (grub for me) menu. It always fixes itself after a hard reset (button presses) so ultimately not a huge concern.As far as Windows 11 goes, it's setup on the Nebula less perfectly than Beelink, with a weird reserved partition at the end of the drive. I'm sure I could reinstall myself more logically, but haven't done so yet... It runs fine, though all I use it for is to update itself, which probably won't change.As I write this I'm waiting on the new Nvme 2TB drive to finish being copied to (giant music collection - 1.3TB!). I should mention that the extra slot is easy to access but it will NOT fit a typical M.2 2280. It needs a shorter one. I had a 2tb  2230 laying around, but that size isn't ideal either. It fits, but can't be secured with a screw or anything. Since that drive won't be getting intensive use I think I'm okay with it just being in there "loose", but at some point I'll need to figure out what size is necessary, as there IS a little screw in the slot area that wants to be used...Overall, I really really like this OrigiMagic Nebula N2 so far. Solidly built, cool running, and best of all you can upgrade the RAM and storage, unlike my Beelinks which are permanently memory-limited to what's soldered on. This was a GREAT deal, as I got it for just over $300. Sometimes it pays to read Reddit!

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I’ve been using the N2 Mini PC as the centerpiece of my home entertainment setup, and it’s exceeded every expectation. Despite its ultra-compact size, this mini PC delivers serious performance. It boots up in seconds, runs silently, and handles 4K streaming effortlessly. Whether I’m watching movies, streaming music, or mirroring content from my phone, everything runs smoothly with zero lag.Wi-Fi 6E and Bluetooth 5.2 make it fully wireless-ready, and the deep sea blue retro design adds a stylish touch to my living room.
