productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Impressive web PC, first time mac user, massive upgrade over a 4 year old Lenovo Yoga 13
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The neo is really impressive for $600. It has a nice screen, an incredibly rigid aluminum chassis, loads web pages and videos super fast, boots quick. Impressive Bluetooth and WiFi range and performance (Bluetooth is so much better then my old laptop), good speakers(for a laptop), good battery life, a decent keyboard, excellent trackpad, decent web cam, looks nice, low heat output and no vents to get blocked, compact and light. Highly recommended for anyone shopping for a compact web machine.The only negatives on the hardware are: lack of keyboard backlight, the interior edge of the chassis is sharp, not enough to cut you, but enough to be annoying when typing in some positions, not many ports just a normal USB C and a 2.0 speed USB C (both can be used for charging) and screen does not fold flat, so the laptop cannot be stood up against the wall.I was a bit unsure about the Neo because of it using a cellphone chip, but that was not a problem at all. The Neo is super snappy, as fast as my Workstation/Gaming PC when loading web pages and videos. Also I have not noticed any issues with the amount of RAM, 8GB seems sufficient for running a web browser, just as long as you do not go crazy on tabs in Chrome or if you use Firefox that actually manages tabs properly. As a web browser machine I doubt that this will have any performance issues. I am sure that you would hit limits of the mobile CPU if you do did something serious like video editing, but it is more then enough for more casual use.As someone who had never used a mac before I was a bit apprehensive about trying a different OS, but really it has been fine. I mostly just use my laptop to run a web browser, so I do not interact with the OS that much and MacOS is really pretty nice in many ways. The hardest thing to get used to will be the copy paste shortcuts using command instead of ctrl. Mostly MacOS functions about the same as windows, just better. You can just shut the lid on the Neo and it actually shuts off without hardly using any battery and instantly resumes when you open it again. When you do shut it down boot time is super fast. Mac's update system is pretty unobtrusive and just not stupid like windows update. Mac wants you to sign up to all of their AI and cloud stuff, but you do not have to. I did not even setup the app store. The only apps that I wanted were Firefox and a system wide EQ for my earbuds. I found eqMac on gethub, the free version works pretty well. Anyway don't let the different OS scare you away, MacOS is pretty decent and not really that much different then windows. I got used to it in 2 days of use. Also it should get 7 years of software support.Here is a comparison of the Neo with the 4 year old Lenovo Yoga 13 it is replacing. The Lenovo was $550 when new so a very similar price category from 4 years ago. Not sure if this will be useful to anyone so I am putting this at the end, but I figure that a lot of people will be in the same situation switching from a budget windows machine from a few years ago, Overall the Neo is better in almost every way, except for the screen not being able to fold around like the yoga and the lack of a backlit keyboard.The Neo is much faster, it way outperforms the AMD 4650u in my old lenovo when it comes to loading web pages and videos. My old laptop had started really chugging lately when loading YouTube and twitch videos. Not sure it there is something wrong my old laptop it or if web sites have just gotten that much harder to run.My old lenovo Yoga 13 has an absurd amount of flex in the plastic chassis, when you pick up one corner of the device the other edge sags visibly, the keyboard flexes noticeably when typing, the entire chassis will twist with very little effort. The chassis has also cracked in several places and I have been having to superglue it back together to keep the chassis from literally falling apart. The Neo on the other hand is completely rigid you can lift it anywhere, no flex in the keyboard, you would have to really try to do anything to this thing, it is amazing for a laptop of any price, much less a $600 one. Unless you really do something terrible to it I expect the Neo chassis to last well beond the lifetime of the hardware.The battery life on the neo is great, I would say it is about twice that of the lenovo, even though I just put a new battery in my lenovo 6 months ago.The Bluetooth range on the Neo is at least 2 times better, my earbuds would loose connection to the lenovo if I walked 20 feet away to go to the bathroom. I can walk anywhere in the house and stay connected to the Neo, range of about 40+ feet in the house and about 80+ feet outside. Not only the range is better but also Bluetooth connects faster and just works kind of flawlessly, while in windows I constantly had odd Bluetooth issues. This is with just some basic $30 Anker Bluetooth earbuds.WiFI range and throughput is also much better then my old laptopThe yogo 13 had a good screen, so I do not find the screen of the Neo a huge upgrade, it is noticeably more vibrant and it is higher res, although I found 1980x1080 to be fine at this size. Also the Yoga 13 screen could fold all of the way back and around into any position you want and it was touchscreen, so some improvements and some downsides. Still the color on the Neo screen is very nice.The speakers in the Neo are many times better then the the Lenovo, my old Pixel phone even easily outdid the Lenovo, it had impressively bad speakers.The webcam on the Neo is also a big upgrade over the Lenovo, higher res and just better all around.The Neo has a macbook keyboard, so generally it is a very good laptop keyboard. It is not my favorite type of keyboard, but it works quite well and is fast to type.The trackpad is great, it is so much better then any windows computer trackpad that I have used, it functions a bit different so it takes a bit of getting used to, but it is just so much better then windows trackpads.As the Neo uses a cellphone chip it does not really need any cooling, so there are no vents and the chassis never gets hot or even warm. My old lenovo would get uncomfortably hot when charging and I had to be careful not to block the vents when using it on a bed or blanket, but that is not a problem with the Neo. There are no vents to block.Overall this thing is just impressive for $600 and I just do not see any windows laptop coming close to competing for a thin and light web machine. Sure if you want something that can game or do more intensive work stuff, but I just wanted something to run a web browser and this does that incredibly well while also being a beautifully well made device.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: It's a budget Mac, I won't quibble over minor issues
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: If I were picking nits, I'd trim a half star for some of the cost-saving choices Apple made with the Neo --- worst among them being the lack of a backlit keyboard (or at least printing the keyboard characters in a highly contrasting color --- like white-on-gray and not dark gray on lighter gray).  Also, having only two USB-C ports in close proximity (rather than on opposite sides) seems a poor design choice and having one of those ports be USB 2 in this day and age seems unnecessarily cheap.  However, as I said, these are minor annoyances and don't detract all that much from the elegance of the machine.What you are getting is the cheapest Mac money has ever been able to buy (cheaper even than most 2020 Macbook Air models on the used market.  You're also getting a laptop that's highly portable, powerful, with great battery life, impressive graphics, Apple Intelligence and that can run iOS and iPadOS apps in addition to those for MacOS.I got the Neo as a (relatively) cheap, take-anywhere traveling companion for a trip to the Amazon and Galapagos Islands. I needed to be able to run my usual software and didn't want to expose my primary laptop to the risks of theft, canoe travel, jungle heat and humidity or wet landings.  I took precautions, yes, but the Neo performed perfectly (as I would expect).For all its capabilities and price, I have no qualms about giving the Neo five stars...but Apple better do something about that keyboard in the next iteration.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Impressive  but know the real-world trade-offs before you buy
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought this with my own money — not a review unit, not sponsored — so let me give you the real picture.I was skeptical about the A18 Pro chip going in. It's the same silicon Apple put in the iPhone 16 Pro, and the idea of an iPhone chip powering a Mac felt like a compromise. After a few weeks of daily use though, I have to admit it performs much better than I expected. Browsing, productivity work, running multiple apps at once, light coding — all completely smooth. It even handles 4K video editing decently for casual projects. The machine runs completely silent since there's no fan, which is a huge plus if you work in quiet environments.The 13-inch Liquid Retina display is sharp and vivid — text looks great and colors pop — though at 500 nits it can struggle a bit outdoors in bright sunlight. Not a dealbreaker but worth knowing. The build quality feels premium way above the $599 price point. Solid aluminum chassis, lightweight at 2.7 lbs, and the keyboard has a satisfying feel to it. The 1080p webcam is genuinely one of the best I've used on a laptop — way better than what you get on similarly priced Windows machines.Battery life is solid. I'm getting around 9-10 hours of real-world use (web browsing, productivity apps, some YouTube), which tracks close to Apple's 11-hour web claim. The 16-hour video streaming claim is probably accurate if you're just watching offline video.Honest drawbacks: Only two USB-C ports and nothing else. No HDMI, no SD card slot, no MagSafe. If you need to connect anything, budget for a hub. The base model only supports one external display, and the 20W charger included is slow — expect about 2 hours for a full charge. The keyboard also has no backlighting, which was genuinely surprising at this price. And 8GB of RAM is the only option — you can't upgrade it, so if you're a heavy multitasker or plan to keep this machine 4-5 years, that ceiling may bite you eventually.Bottom line: At $599, this is an exceptional value if you're coming from a Windows laptop or upgrading from an older Mac. The A18 Pro is no slouch, macOS is rock solid, and the build quality punches well above its weight. Just go in knowing the port situation and the RAM limitation, and you'll be happy with it.

So far, my Neo has easily outperformed all the Windows laptops I've owned previously. Apps open instantly, tasks feel incredibly fluid, and its performance doesn't drop even when I have a Zoom Call along with a dozen tabs open. I've even been able run heavier applications such as some 4k video editing.Additionally, it's been very refreshing having a laptop that doesn't try to force AI and copilot crap down your throat.Definitely recommend for anyone who is looking for that premium MacBook quality without spending $1000+. Obviously this thing won't be able to run some of the applications that an Air or a Pro can run, but if you are only browsing the web/watching Youtube or streaming services/working on docs or spreadsheets, then this is the laptop you want.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: This was the first MacBook I had ever purchased , I only bought it because my daughter loves her apple products. productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Fast, Beautiful, and Worth Every Penny!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The 15-inch MacBook Air with the M5 chip is an incredible laptop. It's amazingly fast, whether I'm multitasking, streaming, editing documents, or using AI-powered tools. Everything runs smoothly, and the performance is impressive while staying completely quiet thanks to the fanless design.The 15.3-inch display is bright, sharp, and perfect for both work and entertainment. The keyboard is comfortable, the trackpad is responsive, and the overall build quality is exactly what you'd expect from Apple.If you're looking for a powerful, reliable, and beautifully designed laptop that can handle everyday tasks and more, this MacBook Air is an outstanding choice. Highly recommended!

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: After spending several weeks using the Apple 2026 MacBook Air 15-inch with the M5 chip, I can confidently say this is one of the most impressive laptops Apple has ever produced. It takes everything people already loved about the MacBook Air lineup and elevates it with more power, better connectivity, enhanced AI capabilities, and the same incredibly thin and lightweight design that has made the Air such a popular choice for students, professionals, creators, and everyday users alike.The first thing that stands out is the beautiful 15.3-inch Liquid Retina display. The larger screen size provides significantly more workspace without making the laptop feel bulky or difficult to carry. Whether I'm working on spreadsheets, editing documents, watching videos, or multitasking with multiple windows open, the display offers plenty of room to stay productive. Colors look vibrant and accurate, blacks appear deep, and text is remarkably sharp. Photos and videos truly come alive on this screen, making everything from casual web browsing to content creation an enjoyable experience.Performance is where the new M5 chip really shines. Apple continues to push efficiency and power forward with each generation of its silicon, and the M5 feels incredibly responsive. Applications launch almost instantly, multitasking feels effortless, and demanding workloads are handled with ease. I regularly switch between dozens of browser tabs, productivity software, video calls, photo editing tools, and streaming services without noticing any slowdowns.The included 16GB of unified memory makes a substantial difference when working with multiple applications simultaneously. Everything feels fluid and smooth, even during heavier workloads. For professionals who frequently work with large files or creative projects, the extra memory provides peace of mind and ensures consistent performance throughout the day.One of the most exciting aspects of this MacBook Air is how well it is prepared for the growing importance of artificial intelligence. The M5 chip's Neural Engine and advanced GPU architecture provides a strong foundation for AI-powered features and workflows. Tasks that leverage machine learning feel faster and more integrated into everyday computing. Rather than feeling like a gimmick, AI features are woven naturally into the user experience, helping streamline tasks and improve productivity.Apple Intelligence is another highlight that makes this laptop feel future-ready. The system helps with writing, communication, organization, and everyday productivity while maintaining Apple's strong focus on privacy. What I appreciate most is that these tools feel genuinely useful instead of intrusive. They assist when needed while staying out of the way when not required. The privacy protections Apple has built into the experience also provide confidence that personal information remains secure.Battery life continues to be one of the MacBook Air's strongest advantages. Apple claims up to 18 hours of battery life, and in real-world use, the endurance is excellent. During typical workdays involving email, web browsing, video calls, document editing, and media consumption, I rarely worry about finding a charger. It's incredibly refreshing to use a laptop that can comfortably last through a full day of work, classes, or travel.For frequent travelers, students moving between classes, or professionals working remotely, this level of battery life is a major benefit. The freedom to leave the charger at home without anxiety cannot be overstated. Even under heavier workloads, the battery performance remains impressive.The design remains one of the defining strengths of the MacBook Air. Apple has created a machine that feels incredibly premium while remaining surprisingly portable. Despite the larger 15-inch display, the laptop feels slim, elegant, and easy to carry. The Midnight finish looks particularly stunning, giving the computer a sleek and modern appearance that stands out without being flashy.Build quality is exceptional throughout. The aluminum chassis feels solid and durable, the hinge operates smoothly, and every aspect of the laptop reflects Apple's attention to detail. It feels like a product designed to last for years of daily use.The keyboard deserves special recognition. Typing on the MacBook Air is comfortable, quiet, and highly accurate. The key travel strikes an excellent balance between responsiveness and comfort, making long writing sessions enjoyable. As someone who spends hours each day typing emails, documents, and reports, I found the keyboard consistently comfortable even during extended use.The large trackpad continues to set the standard for laptops. Gestures are intuitive, tracking is precise, and navigation feels effortless. Once you become accustomed to Apple's trackpad implementation, it's difficult to use many competing laptops without noticing the difference.Video calling has become an essential part of modern life, and the upgraded 12MP Center Stage camera performs exceptionally well. Image quality appears noticeably sharper and more detailed compared to previous generations. Center Stage is particularly useful because it automatically keeps you framed during video calls, allowing for a more professional appearance without constantly adjusting your position.Desk View is another surprisingly useful feature. Being able to share a top-down view of your workspace can be valuable during presentations, demonstrations, teaching sessions, or collaborative projects. These camera enhancements make the MacBook Air feel especially well-suited for today's hybrid work and remote learning environments.Audio quality is equally impressive. The six-speaker sound system delivers rich, clear sound with impressive depth for such a thin laptop. Music sounds full and immersive, movies benefit from enhanced spatial effects, and video calls remain crisp and easy to understand. Support for Spatial Audio and Dolby Atmos helps create a more engaging listening experience that exceeds expectations for a device of this size.The three-microphone array also deserves praise. Voice clarity during calls is excellent, and background noise reduction helps ensure conversations remain clear. Whether attending meetings, recording voice notes, or participating in online classes, the microphone quality consistently performs well.Connectivity has received meaningful upgrades as well. The inclusion of Wi-Fi 7 provides faster wireless performance and better future-proofing for modern networks. In areas with compatible infrastructure, downloads, uploads, streaming, and cloud-based workflows feel exceptionally fast and reliable.Bluetooth 6 support further enhances wireless connectivity, making it easier to connect accessories while maintaining strong and stable connections. Whether using wireless headphones, keyboards, mice, or other peripherals, connectivity remains seamless.The port selection strikes a practical balance. The MagSafe charging connector remains one of my favorite features because it frees up Thunderbolt ports while providing a convenient and secure charging experience. The two Thunderbolt 4 ports offer excellent versatility for connecting displays, storage devices, docks, and other accessories. The inclusion of a headphone jack is also appreciated, especially for users who still rely on wired audio equipment.Support for up to two external displays significantly improves productivity possibilities. Professionals who work with multiple monitors will appreciate the flexibility this provides, transforming the MacBook Air into a capable workstation when needed.macOS continues to be one of the most polished and user-friendly operating systems available. Everything feels optimized and responsive, taking full advantage of Apple's hardware and software integration. Applications launch quickly, animations remain smooth, and system stability has been excellent throughout my usage.The built-in security features provide additional confidence, helping protect personal information without requiring constant user intervention. Regular software updates ensure the system remains secure and continues to improve over time.One of the biggest advantages for existing Apple users is the seamless integration with other Apple devices. If you own an iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch, or AirPods, the ecosystem benefits are substantial. Features such as iPhone Mirroring make it possible to interact with your phone directly from your Mac. Copying content on one device and pasting it on another feels almost magical, while FaceTime and Messages integration creates a unified communication experience.These ecosystem features may seem small individually, but together they create a workflow that feels remarkably convenient and efficient. Once you experience how seamlessly Apple's devices work together, it becomes difficult to imagine using them separately.What impresses me most about the 2026 MacBook Air 15-inch is its balance. It delivers powerful performance without sacrificing battery life. It offers a large display without becoming cumbersome. It introduces advanced AI capabilities while remaining simple and approachable. It provides premium features while maintaining the portability that defines the Air lineup.Whether you're a student, professional, creative user, entrepreneur, or someone simply looking for a reliable premium laptop, this MacBook Air is easy to recommend. The combination of the M5 chip, beautiful display, excellent battery life, upgraded camera system, fast connectivity, and deep Apple ecosystem integration creates a package that feels incredibly complete.Overall, the Apple 2026 MacBook Air 15-inch with M5 chip is an outstanding laptop that successfully combines performance, portability, intelligence, and premium design. It feels like a meaningful evolution of an already excellent product and represents one of the best everyday laptops available today. For anyone seeking a versatile machine capable of handling work, creativity, entertainment, and future AI-powered experiences, this MacBook Air is an exceptional choice and a purchase that is likely to satisfy for many years to come.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Perfect compliment to my other Apple products
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: To be honest, this is probably more computer than I need. However, the MacBook Neo is limited to a 13-inch screen and I did not want to downgrade in screen size. The processor speed is fast, which makes multitasking a breeze. The display quality is exceptional. Having used Windows computers for the last couple of decades is not an issue when switching operating systems, especially if you have experience with an iPad. They are similar in how they function.  I also like the Sky Blue color that I bought. When looking at them at a store I thought the silver looked washed out in comparison and Starlight, a hard no. The Midnight color was a strong second for me. As with all Apple products, the MacBook is very well made and attractive in appearance. It is also relatively light weight and easy to carry around. I was lucky to order this right before the price increase, so the value for the money worked in my favor.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: (probably) the perfect laptop for you(probably) the perfect laptop for you
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: I researched for months before finally delving into MacBook land.I’m a tech nerd who has no need of daily photo/video editing or any amount of creative software, but I wanted the ability to do those things (I have the “someday I might…” illness).Torn between air and pro, 13, 14, 15, and 16 inches (not to mention I’ve been a lifelong windows user who landed on Mac for build quality and battery life reasons, I went to the Apple Store on several occasions to compare them all.I found the 13” Air too small, and the 16” Pro too big, so my options were 14” Pro or 15” Air.Base model price gap on those is around $300, and for that you get a brighter mini-LED screen, a fan, and an HDMI port, SD card reader, and an extra usb C port.I landed on the 15” air because I wanted the extra screen real estate, and the screen quality and brightness in person was not terribly noticeable.The screen on this 15” air is still far better than any windows laptop I’ve ever owned, and it is more than bright enough for me.As you’d expect, the build quality is exceptional, and the battery life is hard to believe. MacOS is very easy to learn and becomes intuitive very quickly.While the 13” air at its price point is very attractive, the cost of upgrading to the 15” was easy to justify, given that you not only get the larger screen, but actually an upgraded processor as well (2 more cores). You also get upgraded speakers over the 13”.I have been an iPhone/airpods user for years and I had no idea the simple conveniences I was missing out on. AirDrop, copy/paste between devices, automatic device switching, etc. all work incredibly well.I can’t believe I didn’t switch years ago, and unless you’re a hardcore user, the Air is the MacBook for you. The air does everything the pro does (unless you’re spending your annual salary on an upgraded spec model).As the saying goes, “if you don’t know you need the pro, you probably don’t need the pro”

features: 【AMD RYZEN 7 7735HS PROCESSOR】This NIMO laptop runs on AMD Ryzen 7 7735HS processor with 8 Cores/16 Threads and a peak boost clock up to 4.75GHz. Crafted on advanced 6nm Zen 3+ architecture, the business laptop handles massive dataset processing, 4K video editing and multi-tab browsing seamlessly to deliver smooth daily professional usage.

【INTEGRATED RADEON 680M GRAPHICS】Powered by integrated AMD Radeon 680M graphics, this laptop punches well above its weight. Built on the RDNA 2 architecture, it delivers smooth visuals for creative design, photo editing, and casual gaming without the bulk of a dedicated GPU.

【Ultra-Fast 100W PD GaN Charging】The NIMO laptop comes bundled with a 100W Type-C GaN II fast charger and a built-in 53.58Wh battery that hits 50% charge rapidly. Supporting USB-C PD 3.0 universal charging standard, one single charger works for your laptop, smartphone and tablet, an ideal pick for frequent business travelers and remote working owners of this portable laptop.

【15.6-inch FHD Anti-Glare Eye-friendly Screen】The NIMO laptop features a 15.6-inch 1920×1080 FHD anti-glare display with 85% screen-to-body ratio. Equipped with a 180° lay-flat hinge, this business laptop enables convenient screen sharing during team meetings, and anti-glare surface lessens eye fatigue during long hours of continuous work on the laptop.

【User-Upgradable DDR5 Memory & PCIe 4.0 Storage】Unlike mainstream ultrabooks with fixed soldered hardware, this NIMO laptop has dual-channel DDR5 SO-DIMM slots plus an M.2 PCIe 4.0 x4 high-speed SSD slot. Users can manually upgrade RAM and storage on the laptop anytime to match expanding professional work requirements and keep the laptop running efficiently long-term.

【Rich Multifunctional Port Layout】The NIMO laptop acts as an all-in-one connectivity hub with dual full-function USB-C, HDMI 2.0 and three USB-A ports, letting users connect dual external monitors and assorted peripherals without extra adapters. Additional Micro SD reader speeds up image importing while the built-in 2MP webcam supports sharp video calls on this versatile laptop.

【Fingerprint Security Unlock & Backlit Full Keyboard】This business laptop installs a fingerprint sensor embedded into the touchpad to support quick Windows Hello login and secure your important personal and work data. A full-size backlit keyboard with standalone number pad is equipped on the laptop for precise, relaxed typing in dim settings such as overnight offices or in-flight trips.

【Lightweight Pro Design】Tailored for modern office users, this clamshell-style NIMO laptop weighs under 3.7 lbs (1.7kg) and is only 19.2mm thick. Featuring streamlined minimalist appearance, the lightweight laptop is easy to carry to boardrooms and cafes, combining workstation-level performance with ultrabook-style portability.

【2-Year Warranty & 90-Day Hassle-Free Returns】We provide reliable after-sales service for all NIMO laptops. Every device is covered by 2-year official warranty and supports 90-day easy return and exchange. Our professional customer service team responds quickly to solve usage failures and accessory problems, bringing you worry-free shopping experience for office, study and gaming use.

【USA Partial Assembly & Strict Quality Inspection】Every NIMO laptop is partially assembled in the USA with refined production techniques. Each finished laptop passes comprehensive quality checks and durability stress testing to satisfy strict reliability standards, bringing stable premium computing experience for every laptop user.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Nice budget computer for light browsing or schoolwork
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: "At the price point (<$300) there is a lot to like about this laptop. It is extremely power efficient thanks to the process (N100), and as long as you are only browsing with a few tabs, or maybe a couple apps at a time you should be fine. It has 16GB RAM, which is helpful and probably makes the bottleneck the CPU. It also has 1TB of storage, which is a really generous amount, as most others in this price range end up with 250 - 500GB. The display has good colors, and the brightness levels are also very good. Although it is a Full HD (1080p) display, Windows is set to scale things to 125% by default, so if you'd rather have more screen real estate, make sure to set that to 100%. It does come with Windows 11, and includes a finger print reader too (optional to use). Getting all the Windows updates installed (as of 3/2025) took about 5 hours watching it pretty closely to keep it restarting and then starting a check again, but that's not too bad, and you can definitely let those happen organically if you would rather.The keyboard is very pleasant to type on, and reminds me of a MacBook Air keyboard quite a bit. It is backlit too, which is another really nice feature for the price. I love that it uses USB-C for the power supply, which makes it so nice that most people can just take a single USB-C charger to keep their phone, laptop, and tablet charged up.It does slow down pretty noticeably when playing media, especially streaming from Netflix or YouTube. It does work though, and as long as you plan on only have another tab or two open, or an application like Word and the video side-by-side it does work. It definitely is not a multi-tasking machine, but if you can focus on just one or two apps at once I think it works really well. I much prefer this laptop to any Chromebook I've tried."
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on March 31, 2025

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I've been using this laptop quite a bit now and I have to say it's pretty quick, can run most everything I need and has a great 15 inch screen that is very bright.  The keyboard is backlit and has a numeric keypad on the side and the built in speaker put out quite a bit of sound.  The weight is about average for a laptop of this size and so far it's been an amazing value for the price.  The only downside is that the batter life isn't the greatest, a few hours give or take depending on what you are doing, however it's not the worst I've seen.  I also noticed that there is something slightly off on the keyboard layout...I'm not able to type as fast without mistakes...I haven't been able to figure out what the issue is but there is something slightly off with the key placement.  Not a deal breaker but can be a little frustrating at times.  For the price difference however I wouldn't complain.  This is a great laptop for a student or a parent that wants to get their kid a laptop and doesn't want to spend a fortune.  The built in camera also has a privacy shutter you can close when you are not using it and the trackpad has a fingerprint id area that you can use to unlock your computer.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on April 6, 2025

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Fast, reliable and packed with features
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I am so impressed with this laptop. I bought it for school and everyday use, and it's exceeded my expectations. The 16GB RAM and 1TB SSD make everything run super smooth even with multiple tabs, video calls, and assignments open at once. Startup is lightning fast, and there is no lag at all. The full HD IPS screen is crisp and vibrant, great for watching lectures or streaming. I also love the backlit keyboard for late night study sessions, and the fingerprint reader adds a layer of convenience and security I didn't know I needed. Build quality feels solid, and it looks sleek and professional. Plus, a 2 year warranty gives me peace of mind. For the price, this laptop offers amazing value and performance. Whether you are a student or just need a reliable everyday laptop, this is a fantastic choice.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Nice little miniPC.  The system boots fast, has quick login.  I had extra ddr4 memory and an unused SSD so this barebones seemed like a good fit.  It lowered in price as the 5500u version went up.  This has a better processor than the 5500u, making pricing a bit confusing.  The CPU is a bit older, but it supports DDR4 and is better deal than the 5500u.  I used a SATA B+M key M.2 drive with 12 GB ddr4 ram and it works well.  The system includes a USB stick with drivers/software.  It also included a little screwdriver for disassembly and installing of memory and SSD.  There are 2 ssd slots and the larger one mounts ontop of the wifi module.  I was concerned about that but manufactures have a thin plastic film in place to separate them preventing any shorts.  The smaller SDD slot stands alone.  I did not configure, test or use the wifi on the system.I marked it down one star related to 3 items.  Setting the date on the system took multiple attempts.  The date was initially a date in 2077.  Correcting it in bios appeared to be ignored.  After correcting it in the OS, i found that after reboot it changed again, yet it was only about 6 months off.  3rd correction for date seems to have stuck and i have not had any issues with date being reset to something strange after that.  The other reason is that if you want to include a heatsink on your 2280 ssd, even a small one, plastic is in the way that will prevent you from closing the bottom completely/correctly.  The plastic that is in the ways seems unnecessary and likely can be shaved down with a file.  It was great that it included a flash drive with drivers/software but the fit on it was extremely tight and inserting/removing the flash drive needs more force and patience than is true with most flash drives.  I was often concerned about breaking the USB interface due to how tight the fit was for that flash drive.Overall the system works well and appears to be a great value is you want new and have extra components like memory and SSD available.Note: the flash drive is bootable, but it appears that if you dont have a real SSD in the system, it powers off the system when you try to boot from it.  I initially thought I would just run small lightweight OS from an USB flash drive instead ofSSD. That likely would work, but i just installed older SSD to get around it.The one star review (which may be present) that is not related to the product but related to amazon search.  That review may still be listed on this product but should be ignored as it is not product nor seller related but Amazon website related.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Fantastic Machine at a Fantastic Value
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I needed a new desktop and was shopping online. I was on a budget but knew that I wanted a decent machine, so I zeroed in on certain features, I wanted a Ryzen 5 or better chip and wanted at least 16MB of ram and wanted to be able to upgrade it if I chose to.When I started looking at traditional desktops, ones equipped with those items (and of course all of the others, bluetooth, wifi, SSD etc) they were all $600-$1000 minimum.  Some were much much more.I literally stumbled across an ad for one of these on Amazon. I clicked on the ad, looked at the specs and the price and honestly thought, this must be some kind of scam.  I started reading about mini PCs and watched a couple of videos, and realized this is not a scam, paying Lenovo or HP $800 for the same specs is the scam.This arrived on a Saturday, I got it out, looked at everything in the box and plugged it all in, it started up like a champ and has run perfectly so far. Windows 11 started just fine, my bt devices connected effortlessly.This is an amazing machine at an amazing value.  I have two caveats, one, this is not a gaming machine, if you want a true gaming machine, you need a dedicated graphics card, you just do, but I am only doing light gaming, like Roblox, Minecraft and this is great. Second, if you need a tower where you want a DVD drive etc, again, this is not it. But for most people looking for a desktop to surf the web, play light games and pay their bills online, this is fantastic and you will be thrilled.  Take you family to some nice dinners with the money saved.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I’m using this as an HTPC with Ubuntu 22.04. Starts fairly quickly, streams fine and plays locally stored media fine. I’ve tried a number of different solutions but I can’t get it to recognize my Microsoft mouse or my Sony portable speaker. Both are known good & work with the same OS on a Dell desktop. Oddly enough it recognizes my air purifier in the other room.Sound- out of the headphone jack there’s some static. I saw others with the same issue on Reddit- one suggestion was to use a USB Soundblaster. Voila! No static, sounds fine.I can’t report on the WiFi because I have it on Ethernet.Overall I’d recommend it (for my use case) if you want a small PC.(tags Ubuntu Linux sound wifi bluetooth)

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: It's definitely bang for the buck
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Hi there,I just wanted to share my experience with the Beelink SER5 Mini PC, AMD Ryzen 5 5500U. I bought it online and it arrived quickly. I was blown away by its surprising speed and amazingly small size. It's so compact that I installed it on the back of my monitor and it barely takes any space. It runs smoothly and quietly, and it can handle multiple tasks without any lag. It's definitely bang for the buck and I'm very happy with my purchase. If you're looking for a powerful and portable mini PC, I highly recommend the Beelink SER5!

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I was on the fence about buying a mini pc. Ive always bought big, heavy desktop towers before this. I needed a new pc and decided to try this one. So glad I did! It was incredibly easy to set up- I was up and running in minutes. Comes with Windows 11 installed with no junk software. It has the connections you need but I added a powered USB 3.0 hub. It runs absolutely silently and I cant detect anything but minimal heat from the pc. A very welcome change from the monsters I was used to! Just try one- I think you'll like it!
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on July 11, 2024

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Wireless keyboard and mouse Issues PLUS
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: DO NOT PURCHASE.  I only used a browser, and only for 3 days. First issue, if you open a tab ( with maybe 2 other tabs open) and go to YouTube, your mouse and keyboard will severely lag. You can adjust the settings but it won't help AT ALL.  You look a a news tab..same issue, lag, lag lag. You need to open a SaaS type of window in your browser, same lag.Also the bluetooth kept falling off.Also the video playback from Youtube was minimal, there's no way this would support 4k. Please note, I have extremely fast internet connection.You want to open steam and play a 2D game?? Nope, so forget anything else. I mean the most basic of 2D games, it will lag.Had 2 monitors connected via HDMI, one of them looked bad, one looked fine, both monitors are the same Samsung.I returned it, OH BEWARE, you must package it up, it only arrived in a flimsy plastic bag and the corners were slightly bumped in, hardly any foam around the unit, so extremely minimal protection. Just note, if you only open emails maybe this would work for you. It didn't work for me.They say not to return it but there's noway I would waste hours trying to get it to work, or even think of wasting hours calling some support. Returned it and bought an Apple Mini M2 for only 300 more, best purchase I've made all year.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on March 31, 2023

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: This was the best purchase I made in a long time!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I have the model with 32gb of RAM and a 512gb M2 SSD drive. I purchased this PC because I needed something more powerful for The Adobe Suite which I use frequently for work and school. Also worth noting that this is the first PC I purchased with these ridiculously fast specs.I spent 2 months researching gaming laptops as a solution for Adobe more than gaming. Gaming is something I was interested in but it wasn't the #1 priority, although I am really happy to be able to play Forza 4 on the cloud, with Xbox game pass. It's not perfect but runs smoothly 90% of the time. I don't bother tweaking the graphic settings, but I have before, and it is more or less the same, so I leave it alone.It's is the best little PC I have ever owned and I saved $750+, as I was willing to invest $1500-1700 on a gaming laptop. This cost me $750 with a $45 off instant coupon and Prime for extra convenience.It is above and beyond what I hoped for and Beelink builds a solid device.

features: 【Powerful Integrated Graphics for Work & Play】Experience smooth visuals powered by the Radeon 680M, an integrated GPU with performance rivaling dedicated graphics cards like the GTX 1650, eliminating the need for a bulky, expensive gaming laptop for everyday tasks.Dive into visually stunning story-driven games with playable performance at 1080p low-to-medium settings, offering surprising versatility for a notebook without a discrete GPU.

【Upgrade-Ready Powerhouse】Dual-channel 32 GB DDR5 + 2 TB PCIe 4.0 SSD comes standard. Tool-free access lets you swap RAM or storage in minutes. The rugged metal A-shell keeps internals safe and looks premium on any desk.

【100 W USB-C GaN Charger】Included 100 W PD charger and 6.5 ft USB-C cable refuel the laptop to 50 % in 15 min—enough for 2 h of use. One compact brick also juices phones, tablets, and cameras; travel lighter without battery anxiety.

【Professional Efficiency & Privacy Protection】Privacy-Focused Backlit Keyboard: Enables secure, low-light typing during confidential meetings or travel, keeping your work discreet.Instant Fingerprint Unlock: Power on and unlock your device in one touch for rapid access to presentations and documents before meetings.One-Click HDMI Connectivity: Instantly project to a conference room display or external monitor via HDMI for seamless presentations and collaboration.

【2-Year Warranty | U.S.-Assembled | 90-Day Returns】Your satisfaction is guaranteed. Every NIMO laptop is backed by a 2-year manufacturer warranty from NIMO Direct Inc. and a 90-day, no-questions-asked return policy. Partial U.S. assembly and rigorous QC ensure lasting reliability. Need help? Our U.S.–based support team responds fast.

【Efficiency for Students & Professionals】A single-chip solution that delivers strong graphical power without sacrificing battery life or portability, perfect for students, casual creators, and professionals who value a balance of performance and mobility.Accelerate photo editing, video streaming, and light content creation workflows with capable integrated graphics that handle everyday creative applications with ease.

【All-Day Battery Life】Built with advanced 6nm technology and optimized power efficiency, this laptop ensures extended unplugged use, making it ideal for working, studying, or enjoying entertainment on the go.A balanced laptop that handles business tasks, media consumption, and entertainment effortlessly—truly an all-in-one solution for students, professionals, and home users.

【Modern Connectivity and Speed】Supports PCIe 4.0 SSDs for fast file transfers and system responsiveness, along with USB4 compatibility for high-speed peripherals and docking.Engineered with an efficient thermal design that maintains strong performance under load while keeping fan noise low during everyday use.

【Professional-Grade Performance】Featuring the AMD Ryzen 7 6800H processor with 8 cores and 16 threads, this laptop delivers powerful multitasking and smooth performance for demanding productivity applications, programming, and creative workloads.Equipped with AMD Radeon 680M graphics, offers performance comparable to a discrete GPU—smoothly running popular online games and select AAA titles at 1082p settings without the need for a dedicated graphics card.

【Thin and light, long battery life】Thanks to the advanced 6nm process technology, it provides strong performance while maintaining excellent energy efficiency ratio. With the large-capacity battery, it supports long-term mobile office and classroom study, so that you don't have to look for power outlets frequently in libraries, cafes or business trips.

features: FAST RUNS IN THE FAMILY — The 16-inch MacBook Pro with the M5 Pro or M5 Max chip brings next-generation speed and powerful on-device AI to personal, professional, and creative tasks. With all-day battery life, double the starting storage,* and a breathtaking Liquid Retina XDR display, it’s pro in every way.*

BUILT FOR AI — Apple silicon, and every major component that powers it, is designed to run demanding on-device AI workloads like LLM inference and training. ALL-DAY BATTERY LIFE — MacBook Pro delivers the same exceptional performance whether it’s running on battery or plugged in.*

BRILLIANT PRO DISPLAY — The 16.2-inch Liquid Retina XDR display features 1600 nits peak brightness,* 1000 nits sustained brightness, and 1,000,000:1 contrast.*
ADVANCED CAMERA AND AUDIO — Stay perfectly framed and sound great with a 12MP Center Stage camera, three studio-quality mics, and six speakers with Spatial Audio and support for Dolby Atmos.

CONNECT IT ALL — Features three Thunderbolt 5 ports, a MagSafe 3 charging port, SDXC card slot, HDMI port, headphone jack, and the Apple-designed N1 wireless chip for Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6.* And supports up to three external displays with M5 Pro, or up to four with M5 Max.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great Chip, Stunning Screen… My One Regret: Not Enough Unified Memory
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I purchased the MacBook Pro 2026 M5 Pro (16”) after owning a MacBook Pro M1 Pro (16”). I had zero issues with my MacBook Pro M1 Pro. I only upgraded because of the chip shortage.I got this MacBook BEFORE the price hikes. I don’t regret it.The biggest upgrade I felt was:- Display (the MacBook Pro 2026 is crispier and brighter)- Device Color (I went from Space Gray to Space Black and the color is premium feel)I run Adobe Apps, Microsoft Apps, Claude and videoconferencing apps simultaneously and the MacBook Pro 2026 is able to keep up with no issue. I purchased the 1 TB so that might be contributing to its great performance. My previous model (MacBook Pro M1 Pro) was 512 GB and I would get heavy SD usage when running multiple apps at the same time.Would I recommend this MacBook Pro M5 Pro?Yes. However, since the price hikes have taken into effect, I would strongly recommend selecting the MacBook with 1 TB… minimum.Do I have any regrets?Yes. I regret not investing the extra money for a 48 GB of unified Memory. I work from home, and AI workflows are becoming more and more a part of my work routine. I wish I would have purchased the extra unified memory to “future proof” my device.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: The MacBook Pro is a Workhorse & Will Last Many Years.
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: I am thrilled with this purchase. The MacBook Pro 16" is a substantial upgrade, and I know it will be a workhorse for many years. This is the first 16" MacBook Pro I have purchased. I do not intend to travel with it, or cart it around much, so the size is not an issue. I am still in the process of setting it up. The delivery and unboxing went well. It came in the original MacBook Pro box, and had not been opened or tampered with. Outside that was a strong cardboard box with the lithium battery warning on the outside, and then it was put inside a regular box. So it was well packaged, and I have no concerns that it was opened, or used prior to receiving it. This was a large purchase, and I am thankful it went well. Great product! Thank you! Update - After a few more hours, I find it so much easier to read, and navigate than the smaller MacBook Pro I was using. It is very intuitive, and an absolute pleasure to sit in front of. I have had many MacBook Pros over the years. Nothing could convince me to change, even to a MacBook Air. One of my past favourites was in 2008. However, in the past, I always had a smaller one compared to this one. This is an upgrade from a 2020 M1 13.3" model. What a difference! The smaller one is still functional, and will be good to have on hand for taking it places. The 16" is closer to a desktop setup. I have tried a couple of stands to use with it so far. The first one interfered with the Internet connection, so I had to return it. The one I am using now is a BoYata, and so far it has not caused any issues with the Wi-Fi connection. It is a good solid adjustable stand for this large laptop.

Who is the new Razer Blade 16 best suited for? 
The Blade 16 is ideal for competitive gamers, streamers, and creators who want flagship RTX 5090 performance in a thin, premium 16-inch gaming laptop. 
Is the new Razer Blade 16 good for gaming? 
Yes. The Razer Blade 16 is built for high-performance gaming with up to NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 Laptop GPU and 165W TGP, delivering smooth frame rates in AAA titles and competitive esports games. 
What makes the new Razer Blade 16 different from other gaming laptops? 
It balances performance, display quality, portability, and premium build in one device rather than prioritizing only raw power or only portability. 
Should I choose Razer Blade 14, Blade 16, or Blade 18? 
The Blade 14 if you prioritize maximum portability. 
The Blade 16 if you want the best balance of performance, display immersion, and mobility. 
The Blade 18 if you want the largest display and closest-to-desktop experience. 
Is the Razer Blade 16 good for AI workloads? 
Yes. Powered by Intel Core Ultra 9 with up to 50 TOPS NPU performance and RTX 50 Series graphics, the Blade 16 supports AI-accelerated tasks such as content creation, rendering, and machine learning workflows.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: High performance all-in-one !!Hey Bro., if you just need something for your desk that looks cool and doesn't cost a fortune, this desktop is actually a pretty sweet deal. That 23.8-inch curved screen is the best part—it makes your whole setup look way more high-end than it is, and it’s awesome for binging shows or just having a ton of tabs open while you work. Plus, since it’s an all-in-one, you don't have to deal with a big, ugly tower or a mess of cables everywhere, which is a total win if you like a clean vibe.Now, just being real with you: it’s not exactly a powerhouse. The processor inside is a few years old at this point. It’ll handle your everyday stuff—like emails, schoolwork, and scrolling—totally fine because it has plenty of memory. But if you’re trying to play the latest games or do heavy video editing, it’s probably going to struggle. It’s basically the perfect "home office" or student computer.It even comes with a keyboard and mouse in the box, so you can literally just plug it in and you're good to go. It’s a solid, "it just works" kind of machine for the price.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I ordered two of these Dell 27 AIO desktops for my small retail office, and every staff member loves the upgrade over our old slow towers. As someone who constantly manages inventory spreadsheets, takes client Zoom calls and processes tax documents, the Core 7 150U delivers consistent snappy performance no matter how many programs I open. The oversized 27-inch screen makes scanning long inventory lists effortless, and color accuracy works well for our marketing flyer designs. The retractable privacy camera is a must-have for us since we handle customer personal data, and adjustable tilt ensures everyone can find a comfortable camera angle during meetings. Dolby Atmos speakers eliminate the need for separate headsets for daily video conferences. WiFi 6E handles bulk cloud backups of business records without disconnections, and dual HDMI ports let our admin team set up dual-screen workflows easily. The 1TB SSD stores all our business archives permanently, while 32GB RAM prevents lag during month-end data sorting. The bundled wireless keyboard and mouse store neatly under the stand, cutting down messy cables around our desks. Windows 11 Pro includes all the enterprise security features we need, and setup only took 10 minutes out of the box. This is a well-rounded machine for any small business workspace.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Large 27” color accurate AIO built for photo & video editing
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I upgraded to this Dell 27 AIO for my e-commerce product photography and graphic design work, and it’s drastically boosted my daily efficiency. The Core 7 150U processor handles Photoshop, asset management software and dozens of browser tabs running simultaneously with zero lag. I chose the 64GB DDR5 RAM + 2TB SSD configuration, and I no longer need external hard drives to store thousands of high-res product images and design drafts.The 27-inch FHD IPS panel is the highlight of this unit. It covers full 99% sRGB and features upgraded contrast, so product colors look identical to real life when editing listing photos. Thin bezels expand viewing space, and ComfortView Plus filters blue light without washing out shades — I can edit for 7+ hours without eye strain.The 5MP pop-up IR camera with HDR works great for client video calls, and physically retracting it fully removes any privacy risks. Built-in Dolby Atmos dual speakers deliver rich, clear sound for consultation calls and after-work streaming. Dual HDMI in/out ports are super versatile: I connect a secondary monitor for spreadsheets via HDMI-out, and HDMI-in lets me hook up my laptop to use this big display during presentations. WiFi 6E holds steady even when multiple devices connect to my home office network. It comes with matching wireless keyboard and mouse that slide under the stand to save desk space, plus pre-activated Windows 11 Pro with full professional tools. 10/10 for creative professionals.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Clean desk, big screen, and plenty of power for office work
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I replaced a tower PC with this Dell all-in-one, and I'm genuinely happy I did. The desk space savings alone are a huge win – no more bulky tower or tangle of cables underneath.The 27-inch FHD IPS display is fantastic for my workflow. I work with spreadsheets and financial reports, and having that much screen real estate makes a real difference. Text is sharp, colors are accurate, and the narrow bezels keep the whole setup looking clean. I'm not a creative professional by any means, but for office work and occasional photo editing, this display hits the sweet spot. The anti-blue light feature is a nice touch for those days when I'm staring at the screen for hours – my eyes definitely feel less tired. Performance has been rock solid. The Core 7 processor with 32GB of DDR5 RAM handles everything I throw at it.I also like that Dell includes a wireless keyboard and mouse in the box. They're not premium, but they're perfectly functional for daily work. The keyboard even has a numeric keypad, which I use all the time for data entry. It's nice to have everything you need out of the box without having to buy peripherals separately.Value-wise, this Dell offers good performance without taking up half your desk. For anyone working from home, running a small business, or just wanting a clean, capable home computer, this is a solid option. I've had Dell desktops before and the build quality has been consistent, so I'm hoping this one lasts just as long.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: An absolute powerhouse with a breathtaking screen!An absolute powerhouse with a breathtaking screen!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I’ve been putting the 2026 Lenovo Legion 5a through its paces, and it has completely blown me away. If you are looking for a laptop that handles heavy gaming and creative work without skipping a beat, this Eclipse Black beast is it.Here is what stands out the most from my everyday use:That 15.3" OLED Display is Next-Level: The WQXGA resolution is incredibly sharp, but the real star is the OLED panel combined with the 165Hz refresh rate. The colors are unbelievably vibrant, and the contrast gives you those true, deep blacks that make atmospheric games look stunning. Going back to a standard LCD screen feels impossible now.RTX 5060 & Ryzen 7 Performance: The new NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 paired with the Ryzen 7 250 chip handles everything I throw at it. I’ve been running modern AAA titles at high-to-max settings, and the frame rates stay buttery smooth.Massive Memory & Storage: With 32GB of memory, multitasking is effortless. I can keep a game running in the background while having dozens of browser tabs and Discord open. The 1TB SSD is lightning fast, giving me plenty of room for a solid game library and quick boot times.Build and Thermals: Lenovo nailed the design on this. The Eclipse Black finish looks sleek and premium without looking overly "gamer-y," so I feel comfortable bringing it to a coffee shop or office. More importantly, the cooling system is excellent; it handles long gaming sessions without thermal throttling, and the fans stay surprisingly quiet under normal loads.Price: Prices are going up. Was $1998 when I purchased, seen it rise to $2200 since then. Get it when the price drops, don't think it will stay low for long.The Verdict:Lenovo has hit a home run with the 2026 Legion 5a. It balances top-tier performance, a gorgeous display, and premium build quality perfectly. I highly recommend it to anyone wanting a future-proof gaming laptop!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Good deal for a budget gaming laptop
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This laptop is a pretty good choice if you're on a budget. It only comes with 8GB of RAM, which is *not* good for gaming, but all you need to do is install another 8GB and then Triple-A games will run perfectly fine. Battery life is to be expected for a gaming laptop. It can get decently hot playing demanding games, but there's a setting in the software it comes with to blast the fans, so no big deal there. When the fans do kick in for games, they can sound pretty loud (my dad calls it an air fryer), but again, that's to be expected for a budget gaming laptop. You can turn the fans down as needed. The Laptop looks pretty good for a budget gaming laptop. It's not a premium body, but Acer didn't sacrifice the internals, so I'm not too worried about that. It's a pretty good deal if you're on a tight budget and are looking for a gaming laptop that doesn't put a hole in your wallet. For $800 (with tax when I bought it), I would definitely recommend.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: US keyboard, packaging pretty dire.  Apart from that, it's a nice laptop.
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: This was a gift for the missus for Xmas.  Her previous laptop was getting slow and unreliable, plus it was not compatible for a Win11 upgrade, so I elected to buy her a new one.I went for what I considered reasonable spec.  I'm only recently getting into AMD processors where everything I read about Intel says they overheat.  It isn't as fast as my Alienware, but then it's a 6th of the price, but it's quick enough for what she uses it for.The screen is nice and clear and a reasonable size. The laptop itself is of a reasonable weight for the spec, it's not uncomfortable to spend an hour or so with it on your lap.  Everything seems quite well built and robust, nothing rattles and the lid hinges are good and tight.Where I've knocked a couple of stars off, the packaging was pretty poor.  Just a shoddy cardboard box, to the point I was amazed when I opened the box and the laptop inside was in one piece.  I mean, kudos for saving the planet and all that, but over half a grand of laptop deserves some foam and bubble wrap, I'd say.My second point, maybe only relevant if you're a UK buyer, and I wasn't observant enough to spot this beforehand, but the keyboard is US layout.  Easiest way to spot this is there is no key between the left hand shift and the Z key.  If you have a high enough resolution picture, zoom in and the "2" key has "@" on it for the shift up rather than the " quote symbol.  I can cope with that, the missus is trying to get to grips with it; this is the issue with buying from a foreign seller; I didn't realise the EU follow the US with this.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Ive used MSI for years motherboard, monitors and video cards. This laptop felt like a safe choice to let my kids use it since  we trust the brand. Specs are specs and I wanted a brand that I’ve used.What makes the Cyborg A15 a great MSI machine is what's underneath. We know that MSI is focused on efficient cooling and stable power and even in this more budget-friendly chassis, that core quality shows:1. Reliable Guts: The combination of the modern AMD Ryzen 7 260 and the RTX 5050 is good enough for my kids usage. It handles data quickly thanks to the 1TB NVMe SSD and the 16GB DDR5 RAM, meaning my kids aren't waiting on load screens—they're just playing. This stability and speed are exactly what we expect from MSI's engineering.2. The Cooling Mindset: Like any good gaming laptop or desktop, the cooling is designed for performance. Even though the fans can get loud under load (well not that load), that's just MSI's Cooler Boost technology doing its job: the thermals are good enough for the GPU and CPU so they don’t throttle during  gaming sessions. That stability is what you need.This isn't just reliable; it's also wrapped in a package that immediately appealed to the kids, which is the perfect mix for a gift:• The whole translucent black look is a fantastic piece of cyberpunk flair. The kids immediately gravitated to it. It makes the laptop feel unique and exciting—far from the generic black boxes• Gaming Experience: The 144Hz screen delivers a smooth playing experience for modern gaming, making even casual play feel responsive and high-end.The Trade-Off for all Gaming LaptopsIf you've used gaming laptops before, you know the biggest trade-off is usually the battery life. This is no exception. It’s an effective gaming laptop placement, but for peak performance, it needs to be plugged in. This is less about quality and more about physics: if you want high power in a slim body, you need a constant power source. If you just use the laptop normally you could get around 4 hours for battery life.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought the ROG Strix G16 with one major concern: future-proofing. I was tired of buying laptops that could handle games at launch, only to struggle with the next wave of AAA releases a year later. I can confidently say this machine has completely eliminated that worry. This laptop is an absolute beast that handles the latest, most graphically demanding games of 2024 and 2025 with stunning results.The star of the show is the NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060. Paired with the powerful Intel Core i7-13650HX, this laptop doesn't just run new games—it crushes them. I've been throwing everything at it, from sprawling open-world RPGs to fast-paced competitive shooters, and I'm consistently able to play on high or even ultra settings at a stable, high framerate.The real magic for keeping up with current releases is DLSS 3 with Frame Generation. This isn't just a gimmick; it's a revolutionary feature that significantly boosts performance in supported titles, ensuring that even the most unoptimized or graphically punishing games are incredibly smooth. It gives me peace of mind knowing that I have this technology in my back pocket for the big releases coming down the pipeline.All that power would be wasted without a great screen, and the 165Hz display is the perfect match. The gameplay is buttery smooth, with no tearing or stuttering. The motion clarity is night-and-day compared to older 60Hz screens, and it gives you a tangible edge in competitive games.Finally, the supporting hardware is top-notch. The 1TB Gen4 SSD means load times are practically nonexistent, and with 16GB of DDR5 RAM, multitasking with Discord or a browser open while gaming is effortless. Even during long sessions, the cooling system does an impressive job of keeping temperatures in check without sounding like a jet engine.If you're looking for a gaming laptop that won't just play today's games but is ready for tomorrow's, the ASUS ROG Strix G16 is a fantastic choice. It offers incredible performance that keeps pace with the ever-increasing demands of modern game development. Highly recommended!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: A perfect upgrade from another ASUS gaming laptop
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Where do I start? I've had this laptop now for ~9 months and do not have one complaint about it. It's fast, it's reliable, and it does everything I need it to and more for gaming.I had an ASUS TUF gaming laptop that I had for over 5 years and it did me very well up until the Unreal 5 Engine decided my cute, little GeForce GTX 1650 wasn't enough to run it.There were 2 things I upgraded right away and that was the NVME and RAM. Glad I did that at the time because WOW RAM is crazy expensive now; thanks a lot AI. Anyways, the 2TB storage upgrade was necessary so I could store more games on it rather than an external drive. Same with upgrading to 32gb RAM, and honestly, it should just be a common thing for PCs to come with no less than 24 or 32 gbs. I know 24 would be a little weird since there would be a 16gb stick and an 8gb stick but 16gb of RAM just doesn't cut it anymore.Anyway, if you're looking to upgrade and still want to stick with a laptop, this one is for you.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: It's been 2 months since I bought this laptop and I written my first review about a week after I bought this laptop. There is 2 things I want to point out. This gaming laptop has upgradable memory ram with 2 slots. Asus indicates that the maximum memory that can be installed is 32gb. I did a lot of research and I had messaged Crucial since the memory cards or sticks what ever you want to call them are compatible with this laptop. I asked if the 64gb which comes in a kit with 2x32gb sticks is compatible with the asus rog strix g16 g614jv model, they replied back to me and confirmed that "YES" this laptop memory ram can be upgraded to 64gb. How ever you have to buy the one that has the same speed as what the laptop has, since this laptop has a DDR5 4800hz sodimm stick that's what you're going to have to get. The memory ram comes in multiple of 2, i.e. this laptop comes with 2x8gb (16gb) .. If you want to add 32gb then you would have to get the kit that comes with 2x16gb and then 2x32gb (64gb). I upgraded to 64gb and had no problems installation was easy. Id did take about 3-5 minutes for the laptop to recognize the upgraded memory ram. Now same thing goes with the SSD storage Asus indicates that maximum storage is 2tb. I bought the 4tb Samsung 990 evo plus and installed it as the main Boot up OS C: drive. Of course you have to clone the SSD drive that come with the laptop but my point is that you can upgrade the SSD to 4tb. With this new upgrade my laptop is a beast. This laptop is worth it.  I'm just happy I bought a really good laptop and was able to make these upgrades .

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: A good upgrade, but could be better
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I had a 2019 model of an ASUS gaming laptop for the last five years, and I was excited to make a much needed upgrade to this one. I'm currently writing this review on the laptop lol. The laptop is sleek and stylish, notably bigger than previous models, and has a decent battery life in a world where laptops seemingly get worse and worse battery life. If you are someone who doesn't want to spend some time under the hood work-shopping things, I would not recommend this laptop. Sometime after a month of using the laptop, something went wrong and all my games started lagging and stuttering and I didn't know why. That's when I decided to entirely throw out all of the pre-baked ASUS software in favor of community made programs that aim to be less intensive on the computer. ASUS is a fine company, but they really like to make their software bloated, clunky, and obtrusive. So, if you're in the market for a gaming laptop, this is a good choice if you are willing to go a few extra steps and be more in control of your hardware.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I purchased the ASUS ROG Strix G16 gaming laptop in November 2024 as a Christmas gift to myself. I wanted to wait a few months and give it some serious work before writing a review.I wanted a gaming laptop that I could also use for some work applications as well. This laptop does everything I need and more! I've used it on games like World of Tanks, Fortnite and Call of Duty. The 16gb ram handles everything with no issues! I've recently started using it for some astrophotography processing and again, it does everything I need with no issues.I was a little worried after reading some of the reviews, but for the price and since most of the reviews were positive, I went ahead and pulled the trigger. And I'm glad I did! I have always bought from Dell and I was leaning that way again this time. Nothing against Dell, I've always had great success with them. But, for the price and what I got ... ASUS may be my new go to!If there is any downside, it would be the keyboard. The function is great, the lights are pretty cool, even though I just needed them be backlit, but the colors are ok too. But the only downsides to me are the Q,W,E,R,A,S,D and F keys are clear which make them hard to see. I assume it was done that way since they are the ones used most in gaming, but it's just an annoyance to me. The other issue is I would prefer a number pad on the right-hand side of the keyboard, this one doesn't have that. But neither issue is a deal breaker for me.I love this laptop! I definitely recommend it!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Had an Issue Soon After Warranty Expired, then ASUS Tech Support Made it Worse
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: One star seems to be the lowest possible.  I'd give it zero stars if I could.Purchased the ASUS ROG Strix G16 Gaming Laptop in Dec. 2024.  12 month warranty.  In February 2026 (14 months later) the built in screen on the laptop malfunctioned.  Couldn't view anything on the built in screen, but the laptop still had full function by using an external monitor.Called ASUS support to troubleshoot the issue with the built in monitor.  One of the steps their tech support rep instructed me to do was to go through steps on the computer to disable the Nvidia graphics card.  I reminded the tech rep that the built in monitor is not working, and that we need to make sure not do anything that will cause an external monitor to no longer work with the laptop.  He assured me that disabling the Nvidia card was the next step to perform and that it wouldn't be a problem.  So I did it, and then the ability to use an external monitor was immediately lost.Without the ability to use any screen, there has been no way to re-enable the Nvidia card.  So now because of ASUS tech support's mistaken instruction I lost all functionality for my laptop when prior to calling them I'd at least been able to use an external monitor with it (which is how the laptop has usually been used anyway).I requested that ASUS do the right thing to fix their mistake by approving action for their service department to restore the function of the Nvidia card so the laptop could again be used with an external monitor.But ASUS has only repeatedly said that because the computer is out of warranty they have no responsibility to fix it, even though it was their tech support that gave me instructions which caused the laptop to stop working with an external screen.Their response has continued to be that I can send the laptop into their service department, which will require me to pay shipping and a diagnostic fee, and then they'll provide an estimate for how much they'll charge to repair the issue that their tech support caused.This has been some of the worst customer service I've experienced for ANY product ever.  I will not ever buy another ASUS, and I'd recommend anyone considering one to choose a different brand instead.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I've wanted something that I could use as an everyday computer for work and use for gaming in my off time, something that could combine productivity and gaming in a compact design. I did a lot of research and found several (Razor Blade, Sager) but they were just too far out of my price range. I was worried I was being unrealistic for my budget. Then I came across the 2022 ASUS TUF Dash 15 (FX517ZM-AS73).From a physical standpoint I find the form factor is great in the hands and taking it mobile is a breeze thanks to it's compact, lightweight and super sleek design. I can easily pop it into my messenger bag when I need it on the go and when at home I can hook it up to a secondary display and enjoy gaming on it like I would a desktop.Under the hood it's clear ASUS wanted to make an impression. The hardware is impressive, yes, but how it synergies together is the most impressive part. Across the board performance is near instantaneous and (if power options and Armory Crate are utilized well) the battery life is also quite impressive when used for productivity tasks, too.The hardware is an ensemble cast with an Intel Core i7-12650H, 16GB of lightning fast DDR5 memory, a 512GB M.2 SSD and a 6GB GeForce RTX 3060 Mobile to round it out. It should be mentioned that while the computer itself supports Gen4 M.2 drives the stock 512GB SSD is Gen3 - likely to cut costs - however don't let that deter you as for an O/S drive it works great. Also, in a nice change of pace this laptop can be completely upgraded and you won't find any hardware soldered to the board. I have since added a 1TB Samsung 990 Pro in the second M.2 slot (for game installs, storage) and could not be happier with the near-instant performance.Speaking of performance I have yet to find a game title that I am unable to max out the settings on, even when hooked up running UHD resolutions on my secondary display (I have an LG UltraGear 27GL83A-B) which takes advantage of the G-Sync support for silky smooth response times. I've not yet even needed to use the "Turbo" mode as everything gets handled quite comfortably using the "Performance" setting.ASUS did their homework when they designed the 2022 iteration and you can tell they were paying attention, the 2022 Dash 15 corrects many of the complaints from the previous years model and then some. The new cooling system design is incredibly effective and helps cut back on a lot of fan noise, even when under load (using the "Performance" setting) the fans when kicked up are barely audible while keeping everything nice and cool.I'm very impressed with this machine and can easily recommend it to anybody interested in this model. No matter if you're looking for a dedicated gaming laptop or something to use for daily productivity tasks and some gaming on the side the 2022 ASUS TUF Dash 15 (FX517ZM-AS73) is hard to beat for performance and value.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great value but definitely not perfect
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Shipment was great and the laptop performs decently (didn't expect too much of a cut down version of an i7 with 3060), it's quite thing for its hardware, lightweight (a bit less than 2kg, my previous one was 2.5kg) and offers somewhere between 3-6 hours of moderate use.It can be charged via type C, only using the none-thunderbolt port (shame, could be great to use on a dock for users who don't use it to its max) up to 100w. works great for none-Asus chargers. charged it with 45w,65w,100w and for light usage it works great. when gaming even 100w aren't enough to keep it charged, but you can expect 2-3 hours of repeated gameplay instead of like 30-60 minutes.Due to it's light weight I find it best to carry it around with a power bank on the go as the combined weight is still a bit less than the average gaming machine. type c charging really is a life changer.The display isn't the brightest but I never found it to be an issue even when working in a coffee shop without any shade so good enough, and the IPS level quality is good.Some downsides:- build quality has some issues. some plastic parts that cover the screen hinges sometimes fall off a bit and needs to be pressed back in.the screen has 4 rubbers at each side to prevent the screen from being too close to the keyboard when closed, but even though I used a sleeve bag to house the laptop, the rubber left a permanent mark on the sides of the keyboard which look a bit off, and the screen still got scratched a bit by the display. mostly not noticeable but it's worth mentioning.software wise this machine isn't the most reliable, all Asus software on machine is buggy as hell so I'd avoid anything but the minimal use of armory crate. the machine registers temperatures, usage percentages and much more incorrectly. sometimes the temps are low, nothing is open, but armory crate says GPU utilization is at like 80% and the fans go hard (they aren't very loud, it's just surprisingly random). then you need to enter armory crate and after 3 seconds it resets.Overall, if you put a microfiber cloth between the display and the keyboard (you can find large ones for like one dollar on amazon and Aliexpress), you can take a very small charger/power bank on the go and enjoy great performance and portability at a great price. usually similar machines cost way more. I'd still recommend to see if the issues are relevant for you and your use case but I am satisfied.
